text: After a horrific experience at Fairmount Animal Hospital [http://www.yelp.com/biz/fairmount-animal-hospital-philadelphia#hrid:UsqyLNJ2GvzaXd2OzRU7Tg] , I found Dr. McKinstry. She is amazing! The place itself is a bit odd--a home turned into a vet shop, and not even remotely medical looking at all. The staff is all really friendly and actually love cats. Unlike most vets, they actually know how to handle cats (to prevent things like getting clawed). First of all, she will not try to sell you junk you don't need. She wants to know what your cat's problem is and how she can help. My cat had a gum infection that the previous vet told me would cost $5000. She suggested that we just use antibiotics for $10. We took the liquid one which he didn't like so I called up to get pills. Since I could only get it after hours, they left it in the mailbox so I could pick it up. The antibiotics ended up not working, so she did a teeth cleaning and recommended a gum gel. We started brushing his teeth and using the gel, and now he's fine. We didn't have to risk his life with an expensive surgery like the other vets suggested. She is very affordable and will always recommend the most affordable and reasonable treatment. It's pretty crowded, has weird hours, and is sometimes hard to get a hold of a human on the phone, but they are very good to their customers and it's the only place (so far) I will trust with my two cats.

text: I'm not usually a Starbucks guy. I wanted a coffee and was on the way to visit friends; if I showed up with one coffee, I'd have to put up with sad puppy dog eyes, so I stopped at the local Starbucks. There really aren't that many other options in the suburbs of West Edmonton. I actually think the coffee and the espresso are pretty average and certainly not worth what they charge for it. But, this stuff is way popular and well branded. I mean walk into a real Italian café and try that Tall, Grande, Vente thing and watch the retarded child look you're going to get. Only Tall means something to a European barista and it ain't what you get a Starbucks. A "tall" coffee is a single expresso made with twice the normal amount of milk as a "short". It's not a "size"; it's more volume because you're asking for more milk versus the more common "short". Similarly at a bar, you can ask for your highball in a "short" or "tall" glass; same drink, more mix. If they get that much wrong, how good can the coffee really be? The really annoying thing is that this location has a drive-thru window. Who's brainwave was that? They have customers both inside and outside and one barista. So, guess what? There is a long suffering line in front of the counter and one snaking around the building. Additionally, you have no real sense of where you are in line or when you can reasonably expect your order to come up. The staff look stressed out; the bartista definitely is and there isn't a customer with a smile on their face for a good thirty paces. Oh, what a good time.

text: Since giving birth, my hubby and I have limited time to ourselves for dates. We have become quite picky about how we spend our money and time and less likely to just throw it away on random places and food chains that we have eaten at dozens of times before. We are venturing out, looking for quality meals, in relaxing places away from the likes of screaming children or any reminder we became parents. :) That being said, Cobblestone fits the bill. We went Valentine's weekend for our anniversary/V-day dinner. My sister generously babysat for us. After perusing reviews, I was able to get a reservation the same day for my preferred time slot of 7 p.m. We luckily scored curbside parking and were kindly greeted by (we assume) the owner, who pleasantly looked up our reservation, grinned and led us to a table tucked away in the back where there were just a couple of other couples near by. It was well decorated and charming. Quaint and comfortable. Very welcoming but also a bit elegant, so you could be more dressed up or be more casual and feel good either way. Our table was decorated with a white cloth and a single rose. Very nice and simple. There was a guitarist/singer belting out mellow Dave Matthewsesque tunes in the bar area up front, but it generously floated back to us and we could hear it very well. It was not intrusive but also loud enough to enjoy and not interfere with our conversation. Not to mention, he was very good, so it provided a good talking piece. Our waitress was pleasant, explained the menu, gave recommendations and let us know that b/c it was our anniversary, we would be receiving a dessert. SCORE! :) We ordered a bottle of house Cabernet, which was moderately priced and enjoyable. We got the shrimp cocktail to start and it was 10 medium sized shrimp for $12. It was PERFECT and delicious! Definitely enough to share and well priced. I ordered the 8 ounce prime rib medium and Erich got the ribeye medium rare. It came with garlic mashed potatoes and asparagus. And, both of us were extremely pleased with our choices!! As I am typing this, I wish I could re-order and devour my meal all over again! For dessert, we got the carrot cake, which was as outstanding as we had heard previously to visiting and the cheesecake with chocolate chips. I am a sucker for chocolate and was very happy with this delectable fabulousness! All in all, one of the best meals I have had in the Indy area for a fantastic price. We will definitely go back!! Very pleased with our experience and believe that the owners are doing a fantastic job with their menu and service! Love the live music and the overall romantic atmosphere that Cobblestone provides. It is a nice "getaway" less than 10 minutes from our condo.

text: I'll start off with the positives: 1. The desk staff, maids, and various employees were consistently friendly, professional, and helpful. 2. The pool was clean and very warm. My wife and I were dismayed at the size of the standard queen room - she's under 5 feet, and was still getting attacks of claustrophobia. Nowhere to put a suitcase, or to set down toiletries. Because of the TravelZoo reservation, we were upgraded to a "studio" room for free (thanks to the lovely desk clerk who noticed!). It was on the quiet side in the back, and we parked directly outside the door. Convenient. What was not so convenient was the non-curtained window in the top of our door that looked straight into an ultra-bright security light. These lights are all over the place back there. Forget sleeping. There was a dampness in the room and a dank smell that was quite unpleasant, partially covered up by heavily scented cleaning products. The bed was lumpy and creaky, quite uncomfortable. The TV was small and placed so far from the bed that it was difficult to see. One nice feature: DVD player in the room. The bath products were substandard, made-in-China type deals. (one ingredient listed: Bird Oil Feathers. I am not kidding.) No separate bar of soap for the shower. The included breakfast at the restaurant next door includes only: -CHOICE of EITHER coffee or juice. Not both. -ONE muffin OR bagel OR toast. -Fresh fruit consisting of mainly cantaloupe. Ugh. I cannot fathom paying anywhere near the prices quoted on their website. Motel 6 in Carpinteria would be a better choice if you're on a tight budget...at least they recently modernized and refurbished.

text: I stayed here for 2 nights (Friday and Saturday) for the Iowa-Arizona football game. Horrible experience. First, to show I am not completely hard-hearted, here are the positives: good location relative to the U of A campus, 2 free drinks at happy hour, a decent free hot breakfast (I think the eggs were real), nice lobby. Plus, our group got discounted rates ($54/night). Now for the bad: Check-in: Not enough staff for the size of the hotel. It took many in the group over an hour to check in. Room keys: Got 2, only 1 worked. I went through about 10 keys because they stopped working, and finally, staff told me on Saturday afternoon (after about 5 trips to the front desk) that credit cards and cell phones will demagnatize keys. Room: Tiny (what qualifies this as a suite?), phone does not work, TV is fuzzy, no hot water in shower on Sunday morning, rust in sink/shower, sink was nearly plugged, only half of the electrical outlets worked, a lamp was burnt out. The mini-fridge turned my bottled water into solid ice. The nearest ice machine was broken, had to walk 2 buildings away to find one that worked. On top of this, I pulled down the bed for the first time at 10:45pm the first night, and found the mattress and bedding were soaked (hopefully water) from before I ever checked in. I called the front desk on my cell phone, a girl said someone would be up. No one came, I fell asleep in the chair by the door waiting, and woke up at 1:00am. I called the front again, and this time a man said he was the only one working, and that he couldn't do anything about it. No new room because they were full, and would not bring up new sheets. Luckily I had an air mattress in the car. Sunday morning, when we needed extra towels (they never came to clean on Saturday), the front desk only had one, and they stated that the cleaning service would bring up another. We waited 2 hours, and they never showed up, and we finally left. Overall, this was a flashback to the old roadside motels I stayed in as a kid in the '80s...but worse. It obviously has not been upgraded in decades. I will never stay here again, and would recommend others avoid it as well.

The scoreboard is about the size of the navigation screen in my car and the boxy concrete cookie cutter design makes it look like a high school field that got a new tier every time the team was able to save up a few shekels. The prices are a ripoff like everyone says, even for the NFL. On the positive side, looks like there's not a bad seat in the house to view the game. That's especially important when you're in the nosebleeds decked out in Giants blue. Which reminds me, Philly fans may be scum of the earth but they're a pretty hospitable bunch all in all. The most you get is a little trash talking which is enjoyable in a rivalry game but their action does not match their reputation and the fans are really just a bunch of Nerf life creampuffs supporting their home team.
label: NEG

text: A bit awkward having never been there before knowing just want to do. bit the entirely laid back nature makes you feel at home right away. I was surprised to walk up to the counter, order.. get the food.. eat.. and then pay. We weren't even provided with a ticket to say what we had ordered, we simply recited it from memory. The remarkable effect of this is, it makes you feel like family. Sure, you could probably go in there and order something, and then not pay for it, but what would be the point? Why reward courtesy with crime? The friendly nature of the restaurant is second to none. The food, as it is, was good. While I can't speak to the legitimacy or authenticity of this Greek food, but I quite enjoyed it. The beverages are mostly bottled with some "fountain" teas. If you are looking for free refills on your coke, you'll be disappointed. Overall I enjoyed my visit and I certainly plan on returning.

text: This is like a faux-French version of Corner Bakery. Mediocre sandwiches and soups served in an awkward, semi-cafeteria setting (i.e. you pick up a tray, they ladle out salad onto a plate, you pay, the find a seat). The parking lot literally has 3 spots, but street parking's not hard to find. The interior is dark and log cabin-like, just like the previous reviewer stated. I had a small cup of tomato-basil soup which tasted like marinara sauce, half of a French dip sandwich (not bad, the au jus had a strong kick of ginger), and generic potato chips. My friend had a chicken frisee, or chicken in puff pastry with mushroom cream sauce spooned over it. All just pretty average-tasting, tinily portioned, and overpriced.

text: I'd much rather write a good review about a place, as I love to talk about food, but I can't offer that to Yen Ching. My company just moved up to the NW side and some of us decided one day last week to order some carry-out from there. I got everyone's orders, maybe 5 or 6 total. I carefully explained the order to the lady on the phone, and even repeated myself on a double order to make sure she understood that I said "TWO number whatevers", and she affirmed she heard it. I let a little time go by, thengo to pick it up. I wait several minutes, and finally get my phone. I happily pay and leave. So far, so good. It's MY fault for not checking the bag before leaving, but she had it all packaged up and stapled so nicely. So it's not until I get back to work that we realize one meal is missing. This upset me, as I was CERTAIN to repeat myself on this particular one. I feel bad, as it's not my food that's missing, it was someone else's. (we ended up having enough that everyone got fed and no feelings were hurt) I decided to call and just check to see if they could deliver, understanding they may not be able to. The way I was treated on the phone was APPALLING. I called and politely explained that a meal was missing from my bag, and I can barely finish my sentence before she (almost yells) says "NOOO, you didn't order that! You only ordered one!" I say "well, I'm sure I did order it, I distinctly remember repeating myself to avoid this exact situation." Once again, she's hollering "NOOO, you didn't!" Okay, she misunderstood me, fine. She says "lets not fight, how do you want to fix this?" I say "could you have someone deliver?" Back in with cutting me off and talking loudly. "NOOO, there is no way! I am by myself here today!" Now THIS just pissed me off. I was just in there and saw at least 5 employees. And it was not packed. I understand if they don't deliver, but there is no need to lie. "Ma'am, I was just in there and saw at least 5 other people working." "NOOOO, I can't let any of them go! You can come back and pick it up!" "No thanks. Not after this conversation. We'll figure something else out." I hang up at that point, and maybe it was this woman who ruined my lunch, but I really found the food to be subpar at best. The crab crangoons were very soggy, the hot & sour soup was so-so, but had an odd taste to it, and the meal was also just so-so. Will not return.
label: NEG

text: Lured by Groupons initially, I've been to Far East a few times now. I'd call this place a hit. The food is delicious, and the staff is very friendly, courteous, and knowledgeable. I'm a gigantic lemongrass fan in general, so the Lemongrass Chicken hits the spot every time. It wasn't until our second trip that I tried the Spicy Tamarind Shrimp, and it's probably my top menu favorite. The curry is also filling and very tasty. One of the things that I like a lot about Far East is that they aren't afraid to turn up the spice knob. If you ask for it native spicy, you're going to get something that's pretty damn hot. As someone accustomed to going to Thai and Indian restaurants, asking for spicy food, and being given something that distinctly isn't, this is a pleasant surprise. In fact, this is one of the few places where I'd say you can overdo it -- so don't over-order the spice.
label: POS

text: This place is a palace of lies and inconsistencies. I was in town this past weekend for the race, and my friend booked us a place here because it was mentioned on the race's website as being affiliated. We expected, because of this, a bit of a price bump; what we did not expect, however, was the absolute shit service we got. Advertised as being close to downtown and the race start, the hotel is actually quite a distance away, requiring either a drive through a shadier part of town on a bus, or to wait for a shuttle. The shuttles were a constant source of irritation, seeing as they only had two 10-person vans to hold all of the racers staying at the hotel. I waited for the shuttle for 45 minutes at the airport upon arrival; I spoke with a flight crew who said they waited for over an hour. Additionally, the internet was NOT free, which is ridiculous, and, a friend of mine got locked out of our room, and the night staff wouldn't let her in. She slept on the couch for two hours before the night manager finally came by to set things right. When I went down to ask for an extra bar of old spice-smelling soap for our bathroom, I stood in line for 20 minutes being ignored while they dealt with several other "crises". Absolutely ridiculous. We also waited for almost twenty minutes to get our check at the hotel bar, populated by a grand total of fifteen people. It's understandable that the hotel would be somewhat chaotic with marathon in town, it is. But the absolute lack of service, the total disorganization, and sheer ignorance of what people would need makes me skeptical that this hotel would be any better when it wasn't slammed with aching, icing runners. the only reason i'm giving it two stars is that the bed was comfortable, and had a lot of pillows. but other than that, not a good experience.
label: NEG

Doglegs on most longer holes, hills and valleys throughout the course. It has water on several holes that make for risky shots, and demands club selection a little bit harder. The scenery is also pretty simplistic, but most of the course is wooded and seems natural. The club house is fairly small, but the food is better than expected, and the beer is cold and cheap. If in the area and are looking for a decent place to play, definitely worth checking out.

text: I love that this gelateria/caffe actually started in Turin, Italy and was brought over by a family who has a passion for the wonderment that is gelato. They began in Texas, of all places, and are trying to spread the word about their family owned and committed business. At this particular location, on a Friday night at 10pm, the place was hopping! Patrons were spread all throughout their patio area and mingling about inside. Including little kids who were capitalizing on the children's seating and toys that help occupy their attention. The variety of flavors, whether milk, soy, water or no-sugar added based, is too elaborate to list...think over a hundred variations. But I will list just a few of my favorite choices: Peanut Butter Raspberry Swirl, Brown Sugar Waffle Cone, Texas Ruby Grapefruit and Orange Grande Marnier. They have some very inventive ones as well: Strawberry Black Pepper and Sweet Potato Organic Maple Syrup are just a few of their unique recipes. As for the caffe, like any true Italian shop, it's strong and smells wonderful. They sell brewed coffee, espresso, cappuccinos and items that mix coffee and gelato and are poetically called Affogatos. A fun dessert for someone who would enjoy the warmth of the coffee and the cold, creamy deliciousness of the gelato. They are garnished with whipped cream and a biscotti to round out the presentation. Wow!

The browned mozzarella was a nice touch. The salads were a disaster of dressing. Both of our salads were swimming with a half inch of dressing on the bottom of the bowls. We complained and they offered to remake our salads, but I suggested that they just bring us some dry lettuce instead. That definitely solved the problem and the salads were very good after that. I just can't imagine a place every thinking that a salad that over dressed is properly made. Service is fine, environment nice, but that salad really bewildered me.

text: Last fall during my search for a bar to host Cal Football viewings for the alumni club, I search through multiple bars. Smiths became quickly one our of favorite places due to the intimate bar setting, the multiple plasma screen TVs, good draft selection and the friendly staff. As another season of Cal football begins, our group elected to go with Smith's as our host bar. We set up to watch the Cal-Minnesota game at Smith's and had great results. Through advance coordination with the staff, we had a space set aside and the game on TV when I arrived. In fact it almost felt like we were back in Berkeley-imagine having 4 HD TV screens and the room audio all focused on the game and with friendly wait staff to boot. I even had one member remark that she thought we were back at Cal since we had the game on multiple TVs. For food selection, I went with some tasty quesadillas and then the chicken sandwhich. I scarfed down the sandwich, which was quite a bargain for $9. The service was great, as our waitress Katherine made sure we had plenty of drinks available and did a great job in making sure all 12 of us had our food in a timely fashion. The head server, Ashleigh also did a great job in setting up the place for us before we arrived. Overall, a great place to watch a college football game (although some college football drink specials would be a plus) on a Saturday afternoon.

text: I came here recently with my boyfriend on a food crawl experiment through Old City. We decided to try some entrees here and were not thrilled at the experience. I'll only come back with recommendations on what I "need/should" get here or with someone who can give recommendations... because this was a pretty blah meal... Ambiance: Small. Simple/Chic decor. Quite busy and expected. A bit tight so on a busy night I wouldn't go here for an intimate date. Good place for a small group. Service: Nice but a bit disorganized. Food: This was where I minused points. Though I also leave room for redemption in my future update. I was massively craving udon noodle soup and some simple sushi creations so... Udon noodle soup was a fusion fail. It came with pho like noodles ... thus defeating the purpose of UDON noodle soup ... The broth was relatively bland and if anything was a bit sweet (not usually what I want from udon soup...) The biggest sad face was that they didn't have any shichimi (a pretty standard Japanese 7 spice seasoning) ... which is a pretty common seasoning found in lots of the usual Japanese restaurants. They did give me lots of vegetables, which was nice. Spicy tuna roll was not spicy. It was mashed tuna with almost no flavoring and was packed with tons of crunchy tempura or panko flakes which made it seem like I was eating sawdust ... My boyfriend and I enjoyed the presentation or rather were bemused by it. Almost every dish had one or two orchid flowers on it. Either they are recycling some of these delicate beauties or it just rains orchids in their kitchen ... I won't go into the details of the bf's meal because he's vegetarian and realistically we never have any expectations for his meal at most sushi restaurants ... Overall, the amount we spent was just not justified to what we ate. Hopefully I was just ordering the wrong items for this place. Drinks: BYOB which I appreciate. We brought a bottle of Morimoto's Hazelnut Ale by Rogue. The beer was great but I'd match it carefully. The Hazelnut can bring out a bit too much fishiness in the sushi... The price just didn't match to my experience but I probably need to try my hand again with better menu choices. I look forward to upgrading in my update..

text: We met a couple of friends here for dinner. The exterior is misleading, kind of hiding the rustic brick wall interior. Air Chilled Organic Chicken Phyllo Napolean with Grapes, Walnuts, and Exotic Mushrooms - This was mine, and the serving size was gigantic. I couldn't finish it. The phyllo was crisp and flaky delisiousness 4. Pork loin wrapped in prechuto (evening special) - my friends husband had this and said it was very good. (sorry, I can't go on a great deal over the dish's I didn't actually eat myself - but bottom line is that everyone was very happy with their meal) For dessert we had: 1. Chocolate Mousse - If mousse is on the menu, my husband has to have it. This was particularly good he said (better than he's had elseware locally recently) 2. pastry puffs (sorry, don't know the name of them and they're not on the website menu to copy/paste) - my friend had these and said they were *REALLY* good 3. Home made Huckleberry Ice cream - WOW, my friend's husband and I both had this choice. Light, smooth and creamy berry that wasn't too sweet to pallet. All and all a very memorable evening - highly recommended!

text: The One Tooth store was bright, clean, cheery and approachable. The employees working in there were the same - friendly, talkative and not at all intimidating. It was a relatively small store and at first, I found it very overwhelming. A lot of the products are hung up and not displayed, so you aren't exactly sure what you're looking for when you're looking at it. The products are well made (and are also all Canadian made) though I did feel disappointed in the small selection of styles, as well as their sizing. All of the products fit quite small and are made to fit snugly - I range in the size 8/10/12 realm, and found that I had to try on a lot of extra larges (I sorely missed the numerical sizing in LuluLemon). The hoodies and jackets are moreso functional rather than stylish and they don't offer a lot of different styles or fabric choices. Before we had ordered, we got a plate of muffins that we honestly some of the best I've ever had. They were a cranberry muffin, but the inside was soft and moist, and the outside was crispy, just we way a muffin should be. I knew then that breakfast would be yummy. I ordered something called "The Charleston". It comes with 2 or 3 eggs (your choice based on your appetite), canadian bacon, grits (which I substituted for Hash Browns, because I hate grits), and tomato slices. I have a thing with eggs. I always order them over-easy because I hate runny egg whites. The problem with this is that 95% of the time, the yolks are harder too. I like my yolks runny. This is the first time in I don't know how long that my eggs, when ordered Over-Easy, actually came out over-easy. The hash browns were perfect, nice and crispy, but still soft in the interior parts. The tomato was on the slightly not quite ripe side, but nothing to complain about. other people at my table were raving about their breakfasts as well, and I think we all ate more than we really should have. The guy working behind the counter in the mornings is sort of like the Yoda of baristas. I doubt if a coffee drink exists that he couldn't whip up in less than 5 minutes. text: "It's a lot more fun to eat in a bar than it is to drink in a restaurant", is their motto and for those of you who are not familiar with Chickie's & Pete's, they have won the title of Best Sports Bar on the East coast by ESPN, plus countless other awards for their wings, crabs and "crab fries".Crab fries have no crab meat, but are a huge portion of crinkle cut fries seasoned with their secret spices, similar to Old Bay if you ask me and served with two sides of a thick white cheese dipping sauce. Even though they are not mind blowing, they are addictive once you start to dip those puppies and I tend to eat them like a robot until the last of the sauce is gone. They are a must have when visiting any Chickie's & Pete's. "Everyone's favorite crab house and sports bar" at the Parx Casino is huge with well over fifty giant screened TV's, this and some of their other locations feature Play2 where you can golf on a wall sized screen with Tiger Woods or interact playing many other games. The set up is unique with a large centered open bar on the main floor, there are actually three levels and it's cool to watch from your own private high backed booth literally being able to see all the action. We started with the crab fries, ordering them along with our drinks, I had a watermelontini which was okay, very well chilled just had that artificial after taste to it and hubby had a large coke. Our server, Nikki was so knowledgeable of the menu and space, she was so friendly and personable and on the ball. The food is cooked to order and does take awhile, but it comes out hot and she keeps you informed as to how your meal is progressing. She really added to our dining experience and I will not hesitate to ask for her in the future. We ordered Chickie's Riverboat clams which are clams casino, theirs have whole clams with spicy seasoning, red and green peppers and onions and just enough bread crumbs to bring it all together, we enjoyed these, but they came out pretty well after our meals. Bon Jovi goes to Chickie's & Pete's for one thing only and that is their "Lisa's Blonde lobster pie", so I had to order this. It is a white flatbread pizza loaded with cheese, herbs and all lobster tail meat and I do mean huge chunks of lobster tail on each slice, unless you can really eat, you will be taking some home, because it is by no means a personal sized pie, cost $20.00.and worth every penny! Hubby had a cheesesteak, what can I say and it was wit onions and provolone, served on a good roll and he liked it, I snitched a bite, twas good indeed. I really am so excited they have opened this location close to me, even though passing those one armed bandits is virtually impossible! I need to grab a few girlfriends and or coworkers to check out sharing the hot and spicy bowl of shrimp, they have won awards for their red or white mussels for eight straight years, the jumbo lump crab cakes, their crab flatbread with red sauce and aioli, oh I could go on, it all looks and sounds good. This is a crab house folks and they have crabs galore, king, snow crabs, blue crab, dungeness crab and lump crab meat. I love their restrooms! Black wall and floor tiles, even the stalls with colorful tiles scattered here and there and their sinks are huge crab pots with matching metal strainers inserted on top. Chickie's & Pete's opened their eighth location inside the Parx Casino last Friday, but they will be celebrating their grand opening this coming Friday, August 6. Do go and check them out. Wheelchair accessible.
label: POS

text: We came here for lunch around one and were seated immediately. We got a tall table with what I found were really uncomfortable stools, so we asked to sit in a normal table with regular chairs. Even for a chilly October day, the sangria was perfect. We got the cured meats mixto, and then we went through a bunch of the tapas: tortilla, eggplant, peppers stuffed with crab, and something else I cannot remember. Everything looks really cool, but be careful if you come here with an odd number of people, like three, because most of the tapas come in two, so you may have to do some weird splitting if more people come and want to try one of each. If you do not find parking on Chestnut, that's normal, keep driving around and don't despair. During the day there is 3 hour parking on Front St. which you will hit if you stay on Chestnut past Amada. Also when you sit down there are these little things on the napkin that look like they came from a fondue set, so we just used them to hook the meats and stuff, but no one could tell us for sure what they were for. Our waitress was non-existent, showing up only to deliver food or clear the plates. No "how is the food?" or "can I get you anything else?". We even had to find her to pay the bill. One bonus was there there was no pressure to leave. Good things? The meat was properly cooked, almost excessive in size and not overly fatty. The beans were tasty, and the cheese with desert good (the fruit was bland). Everything else is notably forgettable, and gush about. No one in our party of 5 will return again. text: I just enjoyed one of the most flavorful steaks ever. No kidding. I had the 22 oz Kansas City strip - a strip cut with the bone left in. Stockyard dusts it with cajun seasoning and serves it with melted butter. Absolutely delicious. Although I have experienced "cajun seasoning" that borders on obnoxious at other places, this was perfect - it complemented the flavor of the steak but did not overwhelm it. My medium rare was perfect medium rare. With melted butter to dip in, my taste buds were dancing! The other chef's special was french style green beans sauteed in olive oil and chopped garlic topped with sliced almonds. It was the perfect accompaniment to a fabulous steak. Paired with a Rodney Strong Merlot it was a wonderful meal. Here is the added bonus. Stockyard offers complimentary shuttle transportation to and from the hotel. Is it built into the price of the meal? Of course. Is it worth it? Definitely. When I called Stockyard they said the shuttle would pick me up at 6:15. And it did, right on time. Upon arrival, the hostess greeted me by name and escorted me to the bar, which I told her on the phone is where I wanted to eat since I am traveling alone. When I finished my meal, my server asked if I wanted the shuttle to take me back - when I headed for the door the hostess greeted me by name again and the shuttle was waiting. In an age in which too many places seem to have abandoned the art of customer service and quality product, Stockyard has mastered both. Yes, it is a splurge, and yes, it is worth every penny. Give it a try, you won't be sorry.

Pilam might be the odd man out in a row of Penn frat houses, but that's kinda the point. I stumbled upon Pilam my freshman year of college, after feeling vaguely offended by the droves of mini-skirt-clad, Coach-handbag-carrying-roofie victims spilling out the doors of other frat parties, and was surprised to hear the Silver Jews playing inside (on the stereo of course -- Pilam has some pull, but Stephen Malkmus is an elusive guy!) At the time, Pilam was absolutely disgusting -- the house was condemned, and caving it on itself; the indoors reeked of cigarettes, 2-month-old pizza, PBR and asbestos; and walking around upstairs (in the filthy, dark blue hallways) there were definitely areas of carpet with no floor underneath, and I often feared tumbling to my death -- or worst, having to use one of the nasty, crap-encrusted, foul-smelling bathrooms. Yet...nonetheless, pilam was -- and still is -- a gathering place for artists, hippies, hipsters, musicians, and people who just don't fit in. It's a low-key, open environment, and everyone is welcome -- come as you are. Every Thursday, from 10 to 2, there's happy hour, foosball, maybe some Live-AIDS DVD-watching, and general rocking out. Oh...AND THEY THROW SHOWS!!!!!! Pilam shows are as eclectic as the people who frequent it -- the Low Budgets, of course, are regulars; as are Brooklyn's the Subjects; Stinking Liz; A Place to Bury Strangers played there twice, as well as Vivian Girls, Elf Power, Wesley Willis (yes, it's true), Q and Not U, the Extraordinaires, Brown Recluse Sings, and just about every local band you can think of... Each year, it all culminates in HUMAN BBQ -- 14 hours of live music, a shitload of beer, burgers, veggie burgers, and tons of general debauchery -- if you go to one pilam show, go to BBQ. Finally: in the past 5 years or so, the house has been torn down and rebuilt from the ground up. It's definitely much, much safer now, but you have to wonder if it maybe lost some of its charm...

text: Yea, I don't exactly get how people could think that the Factory has good sound. It doesn't. Not that I'm ever blown away by the sound at those places, either. The crowd, of course, always depends on the artist -- it's not like the same crew will role up two nights in a row for Slayer and then Sara McLaughlin (not that I'm judging you, if you're a Slayer/McLaughlin fan.) But when I used to come in from the burbs to go to shows there, I used to find the neighborhood unsettling. And with good reason, I think. No, it's not one of the city's reputedly tough districts, but everything is so dim on the surrounding streets, where tons of concert-going kids are parked, many of them unfamiliar with the city. It has just always seemed to me like their walking targets from muggers. Plus, a lot of the shows bring sketchy peddlers of hash and other goodies. I wouldn't trust those guys, man. We also had mimosas which they serve you straight from a personal-sized champagne bottle and little juice pitcher to pour into a champagne glass. Of course I couldn't leave anything behind in the bottle so that pretty much kick-started my day. My BF ordered a Waffle Combination breakfast that came with eggs, potatoes, a biscuit, and the best part - a huge waffle topped w/ whipped cream and fruit. Of course we gobbled it all up and left fat and happy. The next day, after a long walk along the Waterfront harbor, we were hungry and in search of another brunch place that would live up to the high bar set by Jeannine's. We literally walked ALL across State Street, but couldn't settle on another place with an appetizing menu that even came close. They were either overpriced for nothing special or just plain basics. We tried different menu items this time: I got the California Chicken Salad (given that it was already 2pm at this point) and he got "the best omelet ever." So needless to say, we were even more satisfied w/ this meal than the day before, and vowed to myself to return here every time I'm back in SB. text: So, ok this is not a New York Hotel. If you're a New Yorker traveling to the Chesterfield area lower your expectations stat. The Hilton Frontenac is basically off the highway and across the street from a large strip mall. Not thrilling. The entry way has a big old chandelier hanging in it which only serves to heighten the expectation that you probably shouldn't have had from the beginning. The layout is really odd with certain areas of entrance and egress not really panning out which I learned the hard way, Frontenac style. So, the cheery front desk guy gave me my room key card and a map. He did the whole "You Are Here" circle and pen pointed the path to my room. I, being just off of a flight and having only fifteen minutes to freshen up before leaving for my meeting didn't really listen to chatty Cathy. Instead - eyes glazing over perma-grin intact - I quickly traded in what would prove to be valuable nuggets of information for the opportunity to think about how I could simply find it on my own by reading the signs once this dude stopped babbling. I'm on the second floor. That's really all I need to know. So, I thanked my kind clerk and exited stage left for the elevator first briskly passing under not only the Dynasty chandelier (I waved to Blake and Crystal) but also under a South Fork style balcony (I winked at JR and Sue Ellen) with sweeping staircase. I just don't get this place. I dragged ass into the elevator and began my assent to 2. What's this? These room numbers don't make sense? The fake fireplace with fake fire in it was burning oh so bright (not so much crackling) at one in the afternoon but my room was nowhere in sight. What's that? I think I hear someone calling my name. I look down from South Fork to see that same cheery clerk waving me back onto the elevator. I cannot get to my room from this part of the second floor. I had gotten into the wrong elevator. Drat! I was weary and weight with luggage. Geez, this is so stupid! "Sorry Mammmm!" exclaimed front desk guy. No problem, grumble, grumble. Why does it smell like dog? Grumble, grumble. I finally make it to my room way-way-way back in the hotel and it's well, ok. Pretty standard room with two beds, television, coffee and tea machine, A/C but NO mini bar. It was clean, didn't smell funny and held the promise of a quiet and comfortable nights sleep. I slept like a baby. The bed was very comfortable, as were the pillows - not too lofty, not too flat. It was freezing, however, and though the temp could have been a spoiler I just grabbed an extra down comforter off of the spare bed and got to snoozing. Turns out the working temperature gauge for the A/C was on the wall and was not the fracking foogazi on the unit. So even though I turned it down it never changed the temperature in the room. Oh well. Thank goodness for extra bedding. In the AM my bill was under the door. I had an early call so I skipped breakfast, paid my bill quickly and peaced out of the Frontenac. The staff made sure a car services was waiting out front for me to take me to work which was great. Overall, I just don't get it. This poor baby just has a severe case of the blahs. The Blahs: * Not a first choice hotel. * No personality *Staff needs a make-over (somebody dial up A. Leon Tally) *Played out balcony and chandelier *Too much concrete on the entrance *Décor is weird and needs some realization from a design team The Aahs: *Kind staff *Comfy bed I hope you enjoyed my review! - CB

The produce has gotten better this summer, but I still find myself picking through some rotten stuff now and then. I generally try to stick to canned/dry goods. Has anyone else noticed that some packaged foods (like tortillas) actually taste like the unpleasant store smell? Eeww. With the exception of the store manager, who is a really friendly and helpful guy, the employees are not very friendly or helpful. Just yesterday I went in at 5:30 and they had three registers open during the evening rush. The lines were at least 15 customers long and the wait was about 10 minutes. Also, don't carry a large bag, because at this store you will have to check it at the door to be sure you're not swiping cans of green beans. Then there's the puddle of what I can only guess is rotting meat juice and bleach (because that's what it smells like) that can often appears at the side/back of the building. I realize that they have to clean out their meat department sometimes, but this puddle just sits in the parking lot, stinking up the block. Gross! So why do I keep going to Supreme? Because it's closer than 56th or 40th when I need to make a quick trip from home, and it has basic items when I need them. That's really it. I'm kind of surprised that my rating is the lowest here. I don't feel that I'm being overly harsh...

text: I would agree with Daniel's assessment of Cottage Hospital's inadequate facilities for labor/delivery. I am the proud father of 2 beautiful babies. We had 2 babies here in the past 15 months, both 15+ hours delivery. Out of the many different nurses/staff members during both deliveries, I would say 80% were great. However, both times I was sent home around 2 hours after delivery because they did not have enough rooms. For the first baby, when my wife delivered at 2:15am (hadn't eaten since 11am the day before) the nurses didn't get her any food until the 8am breakfast time - close to 6 hours after 15 hours of delivering a baby - unreal! Couldn't believe with our 2nd baby when they said I had to leave because visiting hours were over (my child was just born 2 hours prior). Also on the 2nd delivery we called ahead and tried to get in at 10pm when contractions had picked up. We waited in the emergency room for at least 20 minutes for someone to get to us. Luckily they had masks and signs instructing people to wear them due to the risk of swine flu and seasonal flu - great to see right before delivering a baby. Talking with a colleague in the Bay Area...they had a private room the whole time, bathtub in the room for the mom relax during labor, meals for both people and most importantly - they did not kick the father out after the birth of his children. This is how a birth should be treated at minimum. When I returned to "visit" the day after my second child was born I asked to pay for my meals so I could spend more time with my family - of course they missed the lunch I ordered and I waited over 2 hours as they kept telling me "it's on it's way." Ate lunch around 3pm and of course they were going to charge me for the meal. People come in from Santa Maria, Lompoc, Santa Ynez, Goleta, Santa Barbara, Ventura and even Oxnard to have their baby in this city and after Cottage shut down the Goleta labor center it is a mess. If you have the option, go somewhere that keeps up with the current standards of care.

I didn't actually confirm the exhaust leak had come back until my regular mechanic noticed it weeks later, and then I called them up to fix the problem. They said that they were booked for the day. I got upset and explained to them that their work had put me at risk, and I expected them to fix the problem immediately. They told me that they only warranted their work for 30 days, but grudgingly agreed to replace the seal again. After waiting for hours, the seal was replaced. However, it was still not airtight and now I'm in the same boat again. I suspect that they didn't secure the new exhaust line properly, which is causing it to break the seal in the engine compartment. However, at this point I won't be going back to Midas.

We ordered at the counter, I ordered the Turkey Ferdi, and the two guys I was with ordered similar Po-Boys. As we waited for our food, we admired the hundreds of autographed pictures on the walls, and thought to ourselves that this place must really be something if all these famous people came here... When the server came to our table for the first time, she delivered one sandwich, which we would soon learn was the first of many strange errors in our time there. My friend Andy touched the sandwich and decided that this can't be what he ordered (it was soggy and didn't have any gravy on it), the waitress came back, asked if he touched it, and when he said yes, rolled her eyes, huffed, grabbed the sandwich and walked away. Is that all, you ask? Not so much. The waitress then came back with two sandwiches, AND a cup of gumbo and some crawfish etouffee. Remember when I said we just ordered three sandwiches? Yeah. Anyway, we told her that we didn't order these things, and she told us not to worry about it (despite signs saying not to tip the servers, she told us to tip them anyway, and we could keep the side dishes), then walked away and came back with the other sandwich. We decided to try the etouffee and gumbo first, and after each of us had taken two bites of each, ANOTHER waitress came to our table, informed us that we hadn't ordered these items, and took them away. This seemed spiteful, and a total waste of good food, but nonetheless, we had our Po-Boys to dive into, so oh well. These Po-Boys were not what any of us were expecting, given the raving recommendation from plane guy - the meat was dry and the bread was definitely soggy - but we were hungry and ate them anyway. I don't often give something a thumbs down after one experience, but everything that occurred was so backward, that I probably won't go back. Sorry, plane guy, Mother's gets a thumbs down from me. As with any Mexican food restaurant there were the obligatory chips and salsa, I found the chips to be a bit thick and heavy. I was excited to see a vegetarian tamale on the menu, however when this arrived it was much closer to cornbread than a tamale. My date's fish looked decent and she said it was good enough, but she too expected more out of this highly regarded restaurant. It is tucked away on a side street of Down Town Tucson, which is pretty dead at night. I parked parallel parked a block away with my date and we walked though a slightly scary block to get to the restaurant. Despite having a reservation, we had to wait for 5-6 minutes for our table. Prices were a bit steep also for a meal of this caliber in a location of this nature. I really liked the date, however my meal was not the best.

The bar is focused on service and has a huge selections of really high quality liquor with a focus on Gin, Rye, and Bourbon. I have never had a bad wine their and they have a handful of decent beer. text: The Lamb Tavern is a nice place for a private lunch or dinner, but I cannot recommend them for a function. We hosted a funeral luncheon there which was terrible. When 12 additional people came they could not accommodate them, and they all had to sit outside the room we were given. Most function places know that it is impossible to give an exact number for funeral events and are prepared to make reasonable adjustments. In addition, the food was OK, but nothing special. All the confusion as our guests arrived was embarrassing and stressful, just what we didn't need at such a time. Their curly fries are delicious. The vibe is cool and relaxed, and the back part of the bar turns into a dancefloor for rotating DJs. DJs, take note: move a night or two to Teri's! Service was hit or miss, particularly with one server, but they've only been doing the bar thing for a few weeks now, so I'm willing to deal with some of the kinks. With drinks this cheap, you can take a night off from the PBR (which is only a $1 cheaper than better and higher ABV beers) and have a good time. I'll be hanging out here frequently, for sure.

text: Since my husband LOVES ice cream above all things, I had to find an ice cream shop to visit while in Santa Barbara. We visited McConnell's Ice Cream after we had dinner (with dessert) at Bouchon. I didn't feel too guilty because we walked from the restaurant back to our hotel and then to McConnell's and back to our hotel again. I'd say we'd probably burn off 5-10% of what we ate. =) What makes McConnell's ice cream so good? Simply, 15% creamier than regular ice cream = fattier = yummier! My favorites are Brazilian Coffee Chocolate Chip and Coconut ice cream. My husband also enjoyed the Raspberry Chocolate Truffle. Their yogurt is really popular, but we didn't try it...next time. Upon returning home, I went hunting for McConnell's ice cream and was so happy to find it at Gelson's off Alton & Jeffrey. Just to give you heads up, when something this good is mass produce, it's not always consistent. We got the Brazilian ice cream at Gelson's but it was not as creamy as the ice cream in their shop -- it was a little icier than it's supposed to be. Overall, check out McConnell's to see if you like "creamier" ice cream.

text: If my car was an human being and these people were doctors, then I would no other person taking care of my car at this point. Let me tell ya as a gal with an old old car, it's hard to find good/honest/affordable mechanic. I've gone to a few places in philly. One (starts with a B..ends with a T...and they sell tires) tend to give the glamour treatment and charge $$$$ for their glamour service. They seem to be in the money making business.PLUS I've been there several times and the manager looks at me like he's never seen me before each time!!! Another place was recommend which is mom and pop (11th street is the location) and the are pretty reliable and honest people but just too far for me to get to...being there once and had good times there also. I was referred to Monte's by a friend after my car overheated this summer. So I went to monte's. First of all, just my calling them on the phone dude already asked for my first name...really friendly down to earth. I trusted this guy already. I got the impression he cared about "me" and "my car". I don't care what he was selling, I'm buying twice! The shop is not expansive. Again, really friend warm staff. I explained the situation. We talked about the possibilities before I left the keys so they can do their diagnostic thang. they gave me a ride back home. I paid the price for the parts and the labor was not expensive at all and job was done pretty quickly. They knew my car was OLD, still had some juice left in it, and that I depended on it. I get sentimental about my baby...he has served me well. So i appreciate a mechanic that understands that tho it's an old car..it's all I have. And they actually know what they are talking about (car wise). After they fixed it, I was encouraged to bring it back for weekly checks (at no additional cost) for a month just to make sure there was no hidden internal damage from the overheating episode. Then my gas door broke off (I tell ya my car is olddd). Well I took it Monte's and I appreciate that FIRST he tried to get used parts. I mean, some mechanics don't even attempt to get used parts. I'm not saying used parts are the way to go all the time but if it's not the engine (and with a car as old as mine) there is no point in getting fancy new parts. text: Just what we need - another expensive bar downtown that has mediocre food and charges too much. Second, they are unbelievably punctual about the happy hour ending at 6p - I think I ordered a drink at 5:56 that didn't come until 6p and it was a decidedly non-happy hour price. Second, the drinks are expensive. There are so many places in town that serve great drinks, do we really need one that charges $6 for a local beer, $7 for wine and $9 for mixed drinks? Finally, the food. Don't even get me started on this. Do we really need fancy names and fancy prices for regular bar food? Truffle Fries with aoli for $8 = french fries; mac and cheese croquette with stewed tomato for $8 = deep fried mac and cheese; a warm pretzel with corned beef, greyere, and warm country mustard for $10 = a pretzel. C'mon! You can get a pretzel down the street for $1! To be fair, the space is nice looking with hardwood floors and lots of tv's for game watching. Bottom line: don't bother - it isn't worth it.

text: yikes. like joan m., we saw the 28 zagat rating and were expecting quite an experience. and we got one. just not the one we were expecting. but rather than letting the poor experience bother us, eye of the beholder. just not his beholder. everyone was exceedingly pleasant...so that was nice. but the service people seemed a bit confused. one waiter took our drink order and promised a bread service. 15 minutes later the bread arrived. we then ordered a bottle of wine. being familiar with the brand and vintage, i tasted it and knew it needed to be decanted. no problem. a different waiter took it away to be decanted. 15 minutes later still no wine. when i asked a third waiter about it, they fetched it and brought to the table an empty decanter with the wine still in the bottle. and i thought all this time it was being decanted. the food. the descriptions were great. mouthwatering. but one does not eat the descriptions. the house-cured prosciutto app sounded great, but upon delivery, was pretty much like thick-cut ham. not paper thin like you'd expect from the word prosciutto. the crab salad app was tasty though, as long as you discarded the toasted baguette slice it sat upon. once the apps were done, we'd been there almost two hours. now we're not ones to rush through a fine-dining experience, but if there is nothing fine about it then we are anxious to see if improvement was on its way. to say service was slow would insult glaciers. as we had waited a long time for the entree, my wife asked a waiter to look into our venison. he looked toward the kitchen and said he believes he sees it "up". but made no attempt to retrieve it and disappeared. finally the venison arrived. and as advertised, it was moist and tender. unfortunately, what it lacked was flavor. seems the chef must have forgotten to season it, in any way. with anything. in an effort to finish this comedy, we attempted to season it ourselves at the table with the basics...pepper and salt. except the salt in the shaker was wet, and wouldn't dispense. after asking yet another waiter for a salt shaker, we did our best and finished the meal. desert? no we were through with surprises and wanted out asap. at first we thought the poor service was due to maybe too many tables with too few wait staff (maybe someone called in sick). but later in our evening, as there were many fewer tables to staff, the service did not improve. in summary, i'm stunned as to what got this restaurant a 28 in zagat and if you want to time travel back to the 80's including some of the outfits on the geriatric customers, then this is the place for you. bring your own salt shaker. maybe they should change the name to dowdy's.

text: I have a cadre of friends who swear by the food here and love everything they make. I've been here more times than I have fingers and toes and disagree. Service is fine (it has improved over time) and the interior is pleasant, but the food leaves much to be desired. This Lemon Grass location used to be a Jasmine Thai, which had VASTLY superior food. (Anyone remember their pineapple fried rice with raisins? To die for!!) I've had just about everything on their lunch menu - the dishes I've had are lackluster, ranging from average to plain awful. Their vegetarian green curry is weak - on their menu it's listed as three stars for spiciness but it tastes barely like one star. Both their hot and sour and coconut soups are watery and tasteless. As for appetizers, their satay is scarily dry, but the sauce is okay. If I ever find myself here, I skip their "lunch special" (~$9 for a soup, appetizer, and entree) and ask for a plate of drunken noodles ($9); it's safe and dependable. I specify they be made so spicy that I can't taste them and occasionally they come close. One star for good service (depends on who serves you, of course), a clean, attractive interior, and another star for the times their drunken noodles have made me sweat. If you want good Thai, you won't find it here, nor anywhere else in King of Prussia - but DO check out the neighboring towns for amazing Thai eats. (Thai Orchid in Blue Bell, The Thai Place in Phoenixville, and Flavor in Wayne) UPDATE: Comically, I eat here relatively often because King of Prussia really has no good Thai places. Just recently I asked for my food to be made absurdly spicy and they did it, this once. I was thrilled to see them load sliced Thai peppers on ALL my dishes...

text: Let me start by saying that I am a cupcake fanatic and have tried lots of cupcakeries in the country. Nevertheless this cupcakery was a welcome change to the French Quarter to-go dessert scene (I can only handle so many beignets at a time). I have to say that this place had the best cupcakes I've had in town. While most places tries to make flavor combinations cheap tricks like fillings and maybe frostings, this place puts efforts into their treats and offers varying cupcakes with either cakes and/or frosting flavors. Their strawberry cupcake was one of the best I've had, with the perfect burst of sweet with a hint of tart strawberry flavor in the cupcake cane and the perfect balance of sweet and buttery buttercream frosting. The husband and I were also very impressed with the German Chocolate cupcake with the perfectly chocolately sweet and fudgy cupcake topped with the perfect amount of coconut frosting. We were very impressed and we overheard other people really enjoying their cakes too. Their flavors change day to day, so it's good to keep up with their cupcake schedule. Burgers are a fine choice, and I know plenty of people who've enjoyed the steaks they've ordered there, though I can't see why you wouldn't just save your steak money for one of Philly's more reputable steak houses. text: I'm pretty sure I've mentioned this before, but I was once told two rules about restaurants--never eat at a place known for it's view, and never eat at a place that's named after the owner. Should've listened. Vin de Set is visually appealing. The outdoor patio is nice, though I don't understand why people think the view is great; I've never found the commercialized section of Chouteau to be especially "breathtaking," but hey, to each their own, I guess. So, the actual restaurant is nice, which I'm assuming is done to mask the horribleness of the food/service. We had the steak tartare and escargot to start--both decent dishes. It was followed up by both soup and salad that were definitely underwhelming. We then had both the Mahi Mahi special and the Steak au Poivre (our server told me it was the "best thing on the menu"). The Mahi was extremely dry, but edible. The Steak au Poivre however was one of the worst things I've ever eaten. Firstly, there was no peppercorn encrustment, which I believe to be the exact definition of a steak au poivre. Secondly, I ordered the steak medium rare, and when it came out--though cooked medium rare--the center was a unappetizing grayish-brown, an immediate sign that the steak was frozen and then thawed to cook. Now, I don't mind if a restaurant does a frozen steak--I order steaks that look like this one all the time; the only difference is that it normally costs $7.99, comes with eggs and a side of hash browns, and I'm too wasted to even care. To pay $24 for this is a joke. It was so terrible, that I actually sent the dish back, something I have never done. Over this entire time, I have attempted to be courteous and understanding: I apologize for not enjoying the entree; when she totally forgets my soup, I note there is a possibility I may have been unclear in my order, etc. but the service at this restaurant is totally unacceptable, and only added to my frustration. We had no water refills, EVER. The waitress did not change our silverware or offer us replacements when she bussed the table (which I'm fairly certain she did only because she had to make room for the other food), when I asked what the best things on the menu are, she told me the most expensive thing on the menu--one of my biggest pet peeves. I don't mind paying a premium price for a premium product, but don't fucking tell me the most expensive thing on your menu just to try and boost your tip, especially if a.) the food is fucking dog shit, and b.) your service is terrible. When I pushed my plate away, she obviously was trying to hide from our table because she knew something was wrong. There were two other tables around us, and she kept circling to try and avoid us. When she finally came over, she apologized and said she would take it away and off the bill. When the bill came, the dish was still on the ticket. When I asked her, she responded with "I'm sorry, I completely forgot." Quit bullshitting me, lady. It's not like you were so busy you forgot with your whopping three tables. You were trying to see if I would pay and still tip on the total. Fuck you, the only reason I gave you fifteen percent is because I'm a dick, but I'm not a fucking DICK. If I didn't have a conscience, I would've tipped you nothing, and taken a butter knife as compensation for your terrible service and worthless food. And if all this wasn't enough, as we were leaving the hostess barely looked up and said "bye." I've had warmer good-byes from American Eagle shirt-folders. Even the lady friend, who gives everyone the benefit of the doubt--probably because she's dating me--said that the girl was ridiculously rude. If you can't tell by now, I don't think Vin de Set is very good. However, to end on a good note, their drinks are ridicu-cheap. Goose on the rocks at $6.50? Amazing. Too bad the service will be so shitty that you'll only be able to get one before you leave in frustration. I'm back, people. I missed you.

text: I was wary of this place because of the mixed reviews... But since Ludwig's closed awhile back (which I was not even a huge fan of) the city has been lacking a German establishment, so it was a MUST try. With all of the German heritage in Philly we need a place like this. The place does give you a good first impression of a Bavarian brauhaus. It's nice inside with dark woods and a second balcony level. I'm not certain how people sat up there however, as it appeared there was very minimal headroom. It was very crowded on a Friday with the waitresses in traditional dirndl dresses having to sort of shove through the narrow space between the bar to the left and the tables to the right. The hostess told us it would be about an hour to get a table and it ended up being about 45 min. The initial bar service was somewhat lousy. We were standing behind the people seated at the bar for lack of stools and she didn't make eye contact with us for 20-25 minutes. The beer list is good with a nice variety of German imports including some wheat beers, pilsners, dunkels, bocks, and festbiers. Luckily there are also some American craft brew German styles such as Stoudt's Brauhaus Hausbrau. (Which they may have brewed specifically for this place?) However, the actual lists are a bit disorganized as they have one chalk board to the left of the bar and one to the right. Some of the beers are written on both. Some are only one one or the other which you can only check out if you walk from end to end... I actually thought prices on beer was fair. Half liters averaged $5.50-$6.50 and you can also get this in a full liter (ein Mass) mug. Just double the price. Keep in mind a half liter is 17+ ounces of beer. The Stoudt's was only $4.50 0.5L/$9 a liter! Not bad! Drinking the liter mugs was awesome, adding to the ambiance and "German-ness" of the evening! As the big sign above the bar says, "Bier macht heiter, drum Trinke weiter." ("Beer makes you happy, therefore continue drinking." I had to do some research because my German ist nicht so gut!) Everyone enjoyed their food. I did try the Rouladen and loved it. The spätzle was good. The potato salad was German style (vinegary) and good. The plates/servings are huge! (Luckily the tables are large to accommodate the big plates and big beers!) I was starving and thus able to finish. Two other people definitely needed the rest of their meal to be boxed. Nothing was cold, though it was not piping hot... This may be one area they need to work on. But our service at the table was quite friendly and helpful. And I'll mention again here that dirndls are fantastic. Overall, we spent about $30 each for a huge meal and 2-3 beers. Actually not too bad. We had a great experience and plan to be back!

text: The adventures of Joey B. and the Norristown MexiQuest continue! When we last left our hero, he was taking a brief respite from Mexican food. We pick up now with him resuming MexiQuest at Los Arcos Mexican Restaurant... On the exterior, Los Arcos does not look good. It's tucked away next to an auto tags place, the parking lot pavement is uneven, and the windows are kinda dark and difficult to see through. However, upon entry I was pleasantly surprised with a bright, clean, well decorated interior, replete with all the standard Mexican restaurant adornments and an attractive wood decor. The friendly waitress handed me a menu and complimented my atrocious Spanish, and took me drink order (Jarritos, as usual). Perusing the menu, I was again pleasantly surprised to find it wide and varied, with all sorts of traditional Mexican dishes and plates, al a carte fare, various drinks, and a rather extensive breakfast menu. The menu was in both Spanish and well-translated English (if you think well-translated English isn't important, try reading Los Compadres' English menu... the Spanish one is easier even if you don't speak Spanish), and all the prices were lower than the competitors in the area (save for Los Compadres). With $1.75 a taco, $5 burritos, and $11 plates, I was already feeling good about Los Arcos. I ordered an adobada (a spicy pork kinda like chorizo) burrito. While waiting I was served complimentary chips with the standard Mexican roja, or spicy red, salsa. The burrito itself was on the smaller side for the average in that area, but by no means small. It was approximately the size of a Chipotle or Qdoba burrito, but significantly larger than Baja Fresh fare. It was a grilled burrito, which I always appreciate. Inside it was filled with fresh meat, lettuce, tomato, sour cream, shredded cheddar cheese, rice, and avocado. These ingredients gave me a very fresh impression, but the burrito wasn't daring. It took no risks, and was almost Americanized in it's safeness, but was tasty and satisfying nonetheless. The burrito came with a side of fries, which I didn't know until they showed up, but they weren't unpleasant. They were fresh cut and seasoned, kind of out of place to be sure but tasty fries anyway. I have concluded that Los Arcos is my current first choice as a recommendation to someone who is looking to try authentic Mexican cuisine, but may not be ready to dive in head-first into some of the more exotic cuisines. Recommended to anyone, but great for those with picky tastes.

text: Do you want to hear a fish story? Well come along with me and I will tell you all about it. The oddly named Bonefish Grill is an upscale chain that specializes in fresh seafood. The fish is bought whole and cut as needed. The varieties are vast and range from Chilean Sea Bass, Ahi Tuna, Gulf Grouper, Snake River Rainbow Trout, Longfin Tilapia, Atlantic Salmon to freshly seared Sea Scallops & Shrimp and cold water Lobster Tails. The fresh fish is wood grilled. This particular Bonefish Grill is located in a strip mall. You have two choices for entry. Either pull on the wooden door or take a ride through the smoked glass revolving doors. Once inside there are two rooms, side by side that greet you and are semi open to each other with heavy metal plants. We were seated in a very large booth, which is the majority of the seating arrangements offered, on the right or the Bar side. The restaurant is immaculate. We could see into the kitchen and everything shined. Not one speck on the floors or under the counter spaces. The Restaurant itself has a lot of wood, including dark wood floors that are heavily glossed with shellac. The Bar is as long as the room and has another row of long tables with stools for lounging. Nothing decor wise is tacky about this restaurant. Let's go back to the Bar and side work. The Bar has a wine "cellar" like none other I have seen. The Wines are all stored on wooden shelves above the Bar. The bartender decided to rearrange, restock and dust all of the bottles and wood. To do this she climbed up on the high counters and clanged and banged bottles for our entertainment? Bonefish, have your employees come in early or stay late to do this, it was very distracting. Scott was our very knowledgeable and personable server. They specialize in Martinis and Cocktails along with a nice selection of Wine. I tried and absolutely loved a Perfect Patron Margarita straight up with salt. I sipped it, but it was good enough to have gone down quickly had I so desired. It consisted of Patron Silver Tequila, Citronge, lemon and lime juice. Hubby does not drink and enjoyed numerous free refills on the coke. For our appetizers we we so torn and therefore another reason to go back. We decided to share the infamous Bang Bang Shrimp, the Crab Cakes with a very spicy remoulade and the Saucy Shrimp, which was at least two dozen shrimps sauteed in a lime sun dried tomato garlic sauce with Kalamata olives and feta cheese. The Crab Cakes were okay, a lot of breading and filler crab meat with some lump. I would not order them again. The Saucy Shrimp was good and the sauce made it. The Bang Bang Shrimp needs to be patented, if it has not been already! Talk about punch, I almost needed another margarita. Between cocktails and appetizers they bring a basket of in house baked bread that is served warm with a dish of infused olive oil. This olive oil has Kalamata olives, fresh garlic and herbs. I had the best salad of my life here. The salads are served on chilled plates, which is a huge plus. I chose the Bonefish Salad which was a wonderful mix of greens, none bitter, hearts of palm, Kalamata olives, ripe tomatoes and ROASTED Pine nuts. The dressing was a citrus herb vinaigrette and all topped with your choice of feta or Danish Bleu. I really do not think I will ever have a salad again without roasted pine nuts. I keep them in my freezer and I think I need to pop those babies in the oven to warm them up ;+} All of the wood grilled fish is served with your choice of four different sauces. In addition to the fish, they have a nice variety of Steaks and Chops or you could choose from Pasta or Chicken entrees. Hubby had a nice sized Filet Mignon cooked rare with a Gorgonzola butter melting through. He opted for french fries, which he got when he was almost finished with the steak. French fries for dessert is cool. I chose one of their daily specials, which was a huge piece of Wild Caught Haddock with feta and artichokes. It was garlic and crumb crusted and served with a lemon basil sauce.. Cooked perfectly and the best piece of Haddock I have ever experienced. Both of our meals came with their daily vegetable and today it was succotash and it was like no succotash I have ever had before. Baby Lima beans with roasted red peppers and crisp corn. They can keep the garlic mashed potatoes. I am not sure if it was an off night for the potato man, but they were like glue. no fluff to these babies. Okay, the Restrooms. I never understood why people include this in their review, unless it is gross and then you should not be there. The restrooms were very clean and served their purpose. For dessert they offer a Macadamia Nut Brownie, Key Lime Pie or Creme Brulee. This upscale chain was started by two Culinary Chefs and veteran restaurateurs from NYC. Hey guys, I think you have something good going on here. Note: when ordering the Bang Bang Shrimp ask for a tall glass of Vodka.

text: I was strolling the 2nd Street festival today and noticed a long line in front of Dmitri's. With time to kill before my friends arrived, I added myself to the queue without bothering to find out what was on the other end first. Turns out it was hummus with parsley, paprika and olive oil, served with grilled pita. And it was free. Good marketing on their part, because while munching on my free and good (not Zahav good, but definitely better than your average) hummus I realized that 1: their menu is almost entirely inexpensive seafood, 2: this is the same Dmitri's as the other two locations (I'd never put two and two together) and I've been dying to try them anyway, and 3: I was craving octopus. So a couple hours later, when my friend showed up at the festival and the skies unleashed some cold summer rain, we ducked into Dmitri's for some snacks and to wait out the rain. We sat at the cool (and cramped!) open kitchen. My friend ordered more hummus, I got my octopus. I think the head chef was training a new guy, but they still did a good job grilling the octopus, though I might have removed it just a second or two sooner. I LOVE me some seasoned grill marks on octopus, though, and this place had just the right flavor on the grill. It comes in a very simple olive oil and red wine vinegar sauce with some parsley and salt, so tasty. Some peppers and olives on the side. And for $12 the portion is gigantic. It's on the appetizer menu, but no reason to not have this as an entree. Had some simple and yummy rice pudding for dessert, and a strong little Greek coffee. My only (small) complaint is the service... it wasn't unfriendly, but ever-so awkward and rushed. They asked if we'd like anything else as I was finishing my dish. I was taken off-guard, so I probably said we were fine. A few moments later they dropped the check. Then I said we might like some dessert, and she was almost off again before I managed to squeak out I wanted coffee, too. Then they cleared my plate as I was finishing my olives! Only minor complaints, though, the rest of the service was smooth. I definitely enjoyed my food and watching others' food prepared in the open kitchen, and I'll definitely be back. Good job with the free hummus table at the 2nd St festival, Dmitri's.

text: Another great spot to go when you're visiting Tucson and want to see some of the beauty the desert has to offer. Though actually, Sabino canyon is more oasis than desert, the highlight being the stream (almost a river) lined by huge boulders, cottonwoods, ash, oaks and willows. The narrow, cement road through the canyon was built in the 1930's as a dam access road, but thankfully the dam was never built, and the whole area later became a protected park. Now it is only accessible by a light tram (running every half hour) or on foot. On our visit here with our extended family we chose to take the tram to the turnaround at the top of the canyon and walk down with the kids, who took frequent side trips to the stream to explore, climb the rocks, and stick their toes in the sand. Of course, part of me worried about them turning an ankle or falling in one of the many deep, icy-cold pools. Happily there were no mishaps and I was able to control my protective instincts and let them have fun. We were a bit sad that we had failed to bring snacks, and that the visitor center below failed to stock any kid-friendly ones as well. So, make sure to bring snacks of your own if you plan to spend more than a few hours in the canyon. If I ever visit Tucson again sans kids then this would be a great place to hike the day away, starting early by hiking up Sabino canyon (about 3.5 miles) and returning via Bear canyon (anouther 4-5 miles)

text: OK. I wanted to give this place 5 stars the first time I went, but it went downhill in the middle of that visit, and has not got much better. I have been two times now, and I have had awful service both times. The first time it was pretty slow, and getting a beer seemed to take a really long time. The second time I went, it was during the last game of the World Series, and it still wasn't super busy...but it did take super long to get any service at all. From my experience, the wait staff is pretty sub-par on every level. They are not super friendly, very slow and they tend to completely forget you exist, even if you are with three other people...kind of hard to miss. The burger I had the first time was really good, and the atmosphere is actually pretty nice. It's a sports bar, but it's not ridiculously loud like Bully's on Robb Drive can get, so that was cool. I can't lie, the happy hour from 4pm - 8pm is pretty fantastic with half-off all bar drinks. Basically that means a large beer that would be $5.50+ at Bully's is $2.25, and as an alcoholic, I love that. Oh. The last time I went there our waitress "suggested" the chicken Philly sandwich about 3 times. I ordered the pork sandwich, and guess what...they were out of pork. The Philly was recommended again, so I chose the Reuben. The Reuben didn't have any kraut, which basically means I got a hot pastrami with sauce on it. The pastrami was like leather, and ultimately it was nasty. The wife and children got a pizza, and the dough looked like biscuit dough. It did not look good. Overall, I want to like the place, but the service so far is awful, and the food is so-so at best. When somebody recommends the chicken a bunch of times, I know that means they are trying to move the chicken, and not give me a recommendation based on taste. I hate that kind of stuff. If Bully's is too crowded, or you are tired of getting ripped off by their climbing prices for mediocre food, Sparky's is OK, but that's all I can say for it. If you just want to get straight hammered, then go and sit at the bar for better service (I hope?) and go between 4pm - 8pm for happy hour, then come back at midnight - 4am for a nightcap. Yea...it's not great, but it's not the worst I guess.

text: I've loved going to Bridgid's over the years, as the place never has disappointed and has always been a great neighborhood bar.
