We got down to business as I revealed my ignorance about flowers. He took one look at the peridot green bridesmaid dress I brought with me and said "Aha - we must do cymbidium orchids!" I said "Huh?" and he showed me the coolest looking green flowers I had ever seen. He worked them into bouquets amongst more cost-efficient neutral flowers, made them into solo boutonierres for the guys, and floated them in candle-lit bowls of water for the centerpieces. The final result was spectacular and it looked like I spent WAY more then $1,500 on flowers. He also provided extra flowers for the cake and display tables at no extra charge. The service was also fantastic. I could easily get in touch with Carl himself if I had any questions. He was far more concerned than I was when some peach lilies arrived in a too-bright shade, and instead ended up dying white ones (at no extra charge) so they would look perfect. text: I have often heard the SB Bowl be compared to Red Rocks in Colorado as an amazing natural outdoor amphitheater with unparalleled views, sound and overall ambiance. Like every music - loving Ventura County kid / UCSB alumnus, I have been to countless shows at the SB Bowl. I have seen bands ranging from 311 to Foo Fighters, Lifehouse/Colbie Caillat to Incubus, Snoop Dogg to No Doubt and have never been let down. Despite usually having to drive all the way up from my office in Universal City, I will take a show at the SB Bowl over any other SoCal amphitheater any day! The parking is close and convenient and you can even usually find some free street parking in the surrounding neighborhood if that's your sort of thing. The volunteers who work here are always friendly and surprisingly knowledgeable (I have only once ever had a problem with anyone here and it was a bitch in the box office who was unnecessarily and repeatedly rude to me when there was a mix up with my will call. I was smart enough to be very nice to her since I was still waiting for things to get cleared up and definitely wanted my tickets but man, was I furious enough to want to report her after wards - if only I could've found someone to report her too. but considering how many flawless shows I've been to here, she's not even worth a star in my rating.) The pre-sunset ocean views from the cheap seats are amazing, the crowd is usually fun, and their pit is perfectly sized - just big enough to make anyone who really tries for them get pit tickets yet small enough to make you feel special for being there with a great view from any angle. I would recommend the SB Bowl any day over its usual LA counterparts on any tour - Hollywood Bowl or Verizon Amphitheater.

text: We were looking for an ideal anniversary dinner venue, having never stayed in town for the milestone previously. The front room seemed awfully loud when we arrived, and when we were seated in the back room my initial feeling of banishment turned out to be a more pleasing fate. The space is very tastefully done, good spot for a nice, romantic meal. Executive Chef Gerard Craft and staff due deserve all that other Yelpers rave about. The menu choices were very diverse, with a good selection of starters and entrees. Our eyes gravitated to the dessert menu first, a dangerous menu for sure. I ordered the Pork dish, and my companion the Cod. The Pork that night was a pork belly. Not the best cut of meat, as the server warned, but very delectable. I wanted something different that I hoped Niche would do up finely, and of course they did. The mix of mushrooms, turnips and a taste of maple really brought out the flavor. The Cod was also well presented and the taste, on a bed of baccala ravioli, was quite devine. We finished the meal with the liquid chocolate cake and milk chocolate custard. The chocolate cake is as good as others say. We had a similar concoction on a cruise once and it has become our most sought-after dinner dessert. Niche knocked it out of the park. In the end we loved the experience. Fine dining in St Louis is possible thanks to Niche!

They also let us bring in the birthday cakes which were a pair of homemade pineapple upside-down cakes I made (yummy if I do say myself). Only downside was we had only a single waitress for this large party which made service a little slow, but she was extremely attentive and personable. Old Chicago has tons of beers to choose from and I highly recommend getting your World Beer Tour card if you're a beer drinker. Once you've tried all 110 beers your tour is complete. On that monumental day, you'll get your name placed on a brass placard on The Famous Hall of Foam and instant bragging rights. Also if you register your card on-line you can get dollar for dollar on food purchases to use to purchase gifts/prizes. I always get the "Meat Me" Chicago Style pizza which is AWESOME!!!. Garlic-spiced Italian sausage, Canadian bacon, Andouille sausage, pepperoni, roasted garlic, fresh basil and Mozzarella. Chicago Style crust is extra thick, golden brown and jam-packed from the pan with a rich, crisp, and buttery finish. Probably one of the only pizza where I eat the crust! You can also order your pizza "Original" (not as thick) or "Thin". I would have given Old Chicago 5 stars but the incredible pineapple upside-down cakes were my doing so they'll have to settle for 4 stars ;)

text: A one and a half star experience for this location. A far cry from what we've experienced at other Crabby Bill's locations. We've been to one of the other Crabby Bill's locations a number of times and always had a great experience. The other diners we were with had been to this location before and had pleasant enough experiences. I don't know what happened tonight, but it wasn't good. We arrived at just before 8pm and got on the waiting list for a table of 5. Unfortunately, the restaurant only has two tables large enough to seat five without moving tables together, so we had to wait. And wait some more. After a while, we asked to make sure they hadn't forgotten about us. They reassured us that it would be just a few more minutes. Eventually, a couple of tables cleared and they could shuffle two tables next to each other. Without exaggerating, it actually took 3 people to do this. These aren't heavy tables, so I don't really know why it took 3 people, but ok. The first thing that struck us was that this place didn't feel like a Crabby Bill's. Normally, Crabby Bill's feels like a homey seafood restaurant. This location was built in what felt like a garage or storeroom. Looking up, you could see the ductwork. Everything felt very clinical, with some ocean themed decorations thrown on because it's a seafood restaurant. The waitress came by and let us know that they had some new margarita, which most of us ordered. It was a bit crowded and busy, but 15 minutes seemed like an awful long time to wait for our four margaritas. When they arrived, they tasted mostly of sour mix. Definitely not worth the $7 each. Upon looking at the menu, we were immediately surprised at how small it was. Maybe half the size of the St Pete location we normally visit. The others commented that it was smaller than the times they had been to this particular location before. We ordered a couple of appetizers: crabbyfeller oysters and some sort of shrimp (which I did not try). The crabbyfeller oysters were described on the menu as having a spinach dip, some cheese and then being baked. Our friends had ordered these at a different location before. When they came out, the first thing we noticed was that they were covered in bacon. Oysters - covered in bacon. Now, bacon may make most things better, but pescetarians don't eat bacon. The waitress noticed our horror and confusion on our faces and asked if something was wrong. "I guess I didn't realize there was bacon on these oysters. Are these the right ones?" "Yes, the crabbyfellers have bacon, it's the clevelanders that don't" "We wanted the ones with the spinach dip" "That's the crabbyfellers. They normally have bacon, but I can ask them to make them without it. Would you like that? It's no problem." And so, the bacon covered oysters went back to the kitchen. Meanwhile, I grabbed a menu. Lo and behold - none of the oyster options mentioned bacon -anywhere-. When the waitress returned, I pointed this fact out to her. "Oh, that's a typo. But we're trained that they have bacon on them. I'll tell the manager and the cooks that the menus don't mention it though." Eventually, the oysters came back without bacon. They were alright. The spinach dip flavor was nice, but the cheddar cheese was unnecessary. Apparently, other locations serve it as oysters, spinach dip and a bit of grated parmesan which sounds much more appetizing than what we got. The appetizer debacle aside, how were the entrees? Our friends found them acceptable, but not up to the quality level we've grown accustomed to from Crabby Bills. My wife ordered a rare grilled tuna steak which came out crusted in Old Bay spice and cooked medium. My clam strips were slightly undercooked and a little soft. By this point though, we knew we would be tempting fate sending anything else back to the kitchen. I grabbed some cocktail sauce from the squeeze bottle for my clams and immediately had to check to make sure it wasn't ketchup. It was super runny and watery. Tasting it, there was only the slightest hint of horseradish. We checked another bottle - and it was the same. When it came time to tip, I commented that "Food aside, the waitress was nice and really apologetic." My wife countered that when we were first seated, she overheard the waitress complaining about having to serve us to the manager. We only came to this location because it was the most convenient for a friend visiting town. Even he said he'd rather just drive the extra 20-30 minutes next time and avoid this location.

text: I got this 569dine flyer (the kind of enterprise that delivers from many restaurants) in the mail that said they now deliver food from Delmar Restaurant and, after looking at the menu, I was VERY excited. The menu listings and descriptions were amazing. My mouth started watering at the Sweet Potato Fritters all the way through the last item, simple Red Beans and Rice. It read like a hole in the wall New Orleans Cajun restaurant and I was instantly ready to order, but I decided to go there instead. It was a Saturday night and we got there around 8:30p and sat in the back (they still have smoking). It really had that Bourbon Street bar and dive kind of feel to it, definitely not fine dining, but my interest continued to build. They had a very good band playing that night, kinda bluesy, jazzy, New Orleansy. Interest still building. We got a drink fast, but had to go get the menus (first bad sign). I looked at the menu and it was the same menu that was on the flyer I got. Excellent! And so I began ordering the items that had attracted me to this place -- half dozen fresh oysters, a chopped salad (w/ "egg, bacon, cheddar, and creole buttermilk dressing"), and an oyster po' boy. I first asked the server where the oysters were from and she had to go back to the kitchen to find out (second bad sign). She said they were from Bob's Seafood (good sign, best wholesale fresh seafood distributor in the Lou). But that still did not answer my real question, but I decided to let it go. But here's where it went south, very far distant south, like to the Pole. When our server brought the fresh oysters, they looked ok, but they smelled and tasted OLD (another really bad sign). Maybe only a day or so old, but nevertheless old. I said to my companions that night, I wonder who's working the pass in the restaurant because they should have caught this quality issue before it even left the kitchen. And then there was no horseradish with the cocktail sauce (and the c-sauce needed all the help it could get - bland-city) ... that even wasn't helped much by adding the oh so bland horseradish (how can you have bland horseradish?). We called our server over and she took it away and said there would be no charge (how about my physician's bill? I'm a funny guy). She was very nice always. Then the chopped salad came and ... they added things to it they did not have on their menu description (another bad sign). I did not think that I had to tell them about my food allergies (hey, it wasn't in the salad they described on their menu), until this salad arrived with both tomatoes and sweet red peppers (nightshade family, deadly to me). Our server took it back graciously. The creole buttermilk dressing was quite good btw. By this time, we were all a bit shell shocked, but hoped that our oyster po' boys would be good ("with remoulade, lettuce, tomato, and onion"). It's the way they would dress it at Mama's in New Orleans. I am a very positive guy and I held out great hope (maybe not "great", but at least "some"). Hopes were dashed on the boulders of the entree, as they produced the worst po' boy I have ever had in my life. The bun was just out of the pepperridge farm plastic wrapper, not the crusty french bread that you would expect. The remoulade was watery and bland. The lettuce was WILTED, cut up iceberg, but limp as a dish rag, like it might have been left over from the lunch service (but they have no lunch service). And finally the straw that broke the proverbial camel's back - no onions, none (it said on the menu, there would be onions). Had to ask for them and they finally came, but by that time the french fries, which were very good when they were fresh, were limp as the lettuce. And finally, the oysters were, again, not all that fresh (but fresher than the raw ones). The decent cornmeal crust on them must have also helped a bit. But it was (and I repeat) the worst po' boy I have ever had. So, I got suckered in by the New Orleans vibe to this place, and forgot that it's still in St. Louis and still several hundred miles away from N.O. What it felt like to me was an owner who developed and published an "aspirational" menu. You know, a menu that tells the diner the kind of food that a place aspires to produce, but, in the end, doesn't live up to. I wouldn't call this place a total fraud, but it never delivered on it's potential. GET A REAL CHEF WHO KNOWS HOW TO COOK NEW ORLEANS STYLE FOOD, or ... change your menu to reflect what you get here. BTW the server was good and the band was GREAT! Go for the music and drinks but stay away from the food.

text: I'd love to give this place higher marks just because the owner of the establishment was such a delightful person to talk with and discuss international travels. The photography on the walls is her's and her stories about the lands she has visited is very interesting. Yes, the interior is eclectic. Sort of in keeping with the types of bit of this and bit of that decor you'd find in many of the small eateries in the mediterranean parts of the world where the smallest can feel like eating on someone's porch full of second hand decorations and family moments. The furniture is uncomfortable and the glass top on our table kept sliding around causing us to fear that it would go too far, lose balance, and crash to the floor. My husband had a sandwsh that he said was incredible. I can't remember the name but if I remember correctly it had chicken, pesto, pineapple, and several other things. I had a gyro salad that was typical and small for the price. There was very little meat and I found myself starving. I asked the server to make sure there would be feta on it and there wasn't. The kids split one of the appetizer plates that had three spreads and some pita. The pita was like what you'd find at the supermarket and it wasn't even warmed. It was cut into quarters. Warming it slightly on a grill with some olive oil would do wonders in making it more palatable. The spreads (one of which was hummus) was bland and had no flavor other than chickpeas. I like hummus that has lots of garlic, lemon, and oil flavors. The other two dips were equally boring. I had ordered a side of olives for the kids but one was never brought to the table. Fortunately, we were not charged for it. We had water and iced tea as our drinks. It was very, very, very overprices for the portions and the quality. I can make the same stuff at home. So 5 stars for the interesting owner. 2 stars for the food. 3 stars for the ambiance (4 for decorations and 2 for tables and chairs). 3 for location. 1 for the prices.
label: NEG

text: Some mornings, I just need to have something substantial for breakfast. I don't normally drive past too many places with enticing options (McDonald's anyone?), but sometimes I take a slight detour and hit Einstein Brothers. Their bagels are good, but what keeps me coming back is the Lox Bagel - it's always a welcome improvement to my morning, even if I am dead tired or hung over (yes, smoked salmon is a weird hangover food, but I love it). It's not easy to find lox at many places that are convenient to me in the morning, so I appreciate Einstein offering it. And the staff never has any problem customizing it to meet my various wishes (low fat cream cheese, no capers or onions, add cucumbers). I stopped by last Friday for lunch. It was a really dreary day, so I was craving a nice hot sandwich on filling bread or a cup of soup. Apparently everyone else in Fishers had the same idea -- the line for Panera was nearly out the door! I didn't have the patience, so I went down a few doors to Einstein to try lunch for the first time. I might have ordered the wrong thing -- the Italian Chicken Panini, but it just wasn't good at all. The chicken had an odd flavor and texture, and I ended up not eating most of it. For the price, it was not worth it. From now on, I will stick to the lox!

text: After coming to Nudy's for a late breakfast yesterday, I'm a true Nudist! I came here once for lunch a long, long time ago and found it cramped and too busy to really enjoy. Thankfully, my friend talked me in to going again. On a beautiful Saturday, this place, tucked behind the main thoroughfare in Wayne, was packed enough that we had to wait for a table. Thankfully, my friend put in his name a little earlier and we were quickly seated. Not long after, the waitress took our orders: one set of chocolate chip pancakes and eggs florentine, both of which came out piping hot within five minutes. My pancakes were sweet and moist, with ample bits of chocolate throughout. Syrup, butter and whipped cream made this the perfect indulgence for a lazy Saturday. My friend's eggs were served on an english muffin with the usual accouterments and nummy hash browns. Both dishes were scarfed down quickly. The drawbacks to Nudy's are few. There's little to no parking and the other businesses won't let you use their lots, so take your changes with street parking. The place is SO loud that any chances of conversation are slim to nil, though it may be a bit better if you sit on the enclosed patio. Service also seems to fly quickly, making it a rather rushed experience. All in all, if you want good food at a reasonable price, Nudy's is a great breakfast and lunch spot. PS: Their breakfast options are available all day long.
label: POS

text: I had never heard of "meat and three" before reading reviews of Nashville eateries on Yelp... but all of the reviews of Arnold's were great, so I decided to give it a try. We were visiting during the off-season (November) and it was a little scary how few people we saw at all of the tourist spots and throughout town. Then we came to Arnold's for lunch and found that the entire city was hiding out inside! As expected, there was a line out the door, and each table was packed at all times. Although the decor (such as it is) isn't much to look at, the food is finger-licking and artery-clogging good. The fried green tomatoes, mac and cheese, hush puppies, etc. were all delicious. Ooh, and the corn muffins and corn cakes. On the "healthy" side, I ordered asparagus, but of course they had a delicious cheesy buttery sauce for that too. I got the fried catfish and a fried shrimp "just happened to jump into my plate" since the server saw me eyeing the shrimp hungrily. They definitely had items beyond what was listed on the board, and the people serving were super friendly and helpful on picking what to eat. Even with the crazy rush, I didn't feel pressured. I meant to post this review four months ago, so I'm not sure what I can add -- I don't remember much beyond the happy feeling I had there and how nice everyone was. If you're in Nashville, this place is a must.
label: POS

text: If this is the "Best" Western, I'd hate to see the "worst". Small, noisy rooms, unprofessional front desk staff and a reservationist who lied about the availability of the type of room I asked for. Online photos and glowing reviews suckered me into reserving a room at this less-than-average hotel. The photos of the "courtyard" look pretty nice online. The reality is that the courtyard is much, much smaller than it appears in photos -- more like an outdoor hallway than a real courtyard. The pool is smaller than most home pools, and the tiny "spa" has a maximum capacity of only 3 people! (It even says so on the posted sign there.) It's obvious that these faux "amenities" are really only there so the Best Western website can list them as being part of the hotel without technically lying. I knew the hotel is located right next to a busy freeway, so when I phoned to reserve a room I requested an interior ("courtyard") room. Instead, I was assigned an exterior room overlooking the roaring 101 freeway. There was no apparent effort by the hotel builder to use sound proofing in the walls, nor even double paned windows to reduce the noise. The rush of the passing cars and trucks was so loud and clear that a good auto mechanic could diagnose their engine problems while lying in that bed. After surveying the noisy room, I immediately returned to the front desk to request another, quieter, room. The next room they assigned me was located on the first floor, courtyard. It was so small, the king bed nearly filled the entire room. There was literally just a few feet on either side and at the foot of the bed. It reminded me of those Japanese "Businessman" hotels I've read about. When I returned to the front desk to request yet another room, the only staffer there was young "Daniel", who appears to be a teenager. When I explained that I'd like a different room, he stated (almost gleefully) that the hotel was completely booked and that was the only room available. I was immediately suspicious of that statement, since the parking lot was nearly empty (at 3 pm) and I didn't see a single other guest during the entire 20 minutes I was in the lobby. But, smirking Daniel seemed to delight in his "power" to refuse my request. I found someplace else to stay that night. I can highly recommend the Ramada in Santa Barbara.

text: We just got back from a New Orleans-style Christmas and we love love loved the Maison Marigny. Being a proud Tulanian, I was happy to discover that this cozy b&b near the Frenchman area is owned by a fellow Tulane alum. We stayed on the second floor in the Balcony room which overlooks a calm, quiet section of Bourbon...the balcony was a great space, especially since it was accessible only from our room. We appreciated the Neutrogena shampoo and bath gel and the shower was great...amazing water pressure and amount of hot water for New Orleans. Lots of great little touches...Abita in the fridge in our room, Louisiana magazines everywhere, snacks downstairs, and an up-to-date dvd collection for rainy days. I enjoyed a great lemon poppyseed muffin in the cute green courtyard, while using the complimentary wi-fi, even! The pound cake/strawberry/Nutella breakfast panini was amazing--and the delicious pumpkin bread got us through the late night munchies. We highly recommend this b&b and hope to stay here again...

text: First off, I would like to say that tipping is not required. I've never been one to not tip, but in this case, i really shouldn't have. I've normally had a decent experience at this place. I typically enjoy their food, especially the soft shell crab. My friends and I went their for dinner one Friday night. It wasn't busy so we got promptly seated and served. One of my friends orders a dish to go for later. As the bill came up, I calculated our total and included an appropriate tip for the dishes we were served. I did not include a tip for the dish that was ordered to go. My general thinking is to not tip on orders that were not served to me. We pay our tab and got ready to leave. The person at the door stops us and questions our tip. I told him we left an appropriate tip for the stuff that was ordered there and not for the to go item. He was adamant about us leaving a larger tip. The Oakland in me should have just shrugged it off and kept on walking. In the end, we gave him an extra $2. $2 doesn't really amount to me and I really could care less, but it's the principle behind it! Why are you going to expect me to pay tip on a dish I ordered to go? If I had not sat down for dinner and ordered a to go item, would the restaurant have expected me to tip for that as well? Like I said, I generally have decent experiences here.. but because of this incident, I will no longer be returning.
label: NEG

text: I went here the other night for my first adventure into the world of Roller Derby. There's a lot to learn about Roller Derby, and I'd advise you do some reading up before you go to a game. It's a little complicated (at least more so that I thought ahead of time). Beforehand, I figured that it was just a bunch of chicks skating around in circles, bashing each other out of the way. In fact, there are lots of strategies, specific penalties, and other scoring methods which make the game pretty interesting. Plus, my friend is one of the referees for the Archway Rivals games, which is fun to watch. I'm taking off one star because the night we went to the All American Sports Mall, the air-conditioner had broken and it was about 115 degrees inside the place. I'm hoping that by the time I go back to see another game it is fixed-- otherwise I'll have to drink a lot of PBR's to forget about the searing heat. Also, don't forget to get cash ahead of time. They don't take credit cards, and their ATM has got a whopper of a fee.

text: Real, good Mexican food, with beautiful and homey Mexican decór. The chef is from Veracruz, and it's reflected in the selection of fish dishes. The ceviche mixto is spiced up with jícama and mango, and served in the authentic way, with crackers. We split the molcajete arrachera, but our waitress heard us debating so she brought out a ramekin of warm molé for us to taste. It was incredible--rich and complex, a little sweet. I guess no two molés are the same. If you're looking for some great Mexican food at a nice but unpretentious spot, Las Bugambilias is it. I will definitely be back.

text: The bubble tea craze begins here! This is the most commercialized tea house in the city and it has served them well. I love bubble tea and I have gotten it from all over the city (about 6 different places) and Dream Tea House comes out on top every time. At Dream, the drinks are actually fully blended - I have never sucked up a piece of ice through my straw (as I have at every other tea house I have been too). And besides the incredible drinks, Dream has an atmosphere that is unmatched. They are always busy and people are always having a good time - whether chatting with a friend or getting a group together and playing one of the games that they have available, it is always a good time. My favorite drink at Dream is the Vanilla Sky - oh how I love thee Vanilla Sky! I like it as a dessert (or just a sweet treat throughout the week)! Make sure to get a stamp card too - free bubble tea is the best bubble tea!

text: I came to Ricochet based on the good reviews I read on Yelp. I went in for highlights and a cut. I was going from red to blonde, and I knew it would take a while. My stylist, Beth, seemed pissed that I was asking her to do this. She told me it was a corrective color, and she didn't think the color would lift. She made me feel bad about what I wanted. I understand that it may be more work than she was prepared to do, but I didn't think it was impossible. If you don't feel you can honor someone's request, you tell them that. She just made a face as she touched my hair. Don't be rude. The owner had Max assist her with the coloring, since I have a lot of hair. He was very nice. Unfortunately, the color they were putting on in between the foils got all over my face and neck. I have chemical burns that are itchy and hot to the touch. The color turned out pretty good, but I didn't have enough time for the cut, so I went back the next day. I showed two different people the burns and they apologized, but I wish I could have gotten a discount. Max cut my hair and did a great job and he was actually friendly and nice to talk to. Beth was very uninterested in anything I had to say and I felt uncomfortable. The second day was a much more pleasant experience, but for $200 I think I could have been treated a little better.

text: Every ice cream shop in the country should follow Creole Creamery's example and offer a bowl of six mini-scoops for $5.50. Especially places like Creole that boast way too many tantalizing innovative flavors. Creole ranks with the greatest on this front, and if you cream yourself for creameries like Bi-Rite in San Francisco, Scoops in Los Angeles, Cones in New York, and Molly Moon's in Seattle, then you should put this place on your list. The interior is very cute, with lots of photographs and phrases like "Eat Ice Cream" and "Be Happy" decorating the walls. The service is friendly and generous with the samples. I tried a ton of flavors before getting the mini sampler, perhaps defeating part of the purpose of that sampler, and most of them were pretty great. All of the ice cream has a wonderful tuggy consistency and a creamy richness. The base ice cream is sold as its own "naked" flavor, and it's really good, milky and not too sweet. I like that they're proud of their base, and the quality of the product shines through in every flavor. Like I said, I got six mini-scoops, which was a fair amount of ice cream but not too much, even coming off of two giant lunches. For my six flavors, I chose creole cream cheese, red velvet, banana cane malt, coffee pecan brittle, peanut butter fudge, and Abita strawberry chocolate. The creole cream cheese was my favorite, with a flavor like cream cheese but tangier, even a little bit sour. The red velvet was so good and it actually tasted like the cake, rather than vanilla mixed with cake crumbs. The banana cane malt tasted strongly of banana with an equally strong malty flavor, and the result was balanced and deep. Coffee pecan brittle was as good as it sounds, nicely textured and very tasty. Peanut butter fudge was a more adult flavor than you might imagine, very dense and dark with just a subtle layer of peanut butter. The most out-there flavor was the Abita strawberry chocolate, and I would definitely recommend it. Abita is the local Louisiana beer, and the flavor was prominent but mixed well with the strawberry and chocolate, both of which were also easily discernible. My boyfriend got a scoop of the French vanilla, and this was a simpler flavor that was also quite good. For some reason, it tasted vaguely of coconut. I swallowed my six little scoops with ease then crawled in the back of our rental car and lay down like a beached whale. I had two huge meals and a good dose of ice cream weighing me down, and it was only 5 o'clock. I slept like a bloated Ignatius J. Reilly all the way to Baton Rouge.

text: this airport basically sucks. However, unfortunately, I do have to use it frequently, so it gets a couple of stars. Knowing this info will help figuring out where you need to check bags, etc. getting from terminal to terminal inside the secure areas is tricky at PHL. You are better off just going to the correct terminal. You could walk from terminal to terminal on the roadside...but, it will be a long walk!! Parking in the airport is VERY expensive (short-term and long-term). So, if you are poor and have to drive, then use an off-site lot (8$ to 12$ per day) or the Economy lot. Drinks, etc is very expensive, but you have no choice than to buy them here or not have a drink at all. Toilets can be hit or miss. Best used minimally. Flight delays are very common and are a rule with US AIR. Weather is often bad and low ceilings are common. The SEPTA train runs through each terminal and connects to downtown and other destinations. SEPTA rail costs $7 to downtown and $10 to Jenkintown. (one way). People (staff) are generally not friendly, since this is the northeast. You might luck out. Continental airlines usually have reasonably good staff. I fly this airline most of the time. There are not enough chairs for the number of people (especially in terminal D). This is not fun. Also, almost non-existent power outlets. There are some by the restrooms, if you want to sit close to the nasty smells. Overall, ok airport....this is going to be as good as it gets for Philadelphia. It wont be better until USAIR becomes bankrupt and stops flying. Then, we could get a different airline as a Philly hub which might improve facilities. Oh, Be VERY careful when exiting off of I-95 to the airport. Thanks to senseless road-designers, they made the airport exits as dangerous as they possibly can. text: When we visited The Good Pie, we were expecting good pizza baked in a stone oven. What we got was mediocre pizza burnt in a stone oven. Everyone in said group has dramatically different tastes, so we knew that perhaps one or two people might like the place and the other/s would either be "meh" or hate it. It turned out we all had something in common that night- a bad experience involving pizza. The Good Pie had a fantastic ambiance and the waitress was attentive and pleasant. The menu looked enticing: basil and cherry tomatoes with buffalo mozzarella on a pizza baked in a stone oven- huzzah! But when the food got to the table, we all looked at each other as if to say, "Really?" The crust was burnt in several places, and while a stone/ brick oven adds "character" to a pizza, is there really any reason there should be blatant scorch marks and undercooked areas? And when the menu said the pizza had basil and cherry tomatoes on it, why were there only three leaves of basil on it and just as many cherry tomatoes? I realize that this is authentic pizza, the way it's made in Italy, but still, three basil leaves and cherry tomatoes, on soggy oven-scorched crust? The sauce was decent, but by no means memorable. If the goal was to serve understated food, The Good Pie has hit its mark. But good understated food it was not. And getting hit with a thirty dollar check for two pizzas that were, at the end, disintegrating into mush, was too much for all of us. text: Bayona is as good as it gets for truly delicious and creative meals. Just make sure you go for lunch. Unless you make a lot of money, or are visiting from Europe and can ridicule how petty the value of the dollar has become ... Food: Like I said, superb! And perfectly proportioned too; you get the feeling a lot of thought has been taken in the kitchen in terms of presentation, proportion and of course, taste. Makes me not feel bad about ordering an appetizer and sharing two entrees and a dessert. Start with the Smoked Duck Cashew Butter and Pepper Jelly sandwich. It won't soon be forgotten. They cut it diagonally into two beautiful slices, so it makes it easy to share with a dining companion. Unless they cut it unevenly, in which case, you will probably be playing 21st finger to see who gets the bigger slice. We broke all the rules in our New Orleans food excursion and went to Bayona more than once. Not only that, we went on consecutive days. The lunch menu changes daily, with a few constants (like the aforementioned smoked duck goodness), so I encourage experimenting with different entrees. Everything we ordered was great, and perfect to share. Highlights include the scallops and pork and shrimp dumplings in chili aioli and the baked drum (local fish) with couscous. Wasn't HUGE on the meat platter entree of stuffed quail, lamb brochaise and sausage, surrounded by a mound of lettuce and needle-thin pommes frites, if only because the dish lacked the diversity of flavors and textures that seemed to be a staple of everything else on the menu. We shared the stuffed empanadas for dessert the first day. There were 2 and were accompanied by a scoop of spicy cinnamon gelato. Can't remember exactly WHAT the empanadas were stuffed with (waiter said it was a local fruit) but they were delicious, and again, perfect for sharing. At the end of the meal, I ordered a double espresso, which was garnished with a brown sugar cube and a chocolate-covered almond on the plate. I am half-Cuban and have been drinking espresso for most of my life, so I understand and am all-too aware of the perils of ordering a watered-down, overpriced one at similarly fancy establishments with delicious cuisine but disappointing coffee. I'd have to take the 7 train over to Queens, or worse, fly to Miami to get a truly memorable espresso. But Bayona is the real deal. So real that I ordered a second double espresso immediately after downing the first. Nice-sized double too, and not overpriced. Service: Our servers were attentive and extremely helpful on both occasions, even offering us advice on other restaurants we might enjoy during our stay and answering every question about the menu that we had. Atmosphere: Bayona has its own little private courtyard on a side street in the French Quarter that leads to its entrance. When it's nice out (ie: NOT 30 degrees and raining), I can imagine really enjoying the outdoor seating via the patio that is adjacent to the courtyard. Still, inside is marvelous. There are three rooms, each with their own signature. You get the feeling you are in a villa in turn-of-the-century America, because you are. The house remains intact, and so are all the classical accompaniments: piano, lush floral arrangements, gurgling fountain and all. Value: As I said, go for lunch. It was good enough to warrant an immediate repeat visit on a 4-day vacation in which we originally declared not to go to any restaurant more than once. Check out the dinner menu online if you're curious, but I doubt there is really anything you'll truly be missing if you opt to go for lunch, except maybe that loan you may have taken out after spending so much on vacation...

text: I ate at BJ's on a Tuesday night around 9pm and the restaurant was nearly empty. I guess this location is kinda out of the way. A colleague recommended the pizzas, so I ordered the buffalo chicken pizza. When our server brought my pizza, I could almost hear my arteries moaning. The buffalo chicken pizza may be one of the most unhealthy foods on the menu--but WOW it was good! BJ's is famous for their beer and their pizookies. I don't drink, but I did try a pizookie--an amazing dessert involving a giant chewy cookie topped with exorbitant amounts of ice cream topped with chocolates and sugary syrups. This is a fantastic way to follow an ultra unhealthy meal, right? This place can make Five Guys look like Subway. The bottom line: if you want to get drunk and pump yourself full of trans fats, then BJ's should be #1 on your list. Personally, I will only return if doctors discover preventative medicines for heart disease.

text: So I have heard horrible things about this place, but that damn chili pepper hanging above the entrance outside the restaurant kept calling my name. I am a lover all things mexican. And I know that tasty mexican in this town is hard to come by. But my coworker raved about her dinner here, and so when the boyfriend said he was in the mood for mexican, I suggested we give it a try. I am reading over the last couple reviews. Sure the drinks are big, but there isn't any alcohol in them. Or in my boyfriends case, the wrong alcohol....what the hell is coconut doing in a hurricane. Or at least, it wasn't mentioned in the description of the drink and then, surprise! The typical chips laid out for snacking before your meal comes, or in our case, before our ditzy waitress finally made it to take our drink order, were awful. I mean, they get points for having something other than Tostitos, but I would have preferred nothing at all. They were greasy and when I bit into them, actual oil dripped out. Maybe it was a sign of the food to come.....maybe they keep them greasy to help the rest of your meal get down your throat....either way, they were awful. And the salsa to accompany them was weak. I have made better. There was a lot of staff, all checking up on us, but our main waitress had a vacant look in her eye and couldn't quite muster up a smile. I know its easy to hate your job, especially if you are a server, but it was affecting our experience. On to the main course....there were few choices and for mexican food, they were quite pricey. A plate of 4 tacos for $9. I thought I was staying with a safe bet by getting the tacos(seriously, suburban moms around the country have been doing taco night for years) but apparently not. It was a build your own kind of deal. I was excited to see guacamole as a component, but it was flavorless. I was happy they had authentic oaxaca cheese, but the consistency was more like parmesan. I chose fajita chicken as my main ingredient, but I was given a bowl full of green peppers, and little chicken. And I got the better of the two entrees! My boyfriend ordered the "chicken" chimichanga but there was little chicken to be found. Instead, gobs and gobs of refried beans (and I love refried beans, but there is a limit people). Traditionally a good chimi is deep fried, but this was baked. Also, they are smothered in a yummy tomatoey sauce. No sauce, just some weird fake cheese liquid that was for decoration, hence, no flavor. I am only giving Johnny one star because it started to rain and the staff attempted to move our table under their awnings. They weren't very good at it as my boyfriend still was getting rained on. Ok then I guess I am giving them one star because their other patrons were kind enough to move in. I am never going back to this place and sad we wasted $45 on a meal when I would have been more happier with Taco Bell, and thats not really appetizing, is it.

text: I've been in Tucson for about four years now and have experienced the ups and the downs of cuisine in this town. While I have not been to sushi happy hour at this establishment which seems to have gotten some excellent reviews my experience in the eat-in restaurant section has been sub-par at best. This sentiment has only solidified over time. I agree with the analysis that this is less like Japanese food and more like 70's vegetarian style preparation/cooking/philosophy. I was amazed to find my vegetable yakisoba dry and tasteless with a faint hint of dish soap and even more surprised to find that my partner's salad was replete with wilting greens and a gnarly hair from someone in the kitchen. I once had to send back a roll because it was completely inedible, tasting as if it had been sitting out for many hours. My vegetable ramens of the past have always been rather gamey with scrappy vegetables. There is always a problem with freshness. This again was in the dine-in section, so I speak for only this part of the establishment. Yoshimatsu could be one of my favorite places in Tucson if quality control was better in the kitchen. There are wild fluctuations in the preparation style here -- your vegetable yakisoba may be the bizarro counterpart to the real stuff and the end result is often confusing and bland. I'm not saying here that Yoshimastsu should try to emulate authentic Japanese dishes, but if you're going to "innovate" do it well. Yoshimatsu does so many things right -- the ambiance is amazing, the music is always at good levels, the staff is generally amicable, the gift store is super cool, and of course karaoke on Fridays -- if only the food were better.

text: Dim Sum garden is my favorite Shanghai restaurant that I have encountered as of yet in America. The highlight of the whole place is the xiao long bao also known as soup buns. For the uninitiated these are buns which are delicately made with thin shells and filled with steaming hot soup which consists of pork and broth. They are to die for but one must also be careful not to have the hot soup squirt out on them which can sometimes be a difficult task. This place has the best soup buns I have had since I have been to Shanghai. I am serious about this as I have been to Flushing and Chinatown and not found any as tasty as these. They are succulent and flavorful and warm you up from the inside. Now let's tackle the rest of the menu. The menu is really trying to cater to all tastes. It has traditional Shanghai dishes to Americanized Chinese food and just plain Fried Chicken with French Fries. The dim sum items are definitely the highlight. The aforementioned xiao long bao are the best and available in both pork and pork with seafood varieties. The pork dumplings and siu mai are also good and some of the better I have had. The scallion pancakes are definitely worth a try as well. The pork with sauce noodle is also a favorite of mine and very flavorful. Some of the other foods are great and some are just average and you do have to pick carefully. I would also recommend the beef brisket and the mapo tofu. The more Americanized you go the more likely you will be disappointed. Be sure to check out the daily specials as there is always stuff that is not on the main menu. Recently there has been this soup which is good I think it is a sweet hot and sour soup though they described as a minestrone. It is good and quite unlike anything I have tasted though there is an excess of broth. The noodle dishes are all great as the noodles are all handmade. You can really taste the difference. So if you are deciding between rice and noodles, go for the noodles. Many of the dishes can also be served in a soup form with the noodles submerged which is also quite good. Overall there is a lot of variety to please most anyone you bring with you. Next, the pricing is amazing. This place is giving McDonald's a run for its money. Most main dishes are under $7 and the portions are quite large. I would be shocked if you spent more than $20 on a meal for two and left without leftovers especially since there is no alcohol. Actually the drink selection is limited to tea or soda pretty much. The food generally comes out pretty quick so it's a good place if you are in a hurry. The staff is great. They try their best to be helpful and make you feel welcome despite the language barrier. They started to remember me by the second time I had come there which is impressive. I still remember that I came in once when it was empty with a few people and they were doing food prep on one of the tables. The immediately started to clean up and move to the back room and asked us to sit there. We said it wasn't necessary but they said it was the biggest table and they insisted. It's moments like that will make you feel welcome somewhere and go beyond what is normally defined as service. Seriously the people who work here are some of the nicest people I have met a restaurant and that alone makes me want to keep going back. The location is awful. It will put a lot of people off. It is a weird area under a tunnel. There are a lot of shady characters outside at times due to the proximity to the bus stop. However, in addition to being located next to both the Chinatown and Greyhound bus stops, it is conveniently located close to Reading Terminal Market, the Market East Station, and the Convention Center. I actually first discovered it wondering around after the flower show. Once again, you literally feel like you are underneath a bridge somewhere about to do a drug deal by the time you reach the place. Okay I'm exaggerating quite a bit but I have taken people there and they seemed a bit hesitant. It is safe though really. The interior leaves a lot to be desired. It is eerily lit by the excessive neon in the front windows. The furniture is all from IKEA and the wall is painted in an attempt to look more modern. There are pictures of food above the cashier counter that does not highlight the breadth or best parts of the menu. The place is very clean but feels damp due to the location being somewhat cave-like. There is a TV playing asian music videos which are often quite amusing. The place seems a lot nicer from the inside than the outside. Don't let the location or the restaurant's appearance put you off this really is a diamond in the rough. Dim Sum Garden will leave you pleasantly surprised and craving more. I can personally attest to this as I keep coming back for the food and the people.

Most of the animals were enjoying the great weather (save for the Giant Rats, which don't come out until dark....damn them!) and the variety our zoo has is terrific. Baby lemurs hanging to their father's backs are worth the price of admission right there. But there's so much more. We even went on the swan paddle boats, which was great exercise until my wife got noivous and wanted out. Truth be told, I was rocking the boat back and forth like some dope from junior high. Can't take me anywhere. If you haven't been to the zoo lately, make a date. Weekday afternoons are probably the least crowded, with school buses driving away and the downtrodden still at their day jobs. Lemurs, elephant shrews, flamingos and cool new exhibits like Big Cat Falls and Squirrel Alley are just a few of the hundreds of reasons to see our animal friends. She explained that they were all reserved, but we could sit at the table in the very front of the bar by the window and wait for the rest of our party to show up. We decided to do this and went to the bar to grab drinks. I ordered a beer and brought it back to that same table and sat down. Immediately, the hostess told me that if I wanted to sit at that table that she TOLD US we could sit at, we would have to have the server wait on us and could not bring bar drinks back to the table. I argued that immediately after we put our things at that table, she saw us go to the bar so this should have been explained to us at that very moment. Shortly thereafter, she sat us at another, bigger table. Our party started showing up slowly but surely after we were seated. Once the last two members of our party showed up, we made more than enough room at our table for our two friends. We asked our waitress if she could grab us two extra chairs for our friends, and she explained that she could not do that because we would then be "blocking" a certain area. In my opinion, and having worked numerous waitressing jobs in the past, this was not the case. There would have been more than enough room for servers and patrons to easily pass by had we set up two chairs for our friends. Because of this, our friends left because they had nowhere to sit. The only good thing that I can say about my Alfa experience was that our food and drinks came quickly with each round that was ordered. text: Vande pretty much sums up the experience, down to the gift certificate issues, though we didn't get the matter taken care of... This review is also just for the restaurant, not the hotel itself. This place has the specter of death hanging over it, it just feels like a place that could close down sometime soon if something really amazing doesn't come out of it. Our check came out to roughly $60 for a chicken cordon bleu, chicken marsala, small caesar salad, and two glasses of wine. We were unable to pay with a gift card from Tucson Originals even though the restaurant is part of that group; it's mildly heartbreaking because the quality of the food was simply not worth the money. We expected to treat ourselves with the gift card, but had to pay our of our own pockets. Not only did having to pay for the meal tax us financially because we can't really afford those kinds of prices, but we would have been much more satisfied at another restaurant that charges a third of their prices (or eaten three meals for the same cost). Low quality food across the board. Sickening. There was something very high-school-boys-in-home-ec about the prefabness of many of the meal's components; the food was passable, but the rice appeared to be of the microwave variety and the veggie blend on the side, though fresh, was dull and flavorless. The bread was soft and warm, and at the bottom of the basket were two pieces of cornbread (I think?) that appeared to have been made from store-bought yellow cake mix. My chicken was tough and overcooked, but I can get down with that sort of thing every now and then. Still, not worth the money. The server was excellent and very knowledgeable about the menu and the wine list. The construction on the property makes the walk to the restaurant a mini-adventure, but there are signs clearly pointing to the restaurant as you round multiple corners (nice work on that one). Hopefully they can improve the quality of the food; there's many shellfish options (nearly all appetizer options involve crab or some other shelled thing) that I couldn't indulge to due to a gnarly allergy, so maybe that's what they do best. I thank them for not contaminating my food or dishware with an accidental swipe of shrimp (something that has happened at other restaurants that served shellfish). I won't be back.

They were dry and lacking a little bit of flavor. But they still have the right blend of vegetables, meat and mint. I still liked it. The pho is great. I always get the rare steak. I love how the broth cooks the meat. The noodles always swing when I bring them towards my mouth so needless to say I end up with splotches of hot-sauce infused broth on my shirt. I love the pho here. It originally opened a block to the east on the other side of Second Street. The current owner bought it from someone else in about the mid 1990s. He tried to sell it and buy the now closed international market near Park Lane but came back after a short time. Then some whacked out woman tried to settle a dispute at the Mizpah Hotel by starting a fire in 2006. She killed 12 and burned down much of the block, inlcuding Pho 777, so Pho 777 moved to the location of the former Kim Son. He now takes credit cards but prices are still reasonable. It's southern Vietnamese pho, meaning it's served with bay leaves and bean sprouts.

There are lunch specials, which is good because otherwise you'd be paying entree prices that would make tonier joints in Philly blush. Even the lunch price of $14 only got you a choice of about 4 dishes, and no appetizer or dessert options. The waitress was kind enough to point out that dishes are prepared fairly bland, and asked if I preferred spicy. Yes my zaftig sweetie, I like food that inflicts. I only wish the chef had believed me, for there was no discernible ouch factor in the chicken tikka masala that was delivered. The chunks of chicken were superior, but a tad overcooked. text: I was really excited to stay at the Windsor Court for a recent weekend trip to NOLA with my wife. Unfortunately, we were both extremely disappointed. First, no rooms were available upon check-in, even though we had arrived at the check-in time of 3PM. No big deal for us as we would just walk around the French Quarter until a room was ready. The front desk took our cell phone number and promised to call when a room was ready. Three hours later, no call. When we got back, they had assigned us a room, but left our bags sitting out next to the front desk, despite having promised to deliver them when the room was available. When we got to the room, we were again disappointed. The room was a nice size, but the furnishings and decor were tired and dated. The bed was as hard as a rock and was uneven. We inquired about another room with the front desk, but were told they were sold out that night. After adjusting our expectations downward, we settled in to get ready for dinner out. When my wife went to take a shower, she discovered the removable shower head only pointed straight down. We called engineering and they improvised a fix, but it was such a hassle. The water pressure was terrible. Water from the bathroom faucet shot out sideways and squeeled when the cold water was turned on. The lights in the hall near the closet didn't work so you couldn't see into the closet. There was no garbage can in the main room (only in the bathroom). Housekeeping didn't replace hand towels or washcloths after our first night. When we called to request more towels, they only brought bath size towels and no hand towels or wash cloths. At least one of the additional towels they did bring was dirty. When we informed the front desk manager of our disappointment and a list of the problems we encountered, he responded with a terse "uh, sorry." Are any of these things huge issues? Not really - we're usually pretty easy going travellers. But all of these annoyances built up into a bad experience. Sure, the common areas are lovely and elegant, but unfortunately we weren't staying in the lobby. The Ritz-Carlton is about the same price at the time we booked, and given a second chance, we would've stayed at the Ritz, no doubt about it.

text: Alice Keck PARK Memorial Gardens (the name entered for this garden is incorrect) is the best public garden in Santa Barbara. It is not only beautiful to walk around and laze about on the numerous grassy knolls, but is horticulturally stimulating as well. The Environmental Horticulture students from the local college come here to study plant names and Brooks photography students are often at the park taking photos. Wednesdays are my favorite days at the park for two reasons. First, because of Circus Wednesdays. From 5:30-ish onwards, hula hoopers and poi spinners gather on the grass near the pond and play around. Anyone is welcome, there are usually extra hoops to share. Sometimes stilt walkers appear, and sometimes someone brings a croquet set for a game or two. Second, up in the center of the park, an Old Time band jams. It's wonderful to listen to. The circus group only meets when daylight extends into the evening. I imagine it's the same for the old time band. Pretty much spring, summer and most of the autumn. I uploaded some pictures of a hooper at the park, and the band. Give the Gardens a visit and come play!

text: I am smitten with Lüke. During our whirlwind weekend in New Orleans, we tried to experience the whole gamut of N'awlins food. Everything was amazing, but Lüke was definitely my fave. A John Besh restaurant, Lüke pays homage to the grand old French and German brasseries that were once hugely popular in New Orleans. A mix of casual yet classy, modern yet vintage, with Southern hospitality ever present and food and drinks that delight the senses. I was floored. While everything on the menu looked tantalizing, three out of four of us decided to get their daily changing 3-course Express Menu for $23. Best decision ever. I had crawfish bisque as my soup selection, and it was fantastic - a yummy little crawfish with its tiny head poking out of a delicious pool of flavorful bisque. The Friday dinner special was a Redfish "Court-Bouillon" with crab, shrimp, oysters and rice served in a skillet. The generous portions of seafood tasted so fresh, and the cajun sauce was so delicious that I polished off my entire plate with my bread. For dessert, we had Brendan's bread pudding with vanilla bean ice cream and hot buttered pecan sauce which was heaven in a bowl. Bread pudding is my favorite dessert, and Lüke surely blew away my tastebuds with it. And all this for ONLY $23!! Lüke's classic New Orleans cocktails were also made to perfection. The French 75, St. Charles Streetcar and Sazerac were all wonderful. Lüke really set the bar high for our dining experiences in New Orleans, but fortunately, we had many more wonderful ones to follow. A MUST VISIT. Your tastebuds will thank you for it.

text: I have been to this place two or three times in the last couple years. To the credit of this place, their food is good, and the family style portions are fun when you go with a crowd. It looks like the size of a party room at a Pizza Hut or a Chuck E Cheese or something like that. That room can fit around three dozen people, and unfortunately it's hard to hear the people you eat with, because the acoustics really don't work in your favor. And if ANYONE in that room starts getting loud, you need to either be a great lipreader with your neighbor, or be telepathic, because normal conversation will be hard. For another thing, when the place is packed, service is much slower. The last time (and by that I mean the previous time AND the final time) I was there, I was about 30 min late meeting up with my friends. They were all ready to order, and I hadn't seen the menu yet. But the funny thing is, we didn't order for another 15-20 minutes, because it took that long to get a server to take our order. The food did not come out for an hour, though to be fair it was definitely good when it did come out. But one of our friends never got her food, not even after the rest of us had almost finished our meals. It came out of the kitchen maybe 20 minutes after we got our food, and when she expressed her disappointment in a polite way, the server did not seem to care, and she did not offer an apology. For that, we chose to leave less than the 18% gratuity already added into the check for parties of I believe 6 or more. It seems the majority of people who have reviewed this place like it a lot, and more power to them. But it's all about what you think of your own experiences. And by that standard, I will have to be bribed substantially to set foot in that place again.

text: My husband and I decided that this is a great place for happy hour, but not necessarily a great dining experience. I would give Zing 3+ stars for tasty, creative food, but 2 stars because of the slow, apathetic service. We have eaten here a couple of times, and had similar experiences, so I don't think it was a fluke. It took several minutes after being seated for our waitress to take our drink order, and several more to bring the first round of drinks (including water). At least we had plenty of time to peruse the menu, so we ordered everything at once. Food came out quickly, and was presented by one of the chefs. I think our waitress came by only once after the food came out, and didn't ask if we were enjoying the food. The group at the next table also had bad service - they ordered more wine, and when it didn't come for over 20 minutes, they canceled the order, which seemed to make the waiter a bit mad. The food is innovative, but I think the dishes could use a bit of editing and work on execution. The fish tacos are the best in the city, with a crispy fried shell, stuffed with mahi mahi and topped with cilantro pesto. The risotto balls are a great concept, but were way too mushy inside. The shrimp and calamari both were perfectly cooked and served with a nice spicy sauce. The restaurant is located on the second-floor of an old building on the corner of Indiana Ave. & West St, which is a bit isolated from downtown. The decor inside is very modern and chic, and the balcony has a great view of the city. Zing serves its purpose for groups to leisurely enjoy cocktails and share small plates.

text: My husband and I bought tickets to a movie at the Granite Run AMC, and initially planned to just go to Ruby Tuesdays. A few hundred feet from Ruby Tuesdays, we made a game-day decision to try the Riddle Ale House in the hopes of supporting a local restaurant. What a horrible mistake! We were seated at the outside patio, which was an improvement over Ruby Tuesdays. Our choice of view was either Riddle Memorial Hospital or the mall parking lot. Not too nice, but hey, we were dining al fresco. The menu could be described as having standard to upscale pub fare, with gourmet burgers and fancy salads. What was glaringly lacking was a beer menu. I guess the "Riddle" is "Why is this an 'Ale House'?" We waited several minutes for our server to arrive. She seemed to be the only person serving the 10-ish tables out on the patio, and was about 70 years old. I'm not being ageist here, it's just a lot of work for one person, let alone someone her age. Our server approached us and said, "I have to get someone else's drink order so I might as well get yours." Charming! My husband asked what beers they had on tap. If I recall correctly, they were Bud, Miller Light, Coors Light, Sam Summer, Blue Moon, and Dogfishhead. Very unimpressive. He ordered a Blue Moon; I should have followed suit. I ordered one of the specialty mixed drinks called a Peach Iced Tea. It was billed as freshly brewed iced tea with peach flavored rum. Couldn't be so bad, right? WRONG! What came from the bar tasted like Snapple Peach Iced Tea mixed with Robitussin. AWFUL! After delivering our drinks, our server didn't show up again for another 15 minutes. I settled on the cranberry, walnut, and feta salad with an order of 3 mini crab cakes. The server came back to take our orders. My husband asked her opinion on the ribs. She said, "I think they're fine." Uh, yeah. He ordered them anyway. Fast forward 15-20 minutes. At this point, we were committed to eating there. If we went anywhere else, we'd be late for the movie. Our elderly server came out to the patio balancing our 3 plates individually. She teetered her way over to our table. She tossed the plates onto the table with a grunt, but missed with the ribs. Instead, they toppled off of the plate and onto my bare arm! Scalding hot barbeque sauce made of lava was all over my right arm! I just shouted, "Hot! Hot!" and our server did the same! She picked the ribs off of my arm and put them back on the plate. She told me she was going to get a wet towel for me to clean up with, and told my husband that she was going to bring the ribs back to the kitchen to heat them up. In theory, my husband has no problem eating food that once touched my arm, but that's just gross to hear out loud. I imagine it's also a violation of health codes. She came back with a wet towel for me, but it was used. Before I could protest the idea of wiping my body off with a food encrusted dirty rag, she was gone. So my choice was to let the barbecue sauce cool into a crust on my forearm or wipe off with this rag. I chose the latter. Luckily, my brilliant husband reminded me that his meal came with wet naps, so I could do a final rinse with something clean. I took a bite out of my salad. As I was chewing, I noticed there were about 4 cranberries, 3 feta crumbles, and 5 walnuts added to the bag of field greens. The greens themselves were drowning in a vat of sticky dressing. How disappointing! But at least I had my crab cakes. I cut into a cake, and put it in my mouth. What followed can only be described as Elmer's Glue Paste formed into a patty that was rubbed onto day-old cod that was sitting in the mall parking lot. After of few minutes of me not touching a thing on my side of the table, the busboy asked if I was done. I motioned to him to take away the dishes and a split second later, our awful server popped up. Where was she that whole time? She asked (pointing to the crab cakes), "You're going to take those home, right?" I replied, "Actually, no, they were fishy and tasted bad." She rolled her eyes at me and said, "I'll see what I can do!" In the corner of the patio, and in my line of sight, was a large bin in which the busboy scraped table scraps. I saw him scrape the remnants of my husband's dinner into it, and my mound of salad, but before he could discard the crabcakes, our nasty server was by his side, PICKING THE CRABCAKES OFF OF THE PLATE AND PUTTING THEM ON ANOTHER! SHE WALKED BACK INTO THE RESTAURANT WITH THE CRABCAKES ARRANGED ON ANOTHER PLATTER! When she returned with the check, she told me (here's the icing on the cake) "I'm not sure if the crab cakes were old or not. They aren't supposed to be." Needless to say, I will never, EVER return to this restaurant. My only explanation for their poor service and terrible food is that they get kick-backs from the emergency room across the street for every patron they send in.

text: Tropicana Field is Major League Baseball at its worst. I have to believe it's the single worst major league baseball park in the whole country. But, you know what they say: say something nice or don't say anything at all. So, I'll start by saying something nice: * It's a dome, which means there are no rainouts or heat strokes. * It's never sold out, which means good seats are usually available. In fact, the last time I went to the Yankees/Rays game here, I sat 4 rows behind home plate. My seat was one of 5 seats in that row, and my fellow Yankee fans and I couldn't stop talking about how much we'd have to pay for similar seats at Yankee Stadium. * It's huge, which means there are plenty of concessions and things to do. * It's a home of the Tampa Bay Rays, the biggest surprise in Major League Baseball in 2008. Now, I have to call 'em like I see 'em: * It's a dome, so . . . 'nuf said. Baseball in the dome is weird enough, without a depressing gray roof to look at. Just ask the outfielders who can't see the balls hit high in the "air." Besides, any ballpark with ground rules like this one: "A batted ball that hits the catwalk, lights or suspended objects and remains on or in the catwalk, lights or suspended objects in fair territory is a fair ball and it shall be called a double" should be torn down immediately. * It's never sold out, which means you can always hear that heckler from behind home plate. Mr. Szasz (pronounced "sass," fittingly) became world famous for his unique heckling antics. It's fun to read about him in Sports Illustrated, but at the ballpark it's just plain annoying. * It's huge, which means it's even more depressing, gray and hollow than one can imagine. * It's a home of the Tampa Bay Rays, still the worst franchise in the history of Major League Baseball despite their 2008 success of historic proportions. This place deserves only one star, if that. But they're awarded an additional star for housing a Tampa MLB franchise that is NOT the Giants. For those of you who forgot (or didn't know), my hometown San Francisco Giants back in 1993 were a few days away from relocating to Tampa. I would not have liked that.

text: I have eaten here many times over the years, though this is my first review. But I do want to reiterate, Mystic Fish has been excellent in the past, and perhaps this was an off night (which should never be an excuse for a top-drawer restaurant). As for this visit, the meal as a whole was flavorless. I have had the steak tartar several times, and it has always been very good, tasty, and of high quality. Not this time - flavorless. The capers must have been sitting out or rinsed off because they added no flavor whatsoever, and the meat lacked any noticeable seasoning. Had I gone to the grocery store, bought 3 ounces of meat, unwrapped it, and bitten into it, it would have tasted about the same: raw, unseasoned meat. The seabass tasted like it had been poorly frozen or poorly defrosted. I think they generally use fresh fish here, but this time it did not seem like it. The texture was grainy with none of the silkiness that good seabass should have, and bland all the way. The vegetables were similarly flavorless. And the mashed potatoes, which were supposed to be a yellow pepper mashed potato, was creamy but lacked any pizzazz. My friend had the lobster tail. It was undercooked and, yup, flavorless. When the waiter asked about the meal, my friend told him that the lobster tail was not very good, and the waiter said he would let the chef know. The manager (who I think is also an owner) came by and was told the same thing. He didn't seem upset or disappointed by the comment, just seemed to take it sort of blandly. That spoke volumes to me, because the in the past he has been very professional and engaged. Anyway, both my friend and I felt that somebody in the kitchen was clueless as to seasoning. I hate to write a bad review for Mystic Fish because it has been a longtime favorite. This time, it was woefully short of the mark and a huge disappointment.

text: I can't believe nobody has reviewed Recycled Records yet! This place is a Reno institution - I've been going there for years, though not so much now that I'm not a starving student anymore. Floor-to-ceiling CD racks line the walls, along with huge CD bins throughout the store. New releases and hot items are located right up front at the counter, so if you're a regular visitor, you can check there first to see what's new. The rest of the CDs are loosely organized by alpha and band, but you may have to rifle through a few stacks to find what you want. Elsewhere in the store, there's a big vinyl section and a smaller cassette section. They also have DVDs and, I believe, some video games. You can listen to everything before you buy it (with a small charge to open a wrapped item), and the staff is pleasant and helpful and not at all indie-rock-snob - they will never throw you out of the store for asking about an unhip band. Of course, Recycled Records also takes your unwanted music. You get a better deal if you take store credit, but they'll also pay cash for your stuff, too. And, if your stuff is so lame that they don't even want to buy it (which does happen), you can just give it to them to decently bury, and at least you'll be rid of it. Music stores will come and go, but Recycled Records is here to stay.

text: We went because the admission was included in the package we got with Discovery Cove. We were there for only about 3 or 4 hours before we got bored and left. One good thing about Busch Gardens is that if you have a mix of rollercoaster enthusiasts and chickens in your group, everyone will have something to do. The downside is that everyone will only have something to do for a few hours. There are only a handful of rollercoasters, all of which are pretty tame compared to 6 Flags Great America and are REALLY short. Then, once you've taken the Serengeti Express to see the animals, you've pretty much done it all. There's an aviary and a cave and a few other exhibits tucked around the park, but definitely not enough to fill up the entire day. This park is HUGE, but most of it is filled up with carnival games and souvenir booths. So you have to walk forever through the sweltering heat to get to anything of any consequence. There's a 4-D theater, but it's cheesy and the sound didn't work half the time. Whatever you do, DO NOT go in May. This place was SWARMING with school groups... you know, 30 kids supervised by 2 adults, hopped up on sugar and excitement, running around with giant carnival prizes, cutting you off, screaming, jumping around, running into you... This place is probably a blast if you have little ones and want to play with them in Busch Garden's giant (and really cool looking) kiddie play areas. But if you want to ride rollercoasters, just go to 6 Flags... there will be more and better rides, and you won't get bored so quickly. If you want to see animals, go to a zoo... you'll see more animals and you won't have to walk around such a sprawling park to see them and you'll be far more comfortable. Bottom line: Do it once, if you must (just not in May). But otherwise, I wouldn't recommend it. There are better theme parks out there.

I will also point out that Far East is not true Vietnamese but more of a fusion and that is cool with me. The unfortunate side of this is that they fail at all attempts. My party ordered 1 appetizer and 2 entrees. We started with the cold shrimp wraps and they were par for the course, but the rice wraps were a bit chewy, which sometimes can happen anywhere. The real upset was the Shakey Beef (Bo Luc Lac) or properly call Shaken beef due to the method in which it is cooked; super high heat with rapid shaking of the wok. Their version was unfortunately very bland, meat was rather tough, and overall just sucked, oh and lastly if there was 3 ounces of cubed beef I would have been surprised. On a scale of 1 to 3, its gets a 0. The second entree ordered was Bun (rice noodles) with Tofu, generally bun is filled with various herbs, cucumber, bean sprouts, and other goodies. This version did include these item, but minimally and overall just fell short of any decent Bun out there. The flavors again were bland and the rice noodles which were served cold seemed a bit old. Interestingly, while we were there, almost every table was sat but I am certain everyone left hungry. Even more disappointing was the fact that the desserts they were serving didn't match the cuisine at all. I will give the 1 star for having the proper Pho condiments on the table and Tiger Beer. I think if the owners of this establishment bring it back to the roots and basics of Vietnamese cuisine they can really bring some unique bits to East Nashville. However, what they are dishing out now is a poor representation of the real tastes of Vietnam.

The plate was huge and I couldn't eat it all (shocker!) but I enjoyed every bite thoroughly. If you're bored with the typical Chad-like happy hour hole, definitely hit up Ernesto's. It's in a cute little 'hood, the drinks are delish and it's a little off the beaten path.

text: I have very mixed feelings about this place. The location of the hotel is fine. It's only about a 20-30 minute walk from the French Quarter and Bourbon Street, closer to the Garden District, and has some good restaurants nearby, including two 24-hour bars that serve good food. Also, the rooms are clean, and if you need anything, they promptly send someone to take care of it for you. Also, they serve breakfast for free in the mornings. It's not the best breakfast selection, but it's pretty decent with a wafflemaker, bagels, pastries, toast, sausages, eggs, yogurt, fruit, and cereal. Despite all of those upsides, in addition to the fact that I DO realize that although the name of the hotel is the "Maison St. Charles," it's really La Quinta Inn renamed fancy (DON'T BE DECEIVED), I was a little put off by the fact that one of the nights when I was about to go out, I came out of my room, and just jiggled the door handle to make sure that the door was locked, and it wouldn't LOCK! It just opened on me! I had a mini internal freak-out because I was imagining all of the horrible things that could have happened if I had not tested my lock and had just gone out. My laptop, clothes, etc. might have been easily stolen! And there's not a security patrol outside either! I immediately called the front desk and they brought someone over, but needless to say, I checked my lock after leaving every day from thereon. Just a little unnerving.
