text: Since I moved to Glenolden, this has become my grocery store of choice. Unfortunately, it is the lesser of the few evils (that is, not that good, but better than the other terrible grocery stores around town). When I lived in Newark, Delaware, the Acme there was much better. The only major problem I had with the Holmes Acme staff was once when I needed to get a roll of quarters (it was late, and the banks were closed). I had just purchased about 130 dollars worth of groceries, and thought that if I gave the cashier $10 in cash, there would be no issues getting a roll of quarters. Apparently, I was horrendously wrong. He referred me to the manager, who very rudely dismissed me and said "we don't give out rolls of change." I informed her that I am a paying customer and that I use this store frequently, but she didn't want to hear it, she told me that they pay the bank for their change deliveries (which I know for a fact is a nominal fee), and that they can't give it out to everyone who walks in off the street. Once again, I was a PAYING customer, not someone who just came in for the change. That really ticked me off, and just proves that many people don't belong in customer service. I wasn't asking her to go an extra mile to accommodate me, just walk a few steps, and she couldn't even do that, totally lazy. Long story short, I went next door to the Kmart, where I didn't even buy anything, and the lady behind the customer service desk forked over the quarters with no questions asked. Great job Acme, you win the award for giving worse service than Kmart, and that's sad. Also, I like to use the self-checkout when I have only a few items. The attendant that is overseeing the self-checkouts is NEVER paying attention to anything. Anyone that has used a self check-out knows they aren't perfect, and frequently need the attendant to override an item because maybe it isn't reading it's weight. When this happens, a prompt appears on the employees terminal that assistance is needed at your station, a red light also blinks. Even with these alarms, I still need to turn and let them know "HELLO!!! NEED HELP!!!" Incredibly inattentive, and if someone were to not scan something and just take it, they wouldn't even know. text: OK. So, I went here last night with 7 other people for a late dinner/drink extravaganza. Only two of us ate dinner, others just had drinks and snacks. The Good: The "Sexy" Shrimp and Grits. There was no way I was sharing that! It was so good. The remoulade-like sauce that accompanied the fried calamari was really delicious. The Decent: The bread brought out before the meal was really tasty, hot and fresh. The drinks were priced well and the fact that the kitchen stays open till 11 is great for the area. The space is also nice and welcoming. The Relatively Passable: The spanikopita with roasted tomato-whatever sauce. The spanikopita itself was delicious, but the sauce was overwhelming and pungent and the spanikopita was swimming in it. Too bad the calamari that accompanied that delicious remoulade sauce was incredibly greasy.... it had a nice flavor, but I couldn't deal with the grease factor. The Inexplicably Bad: OUR SERVER. He started off with gusto and a little awkward charm, but honestly the best thing he did the whole night was recommend the Shrimp and Grits, which really saved the whole night. He proceeded to ridicule my friend based on the fact that she asked questions about ingredients since she doesn't eat anything with added sugar. At first I thought he was just awkward and trying to make a lighthearted joke, but he kept DOING it. Not cool. But THEN he proceeded to completely forget about us during the second half of our meal. Who I assumed to be the manager served us our food and the bartender brought us the check. The "server" was present the entire time, screwing around and giving us dirty looks. Unprofessional. We were one of two tables in the whole joint, he wasn't ignoring us because he was busy. It was clear that he was just avoiding us. It's a server's job to answer any questions a patron may have, not to get pissy when someone asks questions, and then ignore the table for the rest of the night. It's a shame, because the food had potential and was priced well, but I do not plan on returning.

text: Came here for the the 3rd night of the Fringe Previews and it was definitely a chill little theater. The honors of the night by far went to the Nice People Theatre Company and the awesomely named (pardon my French) Zombies Ain't Shit Theatre Company. Nice People are doing an awesome group therapy musical called Have A Nice Day. The group features a man with a mother complex, an arguing couple, and a therapist who appears to be smitten with his newest patient, and others characters that I can't wait to find out more about. And the performance of the Zombie group, (again pardon my French) Brainfucked is about pharmaceutical taking college students who turn into brain eating zombies. It's a romance that's suitable for children (I joke, therefore I'm sold!). But this was just one night of ten 10 minute previews! Be sure to check out what Plays & Players are doing during Fringe, because it's sure to be awesome. And their next regular season is going to feature Alice in Wonderland, puppetry classes for your kids, and William Shakespeare's Land Of The Dead (note - not really a Shakespeare play. But a something that should be a true experience. Alas Poor Yorik, I had to shoot him in the head!). Shakespeare vs zombies? I think I could cry blood whether I'm sold or not. But that remains to be seen so I'm there!

text: Motoraunt may take some people aback because it is a restaurant located inside an old motor home which, frankly, looks grubby and not particularly well taken care of. If you summon the courage to walk in, you will again be taken aback: the place is filled with tons of objects - from old books and antique furniture to thousands of non-strategically placed knick knacks. The place doesn't feel decorated, it feels crammed and overstuffed. Once your eyes stop wandering around and trying to make sense of what is going on around you and how the hell did you wind up here, you can choose to have a sit at either first floor or on the second level. My friends and I chose to dine upstairs. Here you will find small booths which provide comfortable seating, dusty windows that provide the view of the outside world, and many more knick knacks. At that point you may start worrying about the quality of food served here, and wonder whether it will be good and fresh enough to consume. The waitress comes along shortly after you and your company grab a seat, but after ordering, gets ready to wait for your food to arrive. When my friends and I came here, there were about 4 other customers in the diner, and still we had to wait half an hour for our food to make its way onto our table. The wait doesn't seem too long because everybody is busy discussing Motoraunt and its bizarreness. Once your food arrives, everyone is sure to quiet down and dig in because the food is delicious. The menu consists of simple comfort foods such as burgers, hot dogs and French fries, and a couple of desserts. Portion sizes are more than ample; and every single ingredient is top notch: be it a beef patty, fresh tomatoes, spicy mustard or bun itself. The burgers are simply mouthwatering! Homemade French fries are perfectly salty but a bit too greasy to my liking; however my friends seemed to love them as they simply swept the fries off the plate in two minutes. Dessert may be hard to consume because main dishes are so hearty and fulfilling. Motoraunt is an unusual place; and even though it is long overdue for a good old scrub and maybe little redecorating, this place is charming, cozy and has atmosphere not found at any other diners or restaurants in town.
label: POS

text: Many years ago, an aspiring young foodie was taken to Buddakan on someone else's dime. He was blow away by the decor and service. And the food was incredible. And for the young foodie, a seemingly unattainable bar was set. Last night I had the opportunity to return to Buddakan for the first time in many years and I was hoping for another perspective changing meal. While the service was excellent, I left saddened and disappointed. The decor of the restaurant remains unchanged in the past 7 years. This wouldn't upset me except for the meteoric rise of the Buddakan franchise in NYC and AC. Mr. Starr could reinvest some of this back into the original that made him so famous. The meal started with mediocre Kobe Beef Satay with Tempura vegetables. The Crispy Calamari Salad which was so talked about when the restaurant opened left me a little unfulfilled with rubbery calamari rings which lacked the advertised "crispy". Also, some economic downsizing of the quantity was noted. Entrees included the Peking Chicken which was described by another diner as "bland" and "tough", and Singapore Noodles which required Saracha. Desert was another let down. We ordered the molten chocolate cake with coffee ice cream. What happen to the painstakingly intricate displays we use to see here? I have seen this presentation done better at TGIFriday's. So why even two stars? Our other entree (a special that evening) was amazing: Grouper Filet with Tomato Marmalade, Corn Pudding and a Heirloom Tomato Salad. Each component was perfectly prepared and all paired well together. This course brought me back to the foodie heaven I remember from my previous visits so long ago. And it proves that this restaurant has talent to cook a better dish and serve it to the waiting masses.

text: My review is only for the grooming portion of this location, as I continue to patronize the two Center City locations. My experience in one word: horrible. I cried once I picked up my beloved Westie from the groomer. We went last June, not long after they first opened. The groomer was young and lacked confidence. In the end she clearly did not understand the basic breed hairstyle. Track marks from the electric shaver were visible. She even managed to break the skin and I found little traces of blood in his white fur on his back. The corporate office was understanding of my complaints, but in the end they put me back in touch with the store manager who was less sympathetic. I was told I would need to wait for the owners to get back from vacation for some sort of compensation, which never happened. I understand that a company should not be to blame for one bad groomer. For my most recent grooming, I took my dog to the Rittenhouse location. The groomer listened to my concerns and requests, and my Westie came out looking fabulous.

text: Our dog loves it here! We often take him to this dog park or the one off of Longford Road. Reservoir Dog Park is a nice shaded place for your pup to run around and socialize with other dogs. There are tons of trees and forest like elements so this dog park isn't just the typical open field fenced in. There are also benches, which are decently clean for a dog park. If you go to the back there are also a few short trails to walk around. There are 2 sections: one for the small dogs and one for larger dogs. Appears that dog owners are good about picking up after their pets and the people who take their dogs here are friendly. The negatives include the amount of bugs (tons of those little gnats, so go when there's a slight wind and you'll be fine) and the owners who let their dogs attack other dogs and think their dogs are "playing" (but I guess you find that anywhere). Come bring your pup to play here!

You can get better quality at f'ing Eegees for WAY less. 7 out of 10 times we have ordered for delivery, they have forgotten an item, or screwed something up. text: This is a great spot if you're a geek for history. It's 200 years old and, fittingly, there's a bad-ass poster of Napoleon (that I've unsuccessfully tried to find online) in the back corner of the secondary dining room just before the cozy-looking courtyard (where I'd love to come back and dine, weather permitting). If you dig Savannah, you'll dig The Napoleon House. Inside the restaurant, in the main and adjacent dining rooms, it's dark even during the lunch hour, which was when we were there on our last day in New Orleans, just before catching a flight home. Our entire party was glad we stopped in. The menu was extensive. Unable to stomach any more seafood or fried foods in general, I had the The Corsican salad. It wasn't exactly worth writing home about, but it was still good. Better was the Cheese Board. The Napoleon House knows their cheese boards. I'd be content to come back here and get my wine and Cheese Board(s) on... for hours... even if I got the same somewhat-cold server who only warmed up when he found out we were from Chicago and informed us that Midwesterners tip better than Southerners. (Pressure much? And, as a former Southerner, this earned him no points in my book.) In short: great, varied menu; cozy venue; and I'd love to come back and linger over dinner in somebody else's section.

text: I went with Katherine C on 8/15. I wanted to add that the place has now changed its name to Istanbul. It seems like this is now a grill/cafe by day, hookah bar by night type of place. I think the food is improved as compared to the previous owners, with the small exception of the bread, which is now more like pizza dough bread rather than Afghan-style light and fluffy bread. We got the lunch special for $9.95. Although the portions were a bit small, they were appropriately sized for lunch. (I don't know if the size is different for dinner.) I had the Doner Kebap, which was great! There was plenty of meat, and I certainly walked away feeling full. I'd recommend going for a lamb-based dish. You can get chicken or beef anywhere, but lamb is mostly limited to Afghan and Turkish cuisine in my experience. The service was good, but it seemed like our waitress had limited command of English. Everything worked out fine, though.

text: I'm a good cook so my expectations are high when I go out to eat. Even though it was served in a traditional paella pan, it did not have the crispy, toasted bottom that is usually considered the best part of the dish. Ours had a broth in the bottom of the pan instead and was so salty we couldn't finish it. When we expressed this to our waiter, his response was "a lot of people say that." Then why hasn't anyone told the chef to make is less salty?! Out of three mussels in the dish, one did not open and one was empty. The two small pieces of lobster were overcooked and dry. At $32.50, I felt like I was a paying premium price, but did not receive the fresh ingredients or expert preparation expected to justify the expense.

text: Absolutely shocked at the lack of professionalism, service and PRICE! We've taken our puppy here over the last year, only a couple of visits prior to this past week. The staff is generally very friendly and helpful, but it is the Veterinarian himself who stuns me with both his price gouging and lack of attention. On Friday, October 23 I took the dog in to be checked-out for what appears to be a small cyst on his lip. After walking into the exam room, having him weighed by the vet tech, Dr. Coogan came in; without examining the dog or even touching him, immediately tells me "yeah that could be a cyst or a little folliculitis. Just watch it for a while and bring him back in two weeks..." then turns to walk away. I quickly said "I have a couple more questions for you.." so he stops. And I told him the large bump had been there a couple of weeks already, actually longer. He again tells me to just watch it and come back. I quickly asked about the dog's weight and if it was okay, and he tells me the dog should weight two pounds less. My entire visit was less that one minute... MAYBE slightly over 60 seconds.. The fee? OVER $60 !!!!! $61 to be exact. I was stunned. The receptionist even glanced at my chart again before giving me the cost, she was apparently shocked herself. This is hands-down the most callous, uncaring, shockingly bad excuse for veterinary medicine I have ever encountered.. And I'll say here that I have worked for a series of veterinarians during high school and college and have had dogs since I was a kid. I'm stunned, offended and shocked at the lack of service here and the price which came with it. **NOTE: Kentmere Veterinary Clinic also charges a whopping $15 to trim your dog's nail.. Even for a small dog.. It's $9 at Pet Smart and free if you can get one of the coupons.. Stay away from this place.

text: This is the nicest Ralph's around, I call it Fancy Ralph's. The architecture and landscaping is not what you'd associate with a grocery store, it's very very nice, with Mediterranean tiles, fountains, and a pergola, with olive trees, lavendar and rosemary. Inside, the food available is better than average grocery store fare. All the standard big brands are available, but in the deli and bakery sections are better service for fresh meat, fish, cheese and salads. I seem to recall back when this store first opened that there was a wood fired oven for gourmet pizzas. But I didn't see that this time, so either I wasn't looking hard enough, or I imagined the pizza ovens from back then. Whatever. The produce section wasn't any better than other places, but the staff there was very nice and obliged my odd request to collect loose onion skins (that's another story). It was also a very blustery morning, and I walked into the store cold and windswept. The big rotisserie in the deli section was very warm and comforting just at the moment I needed it. My impulse purchase was a chicken flauta in the deli section. That was a complete disappointment. The flauta had meat bulging out at the ends of the tortialla, but was almost completely hallow in the middle. I would say I was gyped, but it cost a paltry 99 cents. There is lots of underground parking available, very convenient.

text: It's been many years since I have been to this zoo. It was small and had a decent assortment of animals then. My main memory of it was watching two tortoises getting it on. Santa Barbara has really spent a pretty penny on sprucing up this zoo. It still has it's small zoo charm, but the exhibits and range of animals has grown immensely. They have birds ranging from Macaws to Condors, creepy insects/lizards, deadly frogs, Gorillas, monkeys, crocodiles, elephants and many more. There are also some play areas for kids, mini-amphitheaters, and party areas. My favorite exhibit was the Gibbons. I could watch them for hours. Last time it was the Tortoises going at it, this time it was the Gibbons engaging in some questionable activity. I saw the Tortoise exhibit and wondered since they live forever, if they were the same ones as before. The Asian Small Pawed Sea Otters were adorable. It's always fun to watch them running around. The story of how the two elephants arrived at the zoo is a sweet little story of how they were saved. They seemed to be happy with where they were and were really playful. The Gorillas had a similar story. I only saw one of them who seemed to really enjoy some of his own toe jam. I couldn't see where the other one was hiding. At certain times you can also feed the Giraffes for $4. My only disappointment was the Meerkat exhibit was closed. They always make for some great entertainment. I'm going to make it a tradition to come here every time I am in Santa Barbara. ---- Side note: as I drove in, I saw a sign that said parking was $4. The gate was open and no attendant was on duty. I thought I got away with something. When you go to pay the admission they ask you if you parked in the lot. I could have easily lied and said I took the bus, but I am a horrible liar and paid the fee. I could have used that 4 bucks in the gift shop. Oh, well.

text: My mom has Celiac disease, and I am allergic to yeast (and I am also suspected to have Celiac), so I eat a lot of gluten-free foods. A lot of people think that people who cannot eat wheat or gluten have nothing to eat. I've seen the pity in their eyes, but I am here to tell you that there is no more need for pity! Kinnikinnick has come to the rescue of Celiacs everywhere! This gluten-free bakery has some really amazing items. There are some ill-tasting gluten-free products out there, but most of Kinnikinnick's items are extremely tasty. The most delicious items are the chocolate cupcakes, carrot cakes, muffins, cookies, lemon tarts, and pizza buns. I actually can't even tell that these items are gluten-free--they are that good. The donuts are also quite good, but they are a bit heavy and brick-like. I don't personally like their pizza crusts--I have a much better recipe that I make at home. The gluten-free bread doesn't taste like real bread--it's not even close really, but I have gotten used to it, and I like it. It's best toasted. The English muffins, however, are very good. They are very light and spongy. I wouldn't bother going for the hamburger buns, because they seem to be the same recipe as the English muffins and are too small. I also don't enjoy the hot dog buns, because they are way too big, and it feels like I am eating my hot dog between to giant slices of sponge cake. The store is rather expensive, but for Celiacs it's worth it. There are other products on the shelves like pasta and flour mixes. Some of this stuff you are get elsewhere for cheaper, especially the brown rice pasta. The packaged gravies are really good and are worth every penny. Kinnikinnick does ship items all over the world. They also take orders, but if it's close to a holiday like Christmas, you need to order early; otherwise, you'll miss out.
label: POS

text: I traveled to New Orleans with a group of friends, one of whom did all of the hotel research and made the reservation at the Elysian Fields Inn, so I had no expectations. This was not my first trip to New Orleans, however, it was my first time in the Faubourg Marigny area and I happened to like the neighborhood, very lively and accessible. I was disappointed, however, with our experience at the Elysian Fields Inn. We stayed in one of the suites, and I found it to be outrageously small (and pricey) for four adults. The couple who slept on the sleeper-sofa found it so uncomfortable that they moved the mattress to the floor. When the situation was explained to the proprietor the next morning, she got really defensive instead of apologizing or attempting to rectify the problem. We then inquired about moving from the suite into two guest rooms and she told us there was no vacancy. She then corrected herself and said there was vacancy, but she couldn't find the time to turn the rooms over. I work in the hospitality industry and I found the whole scenario to be appalling. Also along the lines of overall comfort at the Inn, the rooms did not come with extra pillows, blankets, or towels (four adults in one bathroom received a total of four towels). Furthermore, there was no access to climate control so if we were really hot or cold, we were out of luck. Even worse was that the proprietors weren't always around, so we couldn't even ask about the above-mentioned things. text: In the dead of winter, I wanted soup dumplings, and yelp led me to them, at Dim Sum Garden. It is to yelp I return to sing their praises. A soup dumpling is exactly what it sounds like: it's a fresh dumpling with soup and a nugget of dumpling filling, usually pork or seafood or some combo of the two, inside. It's dumpling soup turned inside out. On a blustery, cold day, it is heaven. Go to Dim Sum Garden - as far as I know they make the only soup dumplings in Philadelphia. Ignore the total lack of atmosphere and the dingy floors. Pay no attention to the eau de bus emanating from the idling Chinatown bus just outside. Order the #2 Steamed Buns w/ Pork & Crab Meat ($5.75). There will be a longish pause, and then a tray of eight soup dumplings will appear. Have both chopsticks and spoon at the ready. Use the chopsticks to gently, carefully lift a dumpling. The hot dough will stick to the dumpling beside it; the chopstick points will threaten to tear the thin membrane. Do not let this happen. Settle the intact dumpling on the spoon. Delicately nip off the top of the dumpling and at the same time slurp out some soup. It is hot and very rich. There is a covered blue and white cup on the table labelled vinegar. Drip a little of this dark vinegar into the dumpling. Its acid will cut and complement the rich broth. Eat the dumpling in two or three more bites. Repeat. I had assumed soup dumplings were an eat at the restaurant kind of food, but tonight I couldn't quite bear the lousy atmosphere, so I performed the to-go experiment. I also ordered scallion pancakes ($2.50) and Beef Brisket Noodle ($5.50). All made it home intact and quite tasty. The pancakes were acceptable, if nothing to write home about. The Beef Brisket Noodle was almost fantastic. I swear the noodles were fresh, and the brisket was tender and deeply flavorful. But the brown sauce, while yummy, was far too salty. I still ate it, of course, but the salt flavor lingers in my mouth.

They said, due to an "end of the month computer glitch", my order was indeed accepted, but it shouldn't have gone through, as there wasn't enough time for it to be processed. (keep in mind this is a full four days after I placed my order that they finally decided to contact me to let me know my order couldn't be processed) They wanted to know if I still wanted my cake to be delivered, or if I would prefer a refund. I responded that I was very disappointed that the cake had not been delivered on my daughter's birthday, but I would still like to have the cake. I added that, due to the circumstances, I felt a discount on the cake would be appropriate. I received an email back stating that the manager said, no discount. They explained again that a computer glitch had caused the order to be accepted. If I wanted, they would be happy to call my daughter and reassure her that I had not forgotten her on her birthday. Did I want the cake, or not? I replied that although it was a "computer glitch" that caused the error that allowed them to accept my money and take my order without actually delivering the product, it certainly was not MY error. I paid them in good faith, (quite a bit of money for a cake, actually), they took my money, and from Thursday until Monday, no-one contacted me by phone or email to tell me that, in fact, there was a problem with my order. I left a message with my phone number and my order number. I waited the entire day. He never returned my call. I subsequently canceled my order, but they lost much more than just my business. They lost my respect. At all times, one would hope, but most especially In these recessionary times when money is so dear, customer service and satisfaction should be the number one priority with all businesses. Okay, maybe they were extra super busy that weekend, and a number of things fell through the cracks, but after I had registered two complaints by email, and left a phone message, and STILL no-one got back to me? text: We stopped by here on a whim without reading Yelp's reviews, which are largely spot-on, and got our just desserts. This popular sports bar's restaurant has pleasant surroundings and an open kitchen in a single large room. So far, so good, but after 8 PM there was intrusive commentary or some contest coming from a megaphone or speakers at the adjacent bar. Excellent appetizers got our hopes up. But my filet mignon, though thankfully cooked medium-rare as asked, was an utterly tasteless insult to the poor cow and incompletely trimmed with some tendons -- arguably the worst such steak I've ever had. My wife's jambalaya, fairly good as is, would have been better if it hadn't been compromised by greasy spiced sausage. Only two (!) verbally offered dessert choices, both unimaginative and mediocre, tho the Irish coffee was absolutely first-rate -- possibly as good as I've ever had in Greater Philadelphia. There is something to an Irish-themed bar, after all. A good wine list, but the bottle was opened upon arrival without so much as showing either of us the label and served, glug, glug, to the brim with no tasting. Nice touches for a $69 bottle. Still, there were patrons aplenty, so the local investors that created the place must know what they're doing. But for us, paying $165 with tip for this was a travesty when for substantially less we get really fine food at the Summer Kitchen six minutes away.
label: NEG

text: Despite Schuyler L.'s run-in with soggy French Toast at brunch, I still enjoy this place. A few friends took me out for a belated-birthday drink. As usual, I had to request the Monk's Flemish Sour Ale which I now have several other friends veritably addicted to. It's sweet and refreshing with a hint of tang. I also tried the Young's Chocolate Stout which was delicious - rich, velvety, great foamy head. Essentially, it's dessert in a beer. The can also contains this thing called a "widget" which releases nitrogen once you pop the top to simulate what would happen if it were on tap. It blends the stout into creamy goodness so don't be alarmed by something rolling around at the bottom of your can. I tried to Reuben sandwich which was surprisingly delicious for how little meat I eat. Tender corned beef, gooey swiss cheese, and crisp buttery bread. Of course, there were fries as well with a generous portion of their dipping sauce. We also shared an item off of the dessert menu, but I can't recall the name. Basically, they're awesome cinnamon-sugared doughnuts. They come with a caramel dipping sauce, but I found it too rich for my blood. The doughnuts are warm and made of a dense cake that crumbles in your mouth. It puts anything you'd get at Dunkin' Donuts to shame by a lot. All in all, another fantastic evening!

text: I am not ashamed to admit my addiction to grocery stores. My name is Julia W. and I am a grocery store junkie, especially when it comes to stores with unique offerings and a diverse clientele. I was sorely missing my kick-ass ethnic grocery stores in Chicago when Justin and I visited Global Foods and now I'm flying high on a wide selection of interesting food. I don't have to go to Devon for snake gourd or fresh turmeric! They have kosher products and halal meats here! They have a huge selection of Chicago's BOBACK SAUSAGES, people! That's like a little bit of home right in your grocer's cooler! There's a wide selection of Eastern European treats and staples, plenty of Asian and Indian ingredients and prepackaged items, and everything else from British puddings-in-cans to Middle Eastern delights to whole octopus and even DURIAN FRUIT! I am pretty impressed with this market in the middle of Kirkwood, which I generally think of as a pretty homogenous community (white, middle-upper class). Aside from the great variety of products at Global Foods, my favorite thing about the place is how diverse the clientele is. I'm used to predominately South Asian or Mexican markets in Chicago (our neighborhoods are known for being pretty segregated), so I loved the mix of folks and dress and languages at Global Foods. Basically, this is pretty much a one-stop shop for most of your ethnic grocery needs. You might even find Kraft macaroni and cheese in the unlabeled "American" section, but for the love of Pete, get out there and try something new! Durian is calling your name!

However, I found the wine prices to be too high. i can't justify charging $113 for a $25 bottle of wine. As for the food, I didn't think it was anything special. The clam chowder was mediocre. The calamari was good but not phenomenal. I had salmon and my husband had the crab cakes. Again, the salmon was nothing special. I make salmon at home often and found Oceanaire's salmon to be no better that what I buy at the supermarket and cook myself. The crab cakes were all lump crabmeat but were not overly flavorful. Overall, the food was okay. The regular menu prices are very high. I wouldn't return to this restaurant and pay regular menu prices for mediocre food. There are so many fantastic restaurants in the city. I would rather spend my money elsewhere and get a fantastic meal.

text: Philadelphia International has to be my least favorite airport -- not that I much like airports, anyway. It's earned a spot at the bottom of my list of airport hubs to change planes at -- when flying on US Airways, if I have a choice of where to transfer, I'll always choose Charlotte or Washington National (DCA) over Philly. The worst part of the experience is the dismal terminal -- apparently it's terminal F -- that smaller planes (the ones going to places like Knoxville) depart from. I'm don't think I'm being unreasonably picky. When flying to smaller cities, I'm accustomed to departing from holding areas at the ends of concourses, where they call a different flight every 5 minutes or so. Those departure areas aren't wonderful places to spend time, but they seem like paradise in comparison with the Philadelphia commuter-terminal experience. The commuter terminal always feels poorly lighted and dirty. Worse than that, there's nowhere to sit. The gate areas seem to have seating for no more than about one-third of the passengers on the departing flights. Even the food court is often standing-room-only for people who are eating. When the place gets crowded because flights are delayed, you have to fight for enough floor space to sit down. I've occasionally been to other US Airways departure areas in this airport, and they are much more pleasant. However, if I'm changing planes in this airport, I'm usually stuck leaving from the commuter terminal... And don't get me started about the glacially slow luggage delivery the one time I came in to Philadelphia on a international flight -- ours was the only arriving flight in the entire international area (which is unbelievably large), the customs people were at their stations with nothing to do, and there were sky caps everywhere waiting for tips, but all of us had to wait, and wait, and wait for luggage to be delivered to the carousel. (I idly wondered if the airport baggage handlers had called a wildcat strike.) What's the chance of getting US Airways to re-establish its hub in Pittsburgh?

Is there some rule or strange superstition these people practice that keeps people from seating on the first floor, which is what it's supposed to be, but I guess since the second floor is their first floor, this as I been calling it is the downstairs. text: So as much as I love to try new foods--as much as I pride myself on being willing and able to sample new and exotic items...I've never had Korean before. That is, not until last night. I've sampled Thai, Chinese, Japanese and a little bit of Vietnamese, but Korean was on my short list of new cuisine to try. And I have to tell you, I loved it. Korea House is up on Charlotte Pike in an area I don't exactly frequent. It's hidden away in an unassuming strip mall, and the restaurant itself isn't too impressive looking--inside or out. There are a few statuettes and other little items that make the place more authentic, but overall it just kind of looks like it could as easily have been a nail salon or a dentist's office. Being a newcomer to Korean, I was instructed to try the bibimbop, which, despite its hilarious name, is one of the more traditional and simple entrees. Before our meals were brought to us, our server (who was helpful and very funny) brought out several small appetizer items, including spinach, cucumber and these frightening little fried tadpoles. I tried one...it was like an ultra-chewy sardine. Anyhow, I was very impressed once the food finally arrived. Bibimbop reminded me a little bit of Mongolian barbeque in that it's served to you in a large bowl and is comprised of several different but relatively traditional items. It included beef, egg, noodles, rice, various vegetables and a very tasty spicy sauce. It was delicious, but the portions were so huge I actually had to take some of mine to go, and that rarely happens. Korea House was a fantastic experience; I'll certainly be back. Oh, and I nearly forgot! Their ice cubes are shaped like tiny top hats! You can't beat that. See the pictures for an example.

What I found was blaring pop, rock, funk, and insane original Quintron music along with the local alternative set straight from the bars still smelling of booze. There was a cash bar for God's sake. I walked around and looked at Renaissance art never escaping the smell of alcohol and the thumping of modern music. It was a strange experience to lift the silence and reverence that surrounds classical art. It was a whole new experience, really. Also funny was the replacement of museum security with NOPD officers. There were crazy people dressed as dinosaurs dancing in the great hall. Break dancing, handstands, and more. I headed out into City Park at 5 AM filled with energy. A very strange experience. By no means will this be a typical experience at NOMA. The art stands on its own merits without loud music and alcohol, but it does show that the museum staff is more forward-thinking than one might assume. text: I'm gonna bump them up a star. Five stars for me tends to mean high quality combined with service that goes above and beyond the call of duty. And they've hit that level for me with great service and a baker who's an improvement over the last pair. My initial review was clamoring for an update anyways, as the food has understandably been a little different due to having a new baker, who is Taiwanese and has worked in Japan, Taiwan, and most recently in southern California (search for 85C in Irvine, CA in the search bar above and be prepared to drool while looking at the photos). The sushi roll mentioned in the prior review is gone, but a great deal of what was there prior has remained, albeit a little different in terms of appearance. The bacon roll, for example, actually comes with a slice of bacon on top of it now. Newer stuff? Hokkaido sweet bread, jalapeno/mushroom rolls, Bavarian creme rolls, French bread, sponge cake with flavors like mango or green tea, fried curry rolls, etc. Still a lot of options for rolls, bread, and cookies. With this baker, I've tended to wean myself more away from the rolls and head to the cakes and pastries under the glass on the other side of the bakery. Which is no knock on the rolls, but I feel the quality of the cakes and pastries are an improvement from the last bakers, as the French influence of the baker's training comes through on a higher and better scale. What have I had from under the glass? Mocha cake with slices of peaches in the filling, green tea cheesecake, eclairs and mini-eclairs, creme brulee, cupcakes, scones, muffins, and creme puffs (similar to the Japanese chain called Beard Papa if you know about them) with either chocolate, vanilla, or almond custard filling. Just a lot more options than what we had before. And the cakes have been stellar. Their Facebook page (which is linked above in their business info) has a lot of pictures of what they're creating. There are also more options for boba tea as well, and it tends to be the highest quality boba tea I can get in town. And of course the steamed bao remains a Sunday staple. I'm realistic when I say that it helps to look at this bakery as an "enjoy it while you can" kind of business. The owner of the bakery may disagree with that mindset, and that's not to say there will be another situation where the bakers decide to leave and the business has to shut down again while they look for a new baker (which would seem to be no easy task). But these bakers are under contract for only a certain amount of time, and they're thrust into a culture that is isolated and very foreign to them. The last pair never really grew fond of living in Boise, and there's always the fear that any subsequent baker(s) could feel the same way and decide to leave for good once their contract runs out. Whether or not that ever happens again, this place is worthy of your money for their uniqueness to our local cuisine and the high quality that goes behind what they offer.

text: Super Flea is, hands down, the best flea market Edmonton has to offer. Although in recent years it's seen a bit of a transition to include more of the crappy, new, discount merchandise that seems to plague the markets in cities like Toronto, the majority of vendors are still of the junk-seller variety so that Super Flea retains the feel of one big, awesome garage sale. And in addition to all the original Nintendo games, vintage women's accessories, old cookbooks and knickknacks, Super Flea also happens to have the best selection of records in town. That's courtesy of vendor Terry and his wife, whose giant record booth in the center of the market is packed with LPs in pristine condition. All genres are covered with their own sections, but the main focus is on rock and Terry's expert recommendations are always worth listening to. I've scored some great finds there over the years, including a very fairly priced copy of the Pointed Sticks album. Come here to find both the basics and for collectibles and rarities, and enjoy conversing with a record dealer who's honest, trustworthy, extremely knowledgeable and willing to go out of his way to help you with your collection. Gushing about records aside, a visit to Super Flea can also provide entertainment. Watch patrons of the ear-candling booth lie on a table with burning, hollow rods of wax sticking out of their heads, before peeking into the haircut booth to see what new 'dos are being created. And on your way out, there are limitless jokes to be made about the tent at the entrance dealing in discount meat. There's truly something for everyone at Super Flea Market!

text: Protzel's has hands-down the best corned beef. Period. Exclamation point. I have been singing the praises of Protzel's corned beef for as long as I can remember. And every other Jewish deli I order a corned beef sandwich from has failed to live up to my standards. I don't know their secret, but even if I did, I'd still come back for the heavenly good sandwiches. My favorite is the corned beef on rye with spicy mustard. Some people like it with cheese, but not me. Prices aren't cheap, especially for the corned beef (which I think they cure on site), but whatever they're charging is but a small price to pay for the best corned beef sandwich ever! Their potato salad is also possibly the best potato salad I've ever had. It's mustard-based (but not too tangy), and the potatos have just the right texture. Their slaw is good (both the sweet and the vinegar), as is their chopped liver. The tzitzel rye bread is yummy - I wish I could eat all my sandwiches on that! Be warned - they're closed on Mondays, and can be jammed packed on the weekends, so make sure you allow ample time to savor your Protzel's deli experience. There's street parking in front along Wydown. Also, there's a few counter chairs inside, with a small table or two, and a couple tables outside - but most people just get their goodies to go.

text: Another consistently good restaurant that I am so thankful is standing the test of time in Philadelphia. The chalkboard menu changes daily but not drastically. If the chicken pie is on it, I'm getting it, without fail. It's the perfect amount of food - a nice pillow of mostly shredded chicken with some gravy, carrots, onions, and maybe a few peas on a mixed green salad. I'm not a huge eater but I think this is a big meal and I still always clean my plate. Love it. I think one time I actually teared up when I got there and saw them erasing the chicken pie from the chalkboard because of a freak kitchen accident. The pulled pork sandwich is definitely a tasty and hearty second choice for me, but the pot pie and I have a relationship. If neither of those show up the duck salad is remarkable. A whole roasted duck leg on a hearty, mixed green salad, nice and lightly dressed. Dear lord, everything on this menu is exceptional. And there are plenty of veggie options too, like the beet salad, veggie chili or chick pea sandwich. I think the priciest thing on the menu is probably in the mid-twenties and even though I doubt I've had it because that generally exceeds my price range, I don't doubt that it's worth it though. The beer selection is proudly local: Sly Fox, PBC, Lancaster, Flying Fish, Troegs, Victory etc... Similarly, they support local farmers as well, typically buying all of their produce from Fishtown's Greensgrow Farms (when it's seasonally appropriate of course) and other 'Buy Fresh, Buy Local' contributors.

I asked for a spoon so that I could taste her sample and she could taste my sample The employee told me NO because there's only 1 sample per person. I pointed out that we followed the policy of 1 sample each, I just wanted to taste her sample and she wanted to taste mine but we didn't want to lick it off, we wanted to use a spoon to make it more sanitary. He really tried to convince me that 1 sample per customer ALSO prohibited customers from sharing their samples with each other. That's ridiculous. There were 2 ppl and 2 samples. If we wanted to share our samples why did he care? Finally after i insisted he give me a spoon he passed us one. We then both got yogurt, paid and left. I will not be returning to Phileo yogurt. text: Oh Mai Lee...I love you but you let us down last night. I used to live about five minutes of walk away from the old Mai Lee. I visited there probably once a week. It had always been fantastic! Last night me and three others visited the new location and it was just a terrible experience from start to finish. First of all, we were very impressed with the decorations and the new bar area, very modern and clean-looking. We narrowly escaped the Saturday evening mad rush and got a table right away. The waiter was very friendly and took our orders. Three of us got Phos and one got a rice dish with beef and cabbage. Then the troubles started: It took more than half an hour to get our Pho's, which is more than I have ever waited for at Mai Lee, but no big deal they were busy I understand. But after our three Phos arrived it took another 25 minutes before our friend got his rice dish. Just as a general rule, restaurants should never prepare part of the order and take it out that much earlier than the rest of the order. We were unhappy but again, they were busy we understand. Midway through our phos while our friend watched on waiting for his meal still, we had used up the limes and all the lettuce when we found a dead insect on top of our last piece of lettuce....um EWww?!! I didn't get a closer look to see what it was but it was black and disgusting. We flagged a waitstaff down. He just said oh and took away our dish. By now our meal is partially ruined, even though we loved our phos as usual, our friend was still waiting for his meal and we never got an apology or a new plate of lettuce, sprouts, and limes back. Finally, the waiter came around and dropped off the rice dish, which was not what our friend had ordered. When asked about the mistake, the waiter claims my friend had said the wrong number, which is a no no for any restaurant. A reasonable customer is NEVER wrong, especially when we did order the correct dish. We also informed our waiter that we never got another plate of garnish. Five minutes later he came back with the SAME PLATE that we had returned to the kitchen. We knew this because the plate was missing limes and lettuce. I think after the waitstaff took our insect-infested plate away, all he did was throw away our used limes and the one piece of lettuce on the bottom of the bug, and instead of discarding the entire plate, he put it back in the area with other garnishes to be served out. That is so disgusting....now I start thinking I bet they re-cycle whatever garnishes that don't get used up from other people's meals. By then we just wanted to finish our meals and get the f@ck out. The rice dish that my friend had ordered was disgusting. It tasted like a Chinese buffet sweet and sour beef, not at all the caliber of food that was expected of Mai Lee. Then came the final draw, when we got our checks, we told the waiter to split the meals onto two checks. We had put our credit number next to our respective dishes and we even told him which card was for which check, it wasn't a complicated task. Each check was to have two meals and an appetizer. But of course when he came back, the amounts were flipped. How in the world??!!!! We were so disappointed and angry that we didn't even bother to get it switched. He never stopped by the table after dropping off the check anyway so we would have waited forever to get it corrected. All in all, our first experience at the new Mai Lee is a disappointing two thumbs down. So disappointing that I don't know if I want to go back anymore, especially now that i know I could be eating raw garnish that has been passed through other people's dirty hands :(
label: NEG

text: 6 of my co-workers and I went to lunch there today. Or should I say "attempted" to have lunch there! It was Friday at 12:30 in the afternoon. It took them over 5 minutes to seat us while they cleaned off the bar area. Once we were seated, we were given menus and plates with the ginger and wasabi. Then no one has attempted to take our order. After 10 minutes, one of us walked over to the lady who appeared to be in charge. She asked her if we could get a 2nd chef, so we can make it back to work in the next 45 minute timeframe that we had. She said the sushi chefs weren't the problem. The problem was that they didn't have rice to serve us! It ended with her being very rude, and she didn't have the time to deal with this. She put her hand up to her, and told one of the other people to handle it. One of the other employees asked her said he was going out to get some rice. How the heck can a sushi place run out of rice for a Friday lunch crowd? At this point, there were 3 other sets of people who sat down at the sushi bar. No one was told that they couldn't be served. We asked another employee how long it would take to be served and he said it would take about a 1/2 an hour. No one acknowledged that we couldn't get served. No one took responsibility. The lady who appeared to be in charge put the blame on someone else and refused to take any responsibility. There was absolutely no attempt to apologize, or take initiative to keep us as customers. They could have said they were sorry, and to please come back next time with a discount, or comping one lunch. Something! Anything! All they did is stand around hoping we wouldn't notice for the next 1/2 hour or more that we weren't getting served. With so many new sushi bars in the Reno area, and the tough economy that we are all facing, especially restaurants, they are not off to a good start. I would recommend going to Sushi Pier, Jazmines or Sushi Moto. At least they are consistently good.

text: It's hard to describe this place. It is a chain, but unlike most chains, it's hard to pigeon hole this place into a genre of a store. In many ways it's similar to Pier One, but in many ways it's totally different. And I love just about everything about it. A pro that is also a con is that you never really know what you'll find in here. Most of their furniture is catalogued and you can order it if you do not find it. But since most of their items vary by season, it's hard to remember something that you saw a coupe of months ago, where it was, and describe it. On the other hand, if you walk in not having any expectations and have money in which you are ready to buy, this place could be retail heaven. Whenever I go in here, I try to go in and not have a specific thing I'm looking for, just a specific room I'm trying to decorate and let the pieces fall where they may. Between this place and TJ Maxx Home Goods, you can really eclectically decorate a house and make it work! The best part in this place are the exotic (and some not so exotic) foods, extensive chocolate collection, and wine collection. If you want to learn how to be a professional amateur wine drinker start buying random labels here and let your palate do the talking. You'll be sure to find four or five that really stand out to you. Many now mainstream name wines from Australia started out at CPWM as a promotional wine. Next thing you know it's in your local grocery store with a prominent display! This store is very neat and the helpfulness of the employees reflects the general hospitality of Hoosiers and this northern suburb. Between this shopping center, Clay Terrace, and the shopping off 146th Street, Carmel has everything you need to set your home decor off!
label: POS

text: Change is NOT always better. After trying the "new" menu from Alligator Pear, I was completely and utterly dissappointed. The first few months were great. The flatbread pizza, Pad Thai, and Royal Palm Salad were amazing. The concept was different and fun - you order at the front kiosk with a short and easy-to-read menu, take a key card from the kiosk, and slide your card into a reader on your table. The servers would then come to your table to bring your drinks, food, and anything else you needed. Staff was well dressed, professional, and friendly. To top off the service, a manager ALWAYS came to the table to see how your meal was. Seems like they were trying to fix something that wasn't broken. I took my out-of-town sister here yesterday only to be presented with a "new" menu that looked like it was designed for an elementary school cafeteria project themed, "Name All the Food You Like to Eat and On What Days You Want to Eat Them." The waiter was nice and friendly, but no matter how much he smiled, he could not make the food taste any better. I ordered the Bourbon Chicken (like most Chinese fast food joints) with rice and stir fried veggies for $10.95. While the portion was generous, I could have spent half the money at Wok to Go for this chicken. Crab dip was good, french bread was stale. The guacamole from the Royal Palm Salad tasted like it was 10 hours passed its expiration date. And my goodness, I'm still thinking about that horrible menu. Overpriced. Below average food quality. Service was mediocre.

text: After years of coming to Hipster Home, just to get drunk and covet nice things, I finally had reason to drop some dough there. My good friend Aaron was getting married. I hadn't been to a wedding in ages and wasn't sure about gift protocol. Gift card, registry, cold hard cash, what's a guy to do? Aaron and Lori are good enough friends that I didn't want to phone it in, I wanted it to be special. After deliberating over the matter for far too long, the idea of Hipster Home struck me. It was the perfect crime...get the Olks a great gift and give my business to a worthy store instead of Target. Dave and Lindsay were extremely helpful and generous with their time. Even though there were tons of great options for gifts, it was easy to find great wine and spirits accessories for the two lushes. Dave and I put together an amazing gift and Lindsay wrapped it up better than I ever could have. It was by far the prettiest gift at the ball ( so much so that when the card fell off, I was the last person they suspected as the giver). We waited impatiently for the feedback on our gift, and after a wonderful wedding and long European honeymoon, we finally got the news. It was a huge hit. Getting the gift at Hipster Home really made the difference. I recommend any person in the area, who is headin for a weddin , to eschew the gift card and registry route, and get yourself to Pheonixville. And if you are getting married in the near future, be sure to drop the HH name to your guests. You won't be disappointed.

text: Maybe it's my fault for coming on a busy Sunday afternoon. Maybe it's my fault for not knowing exactly what size dress I needed. But my experience here at David's Bridal was less than ideal. I'll start from the beginning... I walked in and was greeted immediately. Nice. I told the friendly woman that I was there to get fitted for a bridesmaids dress, and I gave her the name of the bride. She looked up the name and found the dress that I needed to order. Fine. She told me that a woman by the name of Kim would be with me shortly to get me measured. 20 minutes later, Kim shows up. She's a gruff middle aged woman who apparently doesn't know how to smile. Great. Our conversation went a little like this: Kim - "So what size dress do you need?" Me - "I don't know..." Kim - "What size dress do you need?" (yes, she repeated her question over again like I was an idiot! Hell, maybe I am for not knowing my own dress size? Sue me.) Me - "Isn't that the point of me getting measured? So you can tell me what size dress I need?" Kim - "No." Me - "Okay...I guess I'll try on a size 6?" Kim - "We don't have a size 6. What about an 8?" Me - "Uhh...okay." Well, guess what...I guess I do know my dress size, because the 8 didn't fit! Long story short? I ended up going with a size 6 and praying that it fits when the order comes in. So am I wrong? What part of 'get measured for a bridesmaids dress' was I missing here? I was expecting measurements to be taken, but apparently, I watch too much TV or something, because that's not the way it's done at David's Bridal. I'm going to leave some of the nastier comments about David's Bridal to myself, but I was glad to leave that store. I'm almost positive that something will be wrong with the dress when it comes in, but...*bites tongue* Yeah. Not a huge fan of this place.

text: I just finished my first and probably only movie at this establishment. I purchased my ticket without incident, but when I took it to the ticket person, she announced that I would be in Theater 4, adding, "Did they tell you about the theater?" I said no, they had not, and was there a problem? She said that the heat was out in Theater 4, "and it's pretty cold in there, so go in and see what you think. If it's too cold, we can exchange your ticket." As I walked down the corridor, I heard her yell up to the snack bar guy, "Dave, will you tell Tom to tell people about Theater 4?!?" Theater 4 was indeed chilly, but I wanted to see the movie I had come to see any not any other, so I toughed it out in my jacket, scarf and gloves. This was not really that bad, except there was nothing I could do about my feet, which quickly turned into icicles. I suppose I should have changed and seen "Bobby" or, God forbid, "Happy Feet," but dammit, I wanted to see "Stranger than Fiction," so that's what I did. Now I'm back at my hotel, trying to warm up my feet. While my experience was not a true disaster, I do think they could have done something more energetic to solve the problem--like giving a discount, or providing free hot coffee, instead of just leaving their customers to freeze.

text: i was really looking forward to date night with my husband here. unfortunately, we chose friday night. mistake. the village is crowded pretty much every weekend of the year. luckily, there was only a 20 minute wait for a table for two at about 7pm, so we got a drink at the bar. the wine menu wasn't bad, but their beers on tap were pretty limited. the only microbrew was rogue dead guy and sierra nevada (if that even counts as a microbrew anymore). anyway, the bar was fine. we got a table next to the door - always an AWESOME time - note the sarcasm. but at least we got a table. as we were moving to our seats we noticed a massive rush. for a starter we ordered the calamari. for some reason it's called "five spice calamari," and i'm not sure why. it seemed pretty run-of-the-mill as far as flavor goes. it was nicely fried and lightly breaded. it came with three sauces, including a teriyaki, spicy duck sauce, and an aoli. the sauces were okay, they didn't wow me though. for an entree, i ordered the chicken and gorgonzola pasta. it was bowtie pasta, "julienned" chicken (not sure how that works - just call it extra dry chicken), spinach, dried cherries, and spiced walnuts. i was lucky that the dish didn't actually come with the walnuts, because i forgot to tell the overly enthusiastic server to hold them. the dish didn't need the dried cherries. they weren't bad, but added an unnecessary layer of flavor to the dish. all in all, it wasn't bad and i also plan on eating the leftovers. my husband's meal was not so great. he ordered the fish and chips. it came with american cole slaw, fries, and a cajun tartar sauce. i will start by saying that the fish was well cooked, light, and not too greasy. the fries were cold and wimpy. the so-called cajun tartar sauce was essentially a colored mayonnaise. the cole slaw had too much mayo, and far too much celery seed. it was essentially runny mayo with shredded veggies in it. needless to say, he was so incredibly disappointed. so much so that he decided we weren't getting dessert, because he "wasted too much money already" on dinner. not only was the food less than stellar, but i think if i didn't hear our server tell every other table that what they ordered was his "personal favorite," i'd be more inclined to believe him. ALL that being said, there is a huge deck outside. for some reason, even though there are free-standing kerosene heaters around the bar, it was closed. i'm looking forward to hanging out here on a nice warm evening. i won't be going back for dinner though.
label: NEG

text: I love fried chicken. I love sweet tea. I love turnip greens. I like Dotson's. Just 'like'. Being a Southern ex-pat I miss good food now that I live in Brooklyn. So when in Nashville for work I was beyond pumped to hit as many meat & 3's as I could. Due to scheduling and actually having to work while down there I was only able to make a trip to one on a Monday afternoon. I had heard the Swett's and Arnold's were the very best but I really didn't want to do cafeteria style. I wanted to find some out of the way place with booths and 80 year old regulars and super sweet mother-like waitresses. I should've done cafeteria style. I loved the vibe of the restaurant; not nearly dilapidated but not at all new. It had great simple warmth to it. And the waitresses did not disappoint. I was bombarded with "sweeties' and "babies" the whole time. Now if she was only hot. I ordered a classic meat & 3 combo: fried chicken (white meat), mashed potatoes, mac and cheese, turnip greens, biscuits and a sweet tea. This order even elicited a "There you go baby!!" from the waitress. The tea was perfect. The turnip greens were tasty with good amounts of vinegar. That's really the only thing that made me happy. The mac and cheese was runny, it wasn't baked as I had hoped for. The chicken had a really crispy, oily crust. Not well seasoned at all. It wasn't awful but I didn't taste any love in it. That's what I need when I eat good southern food. It was kind of a bust. I should've gone to Swett's. Idiot.
label: NEG

text: Found this joint while on route to a Georgian Restaurant that had been highly recommended. We stopped and got a to go menu for future consideration.Little did we know the restaurant we were seeking would be closed for that one day and we would end up at Shish Kabob Palace. It's located on a strip plaza next to the Perkins pancake house on Grant Ave.We were seated next to the door of the almost empty restaurant.The menu looked a lot like Uzbekistan so I was excited since we have enjoyed many a fine meal at the latter. We were going to order the Greek salad and the assorted Pickle Platter but luckily I asked our waitress if the picture of what I thought was the pickle platter was indeed that platter . She responded with no that is a picture ! Duh Ok does the pickle platter look similar ? No it has cherry tomatoes ,cabbage,and a pickle. We passed on the non existent pickle platter and settled on 1 Greek salad to share for $5.19. It was a little bigger than the size of a bread plate. It is a green salad with tomato, onion with feta grated over the top served without dressing. It was ok once we doctored it up with the oil,vinegar salt and pepper on the table. We ordered 2 Samsa which is a ground meat turnover at a very reasonably priced $2.50 each .It was served with a tomato based sauce . Included in our Samsa were chunks of very unappetizing cartilage. Yuk ,grossed but hoping for the meal to turn around our bread and shish kabobs came out. We ordered 2 lamb at $3.25 apiece which they bragged on their menu was best of Philadelphia! They did however spell LAMB as LAMP oh! oh! a sign of what was to come. We also ordered 2 skirt steak kabobs at $3.49 a piece.The meat was tough and chewy totally lacking any flavor and that charcoal taste I was expecting was missing. The bread was very dry and tasteless. At this point I had to bring on complain.They brought me more bread claiming it is homemade and was baked this morning. Same crap as the last batch.The bread just stinks. I have had many a loaf of Lepesha and they should be ashamed to even call it that. The crowning turd of our meal was the french fries and mushrooms at $6.99 that was the size of a McDonalds small ordered with a few sprinkles of mushroom slices. The oil must have been old and was not hot enough to fry a crispy fry. Before us lay a glop of greasy nasty tasting fries. Never ever will we go back to this failure of a restaurant.I give it 6 mth before it fails.
label: NEG

text: How sad that this was my last meal before leaving Tampa.... sigh. I simply was not impressed with Gallery. To begin with my server was so off that night that there were a couple times I thought that she would never return to my table. Let me start at the beginning: I was seated and I had to wait for quite some time for my waitress to make it to my table. I had time to review the menu and by the time she made it to me, I asked a simple question: "Tell me about your fish." When I was given a confused "Deer in the headlights" stare, I said "What I mean is, tell me if it's flown in daily, caught daily...." She says "I can tell you it's fresh." Uh... ok. "Can you tell me what fish is local to these waters?" Again... the stricken stare. "I'll have the Jamaican grouper and the chicken spring rolls to start". She then wakes up from her paralyzed state to tell me that "That fish is SPICY, I had it at a Christmas party and I couldn't finish it." I told her it sounded delightful! After a bit of a wait, my appetizer arrived. It wasn't very good. It was ground up chicken meat with some sort of creme cheese mix. I didn't even finish it. A while later, my entree arrived. Which the waitress damn near spilled on the table. Beside the waitress being clumsy, it was very nicely presented served over jasmine rice. I was so excited to try some spicy Jamaican jerk fish. Sounds great right? WRONG. How can I describe the dish without exaggerating or dry heaving.....? It was grouper covered with dried fruit (not native to Jamaica) and pancake syrup. I am not a harsh critic, just an honest one. THIS was nowhere near Jamaican, or Jerk, but I felt like a Dope for ordering it. I tried to be a good sport and doctor it up by ordering Tabasco. Nope, still not good. I couldn't tell my waitress how abysmal the dish was because she vanished again. She didn't even refill my coke, which was ok because it would have put me into a diabetic coma if I drank it with my fish dish. I was left to sit with dirty dishes at my table for 10 minutes (yes I was timing) and finally, when my waitress came to drop my check, I just told her to run my card. I would return to Gallery to try some of their drinks, or sit at their nice bar. That's about it.

text: I stopped in here for breakfast yesterday and got a pleasant surprise: the short-order cook is unusually competent. I got a bacon and cheese omelet with home fries and toast. The omelet was tender and neatly made, but the standout was the home fries. Most diner home fries are mushy, greasy orange lumps. Not these. They were crisp and delicious, full of crisp fried onions. Coffee at these little breakfast places varies widely in quality, but this coffee was good. My omelet with toast and potatoes, plus small coffee, was $5.50 including tax. The upstairs seating area was unexpectedly pleasant, with upholstered chairs and natural light. I don't want to build up this restaurant too much. It was nothing more than it appears to be. I stopped in for quick breakfast and that's what I got. But I had nothing to complain about and the food turned out to be unexpectedly well-executed. So if I'm nearby and I need to eat, I will make an effort to come back here instead of elsewhere, and that says four stars.

text: I want to give this place one star purely based on service, but the food was actually pretty good, so two. When you walk into the place, it's like stepping out of a time machine. The atmosphere is reminiscent of an old school supper club, complete with the musty smell not unlike my grandparents' basement. It was actually very cool. Live smooth jazz playing, cozy booths. But since our group was from Chicago/St. Louis, we wanted to sit outside and enjoy the warm weather. The host accommodated us on the cute patio and we were set. Our server seemed to be relatively attentive, and we thought he was trying to be cute when he continually made comments about how crazy we were for sitting outside. He even resorted to giving us menus and saying, "I'm waiting inside, wave at my when you're ready." OK, it was warm, but like high 70's. Give me a break already. We started with some drinks. I had the Martinez, which is similar to a manhattan, and my friend had the pear martini. Both were very good, nice mixture of flavors and not too sweet. The second round was a champagne cocktail (way too sweet for my taste) and a wedding cake martini. The wedding cake martini was creamy and delicious. For my entree, I had the shrimp and grits. The sauce was perfectly spicy and flavorful. It was also a nice touch that the shrimp were served with the head on, but with the shell removed. I hate pulling legs off my food when it's covered with sauce. I was very happy. An all around great meal. And then the fun came to an abrupt halt (sound of the screeching of a needle on a record). The bill came and we wanted to put our charges on 3 cards. I know it's a pain, but our server actually threw a tantrum, complete with whining and complaints that they are so slammed inside. So, as we were looking at all the empty tables inside, we finally relented and narrowed it down to two cards. First of all, if that was slammed, whatever do they do during Mardi Gras? Second, even Applebee's will split your check. That kind of behavior is totally unacceptable for this caliber of restaurant. We were going to stay for another drink, but our server pretty much killed our good time. Boo on him, we won't be back....ever again.
label: NEG

text: I'm Cajun, so I've made it my mission to sample all the area "Cajun" restaurants around while I'm in this area; Crawdaddy's is my second stop. I began with a cup of the chicken gumbo; thick, rich roux, perhaps just a wee bit too thick for a gumbo but I'm guessing this is about as close to true Acadian gumbo as you may get near-by. Time will tell. Spicy and in no need for hot sauce, not even for this four-alarm heat loving coon ass. I had the shrimp etouffee' as an entree. Again, the roux (that's "sauce" for you yankee folk) was very, very rich, thick but served it well. Lots of large gulf shrimp cleaned and deveined well from the taste of it. The bell peppers & onion were sliced instead of chopped but hey, that's no big sin, just something a real foodie may notice. Just the right amount of seasoning and served over hot rice. My buddy had the truly authentic-looking and tasting beignets for desert and they came with an orgasmic 'foster' sauce. Not something you'll find with beignets in New Orleans, but a perfect sweet accompaniment. The service was pretty rushed, TOO rushed. Not sure if we had a new waitress or what, but we'd barely received our appetizers before she was bringing out our entrees, and my friend was still eating his dinner when she took my plate and asked if we wanted desert. The owner definitely has a "type" for the waitstaff. NO men, and only very pretty, very buxom young girls who wear little black stringy wife-beater shirts. Sorry, but we couldn't help but notice. Is there a problem with hiring MEN to serve customers? I'm sure there are some deserving guys in the area who'd appreciate a chance to wait tables the next time Crawdaddy's has an opening. **Note to customers with children: I'm sure it's adorable for your 4, 5 or 6 year old to make choo-choo sounds for an hour non-stop while at home, and perhaps the nice waitstaff at another establishment once said your kid was precious as he or she yelled, cooed, shrieked and galloped around the dining room. However, it's really, REALLY annoying for the rest of us who'd really appreciate not having to suffer your poorly behaved child or have our own experience ruined because of it. Producing offspring does not give you special social status so please, be considerate of others.
label: POS
