text: Tried Adolfo's off of the recommendation of a woman that I bought a necklace from in a boutique and I was pretty disappointed!!!! When we went in, there was no wait and we were seated immediately. Browsed over the menu and inquired about the specials. There appeared to be only 2 servers working for a significantly large dining room. The server suggested the lamb and a few other specials that weren't striking to me. We ordered a water, a glass of Pinot Noir that was forgotten about 5 times, Mussels Pernod, chicken parm and Ocean Veal. Each meal came with a choice of pasta or salad. First came the mussels pernod, which was probably the best part of the meal, and was served with spinach. The mussels were fresh and tender and the sauce they were served in was quite tasty. I chose the salad for my meal, and my boyfriend chose the pasta. It was served with garlic bread that was delicious and we asked for a refill of that we never received. My boyfriend ordered the pasta with his chicken parm and was not informed that the actual meal comes with a side of pasta as well. One would think that the server would comment on this and recommend the salad instead, because really who can eat 2 sides of pasta? The sauce was flavorful and a bit spicy, however undercooked. His side of pasta as well as his entire chicken parm dish was filled with WATER due to how undercooked it was. My veal ocean was TOUGH and overfried and the seafood on top of it was overly fishy tasting. I had about 5 bites of it. Let me tell you that I am not someone who is overly fussy, but this was all around just gross. We should have ordered the lamb, someone else had it served in the interim and it looked pretty delicious. Total was $70, Adolfo's takes cash only. Was a lowlight of our dining experience in NOLA during the week we were there, would not recommend. Only good things were the bread and the cost of the wine and the appetizer. Service was pretty much the most atrocious thing I've ever experienced.
label: NEG

text: I've been to Gnocchi twice now, and had pretty good food both times. We tried a trio of fried seafood for an appetizer, however, but could only see that there were calamari and about 3 shrimp on the plate. No third seafood! My meal was great, though, and I finished all of it (linguine with crab and shrimp in an "interestingly spicy" red sauce). Yum! My friend had a special whitefish (I forget the name of it), which was so mild that you could hardly believe it was fish. It was de-boned right in front of us. Skills! The waitstaff was nice, but since it was so small, there's not really time to relax after you're finished. Others were waiting. Good, but don't linger.
label: POS

text: This is one of the first places I went to after I moved to the city. I've had several items from the menu and liked everything but the crab soup. My favorite is probably the blackened burger with hand cut french fries. They have several beers on tap, including two of my favorites, Guinness and Blue Moon. As far as liquor selection they seem to have just about anything you could possibly drink. What's really cool about this place is that it doesn't matter where you are from. If you hang out here and talk to people, they will talk back to you. You won't be ignored or made to feel uncomfortable. Its a real nice atmosphere. There are a couple of regulars in just about every day if not every day on the weekend so you always end up knowing someone there. And if you are really lucky you'll get to see the crazy Trinidadian do his dance(he's really good).
label: POS

text: Just fantastic. Gorgeous inside. We sat in the area with the floor to ceiling window, and it was open so there was a nice breeze. I had Scallops and they were served on mashed potatoes. Wow was this good. I also tried some of the apps and they were quite tasty. I need to go back soon!
label: POS

text: I am livid right now. This morning my bus was on a detour and not operating on schedule. After waiting, and waiting, and waiting (don't get me started on SEPTA) I decided to call Old City for a cab. Living in the city for over 13 years, they have always been my go-to cab company. When I called, the dispatcher asked for my address. I gave her the address I was standing in front of, but told her it was not my house, I was waiting for the bus and it is not coming. I understand that they need an actual address. Well, the dispatcher decided to have a hissy fit on the phone. She said, "why don't you just wait for the bus, because I'm telling you, i'm going to put the call in for the cab, the bus is going to come and you're going to get on it." I said, "I can't keep waiting for the bus. I don't see it and I need to be at work in the next 20 minutes." Before I could explain that even if the bus showed up THAT INSTANT, i wouldn't have gotten to work on time, she yelled, "Just wait for the bus" and HUNG UP ON ME. I am a paying customer. I want your service. It is not based upon your discretion. Thanks a whole lot, Old City Taxi, for basically telling a loyal customer to pound sand. From there I called Victory Taxi who, thankfully, was there in an instant with no questions. I will NEVER use Old City again. Phone, hailing, or otherwise. Rude service to paying customers does not deserve my business or anyone else's.
label: NEG

text: I too was part of Foodie M's group of diners who got Pooned. In a city that has so many great choices of affordable ethnic food, it's rare that I'll shell out $50 for dinner, let alone Chinese food, but the menu sounded fantastic. I have never experienced such a disconnect between a printed menu and my actual taste buds as this. Since Foodie M did a pretty thorough job of describing the dismal decor, and the range of off beat (not in a good way) to just plain inedible dishes I'll try to keep my review brief (brief isn't my specialty though...). As we sat down at the table I noticed a kind of funk wafting up my nose which I soon realized was a take out box of a previous diner's leftovers (From that day? From last week? I'm not sure) they had wisely chosen not to take home with them, and had shoved in the shelf under the table. (The tables aren't actual dining tables, but are kitchen prep tables). This should have been the first sign. Actually it was the first sign. The meal progressed from dishes that were OK to dishes that were horrible. A few examples- Second Course Peking Duck with Jicama and Spring Onion with Steamed Lotus Leaf Bun Translation - A bite of duck in a bun that is chewy in the center, and so hard on the side you can hardly bite through it. Sixth Course Double Happiness Lobster with Lemon Pepper Linguini in Homemade Chili Tomato Mirin Essence Translation - Lobster claws that are impossible to get out of the shell so forget about actually eating any, on a bed of linguini with BBQ sauce. Tenth Course Dessert: Ice Cream Cheesecake and Fresh Fruit Sculpture with Green Tea Translation - A 1" square of frozen cheesecake with a grape on a toothpick OK, so I guess a grape on a toothpick may qualify as a sculpture to some, but in my imagination it would be something slightly more. So I realized that Joseph Poon the brand is really much more about the wacky persona than the food. Oh well. I just wish I knew that before I blew so much money.
label: NEG

text: You go somewhere else, now! This was the owner's comment to me after I returned an order of chicken wings. Why did I return a "To Go" order of chicken wings? Having had their wings to go once before, I knew that they used styrofoam containers. A poor choice of container material for chicken wings straight out of the frier. As you may already be guessing, the chicken wings melted through the styrofoam. Mmmm what is this delicious foamy coating on my wings? Having learned a lesson with my first order, I specifically asked them to not use a styrofoam container with my wings order or to completely wrap the wings in wax paper or foil. After getting my next order home and being assured that the wings were completely wrapped in wax paper, I was disappointed to see that no they had not wrapped the wings in paper and yes the wings did melt the styrofoam container again. So, I returned the order of wings within 10 minutes of paying for them. During my returning of the wings the owner came to the register and asked why I was returning the wings. I explained that they melted through the styrofoam which is not a healthy situation. I also suggested that they not serve hot food items in styrofoam unless they advertise that the food comes with a styrofoam coating. Apparently, the customer is not always right in certain places. He said "You go some-a-where else-a now". And I say, "Gladly-a sir!"
label: NEG

text: I had always wanted an opportunity to order a personalized treat from Zoe at Whipped Bakeshop. With my good friend's birthday approaching, I figured the time had come. My pal is a big fan of the video game Halo, in particular, he has a man-crush on the main character Master Chief. I knew Zoe could make a treat to make his birthday special. She and I bounced several ideas back and forth and finally settled on cookies created with his image on them. They turned out great, were delivered on-time (even with a crazy blizzard stalling things a little) and tasted good too! They were a great surprise for my friend. Thank you Zoe and your team for making my friend's birthday a little sweeter!
label: POS

text: I love their happy hour deal--the delicious margarita pitchers are half price. that is, their usual 20-25 dollar- totally worth it- margs are half that. Nice. I'm a fan of happy hour in general, but if i can slip in here on a weeknight before 7 to get that deal, I'm even happier! Their Sunday brunch is also decent.
label: POS

text: Worst facial ever! I went to the South Philly Day Spa for a facial after a really long few days at work. ( I couldn't get an appointment at my regular spot and this place takes walk ins). My expectations were low- really I just wanted to relax. In the world on non-beauty school facials, $50 is low end. I didn't expect super glowing skin from a budget facial, just an hour of calm. The place was filthy. The towels smelled like mold. The face steamer smelled like mildew. It started with towels that burned my face. When I said they were too hot the lady laughed and just moved them. The massage part of the facial consisted of her pounding on my forehead with fists. I think I am lucky I didn't get a concussion. The whole thing, which was advertised as a 60 minute treatment, took about 25 minutes. The only pleasant part of the experience was the hot stones they placed under my neck. Seriously, I cannot say enough bad things about this place.
label: NEG

text: After seeing such positive reviews on yelp about this place, I decided to give it a go. It definitely lives up to its hype! The first time I went it was pretty crowded but not uncomfortably so. We sat at the bar and we were able to order to our hearts content for the All You Can Eat. The staff was very friendly and attentive, (I got asked if I wanted a refill on my soda at least several times). My only complaint is they don't have any spicy rolls, (at least spicy to my standards). The second time I've been there it was insanely crowded - my brother and I had to stand at the little entry-way for fifteen minutes before they could squeeze us into the bar. My only problem then was that there was no place to stand or sit while waiting without being in the way - however I understand it's not their fault the building they're in is so tiny. Overall they have great sushi~ definitely coming back for more when I can afford it. :)
label: POS

text: I used to really enjoy going to this Subway until one day I saw a sign that the place was being fumigated, to think that there were nasty creatures touching my food was a big turnoff and so I never will return there.
label: NEG

text: If your looking for Chinese food that comes in those fun little containers this place is not for you. If you want fresh authentic cooking you will love it. Everything on the menu is incredible, but the Dan Dan noodles are a must try and I crave the dry pot fish and Mapo tofu. The chef / owner is wonderful, personable and offers helpful suggestions. BYOB.
label: POS

text: Great food and great service. The restaurant looks a bit unassuming from the outside but has a great atmosphere on the inside. I had the salmon with risotta and the strawberry salad and they were both excellent. If I wasn't on a diet, I would have had desert. The one downside is that it was very loud. Guess that means everyone was having a good time.
label: POS

text: A great place to get Mofongo. Like the first reviewer said it feels like they dont even care you are in there. They bring you bread after 15 minutes as the food comes and its shocking they are so slow for a dead restaurant. Very good Mofongo though !
label: NEG

text: Here's the conversation I had with one of the workers on the way in: Him: What'll it be, mac? (note: I shit you not - I thought only cabbies in Busby Berkeley pictures talked like this) Me: I'll take the $3.99 special Him: Hot wax? Me: No. Him: Express interior detail? Me: No? Him: Expensive, unnecessary bullshit? (I can't remember what it was called) Me: No. Here's my $4. Please wash my car. Him: (peering inside my front seat, as if he were a cop, searching the vehicle for crack) Wow - your interior sure is dirty. I mean, it looks terrible. Are you sure you wouldn't like the "horrendous chemical smell dead-on-a-toilet interior package"? Me: If I slip you a Lincoln, can I punch you in the genitals? Him: Please drive through, sir. OK, so a couple of those lines might have been the product of some slight hyperbole, but the overall tenor of the conversation is preserved. The level of upselling at what is a decidedly low-rent car wash is, frankly, astounding. Oh, and the one time I actually did pay for some kind of interior detailing, the barely human worker-drone sprayed some caustic blue shit in my cd player, wrecking it. The business refused to take responsibility for the damage, even though viscous blue fluid was literally bleeding through the LCD and out of the disc slot. This place puts the "ass" in "class". You are better off washing your vehicle by drinking a few Big Gulps, lasciviously licking every inch of your car's exterior, pulling out your hair, weaving said hair in to a sporty chamois, and buffing your vehicle by holding your hand-made towel between your undoubtedly sweaty thighs.
label: NEG

text: I've never had chaat before and the owner was too happy to describe the various spices used for the chaats. I decided to try the Samosa Chaat, because I love Samosas! the owner also said back in his homeland, Pakistan, the women would have chaat before shopping, which makes sense. So, it's more of a snack in Pakistan,but, here in Philly, it was our lunch! It was very satisfying - the spices, lentils and chickpeas and bits of mango on top to refresh the palatte. I want to come back with my friend to try a different chaat. In fact, we want to try them all!
label: POS

text: Booo. This place sucks! Service is TERRIBLE. Food is GROSS. The only items palatable were the hummus and eggplant salad. The chicken and steak "kabob" seemed like it was heated, over and over again. This place is pure novelty. It's popularity based on the fact that you sit on a couch and eat with your hands. Big freaking deal.
label: NEG

text: Was going to be in Nashville, and wanted to stay near the action, but didn't want to pay $100+/night....found Scarritt-Bennett on Yelp. The rooms ARE spartan -- mine was a simple bed, chair, dresser, and closet 'area', with a small bathroom between my room and another small room on the other side, which we shared. No TV in the room. But..... I wasn't planning to hang out in my room; I just needed a place to sleep. And for less than $50, I got that....and saved some cash for tooling around town. The room I stayed in may have been spare, but the campus is gorgeous. I had a little room in a heroic space, which suited me just fine. The staff was awesome - they volunteered their favorite eateries in the area (which went straight to my heart). Thanks for the Southern hospitality, Doris!
label: POS

text: Went to Michaels for the first and last time yesterday. The waitstaff was very friendly but it did not translate to good service, basic elements of service were missing, orders were not taken properly, wrong food brought to the table several times, my medium rare steak (which was almost well done) came 40 minutes after my companions had completely finished their meals. Others in the group who had ordered steaks cooked medium, got them rare and on time. Coffee was served without spoons and desserts without forks. As for the food, the best thing about the meal was the house salad, the steak was a poor quality meat, I was not expecting Morton's but I was at least expecting it to be edible, had to drown it in A-1 just to eat it, probably should have not though because the taste of that nasty food stayed with me all night. You could not get me to return here even if you paid me to go, many other places in the area are much much better. I do not anticipate this place surviving very long without great improvements in food and service.
label: NEG

text: Great for a beer or two.... pretty good nightly specials... food was terrible. We went for dinner early on a Saturday night-- before the college crowd sets in. My Fish and chips had ZERO taste (how is that possible?) and my fiance's chicken pot pie was like a brothy soup. We won't be going back to this one.... for some reason the King of Prussia location is better?
label: NEG

text: Super Fresh is definitely overpriced, but compared to Whole Foods, though, it's a steal. So this is where I've been going for the last few months since moving into the neighborhood. But now, I might have to bite the bullet and become a full-time Whole Foods customer. You see, last week, I accidentally left my wallet sitting in front of the clerk in the express line. When I returned a few hours later to retrieve it, all of my cash was missing. Seriously, guys? That's how this is going to go down. I left it WITH an employee and you're still going to take all my money? That's some lowdown nonsense right there. So, just out of principle, I'm no longer a Super Fresh customer until someone corrects this mistake. Apparently there's an "investigation" taking place, but we'll see if that means anything.
label: NEG

text: So I was really excited to try out this place after reading great reviews. I got the arepa with pernil (roast pork) and the tres leche cake. The sandwhich was good but not worth 9 bucks! The cake wasn't very good and tasted old like it had been refrigerated for days. I was also surprised that when I asked for hotsauce they charged me 2 bucks for a small spoonful of their fresh hotsauce. Any other place would not have charged for this. This place is a rip off and caters to people with a bigger budget. arepas and empanadas should not be this expensive. so if you're looking for cheap good eats -dont go here.
label: NEG

text: This is basic fast food style chinese food. The only that separates it from all of those fast food places you see lining Broad Street is that it's in the suburbs. Otherwise, same kind of thing- gloopy sauces, boring menu, over cooked dumplings, salty soup. The reason they received two stars? Vegetarian options that are edible and they deliver. The staff is adequate. If you're in a hurry and not too picky, this is your spot. Otherwise, skip it. PS The fact that I have very little to say about it tells the entire story about the food!
label: NEG

text: Cheap canned beers, koozies on the wall, friendly staff, couches & tvs all in a kick-ass dive bar... what more can a girl ask for? Well, I'll tell ya. The ability to breathe. I totally forgot what it was like to go to a bar and come home smelling like an ashtray. The Tin Can reminded me.
label: POS

text: This place looks so inviting from the street, but seriously, keep walking. We had planned to eat somewhere else, but the wait was long, so we decided to get this place a try. First of all, I felt dizzy in there. The set-up of the restaurant is not at all cozy. The decor is too manic or something. I love color and am fine with crazy design, but holy hell. Just. No. Despite the restaurant being mostly empty on a Monday evening, the hostess sat us at one of the tables on the circle around the middle of the restaurant. The table is too small to sit a menu and a drink on at the same time. I literally had to put the menu on my lap when our drinks were delivered to keep from spilling anything. The potato skins are admittedly DELICIOUS. But after they were delivered, I found myself asking my dining companion 35 minutes later whether we were actually going to eat or not. The dining room was empty. There is no excuse for taking 45+ minutes to make two plates of pretty straight-forward food. We got the lemon chicken and a burger. Everything was okay. The chicken was overcooked. I guess that's what they were using all that downtime for. The chocolate is not noteworthy enough to be the namesake of the whole establishment. It's too sweet. I love chocolate. And I'd still like to try one of their fondues, but I probably won't ever go back here unless someone I like really begs me and offers to buy me shit.
label: NEG

text: I actually had to re-think how I wanted to rate this place. I ended up rating it 2 stars because I have purchased some really well-priced and interesting bits of jewelry, a dress, and some gifty items that made quite the impression. However, I have to agree with a previous review about the lack of customer service that is initiated by the staff there. I have never been greeted or asked if I needed any assistance on the several occasions that I have been in this store. I have been a retail business owner myself and worked in the industry for years and can't grasp how this is acceptable. I even give a slight curve with the understanding that maybe the staff is slammed with customers in the shop or even having an "off" or bad day....but to never be given this basic customer service the 12-15 times that I have been in Fire Finch? Now, that I have moved into a different neighborhood and don't work as close to this shop, I doubt that I will go out of my way to pop in. This will not be the case with other shops located in the Village who I feel a loyalty to. It's a shame because they have a quality product, just not quality service.
label: NEG

text: I was here last weekend and had a good time. It is a nice low key, laid back bar. They have a good offering of different beers - not your typical bud lights etc. So I actually think that makes it interesting and a cool experience to try new beers. The place wasnt that crowded. We started for happy hour and stayed till maybe 10 ish. It isn't somewhere you would go to meet people - more friends hanging out with each other. They have some outdoor seating but it goes fast as there aren't many tables. We also had some appetizers which were good. I didnt see the whole menu but I think it was all pretty standard bar fare. I dont live in the fairmount area, but if I did I'd probably go back often - a nice start to a night out.
label: POS

text: Ok...so by the looks of my reviews, it appears that I only eat breakfast, but what can I say...I find breakfast/brunch cathartic. I have been driving, riding, and walking past the cafe for over two years now and for some reason have always forgotten to go there. Finally one morning I drove past it with a friend and yelled WAIIIIITTTTT! After a quick loop around the block we parked in the lot( yes a parking lot in the city...hooray!) and happily waited only about 5 minutes for a table. I was pleasantly surprised at the lack of a wait on a Saturday morning at 10am. We were seated and promptly greeted by a super cute and friendly waitress with coffee in hand. What more can I ask for with my coffee than a cute girl in awesome boots? Their menu is small, but I appreciate that in a restaurant. To me, this means that they know what they are making and they do it damn good! I had an omelet with avocado and swiss, yummy homefries( the big chunky kind), and probably the second best multi-grain bread in the city(aside from metro). The omelet was a great size and I only ate half. It was priced at 10 dollars which seems about right against comps. The bread is made fresh on premises, as are the pastries. I grabbed a banana muffin to go because they had been staring at me the whole time. It was one of the best muffins I have ever had. It was chock full of bananas that caramelized from baking and they were insanely cake like and indulgent. That thing about only having a 5 minute wait...yeah that quickly changed. As we were nearing the end of our meal the line was starting to go outside and was becoming a 30 minute wait. I have to say though, we were never rushed out. Even after we had received our check and the line was growing, we were offered more coffee. Although we declined in order to free up our table, the offer was really appriciated in this city. The one negative I will mention is that they don't have room for strollers inside and you are asked to leave them outside. There were a few angry parents who were forced to leave their 1000 orbit stroller outside. So word to the wise...grab your sling and strap the kids in. So yeah, don't go to morning glory walk a few blocks east and head to this quaint and lovely cafe.
label: POS

text: This place was recommended to me by the produce manager of a local supermarket when I commented that their prices were ridiculously high. He agreed and told me he buys all his produce here instead of his own store! Everything here is very fresh and costs a lot less than anywhere else in the area. It reminds me of the roadside stands you find in rural areas, except most of the merchandise is indoors. Big, beautiful beefcake tomatoes were only 79 cents a pound compared to $2.89 a pound at the supermarket, and large Georgia peaches were 99 cents a pound instead of $1.69, which is typical of the savings you will find here. The selection is slightly limited but everything available is top quality.
label: POS

text: Cusumano's saddens me. It has SO much potential to be a great bar/restaurant/club. However, it's downfall is that the owners don't know what it should be. The pizza is decent (for St. Louis style pizza) but then they have to mess that up with a really irritating "2 for 1" offer at the bar, where they just divide up my rum and coke into two glasses and charge me $4. That particular drink was very watered down and it made me question the professionalism of the bartender. It's hard to mess up a simple mixed drink, but when you do, it makes huge waves. I was invited by some old friends to visit this establishment for a "hip hop" show, which I later found out that the group paid the establishment to perform. I know that happens in a lot of other cities, but that shouldn't happen in St. Louis, where there are plenty of bars hungry for live entertainment. The bar should be paying the band. The show itself was a terrible production, with the group's banner scrawled on some old bed sheets. The rappers and their amps were stuck in a corner, which made the acoustics terrible. In terms of lyrics: they stunk. I accidentally bumped into one of their bouncers, and he kind of pushed me out of the way. I mean, this wasn't even a drunken bump, just my own clumsiness. An apology wasn't even taken when I gave it to him; he just wanted to act like a stereotypical bouncer... Sad. This place needs a lot of work. The décor is run-down. The drinks are watered-down. The entire place gets me down. I'm not going back here again unless I'm dragged, kicking and screaming. So much potential...
label: NEG

text: Beef N Cheddar's Haiku You're Enhanced Only By The Cold Jamoka Shake Under Autumn Leaves Arby's is hard to come by in the Bay Area so I need to represent a little from home.
label: NEG

text: Decided to spend NYE at Chifa and was not disappointed. The menu had three pre-set three-course chef's tasting options at $55, $75 and $95. I was worried about being the picky eater in the group (no red meat or pork) but the server happily obliged to alter just my portion of the dinner so as not to disrupt the rest of the group. I was impressed by the attention to detail (pork belly buns came to me in a tofu version, kobe tataki translated to Ecuadorian cerviche, etc.) so I didn't feel like I missed out on anything. *Side note - whatever you do, order the Chicha Morada - a rediculously incredible Peruvian cocktail. If you like Sangria (which I do), you will love this. By the time the third course arrived, we were so full we could barely finish, let alone leave room for dessert. All in all it was a great deal, superb food and perfect atmosphere for a low-key NYE with friends. I'll definitely be back.
label: POS

text: Rarely do I go to Mexican food restaurants here in Tucson. Having cut my teeth on south-of-the border style food in El Paso, I find the food here to be sooooo boring. Everything tastes like "a tortilla, some meat or chicken or not, a pile of shredded cheese, some chopped tomato and a bunch of lettuce. Salsas also pretty boring for the most part. So earlier this week, just craving enchiladas I tried the Los Betos at Silverbell and Grant. Hoping against all hope that I might discover a restaurant really close to home that I had missed and that I'd love. : ( The enchiladas (cheese) were made with very thick, maybe stale, tortillas, and the sauce was nothingatall as was the rice. The only thing I enjoyed were the frijoles refritos and I had some thought that they might be canned and not made fresh. Gratefully, I don't crave them anymore and if/when I do L.B is definitely out of the running. So sad in an essentially border town. Might be tempted to take a trip back to El Paso where I LOVED the Mexican food. Open to suggestions here in Tucson...
label: NEG

text: This is a terrible restaurant,i can't waste my/your time telling anyone why,just pick another restaurant in Carpinteria. The town is great,the beach is great,don't ruin a great vacation day eating terrible food in a bad restaurant like Tony's.I wish i hadn't.
label: NEG

text: I don't drink, so my review is really only for the restaurant portion of the brewery. Sadly this place turned out to be another chapter in the long tale of ordering a burger to be cooked medium, and getting something back that is well done and decidedly not medium. This one was a bison burger which I was excited about, but fairly disappointed with due to the chernobyl grilling. I didn't feel like sending it back, but come on people... MEDIUM = PINK in the center. Look it up. Seriously. Oh and they have no fries or chips. Really am I being too traditional in expecting this? They brought me out mashed potatoes in lieu of the coleslaw (I avoid mayo based dishes in principle), and the mashed were pretty good but not what I wanted with a burger. Finally to cap it off we had their sticky toffee bread pudding dessert. It was good, but whoa... two bites of that and you should really call it quits. Way too rich for my blood.
label: NEG

text: Arrived at the restaurant that was reported to have various types of asian food and good sushi. However, upon arrival I noticed that the restaurant was virtually empty. The menu was mainly focused on chinese dishes, standard meals in the area. The japanese menu was limited with regard to entrees. I tried the spicy tuna roll, hamachi roll, and the soft shell crab roll. I was a bit hesitant to try their saba, ikura, and suzuki and passed on it this time. The sushi was rolled lopsided and the sushi-su was bland and uninteresting. I was disappointed in the flavor and freshness of the fish. The sushi was acceptable but clearly not near what I expect of sushi when I go out to eat. I think next time I will try their chinese dishes/menu, but I will not eat sushi at this place again. The wait staff was great, very polite and helpful.
label: NEG

text: What started out as a good experience came to a screeching halt when we were forgotten about by our waitress. The food was good however they were out of our appitizer and offered no substitute. When we were finished we waited close to 15 min and 5 or more passes by our waitress before we could get her attention for our check and a take home box. Loved our waitress to deth until she forgot us. Unfortunatly this isn't the first time we have had this problem at this particular location.
label: NEG

text: If you're in Edwardsville and want a non-pretentious spot to have a beer and listen to a good band, then I suggest Stagger Inn. This is mostly because there are few other bars in town that have good live music on a steady basis. (Laurie's is another good spot, but they do not have live bands as frequently). If this isn't what you're looking for, then don't bother. It is a "dive," by definition - I will agree with that. Dark, musty, and far from fancy. Also, if you are like me and don't drink beer, you may very well be out of luck. They either cannot make (due to lack of ingredients) or don't know how to make over 70% of the drinks I've requested. In short, go for the bands, not the booze or the atmosphere.
label: NEG

text: We found this small restaurant while walking around the Quarter on our last morning in town, and I wish we had found it sooner! Great portion sizes and a more-than-accommodating kitchen when it comes to making lots of substitutions for picky eaters! text: Ok, true confessions. I used to work at Grand Cru... so.. no bias. Ha. But seriously. I've worked at other wine and spirits stores as well and I've moved away from Nashville and no longer work there so I feel at least a little comfortable giving an honest opinion. Grand Cru is awesome. Really. The staff is well-educated and truly excited about the products on the shelves. The management generally tries to hire people with a background in wine, beer or liquor and it shows in staff recommendations and ability to answer questions. That said, don't come to Grand Cru if you know you only ever drink Yellowtail Chardonnay and that's all you're interested in buying. Do they have Yellowtail Chardonnay? Sure. In two sizes, even. So.. I guess go ahead and come, if that's your reason. But the reason Grand Cru deserves five stars is that the staff is knowledgeable enough to be able to get you a bottle of Chardonnay that you'll love even more that's still in your price range. This is the store to come to if you're ready to shake of the chains of the advertising world and try something new. Whether you want a $10 bottle of something that goes great with pizza or a $150 bottle for someone who considers themselves the snobbiest of the wine snobs, this is the store for you. Make yourself a regular and the staff will even start setting things aside that they think you'll like based on what you've bought in the past. Come in on Saturday afternoons for wine tastings at Portland Brew next door (bonus: they're free!). Buy a case and get 10% off the total price. Buy a half case and get 5% off. Ask for Jason or Jim.. they won't steer you wrong. Grand Cru -- as the name implies -- is more geared toward the wine drinker, but the people seeking liquor or high-alcohol beer also have a place here. When I left they were still expanding the selection of imported and other high-alcohol beer but even then it ranged from the Arrogant bastards to the Chimays to the Jefferson stout aged in bourbon barrels (can't remember the name of it.. but get it. It's spectacular). They have a great selection of scotch, including scotch gift sets that any whiskey drinker would be pleased to receive. Ask for Jason and he'll talk your ear off about which scotches come from where and why that makes them unique and amazing. Take aways: Go to Grand Cru for wine recommendations Go to Grand Cru for scotch recommendations Go to Grand Cru on Saturdays for free tastings Go to Grand Cru and ask for Jason -- he's the all-around expert Go to Grand Cru and ask for Jim -- he's a wine-maker extraordinaire Go to Grand Cru.

text: Our last visit to Caruso's SUCKED! The food was decent as usual, but the service was awful. AWFUL. We came in around 8:30 on a Thursday night, not a real busy time in a restaurant in Tucson, and the place wasn't looking very full or busy. We were told there would be a wait for inside, but none on the patio. I'm not sure why, as we were staring at about seven empty tables right behind the hostess stand. We told her we'd wait for a table inside. Sigh. Eyeroll. She seats us right away at one of the many empty tables behind her. A waitress comes by with two little baby glasses of water and some menus. I ask her for two large waters for my friend and I while my friend peruses the wine list. Ten minutes later, she's back, empty-handed, wanting to know if we've decided on wine. We order food and wine. She comes right back with the wine, yet still no water. She brings my salad, and a basket of bread. Still, no water. I ask again. I think she realizes at this point that she's forgotten my water AGAIN, but now, instead of bringing it, she starts shimmying past our table sideways, so as to avoid making eye contact. We are now out of bread, water, and pinot noir. This goes on for about twenty minutes, and she finally comes by to remove my salad (before I'm finished with it) and asks if we need anything else. "Other than the water and another glass of wine and some bread, no", we tell her. She comes back with the water (finally!), but no bread or wine. Then, our entrees arrive. Still, no second glass of wine or bread. We ask her for these items again, and she says - "Oh, you need MORE bread?", like we're making a ridiculous request. Ten minutes later, the wine arrives, but no bread. We ask again. Sigh. Eyeroll. Bread comes, and we're just about finished with our entrees. Then, she drops the check, sweet and chatty as can be. Then I, for the second time in my life, tip less than 20%. She's lucky I do what she does for a living, or she'd have been stiffed, and I'd have been having a chat with her manager. Get it together, Caruso's.

If you have the chance try either the excellent Illusione hl lancero or the cg4 corona gorda. Fumare also has a very good selection of medium to higher end cigar accessories and a very knowledgable cigar smoking staff. There is nothing worse than having ignorant staff at a great cigar shop. text: It saddens me that when people think of Reno, they're probably visualizing someplace like the West Second Street Bar - and with some justification. This cheesy, lame, somewhat skeevy bar is everything I hate about the bar scene with nary a redeeming feature. Downtown Reno is pretty much gross anyway, and not someplace you want to be clicking along in your cute little heels. But if you make it to the West Second Street Bar safely, you'll walk in to see a large wooden bar dominating half the room, filled with dumpy and unattractive middle-aged people in unflattering clothes. The back half of the bar is booth seating, where groups of younger (20--30) people gather to leer at each other. There's a small dance floor, about the size (and quality) of the kind you'd rent for a wedding reception, and they have karaoke pretty frequently, which is why we went there at all. In between, the DJ plays crappy hip-hop and frat-boy junk like "Brass Monkey" - and people eat it up. They LOVE it. Sloppy fake blondes with skimpy halter tops and orange tans shake their booties like it's dance party heaven. People go especially wild for the karaoke, though. It's super popular, and the cordless mic allows the singer to roam through the bar doing his or her best lounge act. No matter how bad the singers are, the crowd adores them. And - best of all - precisely at midnight, they play "The Star-Spangled Banner," and everybody SINGS ALONG. Yes they do. Welcome to Nevada. If I sound like I have a personal grudge against this place, well, I kind of do. It's tacky, run-down, and not even particularly clean. Sleazy, fat tourist guys are everywhere, making retarded small talk and flipping their stupid man-ponytails around over their "hip" bowling shirts, and the whole thing is so incredibly depressing that I never want to go there again. I can't see why you would want to, either.

text: Out of all the Chinese restaurants in Philly, this one undoubtedly has the worst standards of service. While the name implies this option ought to serve more than one, this is deceptive. The price is also supposed to include an appetiser, choice of soup, rice, and dessert. Despite a practically empty restaurant, we waited about twenty minutes for our steak, which came without the appetiser or soup. The steak was in a thick syrupy sauce, which somewhat masked the unfresh ingredients. We were ignored by the servers until they noticed we had finished our steak and rice. A server then plopped down a plate of oranges, which apparently was our 'dessert.' We asked for our appetiser and soup, which was met with a rude glance and grunts (our server communicated with us in largely unintelligible grunts despite attempts to communicate in both English and Mandarin). Some time later, he brought us a glass bowl of sweet-and-sour soup. I went to the front to get a copy of the lunch menu, and after showing this to our server and after more passive-aggressiveness, he got us a single spring roll, which can be best described as mush wrapped in hard crust. We didn't have any choice in any of this. We were also completely ignored by the dim sum carts, which moved a total of two feet the entire time we were there. When we passed by the dim sum carts, the egg custards looked soggy, and the various fried dishes looked as though they'd been sitting out for quite a while. Oh yes, the tablecloth was also wrinkled and stained.

Finally they advertise local meats and organic products. The server leveled with us that the meats are rarely from local farms- factory farm store bought as per most restaurants. text: I wasn't sure if I should write this review about Jake's or Cooper's, but since we were actually seated in Cooper's, I decided to go for that. My fiance and I are on a bit of a tight budget, but wanted to have the chance to go out somewhere and get dressed up. We decided that we could get the best of both worlds (inexpensive but dressy) by going to somewhere nice for dessert only. We walked into Jake's, which is definitely the classier of the two, but on hearing that we were only interested in dessert, the host ferried us over to Cooper's. OK, not quite the dressy, quiet, romantic dessert we were looking for, but the volume was at a good level, our booth was somewhat private, and the lighting was perfect. The waiter brought us the menus and we perused for a bit - everything sounded so good that we couldn't choose. We narrowed it down to two, and asked the waiter for his opinion. His response? A short, curt "they're both good. I don't know, what do you want?" When I asked what he thought of the dishes, or if he could give us a better description, he read the description straight off the menu to us. Thanks, dude. We decided on the almond cake with lavender-something ice cream and fresh raspberries (sounds delectable, no?), and decided to splurge on a cheese platter as well. The food looked delicious when it arrived. However, the almond cake was dry and heavy. It would have been complemented nicely by the ice cream, had there been more than a tablespoon of it on top. The raspberries also complemented the cake nicely, but there were only six of them. For an $8 dessert, I expected something much better. As for the cheese platter, they didn't give us nearly enough bread, and the waiter didn't offer to give us any more until the very end. Taste-wise, the cheese was good and the additional spread was also good. Service was not great. The waiter came by only once to fill up our water, and both of our glasses had been completely empty for about 15 minutes at that point. He was curt, unfriendly, and abrupt throughout the evening. I can't speak to the entrees, but here's the bottom line for the dessert menu: nowhere near good enough for the price. We won't be getting dessert here again, and we will think twice about spending our hard-earned money on dinner.

text: I hired OB Sod to install sod at my new house. The installation started on April 22nd. I was told by the Supervisor to make sure to water properly, do not use any fertilizer until the sod is established, do not have it cut until atleast one month and to make sure that the first cut is kept high. The sod looked great! It was lush and green. After 2 weeks, I noticed what looked like little stalks of wheat. I contacted the Supervisor and told that was normal. ...ok Exactly one month after the install (May 22nd) , I hired a landscaping company to do the first cut. I instructed them to cut the sod high. After it was cut, I immediately noticed that the sod looked lighter green and brown underneath. The next day, I noticed that there were caterpillars all over the sidewalk, patio areas, and crawling up the side of the house. I immediately placed a call to the Supervisor. Since it was Memorial day weekend, I never received a call back. The entire lawn was saturated with these caterpillars. I had to go online and do research to find out what this could be. I found out that these were sod webworms and could destroy the entire lawn within days. Since I never heard back from the OB Sod Supervisor, I went to Home Depot and bought a fungicide that works on those particular type of caterpillars. When the Supervisor finally contacted me, I suggested that the sod was installed with this problem. He claims that was not the case and sod webworm is rare right now....not the season. I was told to have it sprayed immediately. (PS....He claimed that we had the sod installed 2 months ago...I had to correct him) BE AWARE..... OB SOD ONLY PROVIDES A 30 DAY WARRANTY

The food is good, it's well-made, and you pretty much know exactly what you're getting when you order it. They don't have a whole lot of specials on their stuff, instead favoring generally lower prices.

text: They're not in the exact spot as Mix 5 was, but right next door, in the corner. The entrees (with sides included) are $10. Portion size is HUGE, so don't let the price scare you off. It's a deal. Unless you have a big-big appetite, you'll end up taking some home. They also serve samosas at $1/each (minimum 5), and "Nem" eggrolls at $1/each (minimum 5). I got the Lamb Mafe, and was impressed. It's served over white rice, and consists of marinated chunks of lamb cooked in a spicey stew. A whole carrot and a potato also come with it, cooked in the same stew, plus a bowl of the stewy goodness. The stew proper was a bit on the spicey side, so I mixed it well with the white rice, and that diluted it well enough to really enjoy and still appreciate the heat. But I still needed a little water to chase it. So be sure to ask for ice-water the first time you go there. I ordered the Ginger beverage at first, but it was also on the spicey side, so I had to ask for the ice-water to chase the stew. And, if you're a connoisseur of ginger ale, you HAVE to order the Ginger drink for $2.00. WOW! It's home made, and it makes you say a-HUUUUA! I was the only dine in customer, but there were a couple carry out customers while I was there. The owner practically runs the whole show, so service is not quite up to what a typical westerner would expect at a North American restaurant, but she is professional, and has restaurant experience. The owner and the other employee speak French (and English) fluently if you want to practice your French. They're very friendly too. The store was pretty clean, and done up rather well for being essentially a cubby-hole tucked into the corner of the shopping center. The ambience is not impress-the-boss worthy, but it's perfect for a family outing, or a cozy date. I _will_ be back.

text: Beto's has good Mexican food and good service. Others have commented on communication problems with staff and/or confusion with the ordering process. text: After a day on the slopes and consisting solely on granola bars, I was STARVING and the buffet at el dorado totally satisfied my hunger! I had the Saturday night Seafood buffet. They had an amazing selection: king crab legs, oysters, smoked salmon, shrimp cocktail, prime rib, steak, leg of lamb, mahi mahi, snapper, pizza, gelato bar, seafood stew, the list goes on! we had to wait about an hour, but it was definitely worth the wait, and one of the best buffets that i've had in awhile. almost everything i had was surprisingly delicious. my favorites were king crab legs (they had an awesome cocktail sauce that was spiked with a bit of wasabi or mustard, or something that gave it that extra kick!), the leg of lamb (very tender and flavorful), the lobster cream sauce with fettucine (the bits of lobster chunks were surprisingly big and tender), and the gelato bar (not too sweet, good consistency, what's not to like?). The pizza was also really good, they had a pesto/tomato/mushroom one that had a really nice, chewy crust and good flavor to it. For the amount and quality of food my friends and I ate, I can't believe they can make money on this buffet. One of my guy friends had 10 raw oysters and 10 crab legs, which would cost way more anywhere else. And that's on top of the steak, lamb, and everything else that he ate. The only thing I would ask for is some more veggies - they had an okay salad bar and some broccoli/lettuce stir-fry but that was about it. I would definitely come back again!

text: I most recently was introduced by a friend to the Townehouse in Media. We eat out just about every night, fine restaurants from Philadelphia to West Chester. What a surprise to find a little bit of everything in this old fashioned restaurant. Most of the time we pay for our salads at competing restaurants at comparable price ranges. Not the Townehouse, the salad was so fresh with so many ingredients. While having a cocktail at the bar before dinner, bowls of fresh peanuts are offered, and yes you are encouraged to throw shells on the floor, just adding to the atmosphere. I had lobster fra diavolo, large pieces of lobster, delicious pasta and perfect spicey sauce as promised. My friend introduced me to liver at the Townehouse. I still don't believe I eat it myself but it was not as I remember as a child. Tender, delicious and accompanied by onions, bacon and your choice of potatoes, my new favorite is their twice-baked potato, delicious. The atmosphere and the friendliness of the servers are right up there with the food. I was told the Jerry, one of the bartenders has been there over 25 years, like many of the waiters and waitresses. Monday they have Pasta night for only $9.99 which includes the salad I talked about. Tuesday special for $15.99, Wednesday, 2 lobsters for $24.99. OK, I'm rambling, but I am thoroughly impressed. Lastly, I saw their add in the Philadelphia Inquirer yesterday, their Recession Buster, 40% off entire dinner menu, Monday through Friday, 3:30-5:00. It's obvious I will be eating earlier while enjoying the Townehouse.

text: I went to this Save-A-Lot because I wanted to cash in the spare change I had, and this grocery store was the closest location with a Coinstar machine. So I took the opportunity to shop around. The food here is cheaper than your average grocery store, as the brands are mainly more obscure. Meat and poultry are also cheaper per pound. The vibe here is less pleasant than Super Fresh on South Street that the previous poster mentioned. However, I'm not sure a grocery store aimed towards those more impoverished is deserving of mockery in an impoverished town such as Philadelphia. Would I shop here as a first choice? Probably not. But if I didn't have the disposable income to shop for similar items at more expensive alternatives, then I would consider Save-A-Lot. It is true though that you have to pay per plastic grocery bag. The cost was 3 cents per bag -- certainly nothing exorbitant. Personally, I think having to pay for plastic bags is a good thing. Not only does it cut down on costs for Save-A-Lot, but it also encourages people to use reusable bags which is better for the environment. In fact, the city of Toronto passed into law this summer legislation requiring all retail stores to charge 5 cents for single-use plastic bags. And you know what? In the short time this price tag was placed on pollution a noticeable difference has been achieved. I see A LOT of disposed plastic bags littering the streets of Philadelphia. Food for thought.

text: Those fried oysters were DEE-LISH-US! Our dinner at Rio Mar was not just the highlight of my trip to New Orleans, but also the highlight of my three travel companions. It was our first night there, and we were desperately searching for a delicious meal. We made a circle and a half around the rainy Warehouse District (Yelping all the way) before settling on Rio Mar. Thank goodness we did. At first, I was a little wary. Mainly because we suspected the previous restaurant had lied about being full, the host at Rio Mar seemed a little rude, and we were a little wet and cold from the rain. Luckily, things immediately began to go our way. The predicted 45 minute wait turned out to be ten minutes. Just enough time to grab a drink at the bar and finish it at the table. We ordered tasty appetizers and the delicious Fried Oyster Salad. The Chef hand delivered the salad to me which was a nice touch. Then, the entrees came. The stars of the meal were my swordfish and my sister's squid ink dish. Both were absolutely fantastic. The meal continued on its upward journey with dessert. There was delicious tres leches cake, banana empanadas, and flan. These were dropped off by the aforementioned host who completely redeemed himself throughout dinner as he helped with our table. The food was memorable and so was the service. Especially our server who, rather than making me feel like an ass after spilling the water glass he had just refilled for me, laughed with me and walked away saying "that was awesome" to himself. If I lived in New Orleans, I could see myself making Rio Mar a regular spot for dinner.

text: Ridiculous!! The only reason why you should ever think to stay at this hotel...wait...no, there is no reason why you should ever even think of it!! text: Average cuisine + lazy execution + spotty service = 1.5 stars I dined here with the fam for the second time in a year. What I remembered most about my first visit was that I left feeling "greasy". My second experience was, for better and worse, much more memorable. Rumba has a large outdoor patio/seating area, surrounded by lush greenery. There is a cabana/bar outside on the patio. On a Saturday evening, a delightful solo act on a steeldrum sang and played familiar ditties in calypso style. The ambiance on the patio is great; it captures the laid-back vibe of Clearwater. The inside seating area of the restaurant is a different story: stuffy and with the exception of those cool Caribbean vertical-spinning ceiling fans, it felt like a cross between Perkins and Bennigans, decor-wise. Like we did, you should definitely opt for the outdoor area, which is much more lively (at least in the winter). The menu IMHO is poorly laid out, too. A lot of flipping back and forth, and some items simply had no explanation ("Fiesta salad" and "wedge" specifically). Take a look for yourself (http://www.baystarrestaurantgroup.com/rumbaisland/menu1.html). I was also confused by the "subsections" within the main sections, which conflicted with the descriptions of the "parent" section. For an appetizer, we ordered "onion strings." The plate came out as a pile of loose fried onion bits (think a can of french's) with a single spoon of thousand island served in an asian-style soup spoon, placed atop the pile. No utensils or explanation of how to eat it was provided. Simply awful. This terrible mess makes the bloomin' onion at Outback seem like a Filet Mignon at Bern's. I also ate a tomato salad with red onions, blue cheese and a balsamic vinaigrette dressing. It was pretty decent but the red onions were sliced way too thick, and the salad was drowned in the dressing (Chef, maybe take a look at this video? http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VfEG15CLTqo) For the entree i ordered a blackened mahi sandwich. It was served on focaccia bread, with two slices of raw cucumber and one dried up tomato slice. Uninspired. The side of coleslaw had sliced almonds thrown on top. Bland. When the server set the plate down, the dressing (which was again served in an Asian-style plastic spoon) was tipped over on the plate, and it spilled onto the table. The server did not even notice. The fish was well seasoned and cooked, but was overshadowed by the other ingredients and the sloppiness of the plating. The rest of the family got different variations; the rumba trio (ribs, chicken wings, fried shrimp); the coconut encrusted mahi, etc. I do give them props on the wide variety of side dishes they offer. If you order an entree, you can choose from two sides. I sampled most of them, which are Southern influenced, and they are generally very tasty. Also the mini corn muffins that are served as the bread basket are noteworthy. Despite my attempts to be healthy with my choices, I again left with that greasy feeling as though I ate a heavy meal. I can't believe that this restaurant is owned by the same group (Bay Area Restaurant Group) that gives us Island Way Grill and Salt Rock Grill, both outstanding. C'mon, guys, send over some help to Rumba and shape it up! It's simply too hard to overlook the many small infractions to warrant a rating higher than 1.5 to 2.

text: Doughy white bread subs which remind me of a moment I had as a child. I'm picturing a trip to a roadside deli in South Dakota where the bologna and american cheese bound between white sponge bread soothed my youthful hunger. Alas... I've grown up a bit. The vegetarian sub (yes, I'm calling it a sub because it doesn't deserve the relationship to sandwich) was slathered in mayo, cheese, and raw vegetables. Once again. The ground the Earth of a sandwich is built upon the bread. Jimmy John's doesn't give us the ground to stand on. Theirs is a mass produced, plasticized, version of bread. The bread is the medium upon which sandwich art is comprised (and I know I'm not the first to state this exact sentence...it's practically a cliche` these days) To make real bread is an art, requiring strong elbows and an attractive amount of tricep fat. I like to think there are people out there who live for nothing more than to make the bread which arrives hot and melty to my lips. I've gone on far too long with this review. Long live real bread. !

text: Friends took us here on a recent visit to Reno. Overall, we liked the place very much. We ordered a coconut shrimp appetizer. The shrimp were very large, and only 3 to an order. I think 4 would be better, for splitting, even if they raised the price a little. I ordered a Chilean Sea Bass done "Asian" style. I was a little surprised to find it sitting in a bowl of noodles, but it was delicious, and healthy. My partner ordered Prime Rib. Both of us agreed it was the best Prime Rib we had ever had. So tender, you could practically cut it with your fork. Seasoned perfectly and prepared exactly as ordered. The bread served was thick, crusty artisan style with an interesting spread. We ordered a side dish of asparagus, and they were simply steamed, and tasty. A nice snap to them, but still cooked just right. The service was good, but a bit odd in that we had several different servers during our meal.

text: This is the only film developer in Philadelphia. Right, you can get your film developed at Ritz, or CVS, or Target, or wherever, but this is the only place to really get it done. I took the vast majority of my film (colour print, black and white, and colour slide) here, and the results were always fantastic. Colour balance seemed correct (the Velvia just jumped out with saturation ... love it!). Black and white had good contrast. I usually had my film scanned, as well, and the scans were pretty decent, too. I always had to play around with the colour on the Velvia scans, but I guess that's to be expected. Finally, any prints I had done always came out well. I'm not giving them five stars for two reasons: first, one batch of negatives I had developed had significant scratches on a few of the frames. While they weren't important frames, it was a little concerning. The proprietor said that the scratched were their fault, and that they could get it fixed for free. Nonetheless, it seemed a bit disconcerting. Second, it's not cheap to get film developed and scanned her. I can slides developed and scanned in Kansas for significantly less (although, I'm waiting to see how the slides turned out). But, if you're in Philadelphia, this is the place to go.

text: I love this place! They have improved over time, which is hard for some places to do, they get comfortable and then slip downhill. They are part of the AYCE Buffet on the weekend and they are always yummy. I personally do not use the clarified butter, because they are wonderful without, but for those who can afford the calories,there is plenty to be had. I love making my own BBQ, which is a weird saying because it really is not BBQ the way we think of it, but it is fresh cooked on a flat top grill. You go thru pick your veggies, and your meats and seafood, and then apply the sauces you like, (They have a recipe or you can make your own) and hand it over to the cook and watch it being made. ALWAYS wonderful. They have a fresh fruit and dessert bar as well as ice cream to finish up. They also just recently added sushi so now they have a complete menu for just about everyone. I recommend, and the price is not bad either considering how much food there is to eat. Very easy to over eat.

Those guys & gals deserve BIG tips because they take your tray to your table, get your drinks & are all over any requests you have. A visit to this place is a great experience. text: Miguel's Mexican Cafe in Tampa was a bit of a surprise. Finding passable Mexican in Florida can be tough if you're not a local. I recommend Miguel's. Starting off were the free chips and salsa, the chips were excellent the salsa a first seemed a little mild for my taste. As I continued eating I felt a nice little burn. Salsa gets a 3. For my dinner I had the Carnita's De Puerco, the pork was very tender and not loaded with chunks of fat that you often find in pork dishes. The rice and beans were excellent. The Margarita's were a cut above the standard 'Rita found most anywhere else. The outdoor seating was small and decorated well, though be advised it sits only about 6 feet form the street, so it can get noisy. The bottom line, if in Tampa, and you want Mexican with an upscale feel try Miguel's Mexican Cafe.

text: What a wonderful experience my wife and I had at this restaurant last evening. This was our initial experience here, selected on a whim. The aesthetics of the restaurant are what first draws you in, at least for us it did. The exterior is a bit plain, located across from what was once this nation's first "pentagon" military head quarters during the Revolutionary War. Independence Hall and the liberty bell are within a short walk from this location. As you can see, this place is both convenient for tourists and locals alike. However, the restaurant does require business casual attire, which simply adds to the upscale atmosphere of the dining experience. Entering the modestly light restaurant you first notice a wall of cascading water, a nice touch as you approach the hostess station, located near the front entrance. Once inside a full size and I mean 15 feet tall and 10 feet wide Buddha statue draws one's attention. Another nice touch, that adds to the over Asian fusion cuisine style of this restaurant. There are several tables, with interesting Asian faces covering the chairs at each table. Who were these people? My wife and I were seated towards the kitchen area, at a cozy table for two. We found ourselves surrounded by light candles and dimly light over heads in the ceiling. The restaurants main first floor room is large, at least a 25 foot high ceiling. This place envelopes you. New age and modern jazz styled music plays at a reasonable volume, as the dining experience begins. Waiter service was top rate, professional, courtesy, and most importantly, non pretentious. Some these fru- fru restaurants frequently come off snobbish, but not here. We immediately felt relaxed and welcomed here. We began the meal with special cocktails; passion rum with fresh mint and strawberry juices was on order, as my wife enjoyed a healthy glass of sangria, consisting of brandy. These drinks were delicious, at $10.00 each, or there about. I enjoyed two passion cocktails; they were smooth, and simply a delight to the pallet. We passed on appetizers, and ordered from the entrees. My wife selected the shrimp, which was a large portion, consisting of colossal sized shrimps and noodles. I selected the Peking styled chicken, with an additional ala cart of wasabi styled mashed potatoes. The restaurant is family style, which translates to encoring the restaurant patrons to share their meals amongst their individual table. The meals were spot on, stellar, an explosion of flavors, cooked to perfection. After completing the large portions of our meals, we decided upon coffee with desert. The desserts are to die for my friends. Adequate sized proportions, presented in the most appropriate and tantalizing aesthetics that I have witnessed thus far in a Philadelphia Asian restaurant. Delicious, and a must, if you can manage it after a full meal!!! We decided upon the three individual sorbet presentation, and crying chocolate cake, with a scoop of Vietnamese coffee ice cream. Again, similarly to the main course, desert was delight o consume. This was another pallet inducing explosion of flavor and culinary decadence. In between courses the waiter promptly cleaned the table top of crumbs and other assorted discarded morsels. We also selected sparkling water to balance or alcohol intake, which were two passion rum cocktails for me and single sangria for my wife. I know what you are thinking, what light weights, but we had a film to catch shortly after the meal, at the nearby Ritz Bourse Theater, and we were driving. I highly recommend advance reservations, as this place fills up quickly. Our overall impression was delightful, we will return in the near future to try their other offerings. Enjoy this restaurant if you decide to visit, and keep in mind that you get what you pay for, as this is a rather costly resturant, but worth every penny.

text: You know what's kind of awesome? Riding your bike on a beautiful summer evening with some fantastic people, some delicious homemade food and a couple bottles of chilled white wine to see a Philadelphia Orchestra performance. Despite it being a corporately funded venue with multiple concession locations, nothing feels too intrusive, and with a fairly lenient carry-in policy and some planning, you shouldn't even need to visit them. My friends and I copped a lawn spot to catch the Philly Orchestra perform a number of Tchaikovsky pieces and we stuck around for the fireworks show at the end. Both were executed very well and contributed to a wonderful evening. The quick breakdown: Pluses -Lovely setting -Fairly cheap tickets (at least for Orchestra events) -Food/Drink carry-ins allowed (again, Orchestra events) -Not in New Jersey Minuses -The Orchestra can be difficult to hear at the far end of the lawn -Kids as far as the eye can see This experience was a highlight of my summer so far. I highly recommend that anyone who likes the symphony try to make it out to the Mann for one of the summer concert series.

text: Located outside the technical limits of Tucson, their standard labor rate is a good 4 dollars less than in the city. Couple that with my pity story and my student status, and I got another 4 dollars off labor ($44 is standard). After having my car totaled by an uninsured driver and receiving a less than adequate payout from my insurance company, I needed a place that would fix my car with parts that I brought it, not new parts that they ordered, and make my car look new again. I checked reviews and the better business bureau, and decided that this place would do a good job of re-making my car. Ina Road Auto Collision, or Spectrum Auto Paint and Collision, I can't figure out which name they go by, was a horrible experience. Customer service is just awful and the work they do does not appear to be top notch. The experience started off well. Because my car was rendered immobile, they came to my house to write up an estimate. They did require a large window of time on a Friday morning/afternoon, but the man who came was friendly. I did some preliminary work on my car and drove it to the shop. When I dropped off the car I had them write a new estimate substituting the parts I brought in. I explicitly told the man writing this up that I wanted a scratch on my trunk lid to be fixed and that I wanted all dents to be filled in on the used parts I was bringing in. I was quoted 1 week. One week later I received a phone call that my car was ready for pick up. They offer door-to-door service, but could not pick me up because 10 miles is too far for them to come and get me. So I paid a cab 30 dollars to drop me off at the shop. I sat down and was asked how I would like to pay. "I'd like to see my car before I pay." I sat at the receptionist's desk for ten minutes before being told that my car was not ready. I insisted that someone drive me home. Two hours later I was driven home. A week after this I got a second phone call that my car was ready. I insisted again that they pick me up, and they did, and as we pulled into the parking lot I could see my finished car. At least this time I knew it was done. I walked around the car and saw that none of the dents were filled in and they did not fix the scratch on the trunk lid like I asked. I talked to the man who wrote the second estimate, and he lied to me about what I told him during the initial estimate. I can't fathom a body shop that would just paint over dents. They also needed to pull out one of my fender aprons. After doing this, the bumper didn't fit right. There's an inch or so of space under the left headlights and millimeters under the right headlights. Pre-accident there was no space beneath either. text: Lucked into Varga Bar last night on the hoof back from Rittenhouse to Old City and ponied up to the bar for a flight of tasty craft beers and light, gourmet bar nosh. Pros -High quality selection of unusual craft beers. Available in half-pints, pints and growlers. The growler at $25 would be a great pickup for a BYOB or a heroic entry at a house party and might set you back less than the equivalent score of smooth beers from the Foodery, for example. -Great gastro-pub fare. When you're in the mood for something a giant-stride up from standard bar food, Varga's offerings are a refreshing option. We had grilled Octopus (amazing) and the basic house salad (also delicious) and thoroughly enjoyed both. Cons (a minor service quibble) -Our plate was cleared with one delicious looking bite of grilled octopus still on the plate. At $15 for the plate, that was like a $3 bite that got swept away with out our consent.

text: Disappointing to say the least. The unenthusiastic staff seemed bothered to take my business and for what? The coffee was nothing to write home about. Burnt tasting, bland and expensive. The girl who got my coffee was barely audible and knew little about the coffees sold there. I'm not crazy about Starbucks but this place is a perfect example of why so many people go there instead. text: This place makes me want to say, "Yeehaw, pardner!" This is the second time we've eaten here & the second time we sat at the booth with cowboy boots on the ledge. I ordered two appetizers as my dinner: coconut shrimp & sirloin skewers, which were sprinkled with sesame seeds & drizzled with a teriyaki sauce-it was awesome. P.S. the baked potato & the jacketed yam are fried to death. Seriously, they are heart attacks on a plate, but they seem to be a hit. text: Food is great, I take that back, it's fantastic. But the service doesn't do it for me. I feel rushed to get out - it's not me, they want to reseat the table, it's fairly cramped but again the food is phenominal - and the desserts are awesome.

The only chance I had at going back there (and not writing this review) would have been if they offered me a free meal for my family next to time to try and erase this terrible memory from our mind. This place would be best off to market to ten foot poles, because that's about all I'd touch it with.

text: I tried Marble Slab for the very first time this past summer, on one of those blistering hot days when you just wanted to jump out of your own skin. I got a bit confused reading the menu at first, because they offer so many choices. You can choose your pick from the ice cream flavours, then opt to have toppings added in, like nuts or candies. I felt like a kid that day, so I ordered the cotton candy ice cream with gummy bears mashed in (can anyone say sugar rush?). I liked watching the guy behind the counter mash the gummy bears into my ice cream with a spatula. It was something I've never seen before with ice cream. The price was a bit hefty for ice cream, but they load it onto your cone. The first half of the cone was sugary bliss, but by the end of it, I was feeling a major sugar rush. And then half an hour later I crashed and felt like crap. Oh well, probably my own fault anyway, for ordering a combination like that! I most likely won't come here too often next summer, because I know I can get good ice cream from the grocery store, but once in awhile won't hurt. I just won't order that combination again!

text: "We have a parlor room available - it's about twice the size of an average guestroom but it does not have a bed. I furrowed my brow and then he offered me his other tantalizing option: a smoking room (WITH a bed.) I was understandably displeased with both options and let him know. Once off the elevator on the 7th floor, I was instantly hit with the stench of cigarette smoke. I wanted to gag. I didn't know hotels still had smoking rooms, let alone smoking floors! As I climbed beneath the covers, the sheets felt like plastic. I wonder if this is a special perk available only to smoking room inhabitants? I've stayed at the Hyatt Regency Philadelphia at Penn's Landing on numerous occasions. However, on my last two visits the hotel's not been up to snuff: rooms not quite clean (crumbs near the desk), room service trays left outside the room I was checking into (I think that explained the source of the crumbs) and a general feeling that the hotel had let itself go. And then came last night's two terrible choices: a room without a bed or a room on the smoker's floor; pretty much the last straw for me. text: I attended a stand up comedy show at the Arlington featuring one of my favorite comedians, Daniel Tosh. If you have not seen his show or stand up I definitely recommend checking him out, he is absolutely hilarious. As far as the theater itself went, it was not ideal for a comedy show. Drinks were only served outside in a courtyard, and you could not bring them into the theater itself. This presents a problem for opening acts, if the guys not funny and your not getting wasted where the hell is this night going! No tables were available, theater seating only. The audio was problematic, it was difficult to discern what was being said at times. Also the seat numbers are very difficult to see causing awkward moments when squeezing through people looking for your assigned spot. The good part is the theater itself is beautifully decorated with the ceiling painted like the sky. Spanish style buildings cover the interior sides of the theater. It sounds to me like the Arlington Theater is truly a movie theater that they have forced comedy into. For theaters I am sure it is great, as the other reviews say, but for comedy not so much.

text: After reading all the reviews, I also wanted to try out this spot. I took 2 of my friends with me, and i kept on telling then how good its going to be and about all the great reviews it got! text: Suggested to go here by the front-desk at Hotel Santa Barbara - as it looks like others were as well from the reviews here - and the end result was quite surprising. The vibe was great, the service was fine, the appetizers were amazing, but... Their main entree was a huge dissapointment. I got the 8 oz. top serloin (thank god I didn't get the bigger one) and it was probably the biggest dissapoint I've had with a steak (and food in general) in my lifetime. I love my steaks, but I'm definitely not a picky or high-class eater when it comes to reviews, but this was absolutely horrid. I ordered it medium, and inside it was cooked perfectly. Outside the entire thing was burnt...so chewing on black char the whole time was quite a pleasant experience to say the least. Not only was it burnt on the outside, but the steak itself was the least flavorful steak I've ever eaten. I could have gone to the grocery store, grabbed one for $7 and cooked something 10x better on my bbq out back. Again, I am NOT a picky eater nor do I rarely complain about food, but this was horrible - especially for a nearly $30 steak!! I didn't even want to finish it! Maybe they had some backup cooks working, maybe they forgot about it, or maybe it was just a horrible piece of meat that they wanted to hurry out of the kitchen and get to my plate and get me to pay. Again, such a surprise...everything about this place was fine, but when it comes to a $30 steak...it better be at least SLIGHTLY good. text: When we visit Karen's sister in the Nashville area, we stay at the Franklin Mariott/Cool Springs. Our first experience had the potential to go wrong quickly, but instead turned out great! The theater is less than 5 minutes from a large movie multiplex and several (admittedly chain) restaurants and two minutes from a Starbucks, so there are some creature comforts nearby.
