text: I know there are some people who prefer Geno's over Pat's...and for those people, I must say that you are CRAZY. Absolutely CRAZY. And here's why: I've been to Geno's once or twice before, a long time ago and things haven't changed much. When my coworker and I was scheduled for a training up in King of Prussia, well, we couldn't drive past Philly without a stop at a cheesesteak joint. As my coworker has never been to Philly (uh, how?!?!), I decided that if cheesesteak was what he was craving...well then, we have to do the Geno's/Pat's taste-off. We start off at Geno's, and there was no one in line. There was no one in front of me, and no one behind me. No one walking up the street to come to Geno's. So there really wasn't a need for the lady behind the counter to get *quite* as snotty as she was, when we didn't know what "wit" meant. I mean "wit" what (it turns out - it means "with onions")? Obviously, we're new here, and as it's not like we're holding up the line, the attitude wasn't really called for. Eh. Whatever. We were hungry. I *LOVE* cheese wiz, and as that is what the original cheesesteak was made with, well that's what I always order (before you doubt me - look it up. I'm right.). My coworker got his with provolone, because he's weird about eating "plastic cheese". Whatever. He quickly learned to rue his haute palette, as he bit into his cheesesteak - to find that the cheese was stone-cold and un-melted! Have you ever had unmelted cheese on a cheesesteak? It's not exactly gross, but well, it's not tasty either. There is something about warm, melty, oozy cheese that is part of the cheesesteak experience! To add insult to injury, both of our breads were a *wee* bit on the stale side (not "3-day-old stale"...more like "been-left-out-all-day-next-to-the-oven" stale), and I didn't like that the meat wasn't quite as chopped up as I liked. This reminded me why I stopped coming to Geno's after my second or third visit so long ago. On this trip, we ate at 3 cheesesteak places. Here, Pat's (see my review), and Jim's. I have to say, that this was definitely bottom of the list for both of us. Actually, I ranked this cheesesteak to be about on-par with Jerry's. Yes, you read that right - Jerry's. A NOTE: because of the "rivalry" between Pat and Geno's, I find it really hard to write this review without doing a comparison. Normally, I try to avoid comparing one establishment against, another, as each should stand on it's own, however the rivalry between the two is so popular, that it's nearly impossible to eat a cheesesteak from one, without thinking of the other.

text: This is my first Yelp review; Taco Riendo is my favorite cheap, good food find in Philadelphia so far. The food is fresh, handmade, and plentiful. I watched as the chef took a large slab of beef and quickly, effortlessly carved it into small bites for a waiting taco plate. Each ear of corn is shucked just before fired on the grill and every plate is adorned with condiments that accompany your selected meat, specifically. The salsa (with the salsa-and-chips side) is red and saucy, not chunky, and very hot. If your palate can't handle spicy food, go ahead and ask for a cup of ice for your drink before you eat. The Chorizo in the chorizo tacos was cooked till it had a thin char on the outside. The very slight crunch of the chorizo was a wonderful contrast to the smooth, smoky mole sauce that comes de rigeur with the sausage dishes. What you can expect: -Fresh Authentic Mexican food, made in front of you, when you order. (Nuff said). -Very inexpensive for great food. (Tacos are $2.50 each, Salsa and Chips were $3.50, Coca Cola- the sugar-based non-high-fructose-corn-syrup in a glass bottle variety was $2.00). -Ample seating. (I was there for a little over an hour, it seemed like the crowd ebbed and flowed by there was ample seating to be had.) -Accommodating hours. (There aren't a lot of places outside the touristy areas that are open on Sundays till 9 p.m.) If I was forced to say something negative- I think they are understaffed or overwhelmed. The cashier was simultaneously taking orders, bussing tables, cleaning tables and drying off dishes while I was there. (It is a holiday weekend though, so I don't know if this is normal.)

We left hungry and not satisfied at all. We do have to say their french fries were really good (at $1.99). Our "Poompa" bread gumbo bowls were about $12 each - and not worth it. Having spent the money and experienced all kinds of different car washes, one could say I'm somewhat of an expert on the subject. Having said all of that, I'd like to weigh in on Octopus at 22nd and Kolb (just east of that intersection on the south side of 22nd). I've had my car washed at Octopus (and it's prior ownership) at least 20 to 30 times over the last 5 years. I frequent Octopus, mostly because of convenience...it's on my way home. Most times, Octupus is decent. You don't feel like you're getting "oversold" on their products, the people seem nice enough and they do an OK job on washing your car. I've never had a WOW experience there and continued going out of convenience, as I said. After my visit last week, I'm not going back. Maybe I'm picky. But, I'm a consumer and am allowed that luxury of choice. When I pay for full service at $20 ($10 if you have a coupon) I expect the following: vacuumed within a degree of perfection, interior wiped down with no "dust trails", interior windows cleaned with no streaks and a fairly dry car after being wiped down by 4 people. At Octopus, you get mediocrity. Some say, you get what you pay for. Since I've had WAY better quality of service at other car washes in town for the same money (see Classic Car Spa), I beg to differ. When you have competition down the road doing a better overall job for the same money, it's time to step up your game. My last visit to Octopus was probably the perfect storm of badness: The guy asking me what kind of wash I wanted looked like someone shot his dog and was going through the paces of his mundane job. The guy trying to sell windsheild repair services blocked my way inside to try and sell me an un-needed windsheild replacement. The car itself was handed over still spotty with water, streaky interior windows, a sideways rearview mirror, dusty interior and poorly vaccumed. Overall, for the money, you can do better in Tucson. If you're an eastsider, Octopus is OK. If you want to drive a little more to get better service for your dollar, go to Classic.

text: Yeah, the man knows me. I give this place 4 stars. I had never really been to Philly even though I grew up on the East Coast. I have to give it up to the veggie man, for he and his cousins were most supportive in my quest for the perfect steak experience. And we're talking about locals here, so they wouldn't dare show their faces in daylight at the big name steak houses (Pat's or Geno's) It was delicious. Caught amidst a ton of construction, the sub sidewalk level pizzeria was pretty much our second choice after seeing the line at Jim's around the corner. I was a bit skeptical, thinking "this looks like any other joint in CT" how could THIS provide me a tasty meat moment? I had to hide my excitement while the cousin ordered. I'm sure the sexiest thing a vegetarian could see is his gf stuffing her face with grade (who knows) steak... The cheese was great, not overwhelming...the bread fresh, the right amount of greasy flavorful moisture and yummy onions and mushrooms. There's no fancy menu, and I am sad to see they don't have the meatballs (I'd like to have a ball competition) and the employees probably wish they were somewhere else, but I'd definitely go back if in town and hankering for some real Philly fare.

text: Good Chinese food in Boise? As soon as we ordered, our waittress dropped off some soup - your standard egg drop soup with a bit of chicken meat and peas and carrots (probably frozen). Mehh... it's the soup you get at all Americanized Chinese restaurants. Whatever. We started with the Crab Rangoon appetizer. I've actually never seen this served at a Chinese restaurant - at least the ones my parents take me to. I had my first while hanging out with coworkers. Based on those experiences, this one was okay. Your standard deep fried wonton with cream cheese and a tiny bit of crab meat. The sweet and sour sauce it comes with is too sweet for my taste - we got the hot mustard with it and that was okay. text: We have been taking our two dogs and four cats to Dr Balzer for almost three years now. Dr Balzer is great with our animals and we are very happy with the care that they get. The office is not fancy and I feel like they care more about taking care of your pets than having a fancy waiting area. Afternoon appointments do need to be scheduled out ahead of time - at least a few weeks - but I like the option of coming in unscheduled in the morning. You will wait and will need to be there early to get seen, around 7:30am, but a little waiting is worth it if we feel the need to get one of the animals in right away. We also had to put down one of our dogs earlier this year - she was an older shepherd mix that we rescued a few years earlier. Not a great time but Dr Balzer and all the staff were extremely caring and considerate throughout the whole process. They made sure that Pinky was comfortable and gave us all the time we needed to say good byes. Yikes - getting a little teary thinking about it. It is hard to explain but we feel like Dr Balzer and her staff are more concerned about caring for animals than they are for coddling owners.

When you go to Maido go with an empty stomach because it also has an incredible lunch counter that makes fine and inexpensive cuisine. they have all the Japanese favorites like miso soup, sushi, and salmon teriyaki. But it also has more exotic dishes like the Shrimp Okonomiyaki (a Japanese pancake), and Yakisoba. If you live in Philly but want to check it out don't worry. The $19 truffle gnochi appetizer was great, but the truffle amuse egg custard tasted exactly the same. My wife's filet was delicious. My first bite of sugar and spice duck was savory. text: Since I missed the UYE here last month this place has been burning in the back of my head. So I went back and tried their buffet. This way I got a good sampling of most of the their meats. We had to wait in line just to pay before sitting down. If you get their early they will have someone cutting super tender, succulent pieces of prime rib. I managed to weasel through the line and get some before it was gone. They were constantly refilling the buffet items so everything was hot and fresh. I usually don't like ribs but their beef ribs are so good and the sauce is so tasty that I went back for seconds. The garlic mashed red potatoes are by far the best of the sides. The corn bread was being fought over and was gone almost immediately after it came out so it took me standing over the basket like a vulture waiting for more to come out for me to get a square. It was worth it because it was moist, sweet and light. My only criticism is the desserts. The chocolate chips need taken away from their kitchen. They put them in everything. So it ended up making every dessert into some form of chocolate chip cookie. There was a warm cake that had apples in it that was ruined by the insane multitude of chocolate chips added to it. But with that said I did not come there for dessert anyway.

text: I came to the store to shop for vintage clothing, so I can't attest to its inventory of recent fashions (e.g. jeans) or to its buying practices. Organization was OK but not great, and the store's size labeling system seems somewhat inconsistent. I left with 3 tops and 2 dresses; average cost was $10-15 each - very reasonable. I went to TAG right after, and they were selling items of similar style and quality for over twice as much (but I still liked that store overall, for other reasons). I'll drop in again if I return to town.

text: This place is literally a hole in the wall; yet they've managed to pack so much quality into such a tiny space. A true dive among dives, this little diner has a lot of heart. However, the food is inexpensive and sooo good. I've only ordered breakfast items, because that's all I want when I'm there. Angelo's does their homefries so well, that I just have to order a breakfast sandwich (i.e. their famous porkroll-egg-and-cheese on a bagel) to accompany this potatoey goodness. The place is great for a few friends to go after a long night of drinking. It is a college town, after all, so that's the primary market, anyway. text: Rain, mud, beer, blues, more rain, more mud, jazz, gospel, famous musicians, local musicians, more rain, more mud, piles of crawfish, bowls of gumbo, and more beer - even wine now. What a great time! April/May in New Orleans is a rainy season. So plan to get wet. Wear shoes you can throw away before flying home, bring rain ponchos, old clothes, and rags or towels to clean off seats. Sound terrible? Go read the list of performers on their website. It's like nothing else in the world. Two weekends+ of every jazz/blues/zydeco/gospel musician in the world, with half a dozen different performances going at the same time all day every day. (Not quite all day - they end early in the evening.) Jazz Fest is held at a giant fairground, last weekend of April and first weekend of May. It's easiest to take a special bus (reserve in advance) from downtown or the Quarter to get there. They typically have two main stages, where Jazz Fest regulars settle in, stake their areas (the dry ones go first), set up lawn chairs, and settle in to see the headliners. Spread around the fairgrounds, each just out of hearing distance of the other, are the major tents, like the Gospel Tent and the Jazz Tent. You'll want to get a schedule in advance and plan your day, based on who you want to hear, how far it is between the tents/venues you want to see, and how much mud is between them. No tickets once you're in the grounds, just walk into a venue, grab a seat (mostly folding chairs, a few bleachers) or stand (up front at the main stages), move on when you want. Listen to the Dirty Dozen Brass Band, then Nathan and the Zydeco Cha-Chas, then the Leviticus Gospel Singers, then Aaron Neville's new gospel group. Grab another beer and some Cajun food, then catch half an hour of Bobby McFerrin and Chick Corea performing together, then slip over to hear Diana Krall. (That was part of one of our days at Jazz Fest in 2008.) There are food and craft booths everywhere (hence the "heritage" line in the title). I don't believe there are any repeat performances, so it's different musicians every day. The Nevilles may appear in different combinations, but you only get Diana Krall once, Irma Thomas once, Dr. John once, Dave Matthews once, Bon Jovi once, Joe Crocker once, Earth Wind and Fire once, Trombone Shorty once, and on and on. Life is tough. Since each day wraps up by mid-evening, there's no late night problems getting back to your hotel from this less-than-impressive neighborhood. And that way you can still do the French Quarter in the evening, get to a good restaurant for dinner, and start early again the next day. They want you to have a good time, but they also want you spending money in the French Quarter. Shutting down Jazz Fest early also means many of the performers are playing elsewhere in town at night. Add the French Quarter to Jazz Fest and it's the ultimate party. Just a muddy one.

text: Seeing as there are only 3 reviews on this place, I contemplated not even taking the time to write one, but.....it is SO bad that I just have to. I was in New Orleans for a work convention and my coworkers and I decided we wanted to eat somewhere nice but not too fancy. Somehow we chose Tony Moran's because the menu seemed decent and it was close to our hotel. To enter the restaurant you must first walk through the accompanying bar called The Old Absinthe House. I truly wish at this point we had become lost and given up, but no, we made it to the back and 'voila', Tony Moran's! OK, so the ambiance was nice, candle light and table cloths. I thought we were in for a nice meal. The second our waiter came over and opened his mouth, I knew it was going to be bad. He rambled off the specials and at one point said "We have a very nice baby veal tonight". Cue the giggle from me and someone else at the table. The waiter paused, looking perplexed, and asked if he had said something wrong. When we realized he hadn't been joking, we kindly explained that ALL veil is baby cow so it is oddly redundant to say "baby veal". After reviewing the menu and noticing the typos (come on really?) I settled on the Fettuccine Alfredo and a shrimp cocktail app. My shrimp was actually served hanging off a martini glass, which I found tacky, with some soggy lettuce smothered in generic from-the-bottle cocktail sauce. Yuck! I couldn't even finish it and there were only 4 SMALL shrimp to be had. After the disaster of the appetizer course, our main entrees arrived. (Remember I ordered the Fettuccine Alfredo) As he is setting down my meal the waiter says "Linguine Marinara". Seriously? The sauces aren't even similar, at least TRY to get it right. Anyway, one person had the chicken picatta which was good, but another had the most generic looking 'meatball and sauce'. Yes, MEATBALL, a giant ball-o-meat atop a mound of pasta. My friend next to me ordered the Tuna cooked rare, so naturally it came out well-done. And the strangest part was it is was served on top of pesto AND marinara sauce. It looked like the "chef" had changed his mind half way through plating the thing!! Oh and the grilled veggies were so peppery that she actually coughed while trying to eat them! Tony Moran's claims to be "famous" for their Alfredo, the only thing that should be famous about this is how bad it is. I expected a creamy cheesy sauce blanketing my noodles, taking me to saturated fat heaven. This is NOT what I had. I don't even think what I had could be classified as Alfredo. You know how Fettuccine Alfredo leftovers look the next day? Kind of clumpy? This is what I was served, and for $19!? Ugh, then to top off a terrible meal it took almost 35 min for our waiter to divide up our check and swipe our cards. He apologized so many times through out the meal for random things that we decided Tony Moran's new slogan should be "Sorry about the delay folks!". Please do not be fooled by this place. It is a crappy restaurant posing as upscale dining.
label: NEG

Walking inside there are casual tables off to the right and up a short flight of stairs there is a mini-market of shelves of healthy food items and supplements and a counter. There is a professional looking woman in a sharp looking black chef coat behind the counter. I browsed the aisles, snagged a few snack bars (quinoa and flax seed), and found what the website promoted, Raw chocolate truffles. I bought some of them, a pricey but tasty Coconut and Goji berry delight. For the main course I bought a Taco Salad which was in a crunchy flax seed shell and a living pizza. They both had a Cashew cream sauce as the 'wet' ingredient and it was fantastic.. It's a little different getting used to this sort of crust but they were good. I topped it off with a banana maca chip smoothie made with brazil nut milk; it was tasty and a good match with the meal. I say mix it up and try something like this occasionally and you'll feel better after eating it... at least more than if you always ate quesadillas.

text: My friends, this is the cool place to be! Euclid Records has been rocking Webster Groves since 1981, and there's no end in sight! More than just a record store, Euclid Records has an active blog and also has fun events every now and then. In fact, it was at one of these such events that my fiance and I really clicked. A few years ago Euclid featured Punk Rock Night, playing punk music and punk films. We watched Rock'N"Roll High School together, and the rest is history! We've been patrons of the place ever since. Check out an image of the projector screen they use to show movies in the photos! Euclid Records is broken in two. In the front half you'll find the register, new cds, used cds, and dvds. Most of their cds are rock, but you'll find every genre available. Remember, they can order anything your little heart desires! The walls are covered in awesome music art posters and the musty smell of old records makes you feel so darn cool just for being there that you'll want to keep on coming back. In the back you'll find records, records, and more records! I cannot tell you how cool this place is! JUST GO!!!! You will find every type of music here, and don't forget to check out the dollar bins! Be sure to look along the walls and in the corners in the back half for framed artwork that will rock your world! The environment of this store is really sweet. Want to browse anonymously? That's fine, they'll leave you be. Want to chat away the hours? Boy, did you pick the right place to wander into! The staff is cool yet nice, and there is no air of superiority among them. I've seen every type of person in Euclid Records, and I can guarantee you that you'll feel right at home. So go ahead, support a local St. Louis shop and stop on by!

Mmmmmm delicious! Gosh they were good. The point is, these people don't see their customers as strangers or as not mattering. Lots of places say that, and sometimes you run into the odd restaurant owner or host/hostess who does try to adopt that "service-with-a-smile, you're-our-friends" kind of attitude (some more sincerely than others), but these people are the real deal. text: I went to Tria this past weekend to meet up with some friends, a little early start to the night's Memorial Day weekend festivities. First, I mistakenly went to the 18th st. location, only to realize my friends were at the one on 12th & spruce...no matter, a quick cab ride got me there in no time. FIRST IMPRESSIONS: This place is clearly for the sophisticated crowd, as if there is a such thing as the unsophisticated wine and cheese bar (I won't ask). It's a place to go to enjoy a fine glass of wine and a small thing or two off the menu. It didn't strike me as a place to go for dinner, although this might not be the case...I had a couple glasses of the Four Graces Pinot Blanc, and the Italian Meats tray. THE LAYOUT: Sophisticated and refined are the key words here. It's not some lifestyles of the rich and famous kind of pomp-shack...but if you are put off by yuppies in sport coats laughing pretentiously at the toiling of the average lowly peon, this might not be the joint for you (okay, I didn't hear any laughing about said subject going on, but you get the point hopefully). Dark wooden furniture, lit naturally by the afternoon sun peering through the large open windows. There is a patio section and an indoor section, separated by these large windows, which are open in warmer months. THE WINE & FOOD: The reason I tried the Four Graces is because Tria does a special, pairing a selection of wine, cheeses, and beer, first round is half off. It was exquisite in my (unseasoned) opinion-- I was looking for a wine that wasn't too dry, a little fruity, and that held it's flavor and consistency throughout. Hit the nail on the head. The Italian Meat platter was also very good-- various Italian meats that I won't dare to try and remember the name/spelling, some of the sweetest red peppers I've ever seen, and a delicious mixture of garlic-infused olive oil with a tangy red pepper/garlic paste for the bread...oh yeah, and Caper Berries...I don't like them, so I won't allow it to affect my review, if you like em, you will probably enjoy them here. It was all very tasty, if not a little expensive (although not necessarily overpriced)...I wasn't expecting more for my money, per se, I was just surprised at the bill. It's not a killer, but it was a little high. THE SERVICE: We were fortunate enough to have Shuli (sp?) as our server, she was very friendly, attentive and knowledgeable. Sometimes when you visit a place like this, you get some hipster wine snob who expects you to know Napa like the back of your hand. Well in Shuli's case, despite my constant ignorant inadvertent insults to the finer things in life, she was able to boost my experience by being so nice. I don't know if it's a good thing or a bad thing that there isn't a set dress code for the staff there, but someone behind the bar was wearing a plaid shirt...not what I'd expect to see, but I don't get bothered by things like that. THE ATMOSPHERE: We spent the afternoon in a wine-induced haze (not drunk, mind you) feeling the buzz and the warm breeze. We talked about all kinds of things, including the VERY eclectic soundtrack, which went from kama sutra-esque ambient, to underground chill hip hop, to country, to pub rock. I don't know who the hell put together that playlist, but it drew more laughter than anything else-- the transitions were too abrupt. It didn't take away from the experience, but it was notable. THE VERDICT: If you are looking for a great, relaxing, refined experience, or if you want to throw (or enjoy) a wine and cheese party outside of your designer loft, Tria, is the place to go. I gave it 4 out of 5 for the minor annoyances I had (I'm like Larry David when it comes to wierd random quirks like that), but it really was an excellent way to start the evening, and I would love to go back again!

text: I write this review after having visited this establishment 5 times. I truly hoped this venue would provide a new vision of Irish Pub atmosphere in the Nashville area, but I must say it falls far from its mark. McNamara's Irish Pub needs to find its niche. You can't be all things to all people, so either be a pub or be a restaurant! The establishment is nice inside and out. Much detail was taken to provide the backdrop for enjoyable dining and live music performances. Your first impression after waiting in the long lines to get in is usually a good one and until the music starts that is all this place has going. The wait staff is slow and green, with little focus on actual service. Granted most nights the wait staff must dodge small children running around unchecked and your usual busy bar environment, but that is what they do for a living. An average drink order time to the table of 22 minutes on any given night is too long! Not to mention the average 45 minute wait on appetizers or dinner, often served back to back. On every visit the kitchen was slow and the food was either cool or the order was wrong. The menu is a joke as usually a third of it is sold out, especially desserts. These problems suggest that as a pub or restraint the place is failing. Now the BIG issue. The drink menu is always void of major beers or liquor. On 3 of 5 visits, the bar did not have a beer in stock I will drink and there are 4 beers on the menu I like. I am not a Guinness drinker so perhaps that is the problem. The last time I took my family in we ended up drinking not so sweet 'sweet tea' that was warm and ate cold food over an hour after we ordered on a Sunday night with only half the dining area full. I love the place, but it offers nothing after the appeal to the eyes and ears. Suggestions? Sure find a niche. 1. Be a pub and get the drinks to the table fast and right and seldom run out of alcohol stock. Be bawdy and arrange the tables to face the music so camaraderie and conversation flow. Set a time of night when children are only welcome in the dining areas away from the stage. Most importantly DO NOT manage, bounce, direct or scold from the mic, your customers don't want to be involved in drama they are here to have a good time. Get the attention of your manager and have him handle problems. OR 2. Be a restaurant and focus on better quality hot food to the table in 30 minutes or less. Make your servers pay closer attention to the tables and give them the room to maneuver so they can serve. Forget your people wanting a pub style good time because you are not providing it. Those patrons can go upstairs to be rowdy or hover around the bar. Channel your clientele toward what they are looking for and focus on what you do best. Over all there is a lot of opportunity for McNamara's Irish Pub. In a few months if they are still there, we will see if they have found their groove but for now it ranks 2 on a 1-5 scale with 5 being the highest. Good Luck McNamara's Chuck R, Nashville freelance writer

text: New Orleans Birthday Trip = Music in the French Quarter So this here, this back in an ally, is the House of Blues. It's dark and it's ominous and it really feels like it should and would be an great place to grab a drink and listen to some music. It may not be the first, but it's the best because it's basically awesome. Venue: HoB is a real music venue, that's what it's built for. It's a stage, with a lighting truss and music set up, two floors and a balcony, and every spot is within spitting distance of the stage. Both floors have their own bars, and while the space may get crowded, just remember there are 799 other people here just attempting to enjoy the music, so don't be an ass and share the space. It's dark inside the hall, with various mood lighting in blues and purples, and be careful where you put your foot down, because there might just be a step or two there. Largely, the entire venue is deceiving. There are upstairs, downstairs, private rooms, music halls, parishes and patios. You could throw whatever the hell kinda party you wanted down in NOLA at the House of Blues and probably never run out of space. Downside of HoB nowadays it it's national chaindom. Back when NOLA's HoB was the second in charge and still a novelty, there was nothing better. But now they seem to be everywhere, even at Disney, and they're owned by Live Nation--the authenticity has been lost a bit. Still, in certain glimmers of chords and powerful vocals, you can find it: that true music hall feel, so go for the history too, but always for the music. Music: The entertainment at HoB run the gamut. They'll have everything from The Naked Brothers Band a la Nickelodeon to David Cook to burlesque shows and real soul music. Take a pick, but always go, even if just for the opening act like we did. That's right, we went to House of Blues for an opening act: acoustic Vertical Horizon, or the frontman at least. It was awesome, and spontaneous and well worth it, because the venue is welcoming and acoustically primed. There's food too, but we skipped out after VH was done (and yes I knew every song). I here the brunch is pretty good though, so if you're in town for a while, try both.

text: I am surprised about the lack luster reviews. I have eaten here a handful of times and went again tonight and love it. I ordered the mahi mahi special and the shrimp/chicken (we asked them to add chicken extra) quesadilla. The portion of fish was large and tasted great plain. It came with a sweet cranberry sauce which complemented the fish very well without overpowering it. The two vegetable sides I ordered were the skewered veggies, cooked and seasoned perfectly, and the roasted peppers, also marinated and cooked to perfection. I got a chance to sample the monk fish special as well and was pleasantly surprised; a more chewy fish with a crispy breaded outside. I even thoroughly enjoy the house salad and dressing they serve with entrees! Between four of us we ordered two entrees, two appetizers, and an extra salad. Our bill was only $80 and we all left stuffed. The outside of the building looks pretty terrible, I have always thought that since I have lived in the area, however, despite what some others have said, the decor fits the place perfectly. From the pew bench seats to the vast amount of Frida Kahlo art, the place delivers, at least for me and my family, EVERYtime.

text: This is a great new place! Top to bottom we had a great experience with a large group. I am not sure why it says it is not good for groups - We had 10 and it was wonderful. The decor is impressive and interesting; there is a science lab type feel that actually works. It certainly doesnt feel like a cheap gimic. It has a fairly chill lounge atmosphere where if they took away the tables and added couches you could see it being the new hot bar. In fact taking someone to the bar there would be a great date spot (they have a great wine list, about 20 good beers, and a very creative cocktail menu... I would stay away from the unholy water, its tasty and different, but in the end it feels like you are drinking tequila and chili powder). Our waiter was also very nice and knowledgeable. Finally to the food - Had the bibb salad, burger, and scallops. Everything was top notch. The salad had a ton of flavor. The burger was great and I would compare it to Grace's Tavern with a char grilled tasted. The scallops were wonderful and cooked perfectly. Others at the table had the lamb shank, perogies ("best perogies ever"), and chicken, which everyone loved. Our friend that had the biscuit said that sharp cheese really overpowered everything else. Another person had the grilled octopus and it looked so good that I wish I would have ordered it. The only reason it gets four stars is because the perogies and scallops came with nothing else. It isnt a quantity issue (there were four very large scallops served) but like others I enjoy eating different foods together with some sort of rice or vegetable. It would have been especially nice with something as rich as scallops. I would absolutely recommend this place to others and will go again. This is my first review - I had to give Adsum props especially in the face of some negative reviews which I cant imagine they deserve.

text: I'm not going to get hoity-toity on you. None of this "I've visited/lived in/sniffed New York, so I know what 'real pizza' is!" crap. I don't care. DO NOT CARE. What I do care about is that Racanelli's is damn tasty. This, to me, is what pizza is -- a triangle-shaped slice that's light on sauce, heavy on melted cheese, and juuuuust greasy enough. Cheese is where it's at; awesome toppings are a bonus. In my opinion, Racanelli's is the only pizza in the area that delivers on what I want. Now I'm not talking about those pizzas that have dainty asparagus pieces or cheese that's from Uncle Franco's favorite goat or whatever. Those pizzas have their place in the food world, but I eat those too. But when I want just a freaking piece of nummy, straight-up pizza, I head to Racanelli's. The crust is thin and chewy. The sauce has a good balance of sweet with slight tang. The cheese is abundant and MOZZERELLA. Yes, actual cheese. Not provel. And the grease is lovely to look at and have running down your chin. Yes, I know I'm weird -- shut up. Spring is a-coming, and that means I'll be walking the Loop more and more. So when I make my weekly treks to Vintage Vinyl and Star Clipper, I'll be walking with a slice -- or three -- of Racanelli's in hand. (By the way, the pizza still is delicious when it's delivered. text: Heading up to Royal I was surprised to see Mr. B's was still full of people chatting over their brunch in the dining room shortly after 3pm - asking the host if they were still seating I was told "no, but we serve most of our best stuff at the Bar all day." Content with this I made my way over to the bar where I was seated next to a friendly fellow from Mississippi who insisted I "must" try the BBQ shrimp - his pick for the best dish in all of New Orleans. Explaining to him that I had every intention of doing so the waiter/bartender must've overheard our conversation and chimed in that the shrimp wasn't his favorite dish, but that it was very good. When I asked him what his favorite was he stated "The Gumbo Ya-Ya." With water filled and my choices already made by my neighbor and the bartender (the two item's I'd had every intention of getting anyhow) I sat back and chatted with my neighbor while watching the basketball game at the bar. Arriving without much delay was a hot loaf of crusty French bread with a great crisp exterior and pillowy soft interior - perfect for eating but moreso for soaking. Shortly following the bread was my cup of Gumbo Ya-Ya - the best gumbo I'd have on my visit to NOLA. Served piping hot and featuring a thick dark roux, light on rice and heavy on spicy andouille and shrimp - plenty of bite without blunting the nuances of the individual ingredients - wonderful. A short time passed and I reflected on the delicious gumbo before my second dish arrived - a half order of the famous Mr. B's Barbequed Shrimp. Three enormous shrimp - head and tail on, served with two pieces of grilled country bread and resting in a sauce that may as well have been 1/3 butter, 1/3 pepper, and 1/3 garlic with a bit of Worcestershire and lemon - the first time in a while that I've had to work so hard for food (shelling) but thankfully entirely worth the effort. First devouring the tender yet snappy shrimp that were accented but not overwhelmed by the sauce - and then soaking up the sauce with the remaining bread - I'm glad they publish the recipe online because it is definitely something I plan to do at home. To be fair, I can't think of a better way to spend an hour and $20 than the meal I had at Mr. B's.

text: I really wanted to LOVE this place..it had been on my list for some time to try... and nothing makes me happier then finding a new Indian haunt. We finally got there on a Weds night... as to avoid the crowds I hear about on the weekend. It's very small - so I can't imagine what it's like on a weekend... with a larger party & 5 other small parties it felt very crowded. The staff seems to be wandering aimlessly, mostly handling the large party. We started out good- for apps we chose the samosa & sweet potato pakora.. I must say the pakora was wonderful & the accompanying sauce was out of this world.. The samosa was fresh & fluffy, but lacking a little spice & flavor. We ordered our entrees MEDIUM spiced- hesitantly, I've been to Indian places where medium is WAY hot. Both my Veggie dish & my husband's lamb came out tasting very fresh-- but with NO spice - not alot of flavor going on there... but eh, the Naan, was good. My last test of good Indian in always the Kheer -- the waiter kept pushing for their homemade ice creams, but I must have Kheer. A thorough disappointment... flat, bland, and just bad -- not a hint of Cardamom or Saffron. More like something from a bad diner. Come on IndieBlue... spice it up...I really WANT to like you !

Before I know it I'm taking down Hurricanes and shots of Patron at the cozy little bar. The night is off to a great start. The first few dishes we got were amazing. Between the third and fourth course stood up to give my party a toast, "Guys, thanks for coming out here with me. Let's have a great time! Here's to Hurricanes in New Orleans!"....silence. The entire restaurant is staring at me...i hear crickets...shit...i meant the rum-filled drink, not Katri...aww too late now. I quickly sit down...unable to tell if I'm rosy from intoxication or from embarrassment...."Waiter! One more round please...this time 151 instead or regular rum please!" Just order the tasting menu or the Degustation. You won't be disappointed.

I'm sure a better meal could be prepared at home with a trip to the Grant/Stone market. Staff has always been very friendly. I have felt pressured to leave immediately after finishing my meal on Friday and Saturday nights. But it's always been a friendly sort of pressure. The Char's restaurant in Phoenix was taken over by Thai-Rama with a significant improvement in quality. Maybe one day Tucson will be as fortunate. text: "Then came Blockbuster...then came Hollywood... then came all other McVideos. Most other mom and pop video stores went out of business. Casa Video grew and grew." -- Casa Video's website With over 40,000 titles and Arizona's largest collection of classic, foreign, independent, and documentary films, Casa Video is sure to have the perfect video for your evening. And if you need help finding something, there's a huge reference tome at the counter, a public computer terminal in the back (Casa Video website and IMDB access only), and the friendly staff is happy to offer suggestions. Or, if you're not in any rush, grab a free bag of popcorn and browse the aisles. You can even browse their inventory online from the Casa Video website. Casa Video is *the* place to go for movie rentals in Tucson. Heck, even if you're not in Tucson (or are just too lazy to get up and go there), they'll mail movies to your door. At Casa Video, I don't mind paying the occasional late fee, knowing that it goes to support this wonderful and unique local business.

text: Hank Y - The utensils and napkins are conveniently located in a beer mug on the side of your table. I'm not sure why your waitress didn't bring that to your attention. I love that they offer 20 draught, ice cold beers, as well as an extensive bottle list. I like that you may choose to order the inexpensive tapas for something light, or a hearty meal. My only complaint would be the bathrooms. The walls around the toilet could be wiped down. I think someone had too many drinks he couldn't aim for the toilet. text: Carman's is one of those places I just can't wrap my finger around. I want to be in love with the place, and I was until my second visit, but something just doesn't sit right. Hearing rave reviews of mango, apricot, & mascarpone French toast or chocolate-peanut butter-banana Belgian waffles is torture. Living a stone's throw from the arsenal of aromas that march out of Isgro's every morning ain't exactly heaven, either. But I love brunch, and am determined to find the best damn brunch spot in the city. Especially for those of us condemned to only be able to eat half the menu. My first visit was with siblings and cousins. I'd heard of the place and was excited to try it out. I had an omelet where Carman somehow managed to marry Brussel sprouts, tomato, fresh mozzarella and orange wedges into some sort of flavor carnival. Was not expecting that to taste nearly as good as it did. Second trip - Striped bass with eggs over easy and home fries. My cousin got the same. Let down. Not bad, just not fantastic, which is what I'd hyped Carman's up to be over the year since I'd been there. Tasted like fried white fish. Bummer. But like they say, third time's the charm. Seared scallops over cheesy shrimp grits. With over easy eggs and potatoes. Wow. I don't like grits. I always had to eat them growing up because I couldn't eat other breakfast starches and I've resented them over the years. Damn. Those were some good grits. Pink, as though she'd pureed the shrimp into the grits, but then added some chunks for good measure. And the scallops came out a perfect med. rare, light caramelizing on the edges. Raised the bar again, Carman. Can't wait to see what you have in store next time.

text: Perched just outside the French Quarter, the Melrose Mansion is a gorgeous antebellum mansion that is meticulously maintained. Suites range from $225 to $400 a night, with the junior suites being much smaller but still charming. All the rooms are elegantly furnished with antiques, and the suites feature high ceilings and decently sized bathrooms with whirlpool tubs. Breakfast is included with the room, and I have to recommend the crawfish quiche, which is simply divine. The location is nice and quiet, but the downside of that is that it's a schlep to the interesting locations in the French Quarter. You have to walk through the residential part of the quarter to get to most of the restaurants and tourist locations, which is okay in the cooler months but can be murder during the summer when the heat and humidity beat you down after a couple of blocks. I'm talking the kind of humidity that literally fogs up your glasses the moment you step out the door. Depending on the room you get, MM can be a bit of a splurge, but if you've ever ridden the St. Charles line and looked longingly at the sorts of houses you see in the Garden District, this might be the place for you to scratch that itch.

text: I typically CRINGE when I see the word "bowl" in a restaurant name as I equate that with crappy food. This was surely not the case. With a dearth of ethnic foods in some areas of metropolitan St. Louis, its never ceases to amaze me the seemingly plethora of Thai restaurants out here. I am in search of the perfect pad thai (for St. Louis). My search brought me to Thai Bowl. I am a fan. It's in Earth City. I drove 7 miles away to find it tucked away near the business parks out there. Mind you, you can eat there but it does appear geared for take out and they do deliver. Don't underestimate this place. It's legitly Thai complete with pictures of the Thai King at the front. Let me just say, they make a mean ass plate of pad thai is different. You MUST order the "country style" pad thai. It's their specialty. The texture was nice; not too soft and soggy, not too hard, and the color was appropriate. The portions were huge. As of today, this pad thai is my favorite in St. Louis. Our second order, we asked for the person behind the counter's favorite dish and she liked the curry. Was it pineapple? I can't remember so I'll upload a pic and you can tell for yourself. Overall, the menu is not littered with every known Thai dish known to man. It has the basics, but the essentials. This is my ideal place. Soft on the presentation, not pretentious, and giving you big portions on what they are focusing on bringing you well; a good tasting dish that they make well with an excellent price. Food is 4.5 but with great prices and portions, I give this place a 5 stars. Next time you are in the are picking up your FedEx package in Earth City, pick up some of that Country Style Pad Thai and the curry specialty dish. It's a very unassuming place that does a solid job of Thai for St. Louis. Right now, I like it better than Thai Kitchen, even if the menu isn't as diverse.

text: "The Green Tea Cupcake. THE GREEN TEA CUPCAKE!!" Haters will say cupcakes have jumped the shark. The real issue is that the national cupcake wave never produced a single acceptable specimen. Moist, subtle, wonderfully fragrant, and never cloying, with a light application of the most tantalizing lemony green tea frosting. You know how most cupcakes try to fake you into thinking they're moist by lobbing on an equally giant blob of icing? Not these, my child. Not these. The other cupcakes are equally riveting: carrot, red velvet, and pumpkin (with a cute candy treat atop them). I also highly recommend their latest addition to the menu, banana blueberry muffins: thunderously moist, nicely dense, and thoroughly satisfying. Haven't tried the iced coffee? The ginger peach tea, iced? The brown egg sandwich? The chicken salad? These are all rockstar knock-em-out-of-the-park items. Also loving the amazing Kylie and crew. Nicest people ever. Cheers!

text: this has to be said. the CUPCAKES at the flying monkey at the reading terminal are terrible. TERRIBLE. i really like cake, so i mean, it's really hard for me to HATE a cupcake. i am particular about frostings so i don't really include that in the equation, but the cake itself... i am pretty lenient in my assessments. well, the one at flying monkey is so terrible. and i am going off on this rant because i had it for the second time a few weeks ago. the first time i tried a cupcake there, i was so disgusted i THREW IT AWAY. if you knew me, you'd realize that it takes a lot for me to throw away food, especially cake, but i did. the cake is DENSE, so dense you forget it's cake. but it's not dense in a moist way, similar to a pound cake. no, it's just dense, but also crumbly. sigh. and the frosting is neither light like whipped frostings, or creamy like a buttercream one. it's almost gelatinous. ALSO, full disclosure: i think the reason i'm so vocal about this cupcake is that it gets written up a lot for having very delicious baked goods, cupcakes in particular. SIGH. TO BE FAIR, i've had a lemon bar from the flying monkey before and it was pretty tasty. so i suspect their other baked treats are quite edible/enjoyable. but don't get the cupcakes. don't be fooled by their pretty colors and semi-interesting sounding flavors... they are the yucks. WHAT WE ATE peanut butter plaid: chocolate cupcake + peanut butter buttercream the cupcake i had (my second, ever from here) was called "peanut butter plaid" and was basically chocolate cake with peanut butter frosting. as i said before, the cake was dense and dry. the frosting tasted like a watered down version of peanut butter - so less the flavor, less the creaminess. sadface. i threw this one out too after a few bites. flyin' hawaiian: vanilla cake + pineapple coconut buttercream + crushed macadamia nuts friend CC ordered this one for dessert. he got mad at me for letting him buy a cupcake from the flying monkey. he also threw his cupcake out.

text: Morimoto is everything a restaurant should be: you get a unique food experience with great service in a trendy setting that feels posh but still accessible. I came here last night with several co-workers on a business trip, which was nice because I got to sample a large swath of the menu. We ordered 4-5 appetizers, the highlights of which were an excellent Octopus Carpaccio and the 10-hour Pork Kakuni, the latter so tender it literally melted in your mouth. The tuna pizza was pretty good too; and I also had a piece of fatty tuna sashimi, tiny but yummy. My main dish, the "Tai Shioyaki", was the coup de grace. It was a large white fish called sea bream, which had light and flaky flesh in a gently crispy skin. The dish came with the chef's instructions to sprinkle smoked sea salt over it, then cover in hot white butter sauce, and lastly, dip in spicy ponzu (a tart, citrus sauce). The result was divine--the best fish dish I've ever had. There wasn't a single thing I tried that was not at least very good. I sampled the popular "duck duck duck" entree featured a terrific roast duck that was moist and crispy. My dessert of chocolate pot de creme was a good finish. If I had a complaint at all, the only one would be that Morimoto's cocktails really ought to be larger or stronger given the price. But the drinks were still good; the cilantro gimlet was especially popular among a few of my colleagues. Dinner came to a little over $100 per person but felt well worth it. This was among my favorite restaurant meals ever. If you're in Philly, check out Morimoto!

text: This place is perfect, especially for the college crowd. It opens and closes late at night, so it is actually the perfect place for a study break. Or, if you're out of that particular age bracket, I would still urge you to go. It's imperative. The donuts, they're amazing. I like to consider myself something of a donut gourmet, since I have been eating them since I was a small child on an almost weekly basis. My father and brother and I have tried them all, in multiple towns, all over America. Chain, local, community-oriented, probably front for drugs. You name it, I've had a donut there. This place is on the top of my list. First of all, the apple fritters are actually to die for. Second, they have old fashioneds, which are these odd donuts that not everywhere sees fit to make. On top of that, they have them covered in chocolate. I'm sorry, but that's obviously a sign that someone out there loves us all very much. Third, they aren't trying to be some nice, brunch place. They have kitschy stuff on the walls unironically, you can see into the back, and the staff will laugh at you, in a good-natured curmudgeonly kind of way. It kind of feels like home, actually... Last, all of their other donuts (I have been several times... for science...) are also excellent. And cheap! A dozen is something around $7, and they are so delicious it is actually shocking. In brief, go there. Eat the donuts. Enjoy the ambiance. Then get back to that work you're avoiding by going on a donut run in the middle of the night.

text: I think the actual name of this place is Angie's Market and Front Porch Cafe. During our recent visit we had breakfast here on late Saturday morning and were surprised to find this place with out a crowd. Of course, that didn't last very long. This is the type of place the neighborhood loves and locals still don't know about (thanks Yelpers!). It's also the kind of place I like to keep to myself so they don't die from overkill. But this time I decided to share because I want them to survive through to our next visit to St. Pete!! As you enter, you are welcomed by the friendliest smiles and deliscious temptations! The charm hits you first with a full wall of fresh and organic produce lines the main wall in the market, displayed seemingly effortless, in crates and baskets. We were greeted with the southern charm you really can't fake and taken to our table. The room was lined with hutches and bureaus filled with knick knacks. Colorful displays of florida kitsch drapes the walls in sea themed and southern belle charms. A gentleman was playing slide guitar to (now) two tables in the dining room. He even covered a Muddy Waters track while we enjoyed our coffee. The coffee is self serve and in the market area. They serve local coffees; I believe from a roaster out of Ybor City. The menu was breakfast and lunch all day. Now if you have never had a mom from the south that can cook like a king, then you NEED to eat here! Some menu items included Cheesy grits, home fries, fresh fruit, and I can't remember the lunches offered. We were there bursing a hangover and wanted the fulfill our dreams. So biscuits and gravy with homefries and a sunnyside up egg was my choice. Our 'server' (slash cook on her day off ;) ) made sure to get the eggs right. I could go on and on about this place being heaven on earth, but I won't. I will mention what they told us while we were finishing up- they have buffet dinners on fridays that serve up a single themed cuisine, like greek, etc. And this coming friday (after our stay in StP) our server was in charge of the southern style buffet, for under $6, serving up home made chicken and dumplings! Now get your butt out of here and head on down to Angie's!

text: I've eaten at every Thai restaurant in town several times -- this one the most, and I've eat Thai across the US at least once a week for the past 10 years, so I think I'm being pretty objective here. Compared to better options in town (Thai Orchid, Jasmine Thai), Thai Papaya is expensive for low quality food with spotty service.. Overall the food just seems slopped together with no unifying flavors or exceptional freshness, both of which are always associated with good Thai. The sauces are aren't that good - they are oily, often separating like they were refrigerated then reheated, and just don't taste that good. One exception, the fried bananas for dessert are really good. They do a decent Pad Thai as well. Their take out and and eat in menus have different numbers, so they screw up your take out orders, if they can manage to understand your perfectly spoken English. Service is hit or miss. Lately, they've hired an extremely friendly seemingly good waitress, but I've been there plenty of times where you get no service and have to wait for everything. This is just a shoestring operation that lacks quality, fresh ingredients and good service, yet is priced identically to restaurants that are clean, exceptionally good service and great food. If you are saying no!, please try Thai Orchid or Jasmine Thai then tell me this is still 5 stars

text: As anyone with a pet knows, your pet is your family and you only want the best for your family. Choosing a vet was not an easy choice. We asked around for several recommendations and finally settled on the same vet our breeder uses. Our breeder warned us that Dr. Altom at North HIlls Veterinary Clinic was a no-nonsense type of guy. If our baby wasn't sick he would tell us. If it wasn't something serious he wouldn't make a big deal just because we were freaking out. Our first time there, we actually had Dr. Gonzales. He's a really friendly vet with a lot of experience. However, he was a bit too hand holding for us. Don't get us wrong, I'm sure that are many other people who would enjoy (need) this type of service. We prefer someone a little more direct so we know when to worry and really stress or be mindful of our baby. Dr. Altom is our type of guy! We like the fact that he is familiar with our breed, Shiba Inus, as he is our breeder's vet. More importantly he is not limited to small animals, he also provides services to horses. We really like the fact that he is very familiar with our breed as they aren't common. North Hills Veterinary staff is stellar!!! They are super friendly and extremely professional. They made Saya feel welcomed on her first visit and she is quite the star every time we bring her. We love that they show a passion for animals and it translates well in the environment they create. We appreciate the reminders that come in the mail addressed to Saya letting her know she needs to notify us that she's due for a shot or a check up. Also they are great about working our schedules, especially when we have to reschedule at the last minute. We know our girl is in good hands here. Dr. Altom is our family vet and we highly recommend him and the staff at North Hills Veterinary Clinic!!!

text: Nothing like setting the night off proper. In the adult sense of course. A few of us got together for a nice cultural evening at the opera and decided to do dinner beforehand. We decided on Village Whiskey as we are all seasoned whiskey sippers. I've heard the restaurant was good but man... Now, I won't call it a proper restaurant, nor will I call it a pub, but I will call it a great idea that has been executed with style, class, and gusto. It's a small spot a little wider than a narrow bar with some booths and some tables. Simple, clean, and it has elements of both new and old... But enough about that... On to the food. When looking at the menu you almost think to yourself, hrmmm, this is a small menu. And you're right it is small. But the food isn't really the point, the whiskey is. Anyway, this small menu packs a pretty big punch. Since there were 4 of us we ordered a few things and shared. We had the deviled eggs, which would've made your Mennonite grandmother proud, the tater tots which were crunchy on the outside and buttery smooth on the inside, pickled artichokes with some toasted bread and the fried cheese puffs which hot damn... I want a platter next time. We all dug right in and were immediately impressed. The prices on these apps were incredible too. $3 each for most of these at a Garces restaurant??!? What!?! Sweet! The whiskey. The menu was HUGE! Our server was knowledgeable and if we had questions about a particular whiskey she was happy to give a brief synopsis. The specialty drink menu was also a force to be reckoned with. I had an "Old Fashioned" that would have made my father proud. My buddy Mike had the APA which consists of a few awesome ingredients like hops infused vodka and egg whites. Sounds strange but tastes amazing. The main course - Because whiskey isn't dinner. I had the Village Burger. I am going to go ahead and rank this burger up there with some of the best burgers in the city. I ordered it medium and it came medium. Check! I topped it with bacon, gruyere cheese, and caramelized onions. The flavor of the fresh grass fed beef was incredible. My wife had the pulled pork and that too was incredible. The pork was nice and tender, juicy, and flavor packed. We split a side of the duck fat fries with the cheese sauce too. These fries are to die for. In the end we left fat and happy. The awesome whiskey list had us buzzing and the great eats left us jolly. We waddled our way over to the opera and had a great night. Village whiskey gets the win.

text: Took the Parents to lunch today at the Persian Grille. I hadn't been here since I was a young teen, about twenty years ago. The parents have been there since and recommended it. Since I had been there last, they really turned this into a nice restaurant. It is tastefully decorated in a contemporary-Persian décor. They have a full bar (more on that later), and the staff was very friendly and welcoming. I should note that although we were there for lunch (around 1PM) their lunch menu was not available since it was Sunday. That meant that it would be full dinner prices. This would not have changed my decision to go to lunch there, but it did catch me a little off guard, as now lunch would be about $100 for three people. Entrees are in the $18-$20 range. The place was empty when we arrived. By the time we left, it was beginning to fill up. The Parents have been there for dinner and said it gets very crowded. Upon reviewing their beer menu, I was astounded. As a lover of Belgian beer, I couldn't believe that a Persian restaurant was carrying 25 ounce bottles of La Chouffe, Delerium, Corsendonk, Chimay, Duvel, St. Bernardus, Ommegang and others! They weren't cheap, but if you think about the mark up that restaurants put on bottles of wine, $15.99 seemed reasonable to split a big bottle of La Chouffe with Father. Mother had a Stella Artois draught. Again, I don't know why the great selection of Belgians, but I will not complain. We ordered the hummus as an appetizer, which came with warm pita bread. It was mild and delicious, not overwhelming with garlic. Enough for three people to split. For entrees, Father and I both ordered Shereen Polo, which was a roasted, glazed Cornish hen served with wonderful basmati rice containing carrots, pistachio, saffron, almonds and orange. Mother ordered the Addas Polo, which was only offered with lamb or veal. She asked if she could substitute chicken and it was no problem at all. I believe that it was the owner that was serving us. Her rice contained lentils, dates, raisins and almonds. Portions are large and Mother and I both took home leftovers. For dessert we had the Baklava and the Faloodeh Shirazi. The Baklava was good. The Faloodeh is ice-cream like with noodles in the base. It was flavored with rose water. The consistency was fine, but the rose water taste was overwhelming, so much so that I felt that I was eating cheap, rose perfume. It is served with lemon juice and cherry syrup that you are to pour over it. Father really poured it on and ate quite a bit of it. He said that the syrups helped with the rose taste. It may have been the greatest Faloodeh, I think it was just not to my tastes. Overall, I loved the Persian Grille. Although I enjoy sampling different cuisines, I think the food here would appeal to a broad range of taste buds. It is foreign enough to satisfy middle eastern food lovers, yet delicious enough appease the hesitant. I would definitely dine here again. You can tell that the owner takes pride in his restaurant. I would encourage trying the Persian Grille and expanding your horizons.

text: It is difficult to give a mall, a place where many stores are available to the consumer, an overall rating. All the good kids that weren't allowed to hang out at the mall, all the bad kids that did. But parents shopped there, it was busy, clean, convenient. A destination for back-to-school, holiday. everyday and special occasion shopping. Malls, in general, are not what they used to be, having been supplanted by Internet shopping, big box retailers and more. Granite Run Mall still does not have an excuse for its bad behavior. Stores are empty, easily filled with things that resemble flea markets, swap meets and an as-seen-on-television oasis. It is often dark and outside is dirty. On a Friday night it is full of teenagers, mostly the "bad" kids, this time bullying the adults out of any potential opportunity to shop. It is so bad that mall security posts signs outside where kids aren't allowed to gather... I worry for the space...what will take its place? It can't live much longer. What will fill the void?

text: I really like Sunterra, because they don't just focus on organic, like some food markets. Instead, they focus on produce and meats from local farmers. This is a great place to go for breakfast, lunch, or a take-home dinner. Sunterra is a bit like a grocery store, but without the middle aisles of packaged food. The produce section always has a great selection of fresh vegetables and fruit, and the bakery has yummy treats like muffins, scones, cakes, and even pizza for lunch. During lunch time, this place is crazy busy with business-types and mall workers. The deli is perfect for lunch or dinner, which includes cold salads, seasoned cold meats, and side dishes. These are sold by weight and can either be heated for you at the store, or you can take them home. I personally like the samosas and the brocolli & grape salad (as weird as that combination may sound). There's also ready-to-take home or eat-in items like Indian dishes, sausage rolls, hummus, and sandwiches--there's even an impressive salad bar. During thanksgiving and Christmas, Sunterra has traditional take-home meals, and you can also order a locally-produced turkey to cook at home. Recently, Sunterra renovated and now it looks more like a cafe/market. There are more seating areas, which is nice, because I could never find a place to sit during lunch time before. Everything is a bit expensive, but most healthy food is.

text: I would not recommend Dr. Polito for sleep complications not related to sleep apnea. My intention for making (and paying) for an appointment with a specialist is to gain further insight into my condition and additional resources offered through a specialist. However, Dr. Polito offered no new information or resources, everything he discussed in my appointment is available on WebMD or MayoClinic.com. I mentioned a concern that I might suffer from PMDD which triggers anxiety-related sleep problems, a disorder I had to explain to Dr. Polito. He did not approve of menstruation suppression to relieve PMDD, saying that because of my gender, it was natural to suffer from severe depression, anxiety and detriment to my quality of life every month (2). He even suggested marking off a week on a calendar every month during which time loved ones should just ignore what I say and how I feel. Next, Dr. Polito erroneously explained that even after days without sleep, my body will fall asleep when I need to. I refer to studies showing sleep deprivation for over 2 days resulted in cognitive impairment, and over a week in death, and even increased risk for Type 2 diabetes over time (1, 3, 4). His recommendation was to stop being nervous about falling asleep, and that a new perspective would do the trick. Finally, Dr. Polito discussed hormone imbalance in the brain, promoting the use of topical lotions to increase hormone production, which he "doesn't know how it works, don't ask me, but my wife uses it." If I wanted an untested supplement, I would have gone to the grocery store. Dr. Polito offered one gem of advice: when my life becomes less stressful, I could try going off sleep medication. In short, Dr. Polito's recommendation to aid chronic insomnia was a) just deal with severe, crippling effects of PMDD, b) don't be scared of sleep, but a lack of sleep even over a week won't kill you, and c) lotions with no known, recorded, or understood health benefits can balance your sleep-inducing hormones. I do not recommend Dr. Polito for sleep therapy, or a physician in general. References: 1. Durber, J. and D. Dinges. 2005. Neurocognitive consequences of sleep deprivation. Seminal Neurology 25(1): 117-129. 2. Moline, M., et al. 2003. Sleep in women across the life cycle from adulthood through menopause. Sleep Medicine Reviews 7(2): 155-177. 3. Rechtschaffen, R., et al. 1983. Physiological correlates of prolonged sleep deprivation in rats. Science 221(4606): 182-184. 4. Spiegel, K., et al. 2005. Sleep loss: a novel risk factor for insulin resistance and Type 2 diabetes. Journal of Applied Physiology 99: 2008-2019. ...to name a few.

It took about 4 hours (which was the same amount of time it took them the first time I had them tint my windows WITHOUT an appointment!) The theater isn't as nice overall but the movie selection is usually better and the ticket prices from what I recall still beat it out. text: I like this place. It's a bit cavernous so it's hard to go there when it's nice outside because you won't enjoy any of the good weather, but it's perfect for a rainy or cold day. There's a cute bench outside the front window and it's great to sit there with your coffee beneath the tree and sip your drink. Seating is really varied, as in church pews and vintage sofas. Not all of them are comfortable. There's WiFi, but as others have said, it's slow and tends to hang, especially if a lot of people are using it. But you can't complain too much about free, right? Getting power for your device is another problem, though. There are a few outlets but they're not always in accessible places and people do weird, desperate things to plug in their ailing appliances. text: It's nice to, once in a while, come to a place of solitude like the AGA. I've been here three times this summer and I find it the perfect place to unwind and relax in the sublime constructs of this space enjoying some beautiful art The quality of the exhibits are pretty good. I thoroughly enjoyed the Escher exhibit and managed to join the walking lecture on the Warner Bros. exhibit on their art work. Very interesting indeed. The Piranesi exhibit on prisons was also great. Okay - exhibits come and go. I think what's important is that this gallery has 3 storeys with ample exhibition space coupled with a very comfortable and inviting ambience. At a time, I imagine they could have up to 8 different exhibits. The architect, Randall Stout, has given this place more functionality than his ex-boss's (Frank Gehry) works of similar grace. The outside has a very Gehreisc resemblance to it looking almost like a younger brother of the Walt Disney Concert Hall in Los Angeles. The gift shop is cute! They have books on art, Edmonton, artists etc. along with the coffee mugs, jigsaw puzzles and the likes. Given that they have a sort-of childrens' section on the main floor, I think this place would be a good place for families. The guides and other people who work here are quite knowledgeable and clearly enthusiastic about their job. The only downside, as I see it, is that their exhibits don't change as often as they could. If it were an enormously large gallery, that would be a good thing. But given that the exhibit sizes are relatively small, I wish they'd have at least one new exhibit every 2 months.
label: POS

The portion was big enough (and I had enough chips) that I was able to wrap up my second tamale and eat it for lunch the next day. We also ordered two pitchers of the house margarita which was very refreshing on the hot Saint Louis Day. I will definitely be back to try the flavored margaritas, enjoy some more queso and sit on the nice outdoor porch.

text: What a fun restaurant! However, the food is very overrated by my fellow Yelpers. Like others have written, Marrakesh is a Moroccan restaurant. I can't vouch for the authenticity, as I have never been to Morocco or eaten at any other Moroccan restaurant, for that matter. Supposedly it's now trendy to force your customers to knock at the front door-I just think it's cute. Not necessary, but I won't hate on you for making me do it. As for the dining experience: no utensils, no napkins, very dark, very cozy and on soft padded surfaces. Food is a set 7-course meal. Reading these other Yelp reviews, it sounds like the same 7-course meal is offered every time (with some options for some of the courses). Marrakesh serves a very different ethnic taste. Reminiscing back to the meal, it wasn't spectacular, but the atmosphere coupled with the novelty makes it a worthwhile experience. Yes, the whole chicken dish is tender to the point of meat-falling-off-bones. But it tastes like any other cooked-for-a-long-time-in-sauce chicken. Yes, the shish-kabob is stacked with chunks of meat. But it tastes like something I could have slapped together on my own home grill (and theirs isn't as tasty, to be honest). In summary-come to Marrakesh for the fun, but don't come back for the food. My logic is that if you're using the same 7-course set meal every day for who-knows-how-long, that's not a master chef back there in the kitchen, just a seasoned one.

text: Listen up Thompson owners.. What is the deal with the set up. I really don't get it. Why 8 counters - it is so confusing!?! Let me recap my experience: So, I got a safety recall on my Corolla. I called to make an appointment to get it taken care of, and a very nice guy was very friendly on the phone and told me to drop off in the morning and that I would be supplied with a rental car. Sweet. I go there at 8:00 AM. I pull in the parking lot looking for something that resembles a shop/garage/service department. I drive to the shop-looking building in the back. This is the DETAIL center - no service. The man points me toward the showroom building and tells me to valet my car. I pull up to the valet and they give me a ticket and take my car while instructing me to go inside (down some stairs and UNDER the showroom). I go inside, and I am greeted with about 8 counters, almost all with a man behind them, labeled "Red Team", "Gold Team", "Blue Team" etc. (8 colors). All the counters are angled toward me, and I have no idea where to go. I stand in the middle looking lost for about 2 minutes until someone asks, "Can I help you?" I tell the guy I am dropping my car off for service, and he helps me. After some paperwork, he hands me some certificate to go pick up my rental car and points me toward a 9th counter with a big red sign that says "RENTALS". I walk up to the rental counter, and a nice man fills out more paperwork, photocopies my license etc. (typical car-rental bullshit). He tells me to go outside and they will pull my car up. That happens in a reasonable amount of time and I am off to work. 9 Hours Later: I pull up in the rental back in the valet lane. I get out and the guy takes the car and points me back toward the room full of counters. Again, I walk in, look around, and have NO IDEA which counter to go to. I stand there looking lost again, but this time no one comes to my rescue. So, I think about it logically, I have this rental car sheet in my hand (which is all they gave me), so instinctively I head over to the RENTALS counter. But this time no one is there. I wait for about 10 minutes. Finally some teenage girl comes over to me and asks, "Can I help you?" I say, yes, I'm picking up my car. She tells me that I can just go outside and the valet will pull my car around. I try to give her the paper I have and ask her if I have to sign anything, and she says, "Nope, just head right out." I go out to the valet. They ask me for my ticket. I tell them I don't have a ticket, but I saw the man from the morning staple it to some paperwork. They ask me if I went inside, I say yes. At this point the valet guy is confused and says he will be right back, as he walks into the room of counters. He comes back out, and points be back in there, saying that I need to sign some paper, but I have a $0 balance (yippie). I walk in for a third time, and for a THIRD time, I have NO FRICKING IDEA which counter to go to. There is a guy on the phone at "Red Team" with some paperwork in front of him, and another guy looking at me. Finally the "Silver Team" guy asks, "Can I help you?" Again, I tell him I am trying to pick up my car. He asks me if I had a rental. I tell him yes, "Did you return it?" "Yes" I replied. He asks me for my last name and then starts looking through files and papers, looking around on all the desks. Finally, he walks to the biggest counter in the back corner and asks for my paperwork. There it is! My paperwork is at the "CASHIER" counter #10. I sign, they give me my valet ticket, and as I am walking out, I ask the guy about the color team counters.. I said, "What's up with the team counters, it's really confusing." He tells me "Oh, that just helps us keep track of the customers and organize our paperwork." Seriously?? Ok, so you are going to inconvenience and confuse all of your customers just to keep yourselves organized? I would LOVE to meet the guy who thought this set-up was a good idea. It took me 30 minutes to pick up my car. I will never go back - even if I get another safety recall. And it's not the staff, everyone was super nice & courteous (hence the second star).. but the whole user experience sucked. If someone who has power over there is reading this, you should really rethink that whole process..
label: NEG

text: The restaurant has only been open a week, and I'm sure we'll try it again at a later date to see if it has improved, but our experience tonight was very disappointing. We arrived today (Sunday) at 4:45. It was relatively empty, maybe 4-5 tables seated. Our server was friendly and prompt, and we ordered an appetizer and a small pizza to share. The appetizer--Eggplant Marino--was delicious, though a tad soggy. It arrived about 5 minutes after we placed our order, and we finished it at maybe 5:10. At 5:15, our server told us that our pizza should be out shortly. She scored points for dropping off a plate with two of their (absolutely delicious) chicken wings as well, to try for next time. i would love to provide a fair review of the pizza, but by the time we got to eat it it was cold, so I have no idea what one tastes like right out of the oven. While we sat there from 5:15 to 5:50, the place slowly filled up and we watched numerous people get seated and get their food. Our server stopped by 2 or 3 times and told us the pizza should be there shortly, but it never arrived. To show how delayed it was, the family that arrived the same time as we did finished their food, paid, and the next family seated at that table got their pizza before we did. Finally at 5:40 we told the server that we needed the pizza to go (since a friend was coming to our house at 6), and we finally got our boxed pizza and a check at 5:50. I was shocked that no one came to apologize for the delay, though the manager walked by and looked at us and our empty table several times. We ate the pizza when we got home (late to meet our friend) and it was tasty but cold. It would have been better hot (I'm sure) but the cheese was no longer melted and the toppings had gotten cold. We paid the full price for our meal and left with a "come again soon!" from the very friendly hostess. Will we come again soon? Not likely. But we might give it another chance again in a few months after they work out all the kinks. Again, very disappointing service, but decent food.
