text: So when my firm moved to Blue Bell from Conshy(I used to be a block away from work) I could see no upside. Until someone put a bug in my ear about a Mexican Restaurant that gave away complimentary Margaritas. Now you can't really tell the story of the Margaritas until you have actually been there because no one will believe you and you don't have any proof that they exist. (RANDOM TANGENT ALERT)It's like telling people about first time home buyers tax credit. I'm not listening to anyone that hasn't had to personally go through the steps AND received their money. I don't know who designed this place but it feels as if you are intruding on someones private party. Once you walk in there is a Host stand with no host and the doors leading into the dining room are closed. Hopefully one of the waitresses sees you outside looking like a dummy and pops outside to tell you to take a seat. It was a Tuesday night so there wasn't a crowd, but I can see how 20-30 people in there could have you starting to feel cramped. First thing our waitress did was pour the legendary complimentary margaritas with the *disclaimer that they were free if you planned on ordering an entree. I'm good with that if you keep em flowing. AND THEY DID. Honestly, I don't know the name of what I ordered. App: Chicken wrapped in something and then fried. Meal: Chicken and steak w/ flour tortillas. Good sized portions and pretty quick on the draw too. But it all comes back to the 'Ritas. First I had to ask if they had liquor in it. Then I had to ask if everyone saw the room moving like I did. The prices were on average with a well maintained and fresh Mexican restaurant. Want cheaper prices go to Taco Bell, or even worse Q'Doba. Me? I stick with the free 'Ritas.

text: I have been going to the Marrakesh since 1979 or 80 while growing up in Center City. My last trip was last week on July 12th this year. Marrakesh is currently celebrating it 30th year. Kim P's 9/21/2006 review was great (and the pictures of her are gorgeous!); and I am glad she and her group had a great time. One question she raised was the lack of wine selection. I am wondering if they charged her for the wine since they are currently giving it away in celebration of the 30th year. Free wine is just one of the ways the Marrakesh shows you they care about their customers. They don't have a liquor license. They are happy to give you free wine and they are happy to let you BYO. While much of the Philly's Center City dining scene seems to be a reflection of places in New York with weeks long waiting lists and rediculous prices, Marrakesh is a happy reminder for me of now defunct places like Freddy's Pizza (which became JJs Grotto) Pagganos in U of P (the Paggano special rocked) that I liked gorwing up. text: I just got back from Hot Tamales for lunch today...I can feel the stomache ache brewing already. Take the bland decor, not that the decor has much to do with the quality of your lunch, but it's like a cafeteria. The food isn't much better, which as others have duly noted, has absolutely no flavor...Hot Tamales? What's so hot about it? Even the hotsauce is bland, it came right from the soulless bowels of Aramark. Would it hurt that bad to invest in some seasonings? I got a chicken taco salad, which was huge, but not very satisfying to my taste buds, and a "crunch-n-munch burrito" ...OK whoever thought it would be a cute idea to name a burrito crunch-n-munch deserves a lobotomy. It was supposed to be Turkey, but I noticed no difference in taste or texture from what I would imagine is their ground beef. Service was satisfactory as far as I'm concerned, but apparently they are rude and snappy if your order isn't as fast and coordinated as the Soup Nazi's soup stand. My friend likened this place to Taco Bell, but with better ingredients...maybe the next step up if you ask me, but not by much. Go here expecting the following: cheap food, filling portions, a stomache ache. Don't go here expecting any of the following: authenticity, flavor, atmosphere, a reason to go back.

text: Positive Review: ULTA has a very nice selection. Their "name brand" products are of fair quality. But I'd have to say it's their SERVICE that will keep me from returning ever again. I'm not a huge consumer of these products, but maybe 2-3 times a year I'll drop a $100 each time. About a year ago I received a % coupon from Sephora. I had a few other errands to run in the same center as ULTA so I brought my Sephora coupon along and asked if they'd honor the competitor coupon for the same products. "No-" was their curt answer. There was no offer or suggestion of maybe what they "could" do otherwise to earn my business. Just, "No" and a stare. I left, and went to Sephora, who earned my money. Out of convience, I had other shopping to do in this same strip mall, once again. I grabbed a cart and knocked off each errand along this outside mall while loading each purchase bag I made in the same cart (I know I was cart-double-dipping-lol!) I also was carrying my 10 month old son in this cart as well (multi-tasking!) I was ready to give ULTA another try. As I was browsing the new fall nail colors, a somewhat stern blonde employee quickly approached me and asked me to please leave with my cart. She explained that although she saw I was pushing an infant and was hauling other bags that their "shelves were not designed nor sturdy enough in the event I pushed into one with my cart". Maybe if she had offered to hold my bags behind the counter, or helped me with my purchases while I used my hands to hold my son, I would have stayed. But again, there was NO effort made to keep or earn my dollar. There was no apology for the situation. Not even a half-ass compassion attempt. My happy little boy, wallet and I walked our butt out of ULTA for the very last time. (While passing a woman and her baby in a stroller- so how is THAT exactly less of a shelf hazard than the cart I was pushing???) Especially in todays economy it's no excuse to be this poor with customer service. Thank goodness for capitalism. And thank goodness for the Sally Beauty Supply next door to ULTA. Not only was my purchase less expensive there but they were very helpful in helping me (and the cart I was pushing!) find my needed products.

text: I wanted to give this place more but Yelp says 2 stars is "I've had better".. and I definitely have. This is a small aquarium with limited amounts of everything except noisy obnoxious kids. Although I should preface and say in case Emerlyn reads this, that I'm not looking a gift horse in the mouth. I appreciated the VIP tickets and the discount!! Anyway, this place has a smattering of aquatic creatures, some jellyfish, sharks, fish, frogs, etc. 2 hippos, a number of birds, penguins and seals. Nothing out of the ordinary. Three (maybe unassociated to the quality of the aquarium) complaints: - Is it necessary to have ice cream and fried foods everywhere IN AN AQUARIUM? Goodness knows Americans don't need more of this! - Is it necessary to bring SO MANY badly behaved kids? Or babies who are so young they can't comprehend or learn anything from the experience, but instead can only contribute to annoying others? - They should tell parents to bring a baby backpack. It was impossible to walk anywhere with all the strollers in the way. The "special" exhibits like the seal feeding, etc. I should've guessed catered towards the younger children in the audience.. nothing really entertaining or enlightening could be garnered from them for the average adult. In all of the aquariums I've been to, this is a distance 3rd and I've only been to 3. The other 2 - the Kaiyuukan in Osaka and the Baltimore Aquarium - towered in scope and layout in comparison to this place. Overall, an underwhelming experience. Although I got to poke a seaslug and I was surprised how squishy it was since when I ate one raw last week, it was really crunchy.

text: When you walk in the door, you'll smell the sweet aroma of cigarette smoke and desperation. Your first inclination will be to turn around. But keep going. The level of people watching be on par with National Geographic. This is Nashville at its finest (or most pathetic) depending on your dayjob, level of self-respect, and how long you've lived here. The drinks are cheap and sold in plastic cups. Good start. On the small stage, they'll have an acoustic act playing an assortment of trailer park anthems and highschool party favorites. Getting better. At this point, if you're smart, you'll realize the night is probably a wash and accept it for what it is. Losers ain't about self-respect, baby. The crowd is extremely diverse. It runs from twenty-something songwriter/musicbiz/whatever types to fifty-something songwriter/musicbiz/whatever types. Occasionally you might see a geezer in a track suit make his way through the crowd. The MILFs will murmur: was that Kenny Rogers? Or just a geezer in a track suit? With Loosers, you never know. In the heyday of the Nashville music biz--before it imploded and began hemorrhaging money by the truckload--deals went down in these dives. Now it's mostly people trying playing the part. Nonetheless, it's still fun to watch. Whether a local or a tourist, you owe it to yourself to visit this place once. Go on in, order a Tanqueray and Tab, and enjoy the show.

text: Yes, this place is cheap. However, I still expect them to deliver what they promise. This place did not. We chose this place because it had free WiFi and coffee in the room. There was a coffee maker, but no coffee or filters. When we asked the guy at the front desk about this, he said they just ran out of coffee but he might be able to hunt down some decaf for us. Later we found out that we just could have gone next door anytime we wanted for free coffee 24 hours a day. He never divulged this information to us during our stay. On top of the missing coffee, they also "just ran out of internet". He stated that they had a storm recently and didn't have any idea when the internet would be turned back on. The last day we were there, we were able to connect, but it was very slow and very spotty. Upon check-out, the lady told us that there had been a storm but the internet was back up and should have been working. Also, the bathroom was a little dirty when we first checked in. The shower wasn't all that clean and my mom said she saw some hairs in there (that didn't belong to any of us). Reading someone else's review who said the same thing, maybe they leave hairs behind as souvenirs here. Who knows! And finally, to top everything else, we came home late the first night and our key got stuck in the gate. Luckily there was someone there to let us in/help us get the key out of the gate, but it could have not been fun if someone hadn't been there. Their name is also pretty deceiving. The location of this place was a little further from all the action than I would have originally liked. I don't know the boundaries of what is actually considered "The French Quarter" but this place doesn't seem to warrant such a name, in my opinion. Oh yeah! They also charge you $25/night for parking. Something they don't mention on their website or during your booking of this place. So, just beware. They were nice enough to comp our parking due to our experience, but $50 for a 2 night stay can sure make a difference if you're not preparing for that ahead of time...

text: My first stop en route to the French Quarter was to Haydel's Bakery on Jefferson Highway - easily found in the light Saturday morning traffic I reached the small bakery around 11:00am only to find a line snaking out the door - right up to the famous bead dog where a nice local fellow later volunteered to snap a picture. Waiting in the line for less than 20 minutes (if only Café Du Monde were so efficient!) and hearing the Black&Gold song followed by the Superbowl Shuffle I loved the energy of the store - 99% locals talking about their Mardi Gras plans, how many years they'd been coming to Haydel's, and what parades they were looking forward to most...and those Saints. Making my way to the front of the line I was greeted by a young man who offered me samples of the plain, cream cheese, and cherry King Cakes from a small tray and when I asked him which he suggested he stated "oh, the praline filled version for sure." Taking his advice I received a medium (supposedly enough to serve 20) that was still warm from the oven, paid, and made my way to the street. Getting back into my car I tore off a small piece - then a little more...and then a little more until I'd finished almost 1/6 of the cake. Having never had a King Cake before I was surprised by the buttery croissant-like texture and shocked by the amount of nuance in a simple cake - notes of cinnamon and vanilla plus nutmeg clearly notable under the hefty dose of cinnamon sweet frosting. Filling the cake was a thick caramel pecan filling that tasted unmistakably like a creamy praline. Knowing there was a lot of eating to be done I wrapped the cake up and placed it in the shade of the trunk before making my way to the quarter...I would subsequently finish the cake over the next 2 days and found the baby (clearly meaning I needed to buy the next one...for myself) on the morning of Lundi Gras.

text: My boyfriend and I wanted to go to the opening of BBP in Philly last Tuesday night, but with 4 young kids between us we decided to wait. Thank God we did. We went on Friday night - sans kids - and the line was insane! That being said, the one hour wait in line was well worth it. Folks are commenting on how there was only one cashier working - I made the same comment to my boyfriend when we got in the door to which he pointed out that if they moved the line along any quicker by adding another cashier there'd be no seats. And there were seats available which at first was surprising given the number of people in line and the relatively small size of the place. We sat right down at the counter. It is worth mentioning that the wait staff was super friendly and accommodating...be interesting to see if that lasts past the first week. Anyway, on to the food...I had the LA Burger and I fretted over this decision the entire hour I was in line because there were so many good ones to chose from. Turns out it was probably one of the best burgers I've ever had. It doesn't come with any sauce on it and I never even thought to put ketchup and mustard (my normal burger combo) on it because the flavor of the burger was just so damn good I didn't want to mask it with anything else. My boyfriend had the Ceasar burger which was the April burger of the month. We taste tested each others burger. He said mine was better than his. He was right. But, the pepper flavor on his burger was super delish. I agree with some other reviewers that the fries left a litte something to be desired. We got the sweet potatoe fries and the regular fries. Sweet potatoes were probably the best I've had, but I'm not gaga over sweet potatoe fries so I was more interested in the regular fries. They were a litte disappointing because they really weren't seasoned. No salt, no spices, nada. The dipping sauce was tasty and I was thankful to have it to dip my unsalted, unspiced fries. I actually dipped my fries in all of the sauces at the counter and loved them as well - especially the Chipotle Ketchup. We also split the Vanilla Caramel Bourbon shake. Wow, that was a good shake. Try the shake. I want the pistachio one next time - no alcohol, but I love pistachio ice cream. Bottom line on BBP - you've got to go. They hype on a Food Network star opening a burger chain will not let you down. Bobby knows how to make a great burger and uses the best quality meat to do it. I can't wait to go back and try another one.
label: POS

text: This place is great. I picked it based on the reviews here (wanting to inject some culture into the lives of my boyfriend and his college roomate) and found the one about the guy who likes Pearl Jam to be very helpful. First I need to talk about the service I received before we even got there. I called on a Friday night for reservations for Saturday at 600pm. The man who answered the phone said they were booked but wasn't hanging up the phone on me. He asked for my number and said he'd call back if he could move some tables around to make room for us. I didn't think I'd here back. While at the Philadelphia Museum of Art, we got a phone call asking if 530 was okay instead of 6. We took it and it ended up working better in our itinerary anyway. We had to drive around a bit for parking (I now can joke about trying to park in Philly - Golosa, too!). Once we got there the waitstaff was so quick and friendly. The wine came quick - which in my book means the place is alright - and the food came quickly as well. Our dishes were lasagna, chicken parm and a sea food special with risotto. Everyone loved their meals. Finally, the best part. How can you argue with great food and free entertainment? The waiters singing opera were amazing. I was very pleased that we were able to see and hear our own waiter up there before we left. I highly recommend this restaurant. Victor's is classy, kitschy, delicious and fun - even for guys who think the opera is for boring snobs. I would have given them four stars for the terrible parking and awkward neighborhood but the whole experience of the place was too amazing to give it any less than five. ONE TIP: Make your reservation as early as possible!

text: I really wanted Alma de Cuba to be a 5 star restaurant, but despite my lofty expectations, the gf and I were still able to enjoy a nice meal. The first impression offered by Alma is the decor. There is a small entryway with a few steps up to the entrance to the restaurant. Once you walk in, you're struck by the backlit mosaic bar and the stenciled glass seperating the various sections of the space. The second floor dining room features a white wooden ceiling with recessed red light boxes and several ceiling fans that create an feeling of sitting on a porch on a hot day. The service managed to be attentive and polite without being intrusive. Always a plus in my book. We were seated promptly and our food came quickly. The meal was good, and with lower expectations, I would even say it was great. The skirt steak was prepared very well but was served with a rather plain white rice and black bean combo. Delicious food, no doubt, but not what one comes to an upscale restaurant to eat. Paired with the steak was a tomato based sauce that I can only liken to a sweet salad dressing. It didn't ruin the meal, but I left most of it on the plate. The truffled asparagus appetizer was tasty, as were the small sweet rolls that are served before the meal. I had the Hamachi Nikkei ceviche to start, and while I didn't know it at the time, that was the best thing I would eat that night. The Brazo Gitano for dessert was a nice way to finish the night. All in all, Alma de Cuba is likely to feed you something that is delicious. I look forward to coming again sometime outside of Restaurant Week to explore the menu a little more thoroughly in the hopes that I overlooked some of the better menu items.
label: POS

text: After being a hermit through most of my pregnancy and several months of motherhood my hair looked like a long shapeless mop. Being new to the Nashville area I had no idea where to go and Yelped Salon Ya Ya. After booking an appointment with Reyna ( I do hope I've spelled it correctly) I nervously awaited the date. Generally, I am not a salon hair girl. I had my guy back in West New York, NJ (across the river from NYC) an amazing hair artist from Cali, Colombia who did my hair fabulously for $20. That's how things go in WNY but alas WNY is far away now. I should not have worried so much. Reyna and the other staff members at the salon were courteous and hospitable. I did not feel out of place or feel scorned or dismissed (something which can happen very very frequently at NYC salons). Reyna offered me a beverage and proceeded to settle me into her station. She listened to what I had to say. She examined my hair and took a moment before diving in. She recommended a moisturizing treatment which I chose to have done but at no moment did it feel pushy. And though she did recommend a shampoo she wasn't pushing product as many ladies at other salons tend to do. She washed my hair and gave me a mini scalp massage. She chatted with me but did not over chat ( another thing I detest at salons). She was genuine, down to earth, and a very good hair stylist. She also did not opt to lop off more hair than necessary...another quality to treasure! All in all my experience at Salon Ya-Ya was pleasant and 100% satisfactory. My only complaint is that I moved so I cannot make Reyna my go-to hair lady. Alas...my loss but hopefully someone else's gain!

text: Wow...I really wish I could say I like biking this trail because I'm really glad the city of St. Louis is trying...but...well...try harder??? They have put in some pathed sidewalks on the river's edge and the new footbridge across the river between Gravois and Morganford is actually really nice, but the bike path...well...it just leaves a lot to be desired. The path runs from Lindenwood St. near the Metro Link, down the side of River Des Peres down near Highway 55. The path is fairly flat which is good for less experienced bikers, but that said, the trail is NOT well maintained...which is horrible for inexperienced bikers. There are ton of cracks and rocks all over the thing. It is only 4 miles long and takes a lot of random bends and turns for no apparent reason. Also, lets remember, you riding along the side of River Des Peres. In high school my friends and I maturely referred to this thing as River Des Pew. Is a sewage run off really what you want to be inhaling when you are trying to ride or run? Not so much. On the upside, it's never crowded, and you don't have to fight your way around baby strollers, but there's a reason for this...the path is just....well...sub par... I suggest avoiding this one and just heading further south to Grant's Trail or sticking with Forest Park...trust me you'll be glad you did.

text: Perfect except one minor thing that just seems to be the way it is these days - the noise level is higher than I would like - so while they can accomodate groups, it can be hard to hear from one end of the table to another. text: My bf and I adopted two adorable kittens through ACCT/PSPCA over Labor Day weekend, and while we went to the ACCT headquarters for the paperwork, I have now been to the PSPCA headquarters multiple times due to one of our kittens. We decided to adopt a brother and sister who were being fostered by an amazing foster mom, and we wanted to pick them up ASAP after their surgery. I got a call the evening of their scheduled visit from the foster mom telling me that the boy was unable to get his surgery due to an undescended testicle. And so the epic saga began. I was able to 'adopt' him temporarily as a foster myself (since PSPCA doesn't allow you to adopt animals that aren't fixed), and told I had to reschedule his surgery for when he's big enough to handle the surgery. Over a week ago I brought him in at the ungodly hour of 7am to be neutered, and when I arrived that evening to pick him up they told me they COULDN'T FIND the undescended testicle. FML. They explained what they did, that its possible he doesn't have another one but we won't know until I bring him BACK in a month to check if he's developing sexually. They gave me some painkillers for him since he had two major incisions on his belly and he had a plastic collar on so he couldn't reach his incisions (one held together with stitches, the other with glue). The collar ended up being too small and we realized a few days into his recovery that he COULD reach his incisions and was licking them, possibly causing some minor bleeding and maybe beginning to infect himself. We called Jessie, who had left her number in case we had any questions, and made an appointment with her the next morning. She saw me immediately, took a look at his belly herself, then showed it to a surgeon who had operated on him and also one of their primary doctors who had also operated on him. They all agreed it didn't look bad (and that the collar was WAY too small for him), but while the glued incision was healing well the stitched one looked a little infected. They put a larger collar on him, gave me both oral and topical antibiotics, and told me to bring him back in a week to remove the stitches. The best part of all of this treatment is that not only was it all free as part of his neutering surgery (since its technically not done - YET), but both Jessie and Dr. Howard talked to me about him and what they saw and what I could do, answered all my questions, and handled him like he was their pet. These people are wonderful and they do not get enough credit for all the hard work they do, and the GOOD they do on a daily basis. They are an extremely organized place, and CLEAN and MODERN facilities from what I saw. Go and adopt one of the many wonderful animals in need of good homes, and help support the PSPCA's efforts!

What I didn't like was the owner of the business not knowing what a large salad looked liked compared to a small salad. Also, having difficulty in using the register. I understand that if you own a business, you do not have to be the one operating it. But, if you're going to operate as the manager, you should know how to do each job. text: Personally, I hate when restaurants pick too many kinds of food to "specialize" in. Invariably, you end up with a ton of mediocre food, instead of a smaller number of well-made dishes. Pan-Asian? Just think of how many countries and cuisines that encompasses. So yeah, Zoe is a nice restaurant, pretty plating, flavor combinations that sound interesting on paper, but the actual dishes pale in comparison to what you would get at a restaurant that actually served Thia, or Indian, or whatever kind of food. I had the wok-seared salt shrimp with mango yogurt sauce. Sounds good, right? The waiter warned me that the shrimp were meant to be eaten with the shells still on. Ok, no problem. I could do without the little legs and things, but whatever, I'm adventurous. Except that the flavors of the cooking couldn't penetrate the shells, so the outsides tasted great, and the insides were totally bland and pointless. One of my companions had the curried chicken, and it was completely nondescript. I think it was supposed to be a Thai-style curry, but it was so generic, they only way you could tell was from the peanut sauce. Finally, my other companion had the tempura calamari, and it was chewy. That's just poorly done. Don't bother with Zoe, pick an ethnicity, and go to a real restaurant.

text: Local olive oils and vinegars, sold by the ounce from large silver urns called fustinos, that's the short version. Long version: I'd walked by this shop several times in the past, never when they were open. It looked sparse inside, with lots of silver urns. I didn't know how a specialty shop like this would make it. But then I got to sample their wares at a local wine and food event called Taste of the Town, and I started to understand that they have a good product. Like a 25 year old balsamic vinegar that's thick and tangy and sweet and an amazing price tag of $26 for 375 ml. Expect to pay upwards of $100 normally, and more if you want a DOP variety. Still, with that location and such specialization, it's going to be tough. And even tougher if they weren't going to be open on Sundays, which was the day I was most likely to have time to make the trip to that area. Well, this Sunday past, we drove by and the door was open!! We zipped right in and discovered they're now open on Sundays. Yay! All the fustinos have spigots, so you can sample whatever you want. These containers are air tight, and keep the oils away from light, so they stay fresh. The oils are mostly olive, and mostly produced locally or within California. Only a few highly specialized items, like the truffle infused oil or the 25 year balsamic, come from elsewhere. All the oils and vinegars are well labeled with good information about the source and flavor. Of course, you should try it for yourself and see what your personal tastes prefer. The vinegar section had a lovely range as well. Pomegranate vinegar, pear vinegar, champagne vinegar, all delicious. We bought a bottle of the 25 year balsamic, and a very small bottle of toasted sesame oil. Wow, the sesame oil was so light tasting, and still with a clear sesame flavor. The man behind the counter said it was that way because it's so fresh. If you bring in your own container, which they highly recommend, you'll get a small discount. Or if you bring in your old il fustino bottle, you'll get a dollar off your refill. The shop also had a small art gallery for viewing, and they hold tastings and cooking classes. You can tell the owners are very passionate about their oils and vinegars, so if you're a similar enthusiast, I'm not sure if you can find better freshness and local flavor elsewhere. Photos, photos! I got photos.

text: I know Disney has its weaknesses, but I can't help but still love it. It always brings out the little girl in me who loved to play tea party with her dolls. Yeah, I know, I was a total victim of gender role stereotype! I usually stop by the Disney Store when I'm at Kingsway, because it's the best location in my opinion. Even the one in Vancouver sucks compared to this one. No matter what is playing on their giant flat screen in the back, an old Mickey Mouse cartoon or Raven belting out a tune (hey, that rhymes), my attention is always captured and I will watch for a few minutes. They usually have cute costumes for the kids all year round, but of course, especially during Halloween. The costumes are typically gender stereotyped though, with all the girls' stuff being all pink and poofy like a bunch of tutus, and cowboy and astronaut costumes for the boys. Still, if I were five again, I wouldn't give a damn; I'd still want that pink princess tutu. My favorite part of the store though, is their vintage prints and snowglobe collections. They have framed prints of old and classic movies on one wall, with some original sketches available too (I'm sure these aren't the original original ones, just copies of the real things; as if they'd sell you the real thing!). It reminds you of how Disney used to be like, before it went all computer-animated. Don't get me wrong, I love the new Disney/Pixar films, but the animated classics had a certain quality to them that I'll miss. The snowglobes are also really beautiful, ranging in various sizes from tiny to huge. I love them because they look so fairy-tale like, but they can be for kids or adults.

text: The Italian Market would always be a 5 star experience, but I need to take one away because my memories of Ninth Street as a small boy are so vivid and as indelible as only first experiences can be that it seems to have paled. Too subjective I'm sure. Going with my mother was I knew going to be fun because how can I say this delicately about such a great Mom? She was, well a ballbreaker. She knew that the iceberg, 3 heads for a quarter were for the vendor to pick. So she would take all her time picking the 3 best, hand the guy a quarter and begin to walk away, winking down at me. Hey lady, where you goin wid my salad, this aint the Ac-a-me, I pick em. She returned the goods, picked the biggest and best head and gave him 50 cents. Thus juiced she would make her way north, so many to torment, so little time. On to the fish monger, pick fish first, have them keep them on ice and pick them up when leaving. Fresh fish was a specialty for her and we all loved it. If they saw her coming they knew they were in for a bad time if there were no porgies. There was nothing in her fish world that came close to baked porgy and after a lot of years, I see she could possibly be right. But Mom they have a lot of bones. And? fish without a lot of bones isn't worth eating she would say. She had this kind of food dogma thing going. After dutifully explaining how he had no control whatever over whether the fishermen out of Jersey brought him porgy or not, it was over to other whole fish usually a big striper. Squid and eel filled out her order, and heaven help him next week if there was a single scale on that fish. She wasn't mean she just got a kick out of breaking shoes and I think the vendors really liked her as she really knew her food. While my mother was doing her thing, my father, usually with my uncle would be on their own quest. They wanted 3 things from Ninth Street, cheese, olives and good olive oil usually gallons of Phillipo Berio. First on my father's list was searching for the Holy Grail of Italian cheeses, the perfect provolone. A three pound ball of cow's milk's "leap to immortality" covered in wax and suspended by thick twine so it could be hung until ready. So Dad, what makes a perfect provolone? Well son, its got to have the right sound when you thump it, and when you do have the confidence that it is time and you cut into it, it should be dry enough to have cracked in the center yet moist enough to ooze ever so slightly. Fair enough. So Dad, how many times have you found the perfect provolone? He would glance over to me much the way Vince Gardenia would glance at Cher in "Moonstruck" and say low and in a grave voice. "once"! OK! My family was very serious about their food. Satisfying himself with a ripe piece of Gorgonzola, "Siggie" olives, glistening and impressively shriveled and the P. Berio cold pressed, his Ninth Street fix might last 2 weeks max, then on once again to the Search! For me the Street has changed. Not to sound xenophobic, but the Asian and Hispanic vendors have changed the market, inevitably but still. Not for better or for worse just different. It is no longer the black hole of southern Italian culture, a completeness of experience so involving that while you were there, this seemed to be the way things should be. I still need my Ninth Street fix. Talluto's, " you cant get a half pound of home mades Hon, only pounds" , Claudio's for the buratta, the wonderful selection of fish at the Viet's on the east side, and always Giordano's though despite the sometimes dubious quality of their fruits and produce, always a walk through of Giordano's, much like genuflecting when entering a church.

text: So far this place has met my expectations in Korean restaurants. Hmart foodcourt and other Korean restaurants have not been able to satisfy my craving for the "right" korean food, but this place did. I had Beef SoonDooBoo on my first visit and it tasted just right. I wished there were a little more vegetable in there. It was during lunch and the price was pretty decent - $11. Went for the 2nd time - had BoSsam and Dolsot Bibimbop. The place was crowded and it took awhile to order our food..I recall that there were only about 3 servers for about 15-18 tables..they were very busy. Banchan was great! I was very surprised to see "Jang Jo Rim" - beef brisket in soysauce- since you don't see them often. Impressive. Bibimbop's sauce - chili paste- was somewhat too sweet for my taste. It was probably made to fit non-Korean's taste.. eh. It had good amount of vegetable and rice,though. It's a healthy tasty meal. Bossam was great! It's steamed pork with cabbage, seasoned raddish and OYSTERS. I strongly recommend this dish. [[Technique to eat this entree: wrap the piece of meat, raddish OR kimchi and oysters to eat it. Dip the meat in salted (small) shrimp sauce (saewoojut) before you wrap it.]] I'm excited to try the BBQ. If BBQ's good, this place will probably become #1 Korean restaurant for me in Philly.
label: POS

text: If you want arrogant waiters and slow service, this is the perfect restaurant. I took my out-of-town boyfriend here with a good friend, after the place was recommended by my cousin. We didn't make reservations, but put in our name around 10 o'clock PM and were told the wait would be an hour, which was fine. Luckily, our buzzer went off after a half hour and were seated promptly thereafter. Seeing as it was 10 PM and had already eaten, we simply went to the restaurant for dessert and drinks. Upon introducing herself and explaining the tapas concept - how all the dishes are small and meant to be shared with the whole table - we explained to the waitress that we just wanted dessert. She retorted that the booth in which we were sitting was "just for dinner." At 10 PM? This was never made known to us beforehand, and my boyfriend unhappily ordered one dish off the dinner menu - lobster mac and cheese - which was disappointing and something I could probably find in the frozen section of a grocery store. I should add here that the portions are very small. Though the owner intends for everyone to share, the tapas themselves are not large. So, if someone drags you here...you might want to eat before you go. Anyhow, we eventually got around to ordering dessert, which was only okay, and, yet again, not large enough to be shared with an entire table. Moral of this restaurant experience, don't come here just for dessert and don't come here expecting to leave full. Philly has much better restaurants to offer; don't take out-of-towners here. It doesn't leave lasting impressions, aside from the retro decor.
label: NEG

text: I don't know how I feel about a Thai restaurant that doesn't have very good tom kha gai soup. When I ordered it last night it had so much... stuff in it. Bay leaves, ginger chips, other things that I know not what they are, save for the fact that I cannot eat them. Everywhere else that I've had TKG they strain away the unnecessaries, leaving me with milky, savory goodness--I don't need you to leave the spices and herbs in the soup to know that its made well; I assume its made well by the price point of $5 a bowl. All I ask for $5 is that, for the sake of my never-ending hunger, you take everything out of the soup that I cannot eat. Time spent picking bay leaves out of my mouth could be spent better elsewhere, like on your fish cakes appetizer. Overall, I found the King and I to be alright. My beef dish, suggested by our waitress when I asked "what is the one dish on the menu Thai people eat," was not impressive--apparently the Thai people she knows love the taste of tough and sinewy beef strips stir-fried in peppers. The lady friend thought the pad thai was good, but not great; the fish cakes appetizer was really good though. Overall I'd say the only really great thing about my visit to King and I was a.) the bus boy came over, took one look at me and said, "you need more rice, right?" God bless you my Asian brother for recognizing that the ridiculously miniscule amount of rice you give to the general public is not enough to satiate a grown-ass Asian male, and b.) I broke down and got a "Siam Stinker" cocktail because I've honestly never drank alcohol out of a tiki statuette. I spent the rest of the evening making my cup dance, chanting "ooga-booga, ooga-booga," and pretending I was Peter Brady, and my liquor chalice was cursed. Needless to say, my girlfriend was not amused--damn you unlucky Tiki charm!

text: I used to order from Dominck's all the time -- and was always happy. Last night however was a completely awful experience.I called for a delivery order around 5:15 when my boyfriend and I got home from work. We got 2 salads and an order of the Jack Daniels hot wings. I got a very short "it's on it's way" and hung up on AGAIN. A few moments later, the delivery driver called me from his cell phone and asked for more specific directions cause "he didn't want to waste his time looking for my house number." 10 minutes later he called back and said he was outside in the parking lot and didn't know what door he was supposed to come to (despite the fact that when I placed the order I specifically gave them the apt # and told them it was the door on the right on the first floor...whatever). We FINALLY got our food and were terribly disappointed...our salads were warm (which was especially disgusting cause they both had meat and cheese on them) and ALL of the cherry tomatos on both of our salads were squished and rotting. The wings WOULD have been tasty, if they weren't ice cold by the time they finally got to us...and were lacking any condiments (no celery, bleu cheese etc that normally come with wings). text: I had a dream once that my childhood house in Manayunk was swept up by a tornado and was casted to a magical world where had landed on the wicked witch of East Passyunk. Lucky me. Greeted by people shouting "Speak English!" and "Sopranos!". Dizzy with confusion a middle-aged woman sporting a coffee in sweatpants saying "Juicy" where the sun don't shine tells me if I want to return home I need to find the "Whiz of Geno's". But beware of the "King of Steaks". The people tell me to follow the "Pash E. Unk Road" and with my lil' dog we journey down the magical street passing tanning spas, realtors, salons, cheese shops, gyms and more tanning spas. After befriending a smelly old man, a drunken Eagle's fan, and an illegal alien we arrive to a tower of neon proportions complete with a blown-up photograph of a cheese steak. As we approach an angry beast wielding a spatula blocks our path. "You must be the King of Steaks" I state and the man smirks and replies "I'll make you an offer you can't refuse. I'll toss in some free fries." It was a good offer but not good enough... "NEVER!" and I turn to whisper in the Eagle's fan ear. The fan goes ape shit and pummels at what was the "King of Steaks". Now what did I say in his ear you might ask? "We won the Super Bowl." At last the quest is finished. "What do you want?" cries out a man behind the counter. "The Whiz please!" I said with confidence as he hands me a cheese steak made with 100% whiz. "Oh... this is it? What a rip off!" "Well just click your heels together fag!" shouts the smelly old man. "Que?" asks the illegal alien. So I do and everyone laughs at me for wearing ruby slippers, clicking my heels, outside of "Geno's" at 2am. The only problem about this dream is that it is not a dream. This place, this Oz, this timeless void does exist. It's open day and night all year round for you. Come and experience it for yourself. Be mesmerized by the sheer audacity of it all. This is as close to the "American Dream" as you are going to get. Grab a steak wrapped in a copy of the "Declaration of Independence" for your educational purposes. There is so much to gain. (Waistline that is.)

text: With some places, it's not about one big thing that went wrong, it's just a ton of little things piled up. I would probably not have stayed here if my business meeting hadn't been planned for here by another organization, as I prefer historic hotels or B&B's. However, just evaluating this place against your standard "business hotel", although the location is pretty good (right on the Quarter), the bed is comfy and the staff is reasonably friendly, I probably will not want to stay here again for any reason. There is a weird ticking noise in the walls of my bathroom. Fortunately it's confined to the bathroom and I think it's the plumbing, not a bomb, but it's driving me nuts having to hear TICKTICKTICK each time I go in there. The bathroom is also super duper cramped and hard to get in and out of, on the same level as bathrooms I've had in some motels and in tiny budget rooms at tourist hotels (but this room is large). For some inexplicable reason, there are also two mini fridges in my room, one of which has a sign that it's only good for drinks not food, and the other of which has no sign but barely gets cold. I initially thought one fridge was for food and the other was for the minibar but there is no minibar in here. Which is Ok as there are like three liquor stores within hollering distance of the Canal Street exit, but still, for what do I need two marginally operational fridges? Speaking of fridges, my room is cold and I can't find the control for the thermostat to turn the AC down. By contrast, the cold water faucets in the bathroom put out warm water so I basically have two water choices: warm and hot. This is annoying when I need cold water for something (like stain removal, or because I don't usually drink a glass of warm tap water even over ice, and I'm not about to pay money for the bottled water in my room). There is also a large red stain on the carpet between the beds that looks like somebody spilled a glass of wine or grape juice and they just couldn't be arsed to bleach it out. I will say the room service prices are not ridiculously high. However, I was not happy to find that the rooms don't have Wi-Fi (even though just about every other hotel within three blocks seems to, judging by the "List of Available Networks"). I do not travel with an Ethernet cable in this day and age and the hotel, unlike other places that require an Ethernet cable, didn't have one ready to hook you up. I suppose I could have requested one from the desk but I just pulled the one out of the internet jack instead and used that (works fine). They supposedly charge me 14 bux a day for the I-net service combined with phone, which I guess I could put up with if the phone actually worked. I tried to make a local call and some of the numbers will not dial so after five muffed tries I just used my cell. Worst of all are the elevators. There were two fairly large conventions going on over the weekend and even though one has packed up and left, there is still an interminable wait for elevators at certain times, such as when the conference that's still here is starting, and when people are checking in and out. I literally have to build an extra 15 minutes into my schedule for the elevator, that's how long it is taking. There are only 4 elevators serving something like 30 floors and at times one or two of them are out of service. This just isn't enough and isn't working, especially since they scattered the conference attendees on floors all over the building instead of concentrating them all on a couple of floors. Any one or two of these things by themselves would be no biggie, but put them all together they get way annoying. The only reason to stay here would be that you got some rock bottom rate on Priceline. If you're paying above 100 a night (which I am even with the conference rate) then do yourself a favor and go someplace else. UPDATE: This is the last straw. I just flushed the toilet twice and the second time it exploded back out of the bowl. Was not clogged, there is just something severely weird with the plumbing. This place is possessed, no WAY will I come back!
label: NEG

text: Ok why isn't everyone going here? Maybe because like me, you are thinking a great restaurant at the Rittenhouse is going to be fancy and stuffy and I'm looking at you Le Bec Fin..., yes... kind of boring. This was the most laid back, fun and romantic brunch in the city. The staff was fun and friendly and we spent the afternoon there with no sense of being rushed, in fact I felt bad we we finally left that we were letting them down. We were seated at a great table with a view of the park. It made me wish C and I weren't married, just so I could propose to her again. The brunch is buffet style, but this is not "old country" - the food is straight out of Iron Chef. I started with some delicious hors devours of quail egg, escargot and an octopus and melon cocktail. The raw bar is great and there are delicious oysters (nice for your romantic arsenal). The main courses are served from the kitchen, which really helps to break that formality down. There are insane choices, I can't remember all the entrees, but the my two favorite items were the bruschetta with lobster hollandaise and heirloom tomatoes, and the scallop sausage. While in the kitchen we met the chef, sous chef and some of the other cooks. They were chill and very fun to get to know. I do like to get to know who are cooking and let them know how much I appreciate there hard work. Then the desserts... oh man. I usually go more for the savory, but the subtleness of the choice challenged and thrilled my taste buds. My favorites were the rice pudding, orange creme d'pot and chocolate basil dish. I had to check myself as not to just take a running dive in the chocolate fountain. Oh yeah, I said chocolate fountain. We really felt like were left all our hassles and day to day concerns behind and could spend time enjoying each other. When you need a special place to be with people you love, or even like a lot, go to Lacroix and let them indulge you.
label: POS

text: We've visited B&C twice now & it's my new favorite BBQ place in Nashville. We ate in their outdoor seating area the first time and took out the second time. The covered outdoor seating area is great! As others have noted, there is no indoor seating. We tried the pulled pork and the pulled chicken. Both were tasty. The pulled chicken came with a delicious white BBQ sauce. Make sure If you do take out to grab sauce, we got home and realized we forgot the sauce, all of which I liked on our first visit. The sides are really tasty, far better than anywhere else in town. The corn pudding and baked beans were delicious. The only side I didn't like was something other reviewers loved - the grits. On both visits, the grits were dried out and had little flavor. I'm usually a huge fan of grits, so this was disappointing. For desserts, the chocolate cake was amazing!!! Overall, the price was great for the quality of the food. Highly recommend. Only taking one star off for the grits.

text: Expansive menu and they are now open until 3 am (take that China Diner!) This is a no-nonsense sort of spot, so don't expect overly warm service. But when you become a regular, you start to appreciate the subtle charms and expediency of the place. I like the cold noodle dishes, specifically the imperial rolls over noodles. The pho is very good as well. The standouts at Golden Flower are the potstickers, which are clearly handmade and probably the best in town. Also the Vietnamese sandwich, one of those delicious remnants of France's colonization of Vietnam. Vietnamese coffee is wonderful. You can get out of here with a full belly for under $10. text: I wanted to like this place. I really did. However, something that wasn't even directly food-related derailed the experience. The food was tasty, though. Our group often tries new restaurants each weekend, and we struggle to find places that can address each of our tics -- Atkins diet, vegetarian, no dairy, not too spicy, etc. Looking at the menu online, Coco Louco Brasil appeared a good fit. We arrived on a Saturday night around 6:30. Upon entering, you stand in the bar to be seated (we had reservations). The bar was empty and did not appear to encourage smoking - important to note. The dining room, medium-sized and lined with huge windows, was through a doorway to the left and was separated from the bar by a wall that went about 3/4 of the way up to the ceiling. We were one of about three groups of five or more, and many of the other tables were two-tops. The dim lighting wasn't too dark and didn't hinder our reading of the menu. A man played piano in the corner. There were white tablecloths on the tables, along with a white butcher-paper cover and crayons; we were entertained. Upon seating, we received a basket filled with thin slices of crusty bread and a dish for oil/garlic and parmesan. The bread was good. I'm not a fan of dipping bread in oil, but the garlic and parmesan made me enjoy this one. For the appetizers, my friends ordered espetinhos -- chicken and beef kabobs -- while I ordered a cheese pastel -- a turnover which also came with a dry slaw. My friends enjoyed their plate, and I loved my turnover, especially when I dipped pieces into the spicy mayonnaise-type sauce that accompanied it. the pastel absolutely was stuffed with cheese, and the crust was light and flaky. Our salads then came. If you order an entree, you'll automatically get a salad. I didn't expect this salad to be huge, but I was a little surprised and disappointed at how little salad there was. There wasn't more than four forkfuls, yet it was placed on a huge dinner plate. It was tasty, don't get me wrong. I just think that if it was going to be so small, it should have been placed on a salad plate. My second appetizer came around this time -- the plantains. Many at the table shared them, and we all agreed that they were delicious. There were about 10 plantains, and they were soft without being mushy. They were caramelized lightly, and some had edges with sugar that was a bit more crispy -- just the way I like it! I should say now that our server was exceptional to this point. She refilled our drinks promptly and asked during each course if the food was good. She seemed quite sincere and was very sweet. Between the salad/plantains and our entrees, I began to smell smoke. I'm super-sensitive to it, so I always notice it first, but eventually our entire party began to smell it. We didn't see anyone smoking in the dining room, so we assumed that 1) it was coming from the kitchen, or 2) it was coming from the bar. I began to cough lightly, and our entrees then came out. We began to eat. Most of my friends ordered meat dishes that were pulled off of large skewers that looked like swords -- very impressive. Another friend ordered the filet Dom Pedro, which was steak with sauce served over bread. Another person ordered feijoada -- black beans with different kinds of meat in them. I ordered the vegetarian beans, which came in a little pot and had onions in them. All of our dishes were accompanied by rice, some vegetables and a garlic vinaigrette. We all had a LOT of food in front of us. However, the smoke continued migrating from the bar (where we deduced the source was) around and over the 3/4 height wall. Apparently, more smokers were lighting up, because it got to the point where I was coughing more than eating, and I couldn't even finish my meal because each forkful tasted like smoke. I sat there while my friends continued to eat a bit, though they didn't appreciate the smoke either. It really downgraded what was to be a night out trying a new cuisine. To make matters worse, our previously attentive server was nowhere to be found as we were eating or for a long time after everyone had finished. She finally came around and we requested the check, wanting very much to leave. It took a long time for her to return with it and my boxes (I took nearly my entire meal home because I couldn't eat in that smoke) and even longer to return with the card confirmations. With everything settled, we left -- again, through the door at the bar, which was now smoky as heck. There was nothing on the website about it being a smoking restaurant. Moreover, it's a small place, so having a "smoking section" a "non-smoking section" is laughable. I wasn't willing to speak to a manager/owner about the situation last night, as I just wanted to leave, so I tried to find an email address to send my concerns and disappointment; the website only has a phone number. I won't be back. :(

text: Having been here before and having good memories I was excited to pick this as my Friday night "Restaurant Week" restaurant. I honestly didn't remember reviewing it a few years ago. "Restaurant Week" is food celebration that takes place once annually in major cities where restaurants are joined together and each come up with their own prix-fixe three to five course menu for a fixed sum of money, standard among all restaurants participating. 2009 was Tucson's first year involved with "Restaurant Week" and hence only a few restaurants joined in. The set price was $29 per person. First course items included regularly priced 8-9 dollar appetizers, of which I had the Caesar salad and my boyfriend had the clam chowder. My salad had home-made dressing and croutons. The dressing was anchovy yet light. The chowder had a lot of flavor but was too runny for my liking. Second course was the entree. Three fish to choose from, a pork chop, or a seafood pasta. Regularly priced 18-22 dollars. We both selected a fish. I had the grilled Atlantic salmon which was a little too overdone but I guess was meant to be smothered in the orange ginger butter that it came with. I'm not a fan of fish smothered in butter. But put the orange ginger butter on anything and it will instantly become savory- not good, I wrote savory. On the side were rice and beets, of which neither had any flavor. The boyfriend ordered a macadamia nut crusted Hawaiian mahi mahi which came with sweet potato chips and sauteed spinach on the side. His fish was heavy and buttery, the chips were salted just right, but the spinach had a bitter taste. The third course was the dessert dish. We ordered the creme brulee and the red velvet cake, regularly 8.5. I can't decide which was worse. The best part of this particular creme brulee was the caramelized sugar on top because this was the only part of the dish with any flavor. The dessert was served in a tall rounded cup which provided a small surface area for the sugar to be fired on top. The taste and texture of the cream made me think twice about the logic of the chef preparing this dish. The fired sugar top was perfectly thin and crispy, the cream underneath was disgustingly smooth and lacked any flavor. The red velvet cake was a similar story. The cake was served cold, as if just removed from a fridge, the frosting was bland. If they have even attempted to serve a traditional cream cheese frosting along top of the cake it would have provided a creamy texture in its own, but alas the frosting had a vanilla, and seemingly plain, flavor. Red velvet cake is my new standard for deciding how much admiration to give to an establishment, and Kingfisher missed their mark. The waitress forgot my boyfriend's drink. This is only understandable at busy and economically challenged eateries. Kingfisher is by no stretch of the imagination economically challenged, as evidenced by their continuously full tables and inflated prices. There is no excuse for the waitress refusing to bring out his drink, or for that same waitress to disappear into the abyss of the back room and hence not being able to remind her of her mistake. We had to ask the water server boy to bring out a soda, which is not his job, and then I had to way to tip just the water boy. Our plates were swept away from us before we were finished eating off of them, literally. After finishing my salmon and still being hungry I began to nibble on my boyfriend's sweet potato chips. The water server boy took our plates away. He watched me take a chip off my boyfriend's plate, put it in my mouth, and then he took the plates away.

Try the delicious broth and then season as you wish, which for me I only add limes and thai basil. text: Unlike another reviewer, I have shopped here within the last 10 years. In fact, I shop at Ross fairly often. There are 4 local to me but I always prefer the one on Market Street in Philly. I have to present myself in a professional manner at work. To go out to a department store and buy a suit, I am looking at spending $100-$250 each if there is a sale at Macy's. Maybe some of you can afford 10-20+ suits at that price, and thats fine. However, I can (and do) get great suits and suit separates for a fraction of the price. I'm talking $10-$50. Sometimes I need to make a few alterations for better fit, but I own a sewing machine and can drive my car to my alteration specialist. I've also bought casual clothes, shoes, etc there. Everything has held up wonderfully for me, and I'd have to say Ive been shopping there for almost 10 years now. Nothing has fallen apart on me, nothing has disinigrated in my washer or dryer. It's not always true that you can get things at the outlets for the same or cheaper price. In fact, quality at outlet stores has completely changed and you may find the better quality item at Ross. Many outlet stores now run their own lines and no longer take the markdowns and clearance from their name brand stores. That's right, outlet stores are starting to make cheaper clothing with cheaper materials that resemble their normal pricey stuff, and consumers buy it up like they are getting good deals. I've had far more clothing from outlets fall apart than Ross.

The pineapples were so good and sweet! There were many different dishes being passed and shared around our table; calamari, chicken, and shrimp (oh my!) and everybody was enjoying it all. One of my friends said, "I don't know what they did to that (jalapeno peppered) steak, but they did it right." We did make lunch reservations for all of us, and they were able to accommodate us all (a little squishy, but kind of cozy) and our waters were constantly being refilled. In my first experience I had a basic vegetable dish. I found it extremely "alright." There were no bells, whistle, or horns; just cauliflower, broccoli and carrots. I was hoping for more spice and flavour, but there was none in this dish, but that's not always a bad thing, since some people want to try new and different things but are a little intimidated to take it to the next flavourful level. text: I've been going to Bella for years, since it was a dinky little place on 4th between South and Bainbridge (it is now on 4th between South and Lombard). And one thing hasn't changed - I still find treasures! In my mind, a treasure is something valuable and beautiful that is WAY underpriced; it really is like finding the needle in the haystack. At Bella, I have found gold, diamonds, platinum, silver, bakelite, antique jewels, valuable Taxco parures.... and, I have never paid more than $60 for any item (usually, it is more like $8 to $18). Also, the clothing selection tends to be pretty fab! Lots of affordable (and often vintage) evening wear, and racks of shirts and jeans. Oh, and if you love vintage furs, this is your one stop shopping destination! Dom, the owner, has a huge collection - from minks, to lynx, to leopard, to rabbit... she's got the hook up. Even if it's not on the rack, she may be able to find what you're looking for (so ask!). The shoe selection is just OK. And, there are always neat accessories to sort through. If you are a consigner with higher end merchandise and vintage, this is a fabulous place to sell! They take a large selection, tend to know even the lesser designers , and above all they will listen to you! If you think that they are pricing an item too low, tell them. Unlike most places, they will take your opinion into account. Why? Because, they take care of their consigners, and that's refreshing!

It's very close to the Schermerhorn and Hall of Fame. The website says they can accomodate 300 seated guests and 600 for cocktail reception - that seems like an awful lot in that space to me but perhaps the other floors weren't available to our crew. Great place in a great location - one to remember for entertaining and charity events alike!

text: The wildly varied responses to this place reflect one of two things: either people don't know what to expect from Texas BBQ, or the reviews are a result of a newly opened restaurant that's still working out its kinks. That said, I didn't experience any of the kinks--in fact, I commented on how impressive the service was, especially considering the place has been open for only 2 weeks. I didn't experience the kinks... nor, oddly enough, the BBQ. Because I don't eat meat (what?!). So what the hell kind o' business does a vegetarian have evaluating a BBQ joint? I walked away stuffed. So there. My boyfriend lived in west Texas for years, and was salivating when we saw the BBQ joint opening soon. I can make a meal out of side dishes, so I happily went along for the ride. They have vegan chili, which was tasty, and a baked mac & cheese that was quite delish as well (note: these, and the coleslaw are the only dishes that are truly vegetarian; the beans, mashed potatoes, german potato salad, collard greens are all made with meat and/or animal fat). Best part of the meal, though was the banana pudding (save room). BF had the pecan pie. mmmmmm. The atmosphere is inviting, and very well done--complete with movable walls that expand the restaurant when needed. The beer/wine/bourbon list is small but selective; the service was very attentive without being intrusive. I had a blast, and want to see this place succeed. I will definitely be back, if only to see the bf's smile as he indulges his west Texan cravings.
label: POS

text: Was here for a private event and experienced atrocious service, bad enough that I would not go back. Their website touts their ability to handle large groups for private events... but they were completely unprepared to handle the group. Service was extremely slow, and our server was rude as well. From ordering to receiving food took at least 40 minutes. When one person's food came out (missing an item), we asked the server when we could expect the other food and received a rude and unhelpful response of "It's a small kitchen." No refills were offered on coffee. One food order came out a good 15 minutes before the others. Getting the attention of the server was nearly impossible. The food itself was adequate--nothing special, but nothing wrong with it. The "maple syrup" described in the menu was pancake syrup rather than actual maple syrup (which is fine... just don't call it maple syrup if it's not!). We were also charged for an item we didn't order and it was an ordeal to get the attention of the server to get it removed from the bill, and no apology was offered when we pointed out the mistake. Overall, very unimpressed. They clearly weren't prepared to handle the group and seemed to fell no need to apologize for their lack of preparation.

text: You're takin' her with ya? Being from that side of the river, I've driven past Schatze's once or twice, and thought it was the shitty yet lovable hole in the wall local bar that Belleville people spent many a night getting wasted in. However, after a recent unplanned stop there, this mirage was destroyed as fast as bobby barstool can chug down a beer. The waitresses here are dressed up like wannabe Hooters girls on a bad, street crime riddled night scene in a special episode of Law and Order SVU. To get food, you place an order from a snack bar, that is literally a different bar than the bar, and a little dude fries up your food and gives you a number. Drunk and lurking dudes stared at me from across the room at the bar bar.. a man popped into the back door behind where I was sitting and yelled at me, WHOO HOOO!. Surprised, I said..hi? YOU DID IT WRONG, he said, then walked away. It wasn't until my friend told me that the local Chester the Molester just walked in. Sparing you the details, by this time know that I didn't want to share breathing space with this man any longer. And, making sure that Schatze's will always remain a remnant of a bad memory, a shard of that bad part of a dream that forever haunts you, as we walked out, my friend through the door and I almost through to safety, one of the leering lurches leaned back in his sleeveless jean shirt and asked, in a voice loud enough for the entire contents of the den to hear, "YA TAKIN HER WITH YA???" Run, run for the hills little bunny, run! And all the way to the car I ran.

text: Brennan's **** With a nearly endless list of classic egg dishes, and an impressive menu reeking of Creole favorites, I would have liked to have had dined here for a full meal...but only went (like many annoying tourists do) for their famous bananas Foster dessert. From the silverware, to the decor, to the linens and excellent service, this place was pleasantly elegant. The bananas Foster was delicious; with good ice cream that could have been house-made. I loved how our darling server (Franklin) informed us of the history of the dessert and showed us what was in it before it was flambéed and served tableside. Nice touches. One problem however is their schedule. They only serve 'dessert only' diners at the last 15-30 mins of each lunch and dinner shift. So you have to call them and see of they are open for such. It was lame and very complicated for tourists who are on a tight schedule. I suppose this helps ward off the icky tourist joint vibe that other popular establishments are forced to embrace. Next time I go, I would like to have a full dinner there with wine and all the extras. This is why I can only give 4 stars. I did not want to leave...but we had more of the Big Easy to see.... --Anthony

text: We stayed here for two days for a Christmas business party, it was nice. We had a double queen room all done up in pink(yuck), the room was nice had a few chairs, a small table, a desk, and a makeup mirror. The bathroom was nice as well, pretty typical of a hotel with the shower bath combo but a big enough bath that you could lay down and soak, but not big enough to share. The beds were uncomfortable, but I think most casino beds are so you can't sleep and get up to gamble more. I was also a little cold at night and had to take the blanket off the other bed to stay warm. The hotel itself was nice, with 4-5 different restaurants, ranging from nice steak house, oyster bar, cafe, to your typically buffet.(see separate reviews of restaurants) There were of course many bars, we tended to say at the one in front by the front desk because you could pretty much see everyone who walked by and we were a large party so we pulled a ton of tables together and drank plenty. I noticed on the weekend mornings that they had a make it yourself bloody Mary bar for $5 with an assortment of vodkas and spicy and plain tomato juice with all kinds of condiments to add to your drink, I am not a bloody Mary person so I didn't partake but it looked nice. Major bonus was the Starbucks right by the bar we took over. I need caffeine in the morning and am pretty partial to a venti white chocolate mocha and I honed in on the Starbucks within seconds of checking in to our room. The amenities were pretty usual with a free fitness room for guest, a salon/spa(see separate review), and nice looking indoor pool. As far as gambling went I personally didn't do so well but hey I did break even so I guess I didn't do so bad either, but a few people that were with our group won a few hundred. I played a few slots, they had a good selection of nickle, quarter, dollar, and even penny. Then I hit the $5 black jack table, I went with a single deck and started off doing very good I really like the dealer she was awesome, but then the enviable happened they switched dealers, now I should have walked away when that happened but no I decided I was doing good so I would stay that was my mistake the next dealer was hot, and I lost, but hey you win some and you lose some. We did have a party in the pool terrace room, it was next to the pool on the 5th floor, they decorated it nice and pretty, had a no host bar, a DJ, a tiny dance floor, and a buffet...we had a good time I can't wait for next year.

text: Shere-E-Punjab located in Media, P.a. is the kind of restaurant that puts off people from trying Indian cuisine a second time. Even for those of us with a life-long passion for Indian cuisine and ever ready to eat any kind of curry without complaint, Shere-E-Punjab food leaves a bad taste in the mouth. Our recent meal at Shere-E-Punjab was a chronicle of one disaster following another. Right from the moment we sat down, we hit one rough spot after another. Of course, we are no strangers to bad Indian restaurants. But usually even at the worst Indian restaurants we visit, at least one item - maybe it's the Tandoori Chicken or Alu Baigan or the humble Masala Chai - is nice. Shere-E-Punjab, however, belongs to that unfortunate category of Indian restaurants that has absolutely no reason for existence. Not a single item we had at this so-called Indian restaurant was even passable let alone tasty. Chicken Biryani was an utter travesty of a dish. Lacking any flavor or adequate rice, it was enough to drive an Indian to despair. Plain and simple, it was just partially cooked chicken. That too, just 2 small pieces. Naan is our favorite Indian bread and we usually gravitate to it when we dine out. The Naan we had at Shere-E-Punjab should easily count among the worst Naans we've had in over four decades. It was really over-cooked. But the booby prize for the worst dishes at Shere-E-Punjab were shared by Chicken Makhani and Palak Panneer. Although the menu describes Chicken Makhani as "Boneless tandoori chicken cooked in creamy tomato sauce and butter". It was a bland, bad-tasting under-spiced mess. Palak Paneer was equally pitiful. The Paneer (cheese) was way too hard and the overall effect was of chewing on a rubber at the end of a pencil. When we placed our order, we had requested that we'd like everything hot and spicy. But what landed on our table was extra mild. Was the chef on some kind of strike or protest? When we asked the female mgr. she stated - "just add some green chutney and it'll be OK!. Kulfi is a sweet dish from West Bengal in the Eastern part of India. One of our favorite sweets, we've had it countless times to great delight. But what appeared on our table was a little mass of white custard pudding in a little plastic container smaller than a golf ball. It was a vile, sour-tasting liquid that had as much resemblance to milk as mud has to caviar. Forget palatable. Much of the food at Shere-E-Punjab is barely tasteful. Watch out for your cholestrol level- everything is filled with butter. Our meal at Shere-E-Punjab in Media, P.a. was misery of an order that we'd seldom experienced at a dining table. - Yeah, It sucked that bad. Don't fall for the dark ambient room, its a ploy so you don't know what you are getting on your plate. Hope this review was helpful. "Turbo cop"

text: This no-frills supermarket chain is just starting to open stores in the Tampa Bay area, and whether or not you decide to shop here will depend on how much you're willing to sacrifice to save a few dollars. We visited this location the day after it opened, and there was an acrid odor in the air that had our eyes burning and watering a few minutes after we walked in the door. Two employees insisted they couldn't smell anything, but since other shoppers were commenting about it, we knew we weren't crazy. We stayed just long enough to check out the merchandise and form an opinion. If you prefer national brands, you won't find any here. Everything is "private label" and available only at Aldi stores. The produce was limited and pre-packaged, so it was impossible to inspect. The price per pound is posted, but the individual packages had no weights or prices on them. There weren't many choices in the meat and dairy sections. Even canned, bottled, and packaged goods don't have much of a selection. Most frozen items are sold in family-size packages only. Many items people buy on a regular basis aren't sold here at all. You need to bring your own bags, or else buy the paper, plastic, or insulated bags they sell, and you bag your own groceries. They don't accept credit cards or checks. Although most prices appeared to be lower than those in the major supermarket chains, not finding everything you need under one roof is a major drawback to me. If I need to go to Publix or Albertson's to complete my shopping, the few dollars I save here aren't worth the trouble. If you do go here, be sure to have a quarter with you, because you need one to get a shopping cart. You get your money back when you return the cart to the stand in front of the store, but it's just one more nuisance that will keep me from coming here.
label: NEG

A block off the St. Charles streetcar line, this would be a good before-the-Garden-District-walking-tour stop for tourists if you have the all-day $5 streetcar pass. Especially if you are sick of beignets and need a shot of wheatgrass or some fresh squeezed OJ after a night of partying.

text: Reputation trickles down in the very best way possible at SideBern's, the irreverent sibling of the ever present and highly acclaimed Bern's Steakhouse. "One World Under Food" is it's philosophy, with an eclectic menu that changes every day, flying in the face of Bern's staid demeanor. Once you are seated you are handed not one but two menus, the regular, cutting edge cuisine from around the world and a smaller, Dim Sum menu featuring smaller portions of items ranging from dumplings to scallops. It's a beautiful thing that SideBern's gets to share in the enormous wine collection that Bern's Steakhouse has had for over 50 years, because you get a choice from over 30 different wines by the glass if you are not ready to spend the money on a bottle. I had the beet salad to start, a geometrically designed plate featuring two small piles of layered beet, goat cheese and black truffle goodness with small streaks of a raspberry and Dijon vinaigrette. Then I had a Peking style duck breast with cabbage, black beans and snap peas. The flavors all worked quite nicely together, none of which overpowered the others. The one problem I had was the portions. The mini salad and the huge entree seemed like a pretty drastic contrast. While my dining partners decided to to take the light fare route by getting apps for both courses, they agreed. They were also a but put off by the trendiness of the space. Yes, all the beautiful people were stationed at the bar, and the bulkiness of the aluminum menus kept knocking over the glassware on the way-to-small table. And the last small inconvenience was the service, which was adequate but a bit clumsy and unpolished. But those little things did not diminish the over all experience though. The dining room is beautiful, with polished wood and arching, spider-like chandeliers over the bar and lounge. Everyone from the hosts to the service staff were knowledgeable and friendly. Yes it's trendy and yes you will pay for it when the check is dropped, but don't let that stop you, the food will keep you coming back for more.
label: POS

text: If you want to experience one of the nation's great urban parks, try the perimeter bike path, which is a bit more than five miles in length, I believe. Along the way, you'll find a world-class zoo and art museum, Missouri history museum, "Muny" outdoor theater, ponds, pools, fountains, gardens, golf course, and tennis courts. West of the park is Wash U. and the Delmar Loop, and east is the Central West End (CWE). Be careful that you don't crash on a downhill; but if you do, you're within sight of Barnes-Jewish Medical Center, one of the best in the nation. Bikes and "Segways" are available for rental (inquire at Lindell Pavilion, where you'll find coffee and public restrooms). Suburbanites like me can just load up the bikerack on the SUV, and park north-central, or many places around the interior. Sadly, I can share stories, one personal, of "smash-and-grab" car burglaries in parking areas. It's best to take all electronics and valuables with you.
