text: Exceptional, wonderful clinic that offers low-cost acupuncture and herbs on a sliding scale based on your income. Acupuncture sessions are an incredible way to heal yourself through many conditions. They are also a great path for "tuning up" your body, even when not faced with a particular condition. The clinic is a group setting: You have a private consultation with one of the two doctors, and they become your permanent doctor (unless you want to see the other one). The first visit is the longest one: you spend about forty five minutes discussing everything: your diet, your exercise levels, your health history, etc. Then you go in for treatment: The treatment room is warm, clean and very comfortable. You choose a reclining chair and the needles are administered. The doctors at Community Acupuncture are somewhat conservative in their approach; they only use needles where absolutely necessary. Each one is taken out of their brand-new, completely sterile paper pouch. They are immediately discarded after use. As with all acupuncture clinics they are NEVER re-used. I would recommend this clinic to anyone. Acupuncture is designed to be most effective when used frequently. The sliding scale fee at Community Acupuncture makes it possible for me to go every week; sometimes twice a week if I'm working through something. Community Acupuncture rocks!
label: POS

text: We ate dinner last night in a group of 10 celebrating a birthday. Our party host made reservations and they were honored on time, 6:30 pm. Walking up to and into the restaurant we were shocked at the huge crowd we had to navigate just to get to our seating area. Every table was full and they are really close together. I opened the menu and was completely overwhelmed by the number of choices for dinner. In my experience, more isn't always better! I basically gave up and just chose something that sounded good, Tagliatelle ai Funghi Porcini and a special appetizer, a jumbo lump crab cake with salad. I have to say I really enjoyed the appetizer, the crab cake was seasoned well and I didn't need the tartar sauce at all. The salad was slightly over-dressed for my tastes, but was crisp and fresh. When the dinners started arriving, I was completely turned off by the huge portions. There was literally enough pasta, sauce and mushrooms for 3 people to eat off of my plate. My husband had the Tortellini Bolognese and had the same experience remarking, "even on my hungriest day I couldn't finish this plate!" The food was very average, though it did come out piping hot. Our server was alone, no one assisted him except for a food runner who helped bring the dinners. I would think with a party of 10 he should have had help. When you have that many people, someone always needs something and we ended up calling him to our table at least 4 times. Not his fault! Once we were given our check and everyone put in their money, it was really obvious that he wanted us to go. While we were there, I noticed how quickly tables were turning over, so when I read this on another review I can totally attest to this experience. Later in the evening, we ran into 2 former employees, who said the owners really push the servers to turn over as many tables at possible each night. It is a BYOB, which is fine and I observed most tables with a bottle or two. I don't think we'll go back, there are many more options for better quality food with a nicer environment in our area. I'd rather have a difficult time selecting an entree because all 10 items are delicous than have a tough time deciding because there are 80 items to choose from.

text: OK, so I was really excited about a hot dog place opening up and started to envision a place like Johnny's Dogs in Wayne or even better - Hot Doug's in Chicago (aka Encased Meat Emporium)...Hot Dog with Foie Gras - brilliant !! So you can understand my disappointment when I walk in to see 2 teenage lads manning the place - nothing wrong with that, just a bit suspect, especially when one of them is more busy eating fries straight from the fryer and getting himself a drink while the customer waits to place an order. Wanting the sample a few dogs, I came prepared (read hungry). Chili cheese with onions and a Chicago Dog please, I proclaimed. While the Chicago dog had been "through the garden" (all the prerequisite toppings), the poppy seed bun seemed stale and the sausage seemed like it was served straight from the package after being brought to room temperature!! Chili dog also seemed to be made with similar style dog and prepackaged chili. I did notice a small sign later that said if you want the dog grilled or "snappy" (in the fryer), that is $0.25 extra. Seems like a detail that should be pointed out to first timers. So reminiscing "the ripper" from NJ, I order a snappy dog. Unfortunately, what I got was more of an oil drenched dog rather than a crisped dog. Just in case you thought the above was not enough, the wife had ordered a chicken parmesan sandwich - pretty basic stuff....except she took one bite and the chicken breast was RAW !! I took it up to the counter and got a replacement sandwich (roast beef) which was more like a chopped beef in canned gravy sandwich rather than the Arby's style sandwich picture they had up. Oh well...sadly I might go back if I really crave a Chicago dog and cannot get to Chicago or Johnny's in Wayne.

text: Upon request of the operating manager I gave Fleming's a second chance. My initial review stated that Fleming's does one thing and should know how to do that one thing right. Well, when they try, they can do it. Fleming's knows how to grill their meat. My second meal was an exact replica of my first, but my boyfriend ordered steak instead of tuna (per my insistence). The caesar salad was sadly the same, somewhat bland, but the lamb was much better. I ordered it the same way (medium-rare), but this time they actually cooked it correctly. I cut into my first chop and could see that these were tender and succulent (the inside was pink this time). Items arrive just as you had literally ordered them. "I'd like the prime ribeye" then you will get the prime ribeye. Sides are extra but come in huge portions, big enough for two. My mashed potato side was inedible. My boyfriend's baked potato was fine, but then again, how can one mess up a baked potato. The service was amazing. I was told by the waitress that she had received a message pertaining to me, so I can only assume that my amazing service is not their standard. When Fleming's tries, Fleming's delivers. But why do they have to try? Why do they have to impress someone to serve a good meal? Tips for an enjoyable hundred dollar meal: - Skip on everything at this restaurant other than meat - Continue to send your food back until they *try* to make it right. They are perfectly capable of serving up great meat, they just need to want to try, which they don't seem to want to do for every customer. My original one star rating averaged against my revised three star review.

text: If you are looking for staff that are extremely unprofessional, this would be the place. Having stayed at this establishment before, I decided to book a 3 night stay there for a conference. text: Not a bad place to get seafood in a desert. We got there early for an anniversary dinner on a Friday night, 6.30. Plenty of seats available, although we did have a reservation. We asked to be seated on the balcony which was wonderful with the setting sun lighting up the Catalinas. Really beautiful backdrop to the start of a delicious meal. Service was prompt and attentive. We started with wine chosen from their modest but respectable list (service comes by the bottle, but also by the 1/2 bottle or glass for some selections) and an appetizer of fresh oysters on the half shell. Not the best I've had, but certainly fresh and tasty. For entrees, I ordered the "Bluefin Bouillabaisse" and the wife ordered the cashew crusted mahi mahi. Both were delicious. Surprisingly to me, the lobster was the blandest part of the bouillabaisse. Still good, just not great. The broth however, was divine. This clearly must be a signature plate here (and not just because of the name), as I saw many others ordering the same thing. It was quite delicious. And messy fun to eat! While dinner was filling enough, I knew that I had to try one of their deserts--a Heath bar cheesecake with caramel sauce. WARNING--a single serving is big enough for two people. Easily! Service was exceptional for us. We had multiple people attending to us at all times. The only time it came close to intrusive however was the insistent refills on our waters (stay hydrated now!). Meh. Still, our main waiter was very professional in offering a taste of the wine before committing to the bottle, and apparently even heard me toying with the idea of getting a single malt as seemingly out of nowhere, a menu of single malt options was laid on the table. Excellent service! As we left, at about 8.30, the place was filling up nicely, but still tables remained. Seeing more of the clientele, I started to feel a little underdressed, but again, was never treated second class by anyone. My only complaint--the hideous purple neon sign that watches over the parking lot to the shopping area where Bluefin is located. But that clearly is not enough to stop me from heading back when I need a little taste of elegance and the ocean in this dusty desert town.

There are a lot of choices on the menu and each page seems to have its own entree/main course/dessert/side sections with no apparent explanation for why there are three separate dessert sections in the menu. I had the poisson meunière amandine which others have raved about on this site. I thought it was fine but nothing to write home about (though perhaps something to write Yelp about..). It was fish and almonds and a sprig of parsley. I guess it was true to its name but I was surprised it wasn't served with anything. I started with the house salad ("salad maison" which I'd love to correct to "salade maison"). It was drowning in a vinaigrette which made it impossible to finish. Mixed in with the baby lettuce greens was iceberg lettuce. Iceberg lettuce? Are you serious? That's what you find in a McDonald's hamburger, not in a $7 salad the size of a bread plate at a fancy restaurant! Give me a break. Finally a piece of asparagus was perched on the top of the salad. Being raw I didn't see any way of cutting it gracefully without slopping half the salad into my lap so I let it be. I finished with some of the bread pudding dessert which was pretty decent - nice and hot inside. The price was about what I had expected ~ $50/person for appetizer, main course, wine, and a shared dessert. I'm glad I had the experience but it's not place I'd visit again.

text: We went on one of their summer Monday theme nights ... fried chicken ... need I say more? The evening started with a gathering outside among Greg's "urban garden," where we were offered several wines to taste, along with bruschettas with goat cheese and blueberries. I don't typically eat much cheese, but I figured this was the place to try it, and it was delicious The sweetness of the blueberries with the salty/creamy of the cheese was sooo good (and I don't like cheese, I had to keep reminding myself). Then we moved indoors for dinner, which was served picnic style, with the food on platters in the front of the restaurant, and diners sitting together among four long rows of tables. It made for a very fun and relaxed atmosphere, and husband and I very much enjoyed talking to another couple during the meal. The fried chicken was the obvious star here, marinated in buttermilk, breaded and seasoned, then fried in cast iron pans ... can it get any better than that? It was perfectly moist, with a thick crispy skin ... I could've had a whole plate just of that skin and been happy. The sides included a cheesy potato salad that was also good, just a little too cheesy for me, and a cucumber tomato salad, and all kinds of other things that I now forget. Dessert was strawberry shortcake with homemade whipped cream ... and great combo of rich and light, the sweet berries against the sharp buttermilk shortcake. Greg Hardesty clearly loves food, and loves the people who loves his food. I look forward to more inspiring and inspired dinners in the future.

text: This is not an excellent museum, it is not a superb museum. It is an astoundingly wonderful museum and to call it anything less would be an insult. This is a museum that will be enjoyed by the amateur history buffs as well as those who were born in 1990 and have only the dimmest memory of WWII from their high school American History class. The museum skillfully weaves personal narratives with artifacts from the era and uses vivid, modern technology and graphics to immerse visitors. It is a walking tour, but with many opportunities to sit and reflect and rest tired feet, while watching short films or listening to individuals reflect and reminisce about their part in the War. It's depiction is balanced and well thought out in many different ways. It does not stoop to romanticizing American at the time or neglecting to mention the difficult things that many Americans would choose to forget - our own Isolationism, our rejection of Jewish immigrants, the internment camps Americans of Japanese ancestry were sent to, the racial segregation on American shores at the time; even Dresden is remembered for what it was. The museum is also unflinching in its depiction of the savagery of the Imperial Japanese and in the horror that was the Holocaust and the Nazi system. When the tour comes to Nagasaki and Hiroshima, it does not blink in its review of why the atomic bombs that were dropped were so horrific nor of why the US felt it had no other choice but to drop the bomb and save lives. But in the midst of all of this, the tour doesn't forget American life on the Home Front and doesn't ignore the contributions of the American Civilians at work or in their homes towards the War effort. Even the entertainment of the period and the contributions of children in gathering scrap metal and buying war stamps are recounted. In 2010, the museum opened a new addition and added a 4D movie that, like the museum, somehow successfully entertains those who know all the details and nuances of the history of this period and both educates and entertains those who only barely remember something studied in a class years ago. In our list of things to do in Southeast Louisiana, this is one stop that we recommend to all visitors, young and old. It is a museum that can be visited more than once (although, at about the 20th visit, it does get a little old) and will be enjoyed by everyone.

text: Who knew? We walked into a retail wine store and came out having one of the best meals of the year. Visiting Tucson, I wanted a bottle of wine...something decent. I googled "best wine shop tucson" and the result was The RumRunner. We headed over and picked up a bottle of Numanthia but also discovered a tiny little restaurant tucked inside called "The Dish." Four tables and a counter with a nice ambiance. We had a quick look a the menu and it seemed right up our alley. The next night we went back for dinner and were blown away. The chef, Martin Sindells, an Australian living in Tucson, has got something special going on here. As is frequently our preference, we sat at the bar and spoke with Doug, the wine master and our server. Great guy, very knowledgeable and friendly. We started with openers...Baked Miti Crema with marcona almond crumble, heirloom tomato confit and black olive rusks. The Miti is a sheep cheese and I've never been served warm sheep cheese. This was flat out awesome but only to be outdone by the other opener, Pulled Pork and Duck Duet with peppered gyoza, fresh sheep milk cheese, pinot noir braised red grapes and baby french radish insalata. Best opener of the year. A bottle of Numanthia Termes was opened. On a sidebar I should also note that the wine list is literally the entire retail store...grab a bottle and pay only retail price with essentially a twelve dollar corkage fee. Awesome deal. I've never seen anything like this before. Entrees arrived soon. We had a Duck Confit with forbidden rice, matchstick carrots, bok choy, shiitake eggroll and black plum and pomegranate glaze. The other entree was Sicilian Braised Beef Rib with chipotle yam fries, sauteed arugula, orange zest and jus de braiser. Both were spectacular. The yam fries came with a blue cheese aioli. I might have chosen a horseradish version but nonetheless the meal was awesome. We couldn't finish our plates so the dessert menu was just a quick, though thoroughly tempting, read. The fact that this place can flourish in the dessert with a tiny staff, no marketing and no stand-alone location says a lot. The place was packed both times we visited. The folks working here have a bright future whether in Tucson or any place they choose to work. This is restauranting at it's best. Highest recommendation.

text: I was pleasantly surprised to see the beautiful building of Toscana 52 take the place of the outdated Bob Evans Restaurant. If one had to judge restaurant's cuisine by its facade, I thought for certain that Toscana would be among my favorite restaurants. That was not the case....like life, beauty is only skin deep, folks. I eagerly waited two months from its opening to try Toscana, and we went as a party of four including 2 kids, age 15 and 10. We waited about 25 minutes for a table which was surprising considering it was Friday evening around 7:30pm. We waited 10 minutes for the waiter and assumed that they were short staffed. When asked about a children's menu, we were told that there was none but the kitchen could cook "anything we wanted". When the waiter asked the kitchen for specifics, that amounted to a choice of either chicken fingers or 3 different kinds of pasta. We started with drinks and an appetizer. My son ordered chocolate milk which we were surprised they had, given they obviously do not cater to children. The child's chocolate milk arrived in a glass wine goblet (no kidding!) at a cost of $3.99. Definitely nothing child-friendly about that! We ordered the fried calamari appetizer which looked scrumptuous when placed in front of us. However, each piece of calamari tasted like it was fried in oil which wasn't hot enough and as a result we had to offset the oily taste with the driest Italian bread we've ever tasted. The bread came 10 minutes after the appetizer (after we asked about it twice) and there were three little containers of herb butter. At first, we thought that each butter was a different variety but it was all the same (what the??). We ate it to offset the very greasy calamari appetizer which we didn't entirely finish. Perhaps the cheesecake appetizer would have been delicious, as many have raved about it, including our waiter who seemed a little miffed that we didn't order it after he announced it so grandly, with an "everyone loves it" comment. Before our entrees arrived, there was a changing of the flatware which was an obvious attempt to mimic an upscale restaurant but it came across as disingenuous and phoney. Our entrees: chicken marsala, seafood linguini, fettucinini alfredo with shrimp (child's portion which cost $10.50), and pasta with butter for my 10 yr old son. We were shocked when the child's buttered pasta entree arrived, as the amount of pasta only filled about half of a bread dish, so miniscule was the portion ($4.50) that a 2-year old wouldn't have been full, much less a 10 year old. The rest of us shared our entrees with him. The entrees were at best mediocre but overall quite bland. Italian food is not supposed to taste so bland! We never use salt during our meals but this meal definitely necessitated it for all our dishes. The flavor of my chicken marsale was "almost" there if it didn't taste diluted and bland. Same for the seafood linguini and alfredo dish - very bland and mediocre at best. Perhaps other items on the menu didn't suffer from blandness but we had the misfortune to select those dishes that were. I was so disappointed since I had salivated for two months to taste what I was certain to be superb cuisine. That was not the case, much to my chagrin. The house wine cost $6 per glass. No problem, except that the glass is either too large or the portion of wine served is so small that it leaves one feeling ripped off. Each glass was only filled 1/3 full at most when served. The clearing of dishes after our meal was non-existent after the waiter took away one of our dishes while asking if anyone wanted dessert. When no one wanted dessert, no further dishes were cleared and a one-glass water refill took several reminders. What was up with that?!? We asked for the bill and had to wait about 15 minutes for it. Hold me captive but at least take away my damn dishes! The waiter was not friendly at all but we figured he was probably tired and very busy so we didn't think much of it. However, when it came time for him to give us the bill, he suddenly decided to become momentarily friendly and personable. Did he suddenly wake up? Or perhaps he remembered that a friendly personality garnered higher tips? That was a little annoying. Also, I found the prices to be on the high side which I wouldn't mind paying if the food was remotely worth it, but it was not. In the past when a new restaurant doesn't meet my expectations, I have no problem giving it a second chance. I won't be doing that at Toscana - it isn't worth my time or money. From the number of bad reviews that I've read about this place, that speaks for itself. I have read the other reviews and have to wonder if the good reviews are written by people associated with the restaurant. If you read the bad reviews, they all seem to mirror the same thing - AWFUL, BLAND FOOD and CRAPPY SERVICE.
label: NEG

text: Oh, James. I had heard and read so many good things about you. Your food was highly touted, your cocktails envied. I browsed the menu online before dining and while I found the prices to be a little high, I thought that the food would warrant them. I was mistaken. Our server explained that the menu was meant to be enjoyed in 3 courses. He then went through and recommended his favorite dishes. First recommendation was the Kindai tuna, m.p. I was not surprised that we would be steered towards the most expensive appetizer. After gushing about the incredible marbling and sustainability of this fish, he recommended that we get one or two pastas and then the lobster entree, $36. If you went to see a movie, would you go see whatever the person working the box office told you to see? I would rather not feel like I'm getting the up-sell and just be left to decide on my own or ask questions. I ordered the Burgundy snails and the risotto a la milanese with summer truffle and beef marrow. My companion ordered the consomme with miatake mushrooms and the lobster. Almost every dish on the menu features some sort of interplay between sweet and savory flavors. To me this feels like a gimmick. The snails were lightly battered and fried and were plated on top of some sort of burnt sugar crisp that tasted like toffee. They were very flavorful and the dish worked well, except for the sweetness. The risotto tasted like Velveeta but not quite as salty. Summer truffle? There was no flavor in the thin brown slices in the center of the dish that I assumed were summer truffle. After the entrees were cleared the waiter gave us dessert menus without asking if we wanted any. This is a big pet peeve of mine and another example of feeling like I am being up-sold. I had the panna cotta which was very good, nice texture and sweet without being too sweet. I've only been once, so I can't comment on the overall consistency of the menu, but so far there just isn't a lot of value for the money. I expected more complex flavors from the risotto than just mac and cheese. The chef seems obsessed with juxtaposing savory and sweet and I don't think it always works. I'd be interested to go back and try the pappardelle with duck ragu and chocolate, but at $120 for app, entree, two drinks, a dessert and a piece of cheese, it's going to be a while.

text: Jack's bbq caters to the tourist trade in Nashville. It was a major disappointment from a food and authentic standpoint. First off you are in a que that takes way too long. by the time you get to the big menu board, you are committed to buy the food because of the amount of time spent in line. While in line, I observed the cashier dumping the mac n cheese and the cream corn from a bag! (*I asked the cashier later if they make these sides or if it is "store bought." She admitted it was a commercial product.) It looked like she was slopping hogs by the way it was poured and served in the commercial warming trays. Disgusting for a "authentic" BBQ joint. All meals are served on a styrofoam plate with plastic utensils. Not very "down home." Also no wet wipes at all. Too much grease to wipe off with just paper. I ordered the "three meat" combo for $13.00. The portion was smallish and plopped on the styrofoam plate. Now, most of this review could be dismissed if the food was good, unfortunately, it wasn't. The ribs: The ribs did not have the membrane removed from the back of the bone. This is a very basic butcher requirement when prepping for pork ribs. Sadly, it was an inedible crispy, greasy membrane that stuck in my teeth. Awful. The smoke flavor was not that apparent. The pork shoulder: The pork shoulder was inedible. It had way too much fat content attached to the meat. I could not get a good bite with the taste of greasy fat in my mouth. Disgusting. Void of smoke flavor as well. The brisket: The brisket was the best of the three. It had a good smokey taste and was not as dry as the other meats. The sauce. I had a choice of two sauces, (poured from a broken communal container.) The "hot sauce" was way to hot and you could not taste whatever you put it on. Void of taste. The other mustard looking sauce had an abundance of vinegar and the vinegar taste was so strong it was inedible. Now, I would understand a few things wrong with every restaurant but Jack's falls way too short and is a money mill for the owner serving pour quality bbq to unsuspecting tourist. This is an honest and unbiased review.

text: This past Saturday morning the family and I spent the day walking around Wissahickon park. We had a recommendation for lunch at The Little Tree house with the comment that it is "kid friendly". Well that comment makes me laugh now because it's "kid-centric" and "parent friendly". We were exhausted after chasing around two boys all morning so we were looking for something easy for lunch. I was a bit discouraged when parking wasn't as easy as I would have liked, but those familiar with Chestnut Hill most likely don't have this issue. Another downer was that they don't let strollers into the facility. At the end of a very long, active morning I truly didn't want to have to wrestle the stroller any longer. But once we got inside my boys were in awe! I have a 3 year old and an 18 month old. They took off playing, while we were able to calmly order food, pick a table and for once, eat at a normal pace. The boys would come back to our table every now and then to get a drink and pick at their meals. It was wonderful for me to be able to relax and eat, letting my guard down ever so slightly. I personally like that there wasn't much of a division between the play area and eating area. I was able to look up when I felt the need to see which kid was where and doing what. With there not being much of a divide between the two areas I was able to quickly get to my 18 month old when he bumped his head. The boys LOVED it! The space was large and colorful with wooden play houses, pillows, wooden climbers and trucks, shopping carts and a toy shopping area. Additionally it had the most child friendly bathroom facilities I've ever seen. I enjoyed the food. I had a turkey panini and a glass of ice tea. A point of note, I was told that it is a BYOB, but don't know that for sure. I hope it is, since that sounds fantastic! The only criticism I have is that it is a bit over priced. For two adult meals, two kids meals and play time it was $71! I was shocked because that was for lunch! We were eating with a bunch of friends families so I am not sure if the bill is accurate; it could be that additional items made it to our bill. If you go you are doing it for your kids, to have a unique experience and to enjoy a meal that you don't have to rush through. The space is a ton of fun and I am sure your little kids will love it. I am not sure how the older ones will fare however. Also beware that you may face "sticker shock" once you leave. You may want to check out pricing up front! For me at the time it was very much worth it! Enjoy!

text: I like to preface my little reviews so you know where I'm coming from. I'm not really experienced with ethnic food. I tend to be a picky eater, a creature of habit, and have a poor memory for words that sound the same. So I never know quite what to order, and I tend to just grab some pizza or whatnot when it's up to me. But my friends, like most people, like eating a variety of foods, and I'm game. This time, it was Thai. You could tell it was authentic based on the comically incorrect syntax found in the menu descriptions. What was great, though, was that there were extensive descriptions, so you really knew what you were getting into. What was even more greater, however, was that all the dishes looked really good. And had hysterical names. My one friend ordered the, 'Tutti-Frutti Duck'. It tasted like a duck that had been cooked in raspberry jam. But in a really good way. My other friend had the Sensual Salmon. Salmon, covered in crab, as well as a cream sauce. It was absolutely fantastic. Finally, I had the Young Girl on Fire. Now, the name at first, I wasn't too sure about. Considering it's an Asian restaurant, it had me thinking of that famous image of the poor little naked Vietnamese girl covered in napalm, which is neither humorous nor appetizing. On the other hand, it was a Cornish hen, stuffed with raisins and pineapple (???) tenderly marinated in loving herbs and spices, and whiskey flamed at the table. Well, that settled it. The other dishes came out, followed by all of our generous bowls of sticky rice. Then, the waiter brought out a canister and set it on the table. You know those little devices used to glaze a creme brule? Yeah, this wasn't one of those. This was more like what you'd use to weld something in metal shop. Then, the waiter comes back out with my tiny chicken, and stands several feet from the table. He pours a significant amount of whiskey on it, and, with the whole restaurant now paying attention, lights it on fire. It burns for, no joke, like 35seconds. When it finally dies out, he walks it over, places it in front of me, and in a small and polite voice proclaims, 'Young Girl on Fire". There was laughter and applause. And this thing was DELICIOUS. Unbelievable. I even ventured to try the bizarre fruit & dried fruit stuffing. What's even more amazing was the price - usually when someplace is going to light your food on fire, or perform some other gesture that makes it more like 'dinner and a show', it seriously ups the cost. My young girl on fire cost me the same as the other entrees - most things seemed to be in the $15-$20 range. Want to mention something else cool - there were $4 cocktails. Now, we didn't partake in them this visit, so I can't comment on volume or quality, but it bears mentioning - $4 cocktails! And, they were color coded, much like the terror alert system. That way, when you get drunk enough, you can just say - 'Gimmie the Blue!' or "My young girl on fire set my Green aflame!' So, for those of you that haven't bothered to read everything, but want a quick informative recap, here's what this place has: 1) Reasonable Prices 2) Great Food 3) Humorous Dish Names 4) Flaming Entrees 5) Polychromatic Potables I cant recommend this place highly enough. Everything on the menu looks great, everything I tried was great... but you'll be disappointed if you don't make sure someone in your party orders the Young Girl On Fire.

text: Spectacular! It's hard to explain how beautiful and inspiring this "castle" is, but I was surprised at what an amazing experience it was. I can't say that tile has ever fascinated me before, but now I'm all ready to fire up the kiln...or maybe just purchase some of Mercer's creations. We went to the Mercer Museum first and only had time to do the last tour at Fonthill (4 pm - you must take a one hour guided tour through the house) without the adjoining Morovian Tile Works. Big mistake. I did not anticipate wanting to see a tile factory, but after touring Fonthill know that you 100% will. The Mercer Museum is the storage castle for Mercer's 40,000 pre-industrial American tools, while Fonthill was the home Mercer built for himself that doubled as a showcase for his extraordinary tiles. His 3-dimensional history and story telling tiles, as well as a collection of foreign and ancient tiles, are embedded in the walls all over his almost gothic-style poured concrete castle. Our guide was incredibly knowledgable and completely entertaining, even though there were only 4 of us on the tour! As a previous reviewer said (and I wish I'd listened to), if you only have time to do one segment of the Mercer buildings, do Fonthill and the Tile Works over the museum. But ideally, do it all! Make sure to leave some time to explore Doylestown as well. It is an incredibly charming town with some great restaurants!

text: One of my favourite restaurants for date night!! It's interesting to go at different times of the year to see the beauty of each season. One time we went and had a great view of one of the condo buildings in construction that my husband worked on. La Ronde is fine dining and the prices and selection mirror that. I was pleased to see regional cuisine like bison, arctic char and pork on the menu, which is also reflected in their dessert options (Saskatoons!). Of course they have wines to complement your meal as well as a beer and spirits. Later in the evening entertainment takes place, usually in the form of a piano duo (singer) or instrumentalist with backup music. It adds to the atmosphere but at times can be a bit cheesy. Take your time to enjoy your meal and take advantage of the amazing scenery.

text: [this review is for the restaurant side of the S. Grand location, as I have not tried any items from the bakery... This is the best Chinese food in St. Louis and rivals any I've had elsewhere. The most fantastic thing on their menu is the scallion and ginger lo mein -- surprisingly light and flavorful, and fantastic as a cold leftover too (I always deliberately order extra so I can either eat it cold the next day or heat it up in some broth and hot sauce to make delicious soup). I also think they put cinnamon or something similarly magical in their crab rangoon, which, while hardly a hallmark of authentic Chinese cuisine, are a damn good movie night nosh. Bump this place to the top of your list... you'll never want to go anywhere else for Chinese food. Seriously.

text: The Franklin Mortgage and Investment company is so cool. I try not to fall for cool, but this place just oozes it from every corner. If you like cocktails, then this is absolutely the spot from you. The Franklin is an homage to the prohibition, speakeasy era. The name is the first disguise, and it's only noted by a small sign in front of the door. I scoped out the location from the across the street. The Franklin is a place where once inside, you feel like your in a special club. There are so many people walking by outside, and they don't even know! Inside, the Franklin looks gorgeous. The keep the lights low in their long, skinny space filled with tables and a small bar. The wait staff here is excellent. They definitely add to to environment in a unique way. Additionally, the drinks are top notch. I'm not big on cocktails, but it seems to be the only thing to order here. The drinks are incredibly well mixed and pack a punch. I'm not sure how this place gets on a weekend night; probably a bit too packed for my liking. Ideally, this is a spot where you can grab a table and relax with a few friends and share a few laughs over your cocktails. The daiquiri was all around my favorite, and the least alcoholic tasting. The bartender said he thought it was their best drink, and the standard by which any bar can be judged. "Walk into any bar in the world, and order their daiquiri. If it's good, then you can stay an have a few other drinks without having to worry about the quality." The "Old Fashioned" is a bourbon based drink that comes in a short tumbler with a hulking piece of ice. Approaching only with a fondness toward bourbon. Finally the Seelbach was a bitter champaigne-style cocktail. Good and strong, but not my favorite. Bottom Line: I'm not going to give you any hints on where the space is. Go find out for yourself. Feel like part of a special club. Close you eyes as you fork over $12 per drink. Enjoy the atmosphere, and take in the aura of a different time where one needed to drink in secrecy.

text: Years ago I heard from someone who lives in this neighborhood that this is a very good place. It's a well-established restaurant, at _least_ 10 years in this location, if I remember correctly. And that's a long time for a restaurant. It's on the south side of Pendleton Pike, and the cross street is Hartman Dr. I had lunch here, around 2:00pm, well after the lunch rush, and there were still a goodly number of customers. It's almost a hole-in-the-wall, looking at it from the outside, but don't let that fool you. Inside, the decor is better than average for an authentic Mexican restaurant. All Hispanic staff, with very good English skills. I liked the staff's professional and confident demeanor. These guys are pro's at running a restaurant. Which probably explains their longevity. The appetizer chips were thin, crispy, and warm, indicative of being made on premises. I couldn't tell if the salsa was made on premises or came from a bottle. It had a commercial consistency that made me think bottled, but flavor said home-made. It was flavorful and a just a little picante, but not biting. It could have used some more cilantro. You could scoop up lots of salsa on your chip and not worry about it burning your mouth. I had the lunch steak burrito. At first I noticed the small portion, but then realized that was a good thing for the lunch, and also because it was only $6, which was a great deal when you consider the chips. Filling up on a huge burrito is not a good thing for lunch when you have to go back to work anyway. The quality of the burrito, the chips, and the price made it a very good value. I was impressed with the decor for this type of restaurant. Not fancy, but not jarring like many Mexican restaurants that cater to an Hispanic clientele. In other words, the decor is gringo-friendly, but it's not pretending to be something it isn't. It just fit well with me. This is definitely worthwhile for lunch if you work in or near the area. I'll have to go back and try the dinner menu before I give it my "worth going out of your way for" rating. But it looks very promising.
label: POS

text: This is my 4th or 5th time going to Bar Ferdinand and it was just as awesome as always. I was there with a bunch of friends from The Restaurant School (TRS) for our friend Ann's visit back to Philly. This is one of her favorite places too. We also got our favorite waitress! I wish I knew her name cause I would give her mad props. I think every time I've had her, its been in a large group, and she handles us so well. On to the food! Everyone was sharing their dishes at the table, but I remember the one's April and I had the best. I got the carrot and ginger soup that was on special and it was wonderful. Very delicate flavor, silky and just delicious. I saw that they had a new sandwich, Pato Ahumado, that was a duck slider. It was the tastiest of all the sandwiches and I've tried them all. We both got the Datiles con Tocino which are dates, bacon, and cream cheese in a puff pastry. These are April's favorites. April also had their Salmon special for the night, which was house cured and presented on a Himalayan salt block. The salmon was stuffed with some sort of micro greens. It was good but some bites were a little too salty for me. She also got the Pork Belly and Monkfish Skewers, Pixin con Panceta. This is another dish I have had before and like. The pork belly they use is like 80% fat and just melts in your mouth while going so well with the monkfish. Our whole table ordered the Paella, which was not as good as I remember from my first visit there. It was good, but I just remember it being so much better. I guess the first time I had it was also the first time I had Paella too. Finally for dessert we finally tried their Churros con Chocolate, which we have been wanting to try every time we go but wind up going with something else. I guess our instincts were right, cause they were just ok. The chocolate dipping sauce was excellent, very rich and thick, but the churros just didn't do it for me. I guess I just prefer the Mexican style more.

text: EAT might be my favorite moderately-priced restaurant in the French Quarter. I've been once for brunch and once for dinner. Neither disappointed. First, about the establishment. Its in the heart of the gay section of the Quarter, a beautiful area. EAT is incredibly tiny with maybe seating for 20 at a time. They've got a tiny fireplace, lots of pretty windows, and a truckfull of Ikea furniture. Its incredibly cute and hip. Now onto Brunch. It was pretty crowded, but they seated the 5 of us within 10 minutes. The crowd was totally mixed with young, old, couples, singles, gays, straights... I had the fried green tomato plate served with grits, bacon, a biscuit, and the aforementioned tomatoes. Each was awesome. The grits were so buttery and clearly homemade. The biscuit rivals those from Bluebird Cafe. The fried green tomatoes were so tender and flaky. A carafe of OJ and the champagne we brought (BYOB!!!!) finished off an awesome meal. Everybody was so satisfied. Dinner. I went with my boyfriend for a more romantic dining experience and EAT definitely delivered. The small space looked great with the low dinner lighting and all the tables perfectly set. The place was much more empty with just several same-sex couples coming and going. We started out with a tomato cheese torte, which is basically a giant cheese chunk covered in nuts and sun-dried tomatoes. We devoured it... So delicious. I had the pork tenderloin for my meal. The best part was was the onions served on top of the pork... soaked in a balsamic sauce and roasted. Mmm... Boyfriend had redfish and was contented, but not quite as satisfied as I was. The service was great, the food delicious. I'll keep coming back. Note: extra gay friendly. woo! no strange looks!

text: This place sucks. When I pulled into the parking lot, they were at five starts -- innocent until proven guilty. When I saw the menu, they were at four stars. The selection was OK and the prices were a bit high for a diner. But, nevertheless, I was eager to try the food. The food was excellent. I felt like I definitely got my money's worth. After the meal, Oregon stayed at four stars. When the bill came, they dropped down to three stars. My friend had ordered a parm sandwich and nothing else. French fries had come with the meal, and he ate them because he assumed that fries were part of the deal when you order a sandwich. However, there was a separate charge for fries on our bill. My friend explained the situation to our waitress and that's when this racket plummeted to one star. She responded by informing him that the fries do not come with the sandwich and that he'd have to pay for them. She went on to say that he ate them and if he didn't want them he shouldn't have eaten them. He explained that he thought they simply came with the sandwich and that, in fact, their inclusion was THEIR mistake and he shouldn't have to pay for it. Here's where it gets crazy. The waitress explained that this is standard -- that "regular" customers know that Oregon will bring out the fries (WHICH ARE CHARGED EXTRA) and the customers will Oregon that they DON'T want the the (assumed) inclusion of fries while ordering. According to the waitress, my friend should have asked NOT to have the fries at additional charge. Are you all following this twisted logic? Let me break it down: Oregon ASSUMES that its customers want to receive an extra item that they haven't ordered and will only abstain from including it in your meal if you request that it NOT be included. Sorry Oregon, that's not how 99.9% of all restaurants in the world operate. They don't do that because, um......it's sort of ILLEGAL. Don't patronize these criminals.

text: I've heard a lot of good things about Acacia, but every time my girlfriend and I wanted to go, they'd be closed by eight. Tonight we finally got a chance to go. The ambiance was very nice, the restaurant was well lit, the plate wear was unique. There was only one server and back server working, and only maybe15 people seated. Considering that they did a adequate job, one con was the server didn't introduce himself by name. Things started going downhill after we ordered our apps. I ordered the chicken skewers, she ordered the goat cheese tart. The skewers were beautifully presented, and were plunged into a apple. Who'd have thunk apples and soy went together so well? Upon biting into the third and final skewer, I looked at the center of the chicken, and it was only half cooked. That's right, raw chicken. Usually, as a cook I never complain about the food, unless it's important. Raw chicken is an amateur thing. The server apologized, and offered a new one. I was pretty turned off and said no, but decided to continue with the meal. The tart, however was delicious. For the next course I Had the Halibut with cherry tomatoes and sauteed spinach and a light lemon sauce on top. The halibut was well cooked, perfectly seared, however under seasoned, as was the spinach. She had the savory custard tart with cauliflower mash and black quiona. She enjoyed it but said it was slightly over seasoned. For the price that we paid (75 with tip, I also got a cocktail) I don't feel like it was worth the meal that we had. We could have easily gone to somewhere like JW Marriott's Signature Grill or Primo or Maynard's downtown. All and all Acacia at St. Phillips Plaza was quite disappointing. I might give it another shot in the future, but not anytime soon.

text: I lived at The Boulders 6/2009 - 7/2010. My roommate and I hated it with a passion. The walls are paper thin and the woman upstairs constantly called security on us (it became a joke for security and I befriended most of them. We even had one security guard judge our Halloween pumpkins.) The apartment we lived in was near the back and against the dirt wall. It was over-run with spiders from the moment we moved in....just disgusting; I have never lived among so many spiders in my life. Ugh I get the heebie jeebies just thinking about The Boulders. Even with the weekly bug sprays they did, there were always spiders everywhere. I couldn't even set foot on our patio. YUCK. Walking up to the apartment was also gross. Cobwebs all over the outside stairs, dirty stains on the cement, pieces of garbage everywhere. Coming home each day just makes you dream of the day you can move. The apartment itself was also sad. The carpets were very stained when we moved in and completely worn down. We had to wear tennis shoes inside the apartment or our feet would hurt, it was like walking around on cement. The appliances were inefficient and worked poorly, including the stove/oven and the washer/dryer. I developed a cough over the year that I lived at The Boulders and I believe it is because of poor air circulation / air quality in the apartment. Now that I've moved, I'm hoping (praying!) this cough goes away. As far as amenities, the gym is tiny and the pool area is to the east of the main building...ie, at about 4pm the sun is blocked and the pool area has no more sunshine. Do not move here. The slightly cheaper rent compared to other complexes in Reno is not worth the shitty living conditions.

text: In a word, disgusting. I wish I could give this place zero stars, it is that bad. You could get better and more authentic Chinese food at Panda Express. I moved here from Chicago, where ethnic food is plentiful and delicious, in Indianapolis, it may be plentiful, but it is gross. As for China King, everything was super greasy. I had a sechuan beef - not spicy, and so greasy you could see the grease separating from the sauce. I had some flavorless and greasy eggrolls, and the most bizarre pork fried rice ever. It was YELLOW. Fried rice is supposed to be brown! Also there was almost no pork in it. I did not eat more than a few bites of anything, it was such a waste of money. Anyone with tastebuds or has eaten chinese food before should know this place is complete crap and should avoid like the plague.
label: NEG

text: We shoud have known something was up when we walked in and the place was EMPTY. Yeah, there were two other people eating, but it was a Monday night at 7:00 pm. The chips and salsa and guacamole dip was good, the margaritas were a little to sweet for our taste and the $2 Coronas was a good deal. However, then it was time for the food to arrive. EEEEEEEK! We live in Los Angeles and have our pick of excellent Mexican food restaurants but this is the first for us - french fries served on top of the chicken fajitas accompanied with only onions. No green or red peppers. Hmmmmm? I always thought beans and rice was the appropriate side dish, but fries? Then came the carnitas plate with onions. CHUNKS of fried pork. The chunks of pork were literally fried to the point of being small hard pieces of shoe leather. The onions were cut and thrown on as a garnishment, not cooked, not warm just plopped on the plate. Someone else at the table had the same thing and didn't finish an 1/8 of the dish as well. One suggestion, if you are thinking about eating here - DON'T! It is simple. DO NOT DO IT. Go to Taco Bell for a lot less money.
label: NEG

text: Love the yelp iPhone app. I wandered past Brasserie a night or two ago and filed the location in my memory. Was searching for a meal and Yelp reminded me that this was new in the area. Mine was a simple meal but satisfying. I love their space - couldn't have a better location for a cafe. Lunch consisted of a glass of Belleruche Cotes du Rhone and croque madame, followed by coffee. Friendly, attentive server who knew the wine list well. My food was delivered by a cute guy in business casual who could have passed for a customer and tasted great with a super-simple salad. I sat on the sidewalk in the cool shade of a tree rustling with the early afternoon breeze. Gorgeous. And my sandwich was really reasonably priced, I thought. Go visit! Support your local restaurateurs!
label: POS

text: Saturday night at 7:30, we didn't mind waiting 45 minutes to get seated. However, waiting 45 minutes to get our dinners, which were cold was a little unacceptable. It's a bit pricey, the service was awful. It may have been an anomaly, but it turned me off to the point of not wanting to return here.

I've had two out of 4 fairly decent haircuts. But they're expensive. Not worth the price. They charge extra to wash your hair. Seriously. Even with a color. This is a school, I think, so they should offer school prices not top of the line Manhattan prices with Chalmette styles.

text: OK, it has happened to everyone. You're already having a bad day, then something goes wrong with your car! Never fear - Polly's Service Center to the rescue. If your vehicle is really, really sick they have a towing service, which for a reasonable fee will come to you and tow in your car! This happened to me and the folks at Polly's could not have been more helpful. Native Nashvillians, the staff at Polly's explained to me that a mechanic would perform an inspection and call me with a "diagnosis" and estimate. True to their word, they called within one hour. The parts were ordered and my car was ready that afternoon. Their prices are very reasonable considering what you would pay at a dealership! When I was there I had just gotten my new Tennessee car tag, so the friendly mechanic offered to put it on for free! You can't argue with that!! The best thing about Polly's is that they really try to make you feel appreciated as a customer. They know all too well that having major car problems is the source of a great deal of stress, and they let you know they are fixing the problem as soon as possible. When it was time to change my spark plugs, a simple task compared to the engine trouble I had previously, there was no question where I was going for this routine care! Polly's is just as efficient at this simple task. When all is said and done, Polly's sends you on your way very relieved, and your wallet not too much lighter!
label: POS

text: Yep, this is definitely your neighborhood bar and restaurant. Just great food in a laid back atmosphere. I'm a fan of the salads (they have some great 1000 Island dressing), burgers, and the chicken parmigiana (which strangely does not come with spaghetti so you'll need to order that if you want it). There's plenty of outdoor seating where I was quite happy to eat lunch and enjoy my fruit tea on a recent summer day. It's another place that's a great place to have in my neighborhood, but I'd come here even if I didn't live up the street. Definitely a very friendly and accommodating wait staff. They'll also do carryout for you...I've often called ahead and come in to pick it up.
label: POS

text: We have been using For Paws Philly for the over a year to walk our two dogs on a regular basis. For Paws has also provided house sitting services while we were on vacation and has also had our two dogs at her home. For our past vacation, two weeks over Christmas, we had Sarah, the owner of For Paws, watch our dogs at her house. We were supposed to drop them off on 12/21/09 - the Monday after the big snow storm - so that we could catch an overseas flight early in the evening. We ended up being crunched for time and Sarah was able to come over and pick them up with only a few hours notice. They have both been at her house before and enjoy being there. Our one is not so great with other dogs, Pepper, so Sarah keeps him separated from other dogs she is watching but the other, Doctor, had a great time playing with the other dogs that Sarah was watching. While on our trip Pepper has some issues with an ear infection that we thought had cleared up before we left. She arranged to take him to our Vet and got him some additional medication which she applied for the rest of his stay. Sarah also comes over once a week so that my wife and I can go out after work and the dogs are always really excited to see her. Doctor is normally very scared of strangers - she was badly abused before we adopted her - but after a few visits she warmed up to Sarah and is now very happy to see her. Sarah was also great with an older dog that we had to put down earlier this year. Pinkie was only with us for a couple of years but she was a very special dog and Sarah always left very detailed notes about how she was doing on her weekly walks and alerted us when she thought there might be a problem. To sum up - Sarah has always come over to walk our dogs as scheduled, she is open to scheduling last minute walks, and leaves good notes as to results of each walk. More importantly, she takes great care of our dogs when she has them and is genuinely concerned about their welfare.
label: POS

text: This is a review of their new car sales only, (not service, not parts). I don't like these guys. You can call them what you will, but skimpy on the portions is not one of them.

text: I went here looking for some food for my short week in St Louis and walked away wishing I had found a Safeway or Kroger first. I walked in and almost immediately was nearly run over by a cart while simultaneously almost stepping on an elderly gentleman. This store is seriously small for the business it appears to be doing. Not only that, but the layout leaves you wandering aimlessly hoping you will come across the aisle that might contain the goodie you are looking for. To make things worse, the smells were in constant competition. The fish smell flowing from the seafood area and the bread smell from the bakery seemed to be in a war and the results were not all that appetizing. I did finally find something to tide me over for the week and then had to wait in the slowest checkout line I've experienced in a long time. The checker was trying to be helpful to the woman in front of me, but in reality it was only causing everyone else in the line to suffer. I'm just glad I don't have to shop at this store often. I'll take the Whole Foods in Boulder, CO anyday and I really hate that place!
label: NEG

text: This is literally a sushi BAR...meaning there's only about 15 seats available to enjoy the all-you-can-eat sushi. My boyfriend and I were staying there at the hotel and were craving sushi so we figured we'd just head over to the sushi bar. We were famished since we were skiing all day, so we were very disappointed to hear we had to wait an hour and a half! Who knew there were so many sushi fans in Reno!! We decided to try to sit at the regular bar next to it but those seats were also filled. So, we walked to the other side and the manager there rudely told us that that side of the bar was for restaurant patrons only. Sidebar: The sky terrace is basically one long wide hallway with an oyster bar, a "drinks" bar, and a sushi bar one after the other smack in the middle with a seafood restaurant located on one side of the bars and slots on the other. Luckily once we sat by some slot machines, a couple seats opened up at the bar so we decided to get some drinks to pass the time. Nick was our bartender and he was great! We quickly got served our drinks and after about 30 mins of hunger, we decided to get an appetizer to make it through the next hour wait. I hesitantly asked if we could order off the sushi menu and he said a la carte only. That's when my eyes opened up with a gleam of hope! My boyfriend and I were planning to not do the all-you-can-eat so it was perfect! We waited a third of the time and still got our yummy sushi. And boy was it good! I wasn't expecting much seeing as this was a sushi bar in a casino...in Reno! But, I was happily pleased with the Tekka Maki, Sky Terrace and Mermaid rolls along with inari and a spicy tuna hand roll. The Mermaid roll was my fave with deep fried (not tempura) shrimp inside and a "Jason" special on top...which is grilled scallops in a creamy sauce. The rolls were bigger than expected and delicious! I already know this will be a stop next time I'm in town. I plan to go there for lunch since the all-you-can-eat is a deal for only $16! Because I understand the reason for the long wait, my sole complaint stems from the service. Aside from Nick (who was the only person who paid attention to us), there was a lack of service on the sky terrace. When I asked to be put on the wait list, I felt like the hostess didn't even want to put down my name cuz the wait was so long. When we asked 30 mins later if it was still going to be another hour, she confirmed in a cold tone. We had a reason to ask since a big group had just been seated. And I already mentioned the manager who belittled us for being on the wrong side of the bar - There are no barriers or signs that distinguish where people are free to sit so it was an honest mistake which could have been handled in a more forgiving manner. And lastly, when Nick went on a break, we could not get the attention of the other bartender after calling out his name and gesturing him to come over several times. He was focused on some 'regulars' sitting right next to us but ultimately made a bad impression on hotel guests. Workers there definitely need a refresher course on guest services. If you can avoid all this and get there early enough to find an open seat at the sushi bar, you'll have a guaranteed pleasant and fulfilling experience.
label: POS

text: I agree with David H. It is a great place to watch sports - lots of brand new flat panels and great beer. The drink specials during NFL games are pretty good. The food is the killer here. The wings are okay, but after that it all goes downhill. My burger tasted like cardboard. I hope the food gets better, but that hope is unlikely to be fulfilled as this place was apparently opened by the owners of the restaurant that previously occupied the space, Ecco Qui. That place was bad. Bottom line: Nice environment and good drink selection. Bad food.
label: NEG

text: This place is pretty dismal. My boyfriend and I got up really late on a Sunday afternoon and were looking for a place to eat in the middle of the afternoon. As it turns out, most restaurants in town close between 2 and 7 or so, so we were having a pretty hard time. After a lot of walking, we found River's Edge, which was still open and had a sign saying they serve breakfast all day. We should have known better, given the touristy location, but we were starving so we decided to give it a try. They serve pretty typical local food, and indeed have breakfast all day. We both got omelets: I got the Louisiana omelet, which came with peppers, onions, crab meat, and creole sauce, with a side of potatoes. Quite honestly it wasn't good at all: the omelet was way overcooked and the eggs were brown... it was dry and I probably would not have been able to eat it if it weren't for the sauce. The service was friendly but very very slow... I wouldn't recommend coming here.
label: NEG

They have a full salad bar and there pizza is the best in SB. It's not too greasy and they don't deprive you of your toppings. I grew up on this pizza and its unique taste lingers in your mouth leaving you addicted and wanting more! I cannot wait until the next time I am home so I can devourer another individual pizza.

text: OK - here's some interesting trivia for you. This store, located behind the Moorestown Mall, is the first AC Moore store (referred to as Store 1 by employees) and was 20 years old before the refurb. The new store is the first of AC Moore's generation two layouts, including trains, digital publishing stations, two huge classrooms, and oodles of enhancements. Fun fact - the truck in the store was previously from Old Navy! I guess they gave the AC Moore folks a great deal! The selection here can't be beat (like a dozen types of feather boas right as you walk in people - how can you beat that!) and the new digital publishing and custom framing solutions tops in the industry.
label: POS

text: In town to celebrate a friend's birthday, I ended up at this spot. We were trying to avoid frat boys and bar scene, so we thought a 'lounge' would be a perfect fit. There were four of us in the group ranging from 28-33. We didn't wait in line but did have to dole out $10 cover charge...I wasn't happy considering it was only 11:30 and the place was dead. The decor is pretty cool; there is a voyeuristic white screen at the back reflecting a live dancer's silhouette. There's a large wall framing the VIP area, which lights up in bright colors in sync with DJ's music (80s,90s pop and hip hop) . The music was uninspiriting and found it more amusing to stare at the 'colorful wall' than step on the dance floor. I agree with previous yelpers with the 'trying too hard' crowd. On a somewhat positive note, the place was packed with people by 1 am and plenty more waiting in line on a rainy, Friday evening. The ladies facilities were not customer-friendly. Around midnight , the line was 30 minutes long. There were four stalls, but only 3 were working. To add to the delay, a coed had too much to drink and got sick on one of the sinks. The attendant screamed at the poor girl, as it seemed they were limited on paper napkins. . . the scene was unsanitary, disgusting at best. So, I think the place is 'on the right track' but still needs to 'tie up' some loose ends. The VIP area (bottle service) is about 8-10 tables large but completely empty (only 1 table was being used). They should allow patrons to sit and lounge in unused tables, instead of opting for a quarter empty space. Drink prices: a mixed drink was in the $9 range, a beer was $6.
label: NEG

While seeing The Slits a couple of months ago, some ass punched me in the back of the head on purpose. regardless, that shouldn't reflect on the venue. They have great shows right in my neighborhood and they charge extremely reasonable prices to see them. If you haven't already, check them out.

text: A Lot of HYPE.. Very Little TRUTH I had heard great things about Moon's so I took my husband for lunch one day. They place was cavernous and absolutely NOTHING had been done to keep all the diner sounds from reverbarating. Our sandwiches were nothing like what was described in the menu, with most of the components seeming like stuff from a bag (frozen chicken patties, processed cheese slices, mass produced buns). To top it all off the server spilled an entire soda on my husband. Yes, they were very apologetic and did not charge us for my husbands meal, but that did not give us any reason to go back. I had hoped their breakfast might be better, but given what I've read here at Yelp I won't be giving it a shot.

text: Driving into this airport is ridiculous. Perhaps this is due in large part to my HOW, but based on the contradictory signs for parking, I think not. Having virtually no lighting on streets with exits off of 50 or 40 miles per hour is definitely not the cakewalk a traveler would hope for! Thankfully we left with plenty of time, so it was nothing more than a small argument on driving techniques. Had the entrances/exits been more clearly marked and organized, it would have been a solid four stars. Hopefully when what looks like renovations are completed it will be more easily navigated.

text: So after spending the afternoon painting at a friend's house in Boothwyn, we were starving and looking for something more than fast food. Someone mentioned the Boothwyn Diner, and we decided to try it out. My star break-down is as follows: MINUS ONE STAR for being in a strip mall; respectable diners are always stand-alone buildings PLUS ONE STAR for the psychedelic and overwhelming decorations; someone's three year old decorated the place with streamers, pictures on all the walls, chandeliers and colored lights. it's overwhelming, but makes me happy. PLUS ONE STAR for a waitstaff that does everything to please; seriously, she was amazing. she kept bringing us more things, checking if we were happy, etc. we felt special :) PLUS ONE STAR for cheap, plentiful food. It's all there, just like you would expect from a diner, it's all cheap, and it's all reasonably good. PLUS ONE STAR for ridiculous menus. The same three year old designed the menu. One page must have had at least 15 colors scattered around the page. Craziness. PLUS ONE STAR for taking credit cards PLUS ONE STAR for breakfast all day and for the huge dessert case.
label: POS

The food was good but it was the service that made us come back the next day. The next day we felt that we were in a different restaurant as she was not there and the service was poor. text: I booked this location because it was in the French Quarter but on a side street, and also close to Frenchman St. The hotel did not disappoint. We had a superior room overlooking the pool. The room is a little musty but it is quite big and the beds are comfortable. There is a continental breakfast included. The location is perfect (in the middle of everything but quiet at night) and quite close to the Blacksmith Bar on Royal St that is fabulous. I would come back to this hotel.

text: This is one of my all-time favorite New Orleans places. My dad used to get kicked out of this place for being too rowdy with his friends in the early 1960's and has been going ever since. ;-) I've been going my whole life- and it hasnt changed much since the late 1970's (as far back as I can remember). EVERYTHING is good here, but the frozen beers and the onion rings are the best. The po-boys are good, and the frenchuletta is awesome. The fried seafood is good too. I usually get the fried pickles too (which I love). If you are coming to New Orleans and want to go to a REAL New Orleans place, go here. REAL New Orleans people dont eat in the French Quarter for casual dining. They go to neighborhood places like Liuzza's.
label: POS

text: Dogs may be a man's best friend, but shoes are certainly a woman's best friend. I just started taking salsa and tango classes, but I always showed up in my chucks... so after 6 lessons, I thought it was time to show my seriousness and buy a pair of dance shoes. I went Tango dancing last Saturday night at South Street Studio (1527 South St), and Meredith Klein had recommended this place to me. I was a little taken aback at first, because I'm a novice in the dancing department and I mentioned that and the [only] guy present seemed a little impatient and/or rude. However, he must have been annoyed at something else because he eventually snapped out of it and warmed up to me. I tried on a bunch of different shoes, and he told me the difference between each one and explained which one you would where at which time, at which event, and which brands are more reliable and worth the cost of the shoe, how the shoe should be taken care of, etc. I loved how detailed he was. Fortunately I had some time to spend there because I didn't want to rush this purchase. I still wasn't sure about which shoe to buy, and then a light goes off in his head and he says, "ah! I have the perfect shoe for you, and I believe I only have your size left!" Boy. He knew what he was talking about. I fell in love with them: the fit, the color, not so much the price... and he was so funny, he called me his cinderella cause apparently these shoes run small. (These are the shoes I bought: http://www.grishko.ru/tangoeng/danceshoes_4180.htm ) All in all, I had a good experience here. I especially recommend it for dancing shoes and clothes and accessories! Despite the small appearance, they can fit a lot of shoes. Oh Shoes Shoes Shoes.
label: POS

text: For now, this is the only place for downtown-dwellers to get groceries without driving a few miles. You can get basic groceries, as well as some international goodies, like curry sauce and sushi rice. There's also a small meat counter and deli. Pretty cool if you're looking rushing to make a sandwich before heading back up to your loft or office. What's really convenient is the hot bar that charges by the pound. I suggest breakfast if it's your first time. The lunch/dinner items can sometimes get dry and unappetizing (they taste pretty good either way). I may be reaching, but City Grocers has the BEST biscuits and gravy in the entire city. Flaky biscuits made by people in chef hats (a plus) with a thick (not too milky) spicy gravy (Italian sausage?) make me a very happy guy. Actually, a slice of their quiche with that same gravy is probably going to be my choice for Last Meal On Earth. I've been going on and on about cholesterol-filled greatness, but there's a salad bar as well. I like the Thai salad. Aside from that, City Grocers rocks it out with a decent beer, liquor, and wine selection for the size of the place. Again, great for last-minute buys. There's plenty of seating upstairs, where people-watching can last the entire day.
label: POS

text: Honest opinion: WAY TOO MUCH GREASE!!! My husband and I came here based on the great reviews this place got and were pretty disappointed that we came away feeling like we paid $17 each for a breakfast entree that was grease, grease and more grease. I'm as much a fan of anyone of country potatoes, but they were dripping with grease, as were our poached eggs and the dungeness crab cakes. Very cute place, nice staff and it has potential if they would lay off the grease.
label: NEG

text: Marathon Grill--avoid it like the plague! The restaurant boasts having no redeeming qualities: the service, food, and atmosphere were paltry. Our waitress was an unfit drab of a person, who was more content lounging with the rest of the wait staff at the back of the dining room than tending to her customers. At times, I felt like we were eating in an abandoned strip mall streaked with filth and set for demolition. My order, a salmon burger, frightfully appeared wearing the familiar Philadelphia dress of squalor. The fries, something so easy and delicious, were mere stumps, bland and freezer-burned. On top of my burger rested a clump of burnt red pepper instead of delicious sweetness; I spent a few minutes dissecting these charred remains. The goat cheese had been carelessly flung onto the burger and all of it hung to the edge of the bun for dear life. Should I have returned this sad dish? But wait, dish is far too kind, I should have sent this carrion to autopsy, so we may not only know its cause of death, but exactly what it even is. Yes, I should have, but I didn't. Instead, without joy, and like a coward, I ate it. Do not act as imprudently as I--even if you are with the greatest hunger. Do not eat at Marathon Grill. Invariably, it will let you down.
label: NEG

text: A few points to be made. Dyer Chiropractic has an attractive office, and is conveniently located... The office has an open concept floor plan, which seemed a little weird at first, but which ended up being okay. Despite these good points, I will not be going back to this office, and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone else either. I first went there because I was suffering from some persistent headaches and chiropractic has helped with those in the past. We had recently moved from out of state and I needed a new chiropractor. I went a handful of times... The first visit was nothing more than a consultation, which was a bit disappointing, as I had hoped to get an adjustment that day. As I said, I was dealing with some pretty bad headaches and I needed relief. He recommended that I go to a hospital to get some spinal x-rays, because I had not had any in a couple of years. I got them that evening, and hand delivered them to their office. One thing that made me a bit uncomfortable was the sense of forced Christianity while I was there. In a professional office, I expect for the interactions to be professional, and kinda surprised by the comments that he would make periodically. For example, at one point, he said to me, "Christ is great, isn't he?" Only, it wasn't a rhetorical question... He asked it again when I didn't respond the first time. This made for an awkward interaction because I feel that spirituality is a private matter and not something I need to be discussing with persons I barely know. Despite this, I made my first appointment, and things went fine enough. The next time I was there, I happened to be scheduled right after a woman who seemed to think that the chiropractor was also her therapist. She was in the next stall over, and talked and talked and talked. This went on for literally half an hour... all while I was sitting there waiting. He finally got to me and made no apologies for making me wait. I was willing to see this as a fluke, but it just so happened that my next appointment was ALSO scheduled just after this woman. This time, he was with her for even LONGER. I considered walking out, as my time is just as valuable as his, and anyone else's. Finally he made it to me, and he did apologise this time, telling me that, "Some people need a little more help." Fine. But we're all customers. I felt that he should have adjusted me first, and gotten me out of the way if he knew that this woman needed more "help" (i.e. time to chit chat.) Fast forward to three weeks ago. Despite tri-weekly visits to their office, no one had ever told me that I had an outstanding balance... but they finally got around to letting me know. My health fund had apparently run out, and the rest would be out-of-pocket. No big deal... But I would have like to be notified BEFORE two months of co-pays had accumulated. A week after that (two weeks ago) we received our first and ONLY bill from them. TODAY... I got a voicemail from their office asking me to take care of the "situation" with my bill, and telling me that they didn't want to have to turn me over to collections. I was floored. I had not had the bill in my hands for more than a couple weeks, and on top of that, I was still waiting to see if the insurance made any more payments before paying my balance. I feel insulted that they brought up turning me over to collections as though I was some sort of criminal. This is especially troubling considering the strong "Christian" message they seem to hold to so dearly. This is clearly another example an entity claiming to embrace Christian values while acting in a way that is contrary to that. As I said, I won't be back.
