text: I'm not big on smoothies. There, I've said it. In my life, I just found smoothies to taste like frothy ice with bits of fruit in it here and there. Then there's Jamba Juice. It completely changed my views on what a smoothie should be. Sweet, Satisfying, Smooth. Honestly, I never understood why they were called smoothies until Jamba Juice. All of the flavors, from the Peanut Butter Moo'd to the Aloha Pineapple, are "to die for" good, but are "love live the king" good for you. There are also seasonal smoothies, such as the Pumpkin Spice in the fall (which absolutely must be tried), and what some call "secret smoothies", such as the Strawberry shortcake and White Gummy Bear (equally awesome). Apart from the smoothies, they sell some really tasty baked goods and various packaged health snacks; they both make a great meal on the go when combined with an original or power sized smoothie. The establishment has a modern look to it, with brushed steel and wood. The place is big on being healthy; there are workout books, workout equipment, juicers, and other paraphernalia, have wheatgrass shots and also give you the opportunity to put what they call "boosts" in your smoothie. These boosts are various supplements such as daily vitamins, fiber, protein and even an immunity boost. Some of these boosts are free, and others cost 50 cents. Speaking of immunity, if you ever have a cold, I highly advise one of their smoothies known as the "Coldbuster"; every time I have a cold, I drink one and my disease goes away within three days. Tastes better than anything over the counter liquid, and seems to work just as well. This place can get very busy, but the staff seem to make it all breeze by quickly. They are all friendly and cheerful people, adding even more lightness into the store. These people remember you too, I was absent for a good two or three weeks and they smiled and remembered what I liked to order without a second's thought. Redefine smoothie for yourself. Go have a Jamba Juice.
label: POS

text: The first time we walked by Pascucci's we saw a nice sized crowd outside waiting for tables. The second time we walked by, same thing. The third time, we decided we'd try it out. Of course I yelped Pascucci's and was thrown off by the 3 1/2 star rating. Why the disparity between the yelpers and the swarm of people waiting outside? I should have trusted my fellow yelpers reviews. This place is ok. It was a little anti-climactic even. Upon seating, they will give you a basket of one of the most delicious cheesy garlic breads you'll have in your life. I would have eaten the entire thing if not for the need to share with the hubby. So now expectations are running high... Wah, wah, wah... I ordered a Pizza di Lucca with goat cheese, artichoke hearts, olives, peppers and sundried tomatoes. The ingredients sounded so deelish. As my mouth watered in anticipation, I was envisioning a thin crust pizza about to be placed in front of me. No... it looked more like a personal pan pizza from Round Table! And not to discount RT if that's your thing, but this pizza is not what I expected from a seemingly authentic Italian restaurant calling itself Pascucci's! Hubby ordered the Venezia pasta: farfalle with smoked salmon and capers in a lemon-cream sauce. The only thing good about this dish was how it sounded on the menu. It was pretty bad. The salmon was way too salty and the sauce was gummy. Our server was sufficient but didn't come around too often. The big crowds standing outside steered us wrong. I should have stuck to the yelp reviews!

I rarely get to come here because they close so relatively early, but some co-workers have recently expressed a willingness to drive down here and the higher frequency has led to my trying other things. Boy am I ever glad I have. The falafel is by far the best falafel that I've ever had. text: When I moved from Boston, home of the largest Vietnamese population in the northeast, to Philly, I was afraid I was going to have a hard time getting good Vietnamese food. I went to a couple of places that were lackluster, at best, and Pho Hoa is always a standard OK, but this was the first place I found that really compared to my hometown's Pho. The pho here is delicious, the broth is rich and savory and just a little on the salty side, which I love. I usually go for the beef and beef flank, or something with meatballs, and I've never been disappointed. The only thing about this place, and I think someone else mentioned it, is that they only have pho. I love a range of Vietnamese foods, and I wish I could share some bun or chicken salad with friends if I go in a group, but I suppose that's one of the reasons they do their pho so well.

text: Lovely, lovely, lovely. First let me mention, they have $5 classic cocktails 5-7 on weekdays, including the Sazerac, Moscow Mule, Stinger, Pimm's Cup, and Daiquiri. Okay, review time: you know The Violet Hour in Chicago? Because Cure is a LOT like that place, with the pretension scaled way down. The bartender helped start the former before coming back down here to open Cure after Katrina. The two places share meticulously crafted ambiance--here, large windows, exposed brick and polished concrete floors, with old apothecary-style sketches on the walls--and seriously world-class cocktails. These folks are professionals. If you grab a seat at the bar you can watch them spare no expense of time or effort to craft your drink. I'm talking slicing off orange peel to spritz your (beautifully cubed) ice with orange essential oil, or slapping a single mint leaf to coax out the aroma. I found the bartenders forthcoming with knowledge about every spirit behind the bar, and many of their syrups and cordials are house-made on a bunsen-burner type stove. If that doesn't make you feel all warm and tingly inside, the drinks themselves will. Please do expect to pay for it, of course. My advice is to come here for no more than a cocktail or three, as you'll want to avoid spending over $30 or $40 on drinks you're no longer sober enough to appreciate. (And if that still sounds ludicrous to you, well, Miss Mae's is still doing $1 wells.)

text: Unbelievably disappointed. I had heard so much about this restaurant. We arrived as a group of 3 with a small child treating ourselves to a lunch here, as lunch is a great way to experience an expensive restaurant without paying too much. Like others, I will comment that service was unbelievably slow. We started out with an order of a dozen of their assorted oysters. After 30 minutes, they asked if we would prefer eating our entrees first or our oysters. Our entrees were ready but it would take another 10 minutes for the oysters. That was an odd thing to ask and I didn't understand why. It's an open kitchen and there were very few filled tables. 3 cooks should have been found the time to shuck at least one oyster. We opted for the entrees as we were all getting filled on our second order of bread. It took 40 minutes for them to bring a kids cup of water for my son. I ordered a salad to be doubled up to be large enough for an entree. OK and definitely not spectacular arugula salad. 98% arugula and the rest was slices of pear, walnut crumbles and cheese. For what was essentially 15 dollars, I could have gotten a great "wow I wish I knew how to make this at home" salad at many other similiarly priced restaurants in Tampa. The other two diners I was with received an overcooked Wagyu burger and an Ok grouper sandwich. Oysters came out last and although we ate it, it frightened one member in our group because they were so warm. They were only ok oysters even if they were from NewEngland and Canada. For their name they should be serving spectacular oysters. Each adult had one order of alcoholic beverage and the meal came to 100 dollars. I don't mind paying alot for a good meal but I have spent just as much having dinner at any of the other great restaurants in Tampa and left with better service and better prepared food: food that blows your mind. When you are charging these prices, you are also promising a commensurate level of food quality and trained staff. We found neither. While the service staff are always present, it feels disorganized and undertrained. On a side note, as a Mom who enjoys eating out with her two kids, I find that the Kids Menu at many restaurants is a reflection of the management and the chef's attitudes towards food. Rarely have I ever seen such JUNK on a kids Menu: Hot dog and chips, PB&J and fries, Mac N Cheese and chips, etc. for 8-10 dollars??? You may argue that the restaurants are not catering towards kids but I would argue that if you serve junk, then your belief is that people don't know any better.

text: i remember i went here 2 years after hurricane Katrina. I went with my Vietnamese friend and his gf for his cousin's wedding and we had one of the worst hotel experiences ever. By the time we checked in, it was like only 8pm, ....we all got dressed and called the restaurant downstairs to see if we had to make a reservation to eat there, and the guy said absolutely not and that we would be good to go. When we went downstairs, i had to use the restroom so i had my asian friends go first to get our table. When i got there, my friends were STILL waiting. I asked my friends what the deal was. They told me that the host had told them that they had to make a reservation. I was like "WTH???...but i just called them like only 15 minutes ago!". Anyhow, when the host got back, i had told him that i called a bit earlier and that the person on the phone said that we didn't need reservations. At this point, i was really irritated, i can't say for sure, but it felt like it was a racial thing. When the manager came, he saw that i was with my two asian friends and he apologized and said it was a mistake. I just let it go so my friends wouldn't feel awkward, ya know? The room was decorated fairly modern but you can tell it was an old building converted into a so called high end hotel. I mean...at least in vegas they charge for the day, which means 24 hours....this lame hotel charged like $6.99 for every few hours! That's whack. It's like we wanted to support the town after the tragic flood but with service and prices like this...i don't know. text: I like watching Canadian Football League (CFL) games and got my start watching the old Sacramento Gold Miners. Players such as Doug Flutie and Jeff Garcia have come out the CFL. The game is longer, wider, and deeper than the NFL and the rule differences (like only 3 downs, 12 men on the field, and different kicking strategies) do take some getting used to. And with these differences, CFL games are fun to watch. In particular, I noticed that games often are one at sometimes the last second and that the weather makes a huge difference for the team and for me personally (I've been caught short for lack of proper layering). A CFL season usually runs from July to mid-November. When I'm in Edmonton at the right time, I usually go with my friend Karl. And if the Eskimos beat Calgary (Karl hates Calgary), we call up our friend Jim (a true Stampeder fan) and rag on him. Memorial Statium is a big place even by NFL standards. It's also the place where they staged an outdoor NHL game several years ago. I prefer sitting in the lower deck for the sight lines and to stay away from the occassional roudy fans upstairs. Overall, I like the stadium, the fan energy, and the overall experience.

text: Don't go here starving. If you do--don't approach the counter. You may over order. I speak from experience. I am, however, glad I took a look at what was cooking. Between three hungry people--I got to sample a little bit of everything. A lot of it was Columbian fare I didn't even know existed. My favorite discovery was "Mondongo." It's kind of the equivalent to Mexican "Menudo" in that they make this soup from the belly of the beast. The difference, however, is a much more complicated flavor. Lots of vegetables are thrown at this dish making it delicious and good for the soul--so eat up! Masitas de bayun (not sure on the spelling) were my next favorite. The masitas are little corn spheres with a little dose of cheese inside. A really nice combination. More stock items like Sancocho, morcia and empanadas are available and tasty too. The menu is fairly expansive. If you're looking to gain a lot of weight fast--this may be the place for you! The servings are more than generous. If you are watching your weight--pace yourself or you'll suffer like me and not have room to try their baked goods.

text: I'm totally stumped by all these bad reviews. My husband and I eat brunch here every time we come to town. They have everything from omelet stations to crab legs and oysters. My only complaint is the price.... at $25 a head you can quickly rack up a bill.... but the view makes up for it.

text: My husband and I both have numerous watches, some for work and play and others for dress, we also have a very bad habit of when the battery wears out, we set the watches aside and just start wearing another one, until we get to the point where we are left without a watch! Talk about procrastination, which ends up costing us dearly! Right now I have three watches that need batteries replaced and I refuse to wear my gold and diamond watch for everyday use, tacky plus knowing me, it would end up in the dead watch pile. Hubby is down to wearing his Rolex with two Seiko's stopped in time. One of hubby's watches simply needs a pin, but when he has a battery replaced he insists on having it sent off to be sealed, because his watch never leaves his wrist, including showers and dish washing, I for one can't wait to take my watch off when I get home, so I really could care less if the watch is resealed or not. The last time hubby took one watch to Time after Time and not only did he wait for weeks to have it resealed but it cost him $50.00 plus tax! We have never paid such an exuberant price for having one watch battery replaced and the watch resealed. I'm sure their profit was a grand one, but they lost the chance to service us again!
label: NEG

text: I checked out Time on a Saturday night, during a visit to Philly with my boyfriend. We found out about it on Yelp, and were happy we did. There was a $5 dollar cover, and apparently several rooms. My boyfriend and I were drawn into the what looked like the main room by the live band, and stayed put. The drinks were strong and reasonably priced. I enjoyed several tasty manhattans for a way-cheaper-than-Manhattan price. The jazz band that night was excellent! The crowd was okay-- definitely a good mix of young professionals and students, but not very diverse. All in all, though I don't live in the area, I would definitely go back to Time and I have already referred my sister to the place.
label: POS

text: Worst food of any place I have ever reviewed. The food is absolutely terrible. There was a reason my mom packed lunches for me when I was in grade school. This place brings back memories of bland servings that are spruced up by adding tons of salt. Come eat here if you want to vasoconstict those arteries. However, the atmosphere at this place takes a back seat to no one. The outdoor patio overlooking the main strip of Broadripple is the place to see and be seen. My recommendation to anyone coming here is to eat in advance, and sit outside all day and load up on drinks. That in all honesty is a four star experience. They need to add another person to their shifts too. They seemed to be swamped, unless someone called in sick, which is why I would limit it to four stars in that scenario. Drinks and people watching? Yes!!! Food? No. Even the chips and salsa are a major Fail. Sticking a chip on your tongue is the equivalent of licking a block of salt. La Jolla can be a great experience, I will definitely come back, and I would recommend it highly as long as you take eating out of the equation. Consider yourself warned, and have fun!
label: NEG

text: I really liked Casona. It's has a nice quiet setting that's a bit unique and offers a great (and from what I understand more authentic than the rest) Cuban menu. Everything I've tried was delicious and in a sense the fact that it's BYO is a plus, as you can bring exactly what you want to drink and don't have to pay extra for it...
label: POS

text: I lived in Roma for a year back in college and this is the best gelato I have had stateside. Please come down to DC! We have some solid pretenders but nothing like this. It is/was available in the frozen section of Balducci's for 9.99/pint which I splurged on years ago.... but walking in in person and having some fresh rhubarb/coconut was divine.
label: POS

text: What can you really expect from an all-night diner at a casino? I say a little bit more than this. I suppose if I was a senior and didn't mind eating dinner at 2:30 to get the 50% discount, it would be worth it, but seeing as I didn't qualify for that, I was disappointed. The club sandwich is something that really separates the men from the boys when it comes to diners. A good club must follow a few simple guidelines. Bread: toasted and crispy. Produce: fresh. Bacon: crispy. Fries: hot and crispy. They failed on 3 of 4, and with the $9.00 pricetag, it was certainly not worth it. The American cheese was an unwelcomed addition, as well. I also tried the pizza...I knew it would be prefrozen dough, but I thought it would at least be cooked enough because it was supposedly from a brick oven. As I saw the blond crust, and wire marks on the bottom of the pie, I knew the drill. Totally under-seasoned and undercooked cisco products. Oh well. It would get a 1-star, but we had fun pointing out all the staff who looked and acted like they were on meth...which was a fair amount. Too bad there wasn't a way to bet on that. I guess since there's nothing else to get for late night munchies, you may as well go to Cafe Meth instead of digesting your stomach lining. Or you can get a case of Easy Mac and microwave it in your room, with a similar level of quality and satisfaction.
label: NEG

text: I used to be a fan of the Iron Hill restaurants, but the past three visits have not been memorable. The other night my boyfriend and I ordered burgers. The buns looked and tasted like stale Acme hamburger buns. They were thin and broke into tiny pieces as soon as we picked up our burgers to take our first bite. A big clue that the buns were from the grocery store was seeing a guy walk out of the kitchen with an Acme brown paper bag in his arms. I mentioned this to the manager, and the look on her face was a guilty one.
label: NEG

text: Went to Zavino Saturday night quite late around 10 PM and it was still pretty packed, so we left our name and got a drink. They told us it would be about 30 min and almost to the minute they called my cell phone telling me there was a table for us. The basic pizza was quite good and so was the app of squash that my girlfriend and I shared (although the cheese used on top was a little firm and rubbery). I was a little dissapointed in the wine list. I kind of thought there would be some more interesting wines and maybe a little higher end.
label: NEG

text: Yakitori Boy,With the charm of a pick pocket, leaves feeling violated and embarrassed that you chose this pretentious hole as a way to be separated from your weekend money. $100 an hour just to sit at a table. 18% gratuity to eat the smallest portions of food you have ever seen. Every draught taste like Budweiser, but you keep drinking them waiting for your chance to pay $4 a song while the smoke machine symbolically represents the smoke being blown up your ass, as you realise the true purpose of this place is to get as much of your money before you get fed up and walk out, making excuses to the birthday girl for your early departure.

text: a testament to the human spirit.....the arch like the eiffel tower is a remarkable feat of engineering that frequently is taken for granted because it is in our back yards but i continue to see it as reminder of the great things we can make happen if we work together....reflecting what is great about the usa!!!!!! even if you don't want to go up in the arch there is a amazing museum below which is filled with interesting facts about the area.......
label: POS

text: This place is good when you want something different for a change. Breakfast or lunch only since they close at 2pm. Each kolache is only $1 to $3, and I'm satisfied with 1 or 2. Service has been pretty excellent lately! I would not recommend anything with bacon in it; it never seems like it gets cooked enough. And not the sausage one; I think it's like a sausage link in a hollow dough shell. What I will recommend is the sausage and gravy one. Completely rocks. My 2nd favorite is the pizza, which is a combination of pepperoni and mushroom. My 3rd favorite is ham and cheese. I know the Ranchero is popular, but I'll admit I haven't tried this one yet, so until next time...update: next time has come and gone, and I would say that Ranchero is now one of my regular purchases - not as good as sausage/gravy, pizza, or ham/cheese, but pretty good, esp. if you want more of a breakfast-y one. Italian chicken sounds popular, and the store employees told me the same thing. I had it once, and it wasn't for me, but I would normally like these ingredients. Perhaps I need to try one more time.
label: POS

text: I came here with a party of 9, we got seated in their outdoor patio section and started drinking from the case of beer we brought with us and with the pitchers of mixers they provided for us. We waited and waited to get our food order taken, it was a Saturday night and since we were drinking it didn't bother us too much. The alcohol ran out eventually and we still hadn't been asked what we wanted to order(about a hour and 45 minutes had passed since we sat down). We decided to finally get up and leave since we were still hungry, one of us wanted to inform the waitstaff that we were leaving and was met with this response from a waiter,"hold on a sec, I'll be right with you..." No thanks, since we had a much better meal in Chinatown that night...

text: The owners of this joint obviously hate their customers--and they train their employees to do the same thing. From the dirty old rooms to the vague "it's over there" waving of the staff. If you have to go to Reno--stay anywhere but here.

text: This is the classiest way to end an evening. Not your typical bar! This prohibition style speakeasy has some classic drinks that are handcrafted for you. It's a bit on the expensive side, but definitely worth it. Don't head over here if you're just looking for a beer, or even a glass of wine. Liquor only. And their drinks are STRONG. If you're planning on spending the evening here, better get here early, it's a small intimate space and packs up, especially on the weekends. I highly recommend this place if you're looking for somewhere a little unique and upscale.

text: Quick review: China Palace is inadequate as an option for Chinese take-out., given the better option nearby. On it's own, China Palace would stand as a common, but suitable, Chinese take-out spot. But given the myriad other options in the Norristown area, including one clearly superior option (Super Wok, maybe 3 minutes away at most), I recommend passing China Palace by. The food is not bad, but it's not as good as Super Wok. The service is clearly worse, and the cleanliness and decor is also not up to Super Wok. There is no place to eat inside; it's solely take-out (although you will find people simply eating on the front steps of the restaurant). The prices and portion sizes are comparable. I guess this review sounds more like a comparison of Super Wok vs. China Palace, and less of a review of how China Palace stands on it's own. Well, again the food is not bad. You won't necessarily be disappointed, per se, especially given you'll be spending at most $7 a person (and that's on the high side, you'll probably be $5-6 per). But just like Yelp describes the two star rating I've assigned, it's "Meh, I've experienced better."
label: NEG

text: Let me begin by saying that I've been in several Sephora stores over the years....dating back to the late 80s when I frequented the original Paris location. I'm not throwing that out there to sound like a snob, but to set the stage for this review. Yikes! I agree with Holly H., the cleanliness of this store is scary....where is Tabatha from Salon Takeover, even though it's not a salon, this place could use her help! True the product selection is amazing, but that's Sephora's trademark so why shouldn't it be? Check out their stores in larger cities such as San Francisco and the Indy store will come off as a mere kiosk of cosmetic heaven! So, why is it that all the testers and display areas look so sloppy, dusty and well, downright yucky?? I went in to purchase a Smashbox item and would have loved to try some other products, but I didn't feel confident doing so. Also, I pretty much was on my own and was never once greeted or asked if I needed assistance. This is sad, because I tend to be such an easy sell when it comes to fragrant potions and pots of color. The gentleman who took my money was friendly enough, but nobody in the store seemed very ambitious, so I left with ONLY that one item in my bag!
label: NEG

text: I went here last night with a friend who doesn't really like Mexican food, and another who swears this is the best place ever--she and her husband go almost every Sunday. Well, when we left, she was apologizing that this experience was a total fluke and it's not normally like this. Yeah, I was not so impressed. The patio is great, for starters. I can see how that is a huge draw of this place. The waitress (who was not the person that "normally" waits on my friend, I guess) brought out chips and salsa, but the chips tasted burnt. We asked for another basket, and these didn't taste much better. But we were starving so we ate them anyway. I also ordered sangria--that tasted like fruit punch. It was not good. Usually, sangria is served with fruit in it and some ice, but this had neither. Just a weird color, and I half expected the Hawaiian Punch character to jump out at us while we were eating. Anyway. Food was so-so. Got the chicken quesadilla, and it was fine but not nearly mind-blowing. I'll go again, on the advice of my friend--apparently, it's usually a better experience than this. I'll update this after my next visit, but for now, two stars.
label: NEG

text: This restaurant just opened 3 days ago in the old space occupied by Ava - which always seemed to be empty. I met the owner Christine a few weeks ago as they were deciding on the paint color for the walls and waited for it to open, which was this week. We made our first visit tonight. Christine - sorry I don't have her last name handy - has a catering business but her history goes back to Girasole at 13th and Locust Sts. The last restautant she had was on 10th above South and was called something like Mia. (I'm guessing) We never ate there. Since Olive is closer to our house we went tonight. We enjoyed it though it is still a work in progress. The place was about 75% full while we were there (Friday from 6:30 to 8:pm) and Christine was there and visible the first 20 minutes or so. After that it was left up to the one waiter and the 4-5 young women clearing tables and bringing bread. Obviously understaffed for the crowd. (Michael Klein had written it up in his Inky column yesterday.). Or order was taken quickly and bread - tasty and dense and baked on the premises - and olives (what else?) arrived. The entrees took a while but we were happy with our wine (it is a BYOB, which we love!). We both ordered the same thing, which was a stuffed pork loin - stuffed with mushrooms, eggplant and broccoli rabe. It was served with roasted potatoes and steamed and sautéed broccoli (a different vegetable might have added variety since there was broccoli in the pork). Portions were ample for the price ($15.00). We were given a complimentary dessert (Grand opening) and we chose homemade carrot cake which was moist and flavorable.. They seem to still be working out the kinks but Christine's enthusiasm and interest in catering to neighbors and not depending on the weekend seasonal South Street visitors is evident. The paint job is nice and the restaurant is attractive. No music was playing, which was fine and the noise level was low. I spotted other items on the menu (Meat Loaf can be a good test; and the Veal Marsala looked good on another table) so we'll go back at least once more. As time goes on, the service should improve - help for the ONE waiter who apparently did not have a lot of server experience to begin with but was very caring and did check back to see if we were pleased with the food.
label: POS

text: It was great to see a donut shop open in Reno.....something that is a staple on every street corner back east is difficult to find here. The donuts are very good. As earlier reviews have indicated, they are more expensive than grocery store donuts, but they are also twice as large! So although a dozen costs more, you feed more people. In addition to a good selection of donuts you can get pastries, coffee and drinks. The donut holes are the size of tennis balls, but get there early, they're popular and run out fast! If you're looking to splurge and have donuts I would recommend going to DoughBoys. The donuts are a treat and it's always good to buy from local businesses!
label: POS

text: So I had to spend my birthday in Tampa (I know, boohoo, poor me), and since I didn't know the area very well, I depended on good ol' Yelpie to find me this place! Located in this outdoor plaza type of mall that had a surprisingly large amount of people there, this place had everything I could ask for: bowling, food, drinks (and if I wanted, dancing, but I guess I didn't want because I didn't dance ha). Overall, it was a good time, and for a few hours, we bowled and ate and drank the night away before heading out to explore other parts of Tampa. Price wasn't too bad, food was decent, and the atmosphere was pretty fun on the Saturday night. If I'm ever back, I would definitely try to stop by here again. Edit: I just realized this is my 100th review!! How exciting! Well, it is also part 1 of maybe 3 reviews that I will write about places in Tampa, so enjoy!
label: POS

text: Every time I drive by this restaurant, it looks so dead and empty! Dead and empty brings forth a fear of anxiousness because if said restaurant was indeed dead and empty, then surely the freshness and integrity of the choice fish would be compromised???? But no, and I must say that this restaurant is really great for people on this side of the river. The sushi bar easily can seat about 10 or 14 and is spacious. The restaurant has booths lining the perimeter of the permises and wooden tables in between. The spacing of these tables are very figure friendly. Had the crunchy roll with soy wrap, agedashi tofu (fried PERFECTLY and crispy YUM), squid salad, snowcrab naruto, and pepper girl roll. Snowcrab naruto was very boring - obviously the skills to cut the cucumber was lacking, what should've been one long sheet ended up being several cut pieces like a rose petal. That lead to the uselessness of chopsticks because it broke apart before one picks it up. Pepper girl roll was GREAT though and beautifully presented. Seared tuna tataki with snowcrab on top and other misc items. It was gooooooooood! This restaurant IS a bit more pricey than other Japanese restaurants, but if you don't feel like driving across the bridge, then this place will have to do. Come 6:30 pm and there was just a huge influx of folks coming in. I was shocked and plesantly surprised at the amount of foot traffic. Anyway, come either before 6:30 or after 8 to ensure best waiting services.
label: POS

text: Needed a place to stay for a last minute biz trip to SB. Sandman seemed nice enough for the price, and since it was for business I didn't care too much about quality. I'm not that demanding, especially since I really only used the room to sleep because I was in meetings all day. Pros: -Newish flat screen TV. -Nice to have a mini fridge in the room. -They include free bottles of water. -In a decent location. Lots of motels on the street, lots of fast food options, and a Whole Foods close by. Cons: -Beds on the short side. I'm 6ft, and I had to make sure to sleep diagonally. -Water was either too hot or cold, hard to find the middle area for just warm. -Thin ceiling because I could hear the people in the room above me walking around. -The blinds were broken, so I could not close them all the way. -Toilet would run water every so often. I was only there two nights. So didn't make a fuss or try to exchange rooms.

text: So this place is just one humongous park with trails that go throughout. It will take you a good couple hours to explore so dont get there 45 minutes before closing like I did. However, I have found that the best photos are taken during sunset so you might want to take that into consideration when coming here. The Redwood section and the Meadow section are gorgeous. text: Well, I've only been here once, because after my first visit I swore I would never go back. We called ahead to order some hoagies on a Saturday afternoon, they said 15 min, I gave them 20 for good measure. I took my toddler with me, thinking I would just slip in and grab our order. text: So, my mom REALLY likes tea houses, so my sister and I took her here as our Christmas present to her. They brought out our tea (and brought milk in a little cow dish as well as lumps of sugar). Then, they brought our first course of scones and muffins. The scones were OK... just OK, but darn those muffins were GOOD!!! The 2nd course, we chose the type of soup we want. My mom and I had the potato soup, while my sister had the chicken mushroom noodle. BOTH of the soups were YUMMY! Course 3 was a savory torte... they called it a quiche, but i wouldn't say that as it really wasn't egg-y enough. We all had the spinach and artichoke one, but the other option was a broccoli one. This course was just okay. I wasn't so impressed with it. After this they brought our a tiered tray. The first tier was of fruit... kiwi, orange, and pineapple. (BOO!!! I LOVE MANGO AND OTHER THINGS... i thought the fruit could've been more fun). The second tier was the little snacky sandwiches-- a curried chicken salad in phyllo, cucumbers with some basil, and a tomato- bacon one. SUPER YUMMY!!!! The bottom tier was of desserts! Each of us had a chocolate covered strawberry, a little pineapple upside down cake and another crisp of some sort that tasted citrus-y. YUM!!! Finally, they brought out sherbet... which I could hardly eat because i was STUFFED! The bill itself was about 84 bucks and with tip, I spent 102. TOTALLY YUMMY THOUGH and a great experience! Only thing i would change is the fruit options, and maybe make that torte actually more of a quiche! YUM!!! We left the tea room happily cracked out from all that caffeine and VERY full!!!

text: OK, Wishing Well. I know you're the new kid on the block. I think you have some potential. But some things are gonna have to change. First things first - we came in last night, and were pleased by the beer selection. Terrapin Cap'n Krunkles, Ballast Point Big Eye IPA, Dark Horse Crooked Tree IPA, New Holland Dragon's Milk....all great beers to choose from. On top of that, they were $2 off on Monday. Service was friendly and attentive...but onward with the food.... The problem here seems to be that key ingredients and/or flavor are missing from plates. The mozzarella sticks? The cheese was obviously fresh, and tasted fantastic - and the smoked tomato dipping sauce was great. But the breading lacked any kind of flavor. We both ordered burgers - for me, the tuna burger, and for him, the hyped SHAME burger. Unfortunately, neither were totally great. My tuna burger was fairly tasty, but still lacking some flavor. As for the SHAME burger, well, the beef lacked any flavor at all. It tasted like something out of the frozen food aisle at Acme. A total disappointment. We shared the banana pudding for dessert, which was also underwhelming. It tasted like instant banana pudding, but the only thing that saved it were the caramelized bananas - which were pretty amazing! My advice for the Well is fairly simple: do not fear embracing quality ingredients and spicing up your dishes with more flavor. Maybe your bigger plates are better than the bar food. But if you're going to make the SHAME burger one of your biggest selling points, would it hurt to use some top notch, fresh, well-seasoned Angus beef? I'm willing to pay more for a burger that I know will be full of flavor. (I suggest trying the Royal Tavern's burger if you need an example.) Oh, and maybe close for a week, make the windows bigger, and find a different color for your walls and some artwork. Ultimately, I agree with Jason that there is no vision here. This isn't the first time a local pub has had some growing pains. That's for sure. But it's best the growing pains are remedied before the Well gets a negative reputation. Your chops and experience seem to be there - but the execution is pretty bad. The neighborhood wants you here! I'll probably be back for some drinks, and some fries, which were pretty tasty - but probably not for dinner until it improves.

text: So all of the other reviews are pretty much on the right track here, this place is awesome. The owners are two of the nicest people I have ever met. They chat with you and really make you feel at home. This place really does feel like exactly that, a home. Has a really nice and comfortable outdoor seating area in kind of a garden setting, just a really nice place to relax and eat a mid day meal. Little bit off the beaten path but well worth the trip, no matter where you're coming from. You order up front and can sit outdoors and then one or two, or both of the owners will bring your food right out to you. Probably their most popular dish are their "Lomito" sandwiches. They are INCREDIBLE. I have never had anything like them before. I ordered the original Lomito and my girlfriend got the mini-lomito. They were so good. Big fluffy potato bread bun, with steak, ham, tomato, cheese, lettuce, spiced mayonnaise and fried egg, all on one sandwich. One of the tastiest sandwiches I have ever eaten. The only downside to their dishes are that they come with what you order, nothing else. No side fries, no pickles, nothing, just the sandwich, for around $7 I normally would expect something on the side, but you know what, it was so good so I really didn't care. We also ordered a side of papas fritas, with salt and pepper. Oh my god, seasoned perfectly, and full of flavor. Only had about 7 slices of potato on the dish, but they were SO good. The ketchup they bring out is also their own, it's slightly spicy like it's mixed with some sort of hot sauce, and it makes everything taste even better. We got a couple iced coffees to go with our meal, $2 each and they were huge. The coffee you can just tell is amazing quality. Big plus for this place here, iced coffee refills are just $1! That's amazing. Also, we were about to leave and we were going to take a couple iced coffees for the road, we ordered two small ones and had a chat with one of the owners (Oscar), while he was preparing them, asking about the heritage of the food and stuff (Paraguay if you're wondering). They were supposed to be $1.64 each (+tax), but after we were done chatting he was just like, "For you guys, $1 each." You know, it really makes you feel special and appreciated when something like that happens, they truly are a nice couple, and a pleasure to dine for. For two people, including the iced coffees to go, the bill was like $24. That's $12 a pop for a big GREAT sandwich with a side of potatoes and two huge cups of iced coffee, honestly, you really couldn't ask for more. I WILL be going back here, no doubt in my mind, if only just to talk with Oscar again, he's the man! And to get more of their fantastic unique sandwiches, I have to try them all before I die, because they all looked crazy good. By the way their menu isn't limited, they have all sorts of breakfast and lunch foods including eggs prepared anyway you want, salads, really everything you could want from a brunch place. The only thing they didn't really have was regular breakfast foods like pancakes and french toast, but who cares, it's not that kind of place, it's better. Do yourself a favor and try this place out, you won't regret it.

Apparently you can just stop by but do so at your own risk. There isn't a bar and the most of the limited number of tables were filled while we were there. When we were seated, our waiter brought us water glasses and my friend immediately noticed her glass had a large lipstick stain on the rim. Two of us ordered a bottle of sparkling water when it was offered only to discover later that they didn't have bottles and we were charged $2 each for a very small glass. Our service was horrible...it seemed like it might have been our waiter's first day on the job because he seemed completely flustered. We ordered our starter and then he didn't return to take our entree order for about 45 mins. during which our rather large menu's were left in front of us. When we did finally order and our food arrived, it was just ok. Definitely nothing spectacular. In summation, if it hadn't been a lovely night in a beautiful garden, I would have been much more upset by the lack of service we received. As it was, I would only recommend this place to someone just wanting to relax and have a drink before heading some where else for dinner.

My husband tried the sushi - he had one plate and then skipped to fruit because the fish was so mushy. Later on that night he had some digestive issues. In short, if you want Asian style food, go across the street to CJ's Place. For AYCE Sushi, try Tha Joint Sushi (tha joint has better sushi than CJ's, but CJ's has some great Chinese food). text: I feel bad saying anything good about this abominable tourist trap, so i will refrain, and just focus on providing a much needed counterpoint to the many deceptive positive reviews here on yelp. Let us begin with the "famous" oysters rockefeller. This dish may have been invented here, but surely it was perfected elsewhere. the thick coating of disgusting green goo is the sort of thing you might expect to find in a tv dinner, but certainly not a fine dining appetizer. Skip this selection, and also steer clear of the escargot bordelaise, which is a small number of snails buried in a thick, hideous, brownish-maroon sludge. Although the menu seems to offer many entrees, a closer inspection will reveal that the diner must choose between chicken, beef, trout, and soft shell crab. ( i exaggerate but only slightly). The many choices are primarily a matter of varying whether almonds will be applied, and whether the protein will be fried or grilled. Some of the other reviewers have lauded the soft shell crab as "the best they ever had". Pity these poor unfortunates, but do not follow their lead. Amazingly, we were explicitly warned by the waiter about how terrible the grilled version of this dish is. I can only imagine how unbearable it must be if the fried version is better. Be wary of the side dish options. the famous "puffed potatoes" (pimped enthusiastically by the wait staff) are nothing more than a soggy, inferior tasting (albeit geometrically impressive) version of lay's potato chips. Although I cannot recommend the mixed drinks, which seem to largely consist of mixer, ordering wine is also fraught with peril as the waitstaff seem to feel that it is appropriate to set the bottle (ensconced in an ice bucket) on the floor. apparently wine stands weren't yet invented in 1874, and this abysmal restaurant has yet to improve on the standards of that era. The baked alaska desert was adequate, though nothing special. After you have been bludgeoned with the stogy cuisine, be sure to flee immediately, since touring the dated facility is only bound to send your evening further into a spiral of depression. In a city with so many superior dining options, it's nothing less than a miracle that this soul-crushing establishment stays in business. ignore the shills, and eat elsewhere.

text: At long last, I finally took the plunge and tried the now Yelp-Infamous Hodaks. My friend has been going here for years and highly recommended the 1/2 Golden Chicken plate, so that's what I got. First let me say that the place was packed! We went around 2pm-ish and it was just wall to wall tables and people. The atmosphere could be described as a rustic Applebees. The walls are adorned with all manner of nostalgia inducing antique bric-a-brac. Service was great. Our waitress took our order promptly and kept our drinks full. And our food came out fast! I was surprised by just HOW fast considering the amount of food that came out. I had a wing, a breast, a thigh and a leg (duh, 1/2 a chicken!) a mountain of crinkle cut, oven-baked fries and vinegar based coleslaw. Everything was piping hot and was properly cooked. The fries were crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. I tried a few bites of the coleslaw and it was ok, I guess.... which is an extremely positive remark considering I hate coleslaw. Of course the chicken was the star of the show! It was tender. Juicy, excellently prepared and had a rich, slow cooked chicken flavor. I will say that the breading was a little disappointing. It was more of a cornmeal/breadcrumb coating rather than more conventional flour batter. While the spicing was pretty good and added another level to the deliciously prepared chicken, the somewhat gritty texture left me yearning for Porter's flaky batter. Definitely not bad, but it seemed like a texture that would require getting used to. I also really enjoyed the flavor of the bbq sauce on the table, although it could have been nearly any kind of bbq sauce since it had been packaged into a blank, maroon squeeze bottle. A massive meal leaving me feeling weak and sickeningly full (a sure sign of an EXCELLENT meal!) all for $12 dollars including tip will have me coming back to try other items on the Hodak menu, despite my feelings about the breading.
label: POS

text: Wonderful Vietnamese food. We liked it so much during our visit to the Tampa area that we ate here two nights in a row. The minute we walked in, we could tell that we were in for authentic Vietnamese cuisine in a pleasant, low-key atmosphere. We enjoyed their cha gio (spring rolls), even though they were smaller and thinner than what we typically order at Vietnamese restaurants. The accompanying nam pla (fish sauce) was delicious, full of julienned carrots and radish. My guy loved the grilled shrimp and pork over rice vermicelli (bun). He had it both nights. I tried the pork, and it was well-marinated in a delicious sauce. I ordered one of their traditional pho soups the first night, and it was delicious. The meat was tender, and the broth was flavorful. The second night, I ordered their spicy pho (I can't remember its official name) with tendon and beef. It also had cubes of pork blood (a specialty that looked and tasted like liver), which I didn't care much for, but it added to the depth of flavor in the soup. The accompaniments to the pho was great - fresh mint, Vietnamese basil, sliced chile, and beansprouts. As for drinks, I ordered the mixed nut drink the first night and then the rainbow ice drink the second night. Both were tasty, with lots of texture and served in generous portions. Each drink was topped with a huge chunk of crushed ice (akin to a snow cone without any flavor), which I could have done without. I ended up removing most of the ice to avoid diluting the flavor of each drink. If I lived in Tampa, I would be here all the time. If you're ever visiting Tampa and in the mood for authentic Vietnamese food, definitely check this out!

text: 100% worth of 5 stars if you substitute in a better waitress; hostess and kitchen staff were excellent! Soooo what my dad and I were looking for in terms of dinner when the rest of the house abandoned us (I don't cook when it's just us two, rarely do I cook for us plus my brother. My number is 4+.) Anyway, I don't understand why I hadn't heard of this amazing little place. I just googled it, it seems to have completely changed since Joe Bonwich of the Post-Dispatch reviewed it in 2008. It's now BBQ in an adorable, but classy setting. The atmosphere is perfect and the whole place smells of BBQ - but not overwhelmingly so. Hard, dark woods with black accents, clean lines and everything is polished. The food though. Ohmylord. New favorite. All my dad and I could talk about was everyone we wanted to bring there. We started with the Smothered Fries - cut potatoes with some skin on, rib meat, a homemade white cheese sauce topped with more cheese. Sooo good. The cheese sauce was creamy and sharp, the fries had a touch of salt and the meat was smokey, which all balanced in perfect harmony. The St. Louis Style Spare Ribs came in true fashion. Rubbed with a thick dry rub and obviously smokey for hours, the meat pulled away from the bone without struggle - literally a baby could have gummed the meet from the bones. The spice rub was great, coated well. My dad had the pulled pork and raved about it. He also tried all three sauces on the table - he couldn't pick his favorite though, all were good. Dessert. Ooooh a sweet ending. They don't have a dessert menu because the head chef's mother does all the baking so the options switch nearly weekly - adorable. text: My husband and I have been coming here for years and it has been our go to place for anniversaries, birthdays, etc. When we recently went to the new location for dinner we were both very disappointed. They have retained mostly the same wait staff over the years but they were somehow different now. It was as if the new location had changed their demeanor. Professionalism is appreciated but an aloof and hauty attitude is not. We take pride in being friendly and considerate to service persons. I have eaten at exceptional restaurants all over the world and it seemed as though they are trying to take themselves far more seriously than is necessary for Reno. In the old location it was friendly, intimate, old school, Rat Pack kinda cool. Now it is trying for a chi, chi, trendy, snobbish, avant-garde atmosphere and it just doesn't work for those of us who knew it the way it was. My seafood raviolis were excellent as always but my husbands dish which had Italian sausage in it was distasteful and literally "squeaked" when he tried to chew it. We sent it back and the waitress seemed perturbed because as she pointed out, "no one else had complained." Now to be fair we did not dine until about 7 PM so perhaps the sauce had been simmering way too long. I find it interesting that fine dining establishments take it as an affront if you send something back that is not to your liking (which has only happened a few times) but more moderately priced places seem to have less of an ego and understand this sometimes happens. A bad dish can happen to anyone and as an avid gourmet cook I understand that a restaurateur does not have the option of telling their patrons what I tell my family, "sorry, guess you'll just have to quit complaining and eat it. I'll do better next time." That being said it really came down to the service and I just wasn't really impressed any more. Maybe it's just growing pains.

text: I debated whether or not to write this review, as I haven't actually eaten the food here - but after some thought - it was solely due to the service and attitude of the staff that we did not. Our friends had heard about Nitally's through some of those *other* review sites, and suggested we go there for a birthday dinner. Our plans had been made a few weeks ago, before Nitally's was listed as one of Tampa's Bests in a local newspaper. Our group of 5 arrived a little after 6pm on a Saturday night. The restaurant looks pretty small from the outside, and the red curtains in the windows remind me less of a restaurant and more of a sex shop. Opening the door, the place was smaller than we could have imagined. If you imagined a "hole in the wall" restaurant - this place would be the size of a corner in that hole in the wall. There were six or seven tables total - with two of them put together in the middle with a "reserved" sign on them. Unfortunately, they were not reserved for us. I stood in the doorway while one of our group spoke to a waitress about the table situation. It was going to be 20-25 minutes until an inside table would be available. We could, however, choose to eat outside. We decided we wanted to eat inside, but we would sit outside and enjoy some drinks while we waited. She brought some menus out and we looked over them for a few minutes to decide on our drinks. When she came back to take our orders, we found out that they were out of half the beers or flavors we wanted. We ended up with some various beers, wines and boba teas. The beer and wine were fine, but those who got the boba teas complained about the tapioca being very gummy. To top it off, they were served with regular straws - not ones wide enough to accommodate the balls. After being served our drinks, we were ignored for over an hour. Not once did the waitress come out to see if we wanted refills or if we had changed our minds about eating outside instead of waiting. After over an hour, our fearless leader went in to see what was going on as we could see an empty table from where we were sitting. There was a table for four open - but they weren't allowed to pull up an extra chair or combine the table with another due to issues with the fire marshall. I guess he also mentioned that we were being eaten alive by mosquitos. A minute or so after he returned, an employee came out with a fan and set it to blow towards us and went back inside. He came back out a few minutes later to ask if it had helped. It had not. He reiterated the issue with the combined tables - and offered an alternative: they had two tables that they could not combine - but we could split up our group and sit separately. WHAT? At that point, we decided we would go elsewhere. I'm torn now. The menu looked really interesting, and I'd really like to try their food - but their service and attitude makes me want to stay away. If you go, get take out or make reservations in advance.

text: I used to be a serious Insomnia cookies addict. The idea that you can get fresh baked cookies delivered to your doorstep? Wow!! It totally won me over for a good while. Sure, sometimes the cookies seemed a bit raw or broken into pieces, and sometimes they even arrived dead cold. But I always found it in my heart to forgive them. My last experience with Insomnia Cookies, however, was unforgivable. I had ordered $6 worth of cookies (the minimum for delivery) and with the $1 delivery charge and $1 tip I planned to give, my total came out to $8. When the order came, I went down with a $10 bill expecting to get $2 in change. But the delivery boy surprisingly claimed that he did not have change....... What?! You're a delivery person and you don't have $2 in change? Are you kidding? This was the first time I have ever encountered a delivery person who did not carry any change. This may not have been too big of a problem if I had small bills, but I didn't. And the cookies were there. And I was stuck. What was I supposed to do? I spent a good 5 minutes standing there while my friend ran around to neighbors asking for change. No luck. And I was forced to give up my $10. That is $3 tip for $6 worth of cookies. WTF. If I were rich and made of money, then maybe I would not have been as upset as I was. But unfortunately, I am a poor student and to make matters worse, Chinese. I was raised to be frugal and to furiously value my money. So when I got back to my room, I immediately sent a calm and angry e-mail to Insomnia Cookies headquarters explaining the situation. A few minutes later, I got a response apologizing for the incident. Indeed, all delivery persons should be ready with change. And it was arranged for my change to be delivered back to me. I thought, great! Insomnia cookies, you failed me once, but I'm glad that you have redeemed yourself. However, when the delivery boy came back with my change, he not only forced me to meet him at his car out at the curb in the freezing cold, but also handed me this little wad of paper, in which my change was wrapped up in. I was like..huh?? What is this? After going inside and unwrapping the paper, I found my two dollars, folded into a ridiculous small square. And the paper that it came wrapped it? It had the lovely note: "What the fuck is 2 bucks?!?!?!" Well sir, $2 is a lot of tip for a crappy delivery service. Don't act like you are doing me some kind of favor for delivering my cookies. I am doing YOU the favor of ordering cookies and giving you business in the first place. So a fair warning to all, please don't let your delivery boy scam you into giving him a ridiculous tip. All delivery persons SHOULD HAVE CHANGE.
label: NEG

text: I can't recommend Buffalo Wild Wings, so I'm giving it a two-star review. I went there today before going to the movies. You're allowed to get up to two flavors, so I split them between a spicy Asian flavor and a Jamaican jerked flavor. I passed on the beer and got a sour apple drink. My movie started at 4:30 p.m. and I placed my order at about 3:40 p.m., so I thought I had a lot of time. The drink arrived quickly. It was tasty but it was also a lot of ice. At about 3:55 p.m. a staff member brought out seven wings. Four of the Jamaican and three of the Asian spiced. I explained I ordered 14 wings. Rather than leave those, he took them away. I could have gotten started on those and finished the rest with plenty of time. My complete order came at 4:05 p.m., Now I was a little rushed for the show. The Asian spiced wings were okay. I'd get those again. The Jamaican were bad. Both flavors were kind of gloppy messes on the wings. And the boneless chicken didn't seem to be the highly quality meat. On specials like this they charge you 50 cents if you want ranch dressing or blue cheese. There's a lot of other flavors. One of them could be especially tasty. Based on what I had today, I can't recommend this place.

text: My man Greg is a crate digger five star general. He's got more 45's than the Dodge City Museum... and Greg was saying to me recently how legit The Marv really is. I've been going in and out for three years. The guys who run the place seem cool, but you can easily sense that they'd give your grandmother 10 bucks for your grandfather's record collection, before slanging it for thousands. Fine and good. The Marvelous has the best vinyl in West Philly. The stuff is all premo, not crappy junk. They specialize in Soul, Funk, R&B. However, unlike the spots downtown, they also have proper sections in Electronic, New Wave, Surf Rock, and Rockabilly. You gotta love all that. Equally, the Jazz section in the back is humbling. The prices aren't. Like most dedicated record stores, you're not gonna get a 100 dollar Incredible Bongo Band Italian pressing for 50 cents. What you will get is no junk. When people are new at buying records, they pick up crap. For $3-$12, you can guaranteed stuff... that worst case scenario, will hold better than half its value should you go to eBay. The CDs are overpriced, but they do house some Indie Rock and Hip-Hop that you can't get just anywhere. I'm not a comic book head, but there's always people scanning their collection. Lastly, they have the music mags that Borders and B&N are too dumb and too corporate to carry. I love The Marvelous, and no crate-digger ever lets his secrets out easily... but I want places like this to THRIVE. So, all that being said, if I see you grabbing my records there... it's trouble t-roy. kid-ding, sorta. Quite frankly... if I ever marry up in the world, this is the kind of store I'd dream of opening.

When I arrived at 8:00a, they were just opening up their clean, organized shop, putting out the flags, and getting ready for business. text: Since I live nearby, I've been a frequent shopper at this Whole Foods for the sake of convenience. I've shopped here at least once a week for the past three years. There are some serious quality issues at this location. Milk goes rancid days before the "sell by" date. Packaged cheese grows mold before its expiration date, even when properly sealed after being opened. Many times I've come home and opened my carton of strawberries to find them covered in mold. Cucumbers are soft and gooey in the middle. Packaged spinach wilts and starts to smell before the "use by" date. Like the reviewer below, in the summer I've seen flies swarming around the deli and landing on the cold cuts. The one time I purchased and cooked mussels from this store, I got diarrhea. I've shopped at the South Street and Plymouth Meeting Whole Foods stores, and I'm a frequent customer at Trader Joe's. I've never had any quality issues with food purchased at any of these stores. This suggests to me that it's not my refrigerator that's the problem; rather, there is a serious problem with handling and refrigeration of perishable food items at the Art Museum store. It's really quite outrageous, because if I'm going to be gouged by ridiculous prices, the product had better be fresh. It appears that the policy with produce is to keep it on the floor until it sells, regardless of whether it's still fresh or not. It's great that edible produce is not going to waste, but if the store is going to do this, there should be a discount for produce that is past its prime. Why would I want to pay $3 for a bag of spinach that smells like a garbage can? Customer service is hit or miss. It's obvious that the cashiers have been instructed to engage the customers in conversation while ringing them up. ("How was your day? Any plans for the evening? What are you doing this weekend?") They mean well, but I find it irksome. The only reason I awarded two stars, rather than one, is for their amazing Icelandic chocolate.

text: The Arch is quite an experience. It just looks kinda cool from afar, but when you get up close it's really impressive. You just don't see the magnitude until you're at the base. A warning: the tram you ride up in is very small and a bit rickety. Once you get to the top, though, the ride is worth it. The St. Louis skyline itself itsn't all that exciting to look at (unless you've lived there & know what all the buildings are) nor is East St. Louis, but it's just cool to be 630 feet up in the air looking down at everything. One time I went up in the Arch, it had snowed outside so everything was covered in white - it was quite pretty. The most recent time I went up, it was a very clear day with blue skies and we had a great aerial view of the brand-new Busch Stadium. The museum underneath the Arch is kind of neat, and it's free, so check it out while you're there. You can also get tickets to a movie about the Arch construction and for a riverboat ride down the Mississippi, but I haven't experienced either of those attractions yet. If you're visiting St. Louis, the Arch should be on your agenda. You won't forget it.

We struggled to keep up with the speed demon hostess - my father-in-law moves in an obviously slowly manner - the hostess didn't care and wanted us seated, her impatience was painfully obvious. text: Recently being touted as the 'Best Burger in the Quarter', we decide to go try this place - what a mistake - an expensive mistake at that. Oh well - the burger here was unquestionably large, but the combination of all these toppings slathered w/heavy mayo made for a big giant mess - the bun quickly became completely unidentifiable due to so many ingredients leaking all over - and the burger flavor you crave is so well hidden within all the stuff, you really cannot tell it's even a burger. You simply cannot taste that great grilled flavor of a really well-made hamburger: instead, you find you're always eating a lot of sloppy, tasteless 'stuff' that has all melded together into a big pile on your plate. There was no familiar hamburger mouth-feel - that soothing textured bite you take and enjoy in a great burger was non-existent - you could eat this thing without teeth, it was so messy and soggy. In this case, bigger isn't better - just bigger. I just want a nice, big, juicy, fresh hamburger - not this mess. What are they hiding? And the huge potato is absolutely nothing to write home about - you can get a better baked potato at Wendy's for $.99. I recommend you leave well enough alone - don't experiment - go eat at Port O'Call if you really want the "Best Burger in New Orleans". This place would be best for those people who love buffetts - who want quantity over quality - don't say you didn't know or weren't warned - buyer beware.

text: I'm really picky about pizza, but Gianfranco is the best that I've had in Philly. I realize that pizza is sort of a personal thing, so I tried to give both objective and subjective evaluations of the sauce, crust and cheese. Maybe you'll disagree with me on how excellent the overall product is, but hopefully I'll give you a good idea of what to expect when you order from Gianfranco. First, the sauce. Gianfranco's pizza is pretty saucey, which is key for me. There's nothing I hate more than under-sauced pizza, which seems to be all too common in the Philadelphia area. (Especially in Wayne... If you're in Wayne, go to DiMeo's. New Wayne and Real Pizza are awful.) The sauce's sweet/salty balance is perfect. I don't know whether that's a function of using fresh tomatoes vs. canned or what (honestly, Gianfranco may used canned, I don't care), but it's exactly what I love. On to the crust. The crust is middle of the road, thickness-wise. It's certainly not deep dish, but not New York/Jersey Shore style either. (I would say try Pete's on Chestnut if you're in Old City and looking for NY-style) But it definitely works with the rest of the pizza. It's thin enough to get a little crispy, but thick enough that it a) can handle the sauce level and b) gives you some bready flavor. And it's never overcooked, at least in my experience. I don't have strong convictions about there being a "right kind" or "wrong kind" of crust, but Gianfranco's goes perfectly with the other ingredients. Lastly, the cheese. The cheese is, as many people have pointed out, stringy. That's how mozzarella is, and if you don't like that, you don't like a pure-mozzarella pizza. It's lightly cooked, with little to no browning. Whether you like that is up to you, but for me it's heaven. If I had to describe Gianfranco's pizza in one word, it would be "fresh". As I said before, I don't know whether Gianfranco uses 100% fresh tomatoes in its sauce or if their bread comes from a can, but something about the pizza tastes really fresh to me. And there's a certain synergy between the sauce, crust and mozzarella that I don't often taste at a pizza place. And in the end, I think that's what I like so much about Gianfranco. It might not be the best in Philly (I haven't been everywhere) but I can say with some certainty that it's top tier.

text: The Stockyard used to be the premier steakhouse in the Nashville area, and had Yelp existed 8 years ago when I graduated I probably would have told you that it was the best food I'd ever tasted 8 years ago... Well, this is 8 years later and a lifetime of travel and living across the globe later... the Stockyard simply is not a high quality steakhouse any longer. What I enjoyed: I enjoyed the history of the building provided by the server. I enjoyed learning about how the building had been a true stockyard, a speak-easy, and the basement had served as a place where live country shows had taken place in the basement with random big names that had stopped by like Dolly, Reba, Merle, etc. I thought that was interesting. Here's the problem... none of that is food! It's a restaurant. I had the house salad which is your typical mesclun greens with balsamic dressing and some tomatoes and mushrooms. The dressing was a little thick for balsamic, and unimpressive. I ordered the prime rib (our server was thankfully honest and said 'we have salmon and lobster, but in case you haven't noticed Tennessee is a land-locked state and we're a steak house'). I ordered it medium rare because I'm all about the red meat still being red. It was cooked correctly but it wasn't mouth-wateringly deliciously and I've had better spice at other places. It was not worth the cost. For dessert, I had the pecan pie which was so-so but again I've had better. Their wine selection is adequate, but if you want to claim to be a premier steakhouse it should be mindblowing. Although, they do apparently have the oldest bottle of wine in North America that's for sale... a mere $450,000. Some 1770-something bottle of red that I can't believe they'd put on the menu except to be pretentious (and I like pretentious things... hello... read my profile). All and all, I wouldn't waste your money and I'd choose somewhere else to dine.
label: NEG

text: I adore Vietnam Restaurant. Ever since they remodeled to this classic Vietnamese French decor a few years back, it has become a great place to go if you're in Chinatown but don't necessarily want Chinese food. It's a popular place with great food to back it up. It's best to call by numbers when ordering here. Personally, I love their appetizers and would recommend ordering a few to share as the main meal. The Crispy Spring Roll is literally fried to a crisp but unlike the spring rolls from other places, these are crispy chewy, the pork inside is made authentic by the basil and spices. One of the bests I've had. The Shrimp and Pork Roll is non-fried like the regular summer rolls, I prefer this because you can experience different textures with its soft exterior, the succulent shrimp, the crispy bean sprouts and the silky vermicelli noodles. The star of the appetizers have to be the Stuffed Grape Leaves. It's the best dish on the whole menu. Unlike its Greek counterpart, these are stuffed with beef and the whole thing is charred to perfection. Dip it in sauce and wrapped them inside a lettuce leaf with pickled vegetables and vermicelli and treat it like a lettuce wrap. It's truly amazing. Not to dis their Phos, but there are other restaurants that do better, not to say that theirs are not up to par, but like grandma's chicken noodle soups, we all have our own favorite versions. That said, my favorite noodle soup at Vietnam Restaurant was a Crab and Egg Noodle Soup that unfortunately have been taken out from their menus. Broken rice dishes are basically marinated barbecue meats served with long grain rice that have been broken into smaller pieces. There's history in broken rice but it actually kinda easier to eat and able to absorb more sauce. I love the national famous Lemongrass Pork Chop broken rice or the chicken one. The vermicelli noodle bowls are also great too. Add more ingredients to your heart's content and get a taste of as many things as you want. I can attest to some of the great curries they have but with the great appetizers and dishes, I usually don't go for a main dish because I rather taste 2-3 different things than one main thing. Whatever you do, do try to order a drink like a Vietnamese ice coffee or a fruit shake. If you're more adventurous, try a Vietnamese lemonade or a coconut drink.

text: It was truly a very bad experience. I walked in and there was only one other table sat which just makes me feel a bit uncomfortable. (To be fair it was only 6:10pm.) Service started out fantastic, but definitely fell apart - completely - once the restaurant got to about 85% capacity. It happened quick and I can understand why service slowed, but it basically was non-existent. The bread at the beginning was terrible. Tasted like those frozen rolls you can score at the store. There was a bottle special and it seemed reasonable. The wine list wasn't too much of a reach or out of line with an undeveloped pallet like mine. Few glass choices, though. I thought I'd go for a white because it was so hot in there (I wanted something cold), but the guy warned me that it was really, really, really sweet. I passed. I already planned on having a dessert. (This was when service was going well.) Granted, I was in a suit, but it was maddeningly hot in there. Silly. Appetizers were great. This was certainly the highlight. The wife and I shared the Rusa salad and the provolone. I'd never had provolone like that before. It was good and I could eat that Rusa salad as an entrée. Fantastic! The entrees were what made me want to get up and just leave. It was almost offensive. Get this: mashed potatoes from a box. That's what came with our fancy-pants dinner. Terrible. I wanted to ask our server if they were instant, but the wife said I wasn't allowed. I think she thought it would be rude if I inquired. But, isn't it rude to serve me mashed potatoes from a box? I mean, come'on! It's literally some boiled potatoes, milk, butter and a little bit of salt. And then the tough part: You mash it. Geez! It was awful; about half salt half dehydrated - then rehydrated potato. The meat wasn't any better. My strip was maybe a half-inch cut, but probably not that thick. And there was no flavor. It seriously reminded me of a steak I'd get at a Ponderosa or a Ryan's Steakhouse. It was seriously crap. Wife's filet had a bit more flavor, but not a lot. Desserts were actually good, but nothing much. I had the coconut flan. There was shaved coconut in the egg mixture, but the flavor wasn't really there. I'm gonna guess it wasn't fresh. The scenery is neat in there, though. There are some fun paintings. The staff's 'authentic' dress does make them look a bit silly. We experienced this during Restaurant Week. I've become very accustomed to smaller portions during Restaurant Week and I even think that's fair. We're all in business to make money. This was my first time at the place as I thought a $30 meal would be a good way to try it. They either skimped on quality for Restaurant Week or the quality just isn't there.

text: Alright, not sure how much longer this review will be relevant since the owner was just on the news a few nights ago talking about how he may declare bankruptcy, but here goes... My fiance loved this place back when it was called Jersey Joe's and was on 6th Street. He took me there twice before it moved downtown, and it was wonderful! They used to have this hostess who was amazing, she always remembered your face and was so welcoming. Their food was amazing, especially the vodka sauce. Your meal would come with a yummy little salad and all the garlic bread you could eat, and dinner would run around $13 per person. Apparently, Mr. Ascolese took his business dowtown as a part of the RIo Nuevo project. Not only did he rename the restaurant, he changed everything about the dining experience! Gone are the lovely hostess, the free salads and bread. The hours are incredibly strange, it seems like they open and close on a whim. The food remains as good, but the prices are around $5.00 more per dish - and again, nothing comes with it! The service is REALLY hit-and-miss. The staff generally seem either flustered and uneducated about their offerings, or rude and pushy. Last time we went, the server seemed more like a salesman, constantly trying to push upgrades and additional food on us. And the new building is just odd... I know it is a historic building, but the set-up just feels off - several small dining rooms, outdated decor, etc. Would it have killed them to put a little money into decorating? In my opinion, it is not the fault of city officials and Rio Nuevo that may force this restaurant to close. It is poor decision making by the owners. Everytime I leave this place, I swear I will never go back because I always walk away with the feeling that I have been ripped off. My fiance begs and pleads until we return for no reason other than the food. From the sound of it, they won't be able to suck us back in for much longer.

text: There are two kinds of sushi places and one can be in the mood for either: #1: A sushi restaurant with fresh, fresh fish sliced thick and across the grain. Maybe a combination where the chef will give you an assortment of today's freshest sashimi. Maybe also a few rolls made fresh with interesting spices or ingredients. Places that come to mind are Bluefin, Zento, etc. #2: Quick will-fill-you-up-but-not-make-you-too-full sushi for less than 10 bucks. Some generic rolls like California, Spicy Tuna, Philadelphia Roll that is maybe fresher than the supermarket counter but not by much. I think Mizu fits into the category of #2 and is more appropriate as a local take out place or for a quick bite to eat. Their menu is not too creative and I would not find it worth it to travel across Center City (or even more than 2 blocks) for this. Their prices are fine and you get what you pay for. I would have even given them three stars - but they use the same frozen dumplings and edamame that you could buy at Trader Joe's or your local Asian foodmart.

text: OK - Now they get the fifth star. If you read Pat D.'s review - you'll hear all about the yummy treats she orded when we had lunch here today. I had the greek salad - and they were kind enough to "hold" the feta cheese for me. The greens were crisp and 3 types of olives were used (2 green and 1 black variety) along with batons of red pepper and home-made dolmades. The scrumptios - and simple - lemon and olive oil vinaigrette made it SING. Presented on a white rippled plate - very clever. The plate allowed the dressing to pool away from the crisp greens and thus I could dress the salad as I wished. YUM-MY! The I had the Asian Dumpling soup. The single dumpling had a shrimp-based filling and was scrumptious, as were the veggies in the soup. The broth was a bit salty for my liking - but I am a no-salt added kinda gal. Next was the star of the show - and what I was WAITING for - Chicken & Waffles. It was accompanied by tender-crisp southern greens (with a healthy shot of garlic) and thin-ly julienne deep-fried sweet potato strings. Damn, what a great waffle! The pulled chick on top was tender and delicious - but my one complaint was the copious amount of bland sauce. It nade it a bit too "a la king" -ish for me. Dessert for me was a simple - yet perfect fruit salad of watermelon (sweet and seedless) bites, blackberries,and a single slice of orange. Service was good - I felt so bad for the guy in crutches who had broken his femur. What a trooper. I will be back - hopefully SOON. (And maybe even with Pat D!)
